meanings.note: Placed directly before an indefinite noun without ال- to mean 'the last' (آخر يوم 'the last day', آخر الساحة 'the far end of the courtyard').

examples.trans: The attic room is at the end of the floor.
Today is the last day of the week.

meanings.note: Used in Jordanian speech with subjunctive forms like أأذيها ('hurt her') and يأذوا ('they hurt').

examples.trans: I didn't mean to hurt you.
They won't hurt anyone.

meanings.note: Common Levantine word (from Italian arma) for a shopfront sign.

examples.trans: The shop has a big sign outside.
I saw the blue sign above the door.

meanings.note: Agrees with the speaker's gender: a man says أنا آسف, a woman says أنا آسفة.

examples.trans: I am very sorry for the delay.
Sorry for the bother, sir.

meanings.note: Describes a place or thing that is safe; for people 'safe and sound' is سالم.

examples.trans: The neighbourhood here is safe at night.
These stairs are not safe for children.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for both casual 'yes / yeah' and 'oh! / ah!' upon noticing something.

examples.trans: Oh, the door opened! Thank you.
Yes, eight rooms and eight keys.

meanings.note: Exclamation when a puzzle clicks into place ('aha!').

examples.trans: Aha! Now I understand the whole story!
Aha, that is why you took the bus!

meanings.note: Spontaneous Levantine exclamation when bumping or twisting something.

examples.text: آي! زحلقت رجلي عن طرف الطبلية!
examples.trans: Ouch! My foot slipped off the edge of the low stool!

examples.text: آي، إبريق الشاي لسا سخن كتير!
examples.trans: Ow, the teapot is still super hot!

meanings.note: Classic Arabic phrase meaning 'forever' or 'for good'.

examples.text: رح نضل صحاب للأبد مهما صار.
examples.trans: We will stay friends forever no matter what happens.

examples.text: هادي الذكرى رح تبقى بقلبي على طول الأبد.
examples.trans: This memory will stay in my heart for all eternity.

meanings.note: Reinforces negation ('not at all, never'): ما في زبدة أبدا ('no butter at all'), لا تقلق أبدا ('do not worry at all').

examples.trans: There is no butter in the fridge at all!
Do not worry at all, sir.

meanings.note: Reinforces negation to mean 'at all' or 'never'.

examples.trans: I didn't talk to him about the subject at all.

examples.text: الجو اليوم مو بارد أبداً، بالعكس دافي.
examples.trans: The weather today isn't cold at all; on the contrary, it's warm.

meanings.note: Verb أبدع means 'to excel / do brilliantly' at something.

examples.text: الفرقة أبدعت بالحفلة مبارح والكل انبسط.
examples.trans: The band performed brilliantly at the concert yesterday and everyone loved it.
You really outdid yourself with this drawing—it's truly amazing!

meanings.note: Covers transitive 'push someone away' (أبعدها عني) and the everyday imperative ابعدي ('step away').

examples.trans: Step out of my way.
I wanted to push her away from me.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: Feminine Arabic word meaning 'foreign', agreeing with بطاقة.

examples.text: في سياح أجانب كتير بوسط البلد اليوم.
examples.trans: There are a lot of foreign tourists in downtown Amman today.

examples.text: صاحبتي بتدرس أدب أجنبي بالجامعة الأردنية.
examples.trans: My friend is studying foreign literature at the University of Jordan.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بأجر, بيأجر).

examples.trans: We do not usually rent out the attic.
We rented out all the rooms this week.

أجّل.gloss: to postpone; move to a later date

meanings.en: to postpone; move to a later date
meanings.note: Form II Jordanian verb; spoken text omits shadda (أجلت تذكرتي 'I postponed my ticket').

examples.trans: We moved the meeting to Wednesday morning.

examples.text: رامي أجل تذكرته عشان يحضر الافتتاح.
examples.trans: Rami moved his ticket so he could attend the opening.

meanings.note: Usually preceded by يوم (day) or definite الأحد in Jordanian schedules.

examples.text: يوم الأحد الصبح بنفتح المكتبة بدري.
examples.trans: On Sunday morning we open the library early.

examples.text: رح نتجمع كلنا بالحديقة يوم أحد هادي.
examples.trans: We will all gather in the park on a quiet Sunday.

meanings.note: Plural of حرف (harf), meaning letters.

examples.trans: How many letters are in the word?

examples.text: لازم تكتب اسمك بأحرف واضحة عالاستمارة.
examples.trans: You need to write your name in clear letters on the form.

meanings.note: Elative form of حسن (hasan), used for comparison.

examples.trans: This is better than that.

examples.text: صحتي صارت أحسن بكتير بعد ما ارتحت يومين.
examples.trans: My health got much better after I rested for two days.

meanings.note: Elative of حلو (ḥilu), used for pretty, sweet, or nice.

examples.trans: This is the prettiest car I've seen.

examples.text: القهوة بدون سكر أحلى مع التمر.
examples.trans: Unsweetened coffee is nicer alongside dates.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine حمرا (hamra); شاي أحمر means black tea.

examples.trans: Would you like coffee or black tea?
There is a red ribbon on my suitcase.

meanings.note: Everyday adverb 'sometimes'.

examples.trans: Sometimes air gets into the pipes at night.
Sometimes we have tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Takes a long -uu-/-oo- stem with possessive endings in Jordanian (أخوي my brother, أخوك your brother); dual أخوين.

examples.trans: My older brother lives in Amman.
The brothers sat together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باخد, بياخد).

examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!
Old buildings take time to warm up.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خضرا, plural: خضر).

examples.trans: Pass beside the green pharmacy.
Put the green herbs on the eggs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective placed after a definite noun (السلم الأخير 'the final scale'). Feminine: أخيرة, plural: أخيرين.

examples.trans: This is the final scene in today's episode.
We played the final scale in complete calm.

meanings.note: Everyday adverb meaning 'finally / at last'.

examples.text: أخيراً خلصنا شغل الديكور بعد تعب أسبوعين.
examples.trans: We finally finished the decorating work after two weeks of effort.
Thank goodness, the bus finally arrived!

meanings.note: Form IV verb أدار meaning 'to manage, direct, or run' a kitchen or business.

examples.text: عمي أدار المخبز لحاله أكتر من عشرين سنة.
examples.trans: My uncle ran the bakery on his own for over twenty years.

examples.text: المديرة الجديدة بتدير الفندق بطريقة كتير مرتبة.
examples.trans: The new manager runs the hotel in a very organized way.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of دافي ('warm'); also spelled أدفا.

examples.trans: The piano's sound is warmer when it rains.
The attic is the warmest room in winter.

meanings.note: Plural of دليل (dalīl), meaning proof or evidence.

examples.trans: The police found new evidence.

examples.text: جمعنا كل الأدلة والوثائق قبل الاجتماع.
examples.trans: We gathered all the evidence and documents before the meeting.

meanings.note: Plural of ذكي (ḏakī).

examples.trans: The students in this class are very smart.

examples.text: الأولاد بالمدرسة أذكياء وبفهموا الدرس بسرعة.
examples.trans: The kids at school are bright and grasp the lesson quickly.

meanings.note: Standard/polite word for 'ear' alongside colloquial ذان; feminine in agreement.

examples.text: قرب أذنك واسمع رنة الوتر الصافية.
examples.trans: Bring your ear close and listen to the clear ring of the string.

examples.text: مدام سعاد عندها أذن موسيقية ما بتخطئ نغمة.
examples.trans: Madam Suad has a musical ear that never misses a note.

meanings.note: The number four, used with feminine nouns.

examples.trans: I have four cars.

examples.text: ضل أربع ساعات على موعد الطيارة.
examples.trans: There are four hours left until the flight time.

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: I bought four books.
The guests arrived at four in the afternoon.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'fourteen'.

examples.trans: What does clause fourteen say?
It is seven fourteen.

meanings.note: Numeral 'forty'.

examples.trans: The bus arrives in forty minutes.
I do not wear size forty-four!

meanings.note: Literally 'I beg/hope of you'. Uses -ak/-ik/-kum endings depending on whom you address (أرجوكي to a woman, أرجوكم to a group).

examples.trans: Please let me write the new label!
Please wait a moment by the door.

meanings.note: Everyday word for rice. Often pronounced 'ruz' in Jordanian.

examples.trans: We cooked rice and chicken today.

examples.text: حطي كاستين أرز بسمتي مع مرقة الدجاج.
examples.trans: Put two cups of basmati rice with the chicken broth.

meanings.note: Feminine noun in Arabic despite having no -a ending; means ground, land, or indoor floor.

examples.trans: The floor is clean and dry now.
Set the box on the floor for a moment.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: أرضية, plural: أرضيين).

examples.trans: The kitchen is on the ground floor.
The ground-floor rooms are close to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: أرضيات.

examples.trans: The floorboards are old and sturdy.
We wiped the floor in the morning.

meanings.note: Elative of رقيق ('delicate, thin'); in exclamations after ما (ما أرق هاللحن! 'how gentle this melody is!') it stays invariable.

examples.trans: How gentle the sound of the piano is at night!

examples.text: هاد الورق أرق من ورق الدفتر.
examples.trans: This paper is thinner than notebook paper.

meanings.note: The color blue.

examples.trans: The color of my car is blue.

examples.text: السما اليوم لونها أزرق صافي وما في غيم.
examples.trans: The sky today is a clear blue and there are no clouds.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بزعج, بيزعج).

examples.trans: There is no way I would bother a guest with our problems!
Sorry if we disturbed you at night.

meanings.note: In everyday Amman speech, أزمة most often means heavy city traffic.

examples.trans: Downtown traffic at noon is slow.
We arrived ten minutes before the traffic jam.

meanings.note: Refers both to physical foundations and to the base of a recipe or argument.

examples.text: أساس الكيكة لازم يكون خفيف ومستوي منيح.
examples.trans: The base of the cake needs to be light and baked well.

examples.text: الثقة هي أساس كل شغلنا بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: Trust is the foundation of all our work in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسابيع.

examples.trans: Next week I have time off.
We stayed at the guesthouse all week.

meanings.note: Polite Jordanian title for any man ('sir / Mr') as well as 'teacher' or 'professor'.

examples.trans: Please have a seat, sir.
Good morning, gentlemen.

meanings.note: أستاذ (teacher) + ك (your).

examples.trans: Where is your teacher?

examples.text: اسأل أستاذك عن موعد تسليم البحث بكرا.
examples.trans: Ask your professor about the deadline for submitting the paper tomorrow.

meanings.note: Locative noun أسفل ('bottom/lower part'), forming a prepositional phrase.

examples.text: التوقيع موجود بأسفل الصفحة على اليمين.
examples.trans: The signature is at the bottom of the page on the right.

examples.text: نزلنا لأسفل الوادي عشان نشوف النبع.
examples.trans: We went down to the bottom of the valley to see the spring.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of سيئ ('bad').

examples.trans: The news is worse than we expected.
This is the worst time for rain.

meanings.note: The color black.

examples.trans: I wore a black shirt.

examples.text: اشتريت جاكيت أسود دافي عشان الشتا.
examples.trans: I bought a warm black jacket for the winter.

meanings.note: Form IV verb paired with على ('supervise / oversee a task').

examples.text: سلمى بتشرف عالمطبخ وهي قاعدة عالكرسي.
examples.trans: Salma supervises the kitchen while sitting in her chair.

examples.text: أبو طارق أشرف على تركيب الشيش الأخضر.
examples.trans: Abu Tariq oversaw the installation of the green shutters.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for seeing a group of people.

examples.trans: I will see you tomorrow at school.

examples.text: يلا مع السلامة، أشوفكم الأسبوع الجاي إن شاء الله.
examples.trans: Alright, goodbye—see you all next week, God willing.

meanings.note: Plural of شيء (šayʾ), meaning thing. Pronounced asyāʾ or ašyāʾ depending on the speaker.

examples.trans: There are many things we need to do.

examples.text: اشترينا أشياء بسيطة للبيت من السوق.
examples.trans: We bought a few simple things for the house from the market.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بأشر, بيأشر).

examples.trans: Salma motioned to me from the kitchen.
Rami is pointing to the two chairs.

أصبح.gloss: to wake in the morning; become

meanings.en: to wake in the morning; become
meanings.note: Used nightly in the warm Levantine farewell تصبحوا على خير ('may you wake in goodness' = good night).

examples.text: تصبحوا على خير يا جماعة، منشوفكم الصبح!
examples.trans: Good night, everyone—we'll see you in the morning!

examples.text: تصبح على خير يا عمي، ارتاح الليلة.
examples.trans: Good night, uncle, get some rest tonight.

meanings.note: Plural of صديق (ṣadīq). In Jordanian, صحاب (ṣḥāb) is more common.

examples.trans: These are childhood friends.

examples.text: صرنا أصدقاء مقربين من أول سنة بالجامعة.
examples.trans: We became close friends from our very first year at university.

meanings.note: Comparative/superlative elative of صغير ('small/young'); invariant in spoken comparative use.

examples.text: تحت الاسم كتبنا السطر التاني بحروف أصغر.
examples.trans: Underneath the name we painted the second line in smaller letters.

examples.text: المرتبان الأصغر مخصص لملح البحر الخشن.
examples.trans: The smaller jar is reserved for coarse sea salt.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صفرا, plural: صفر).

examples.trans: A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.
The yellow lemon cake is ready.

meanings.note: Arabic noun meaning 'origin', used in من أصل to express 'out of a total'.

examples.text: نجحت بتسع مواد من أصل عشرة هالفصل.
examples.trans: I passed nine courses out of a total of ten this semester.

examples.text: عيلتنا أصلها من السلط بس ساكنين بعمان.
examples.trans: Our family originally comes from Salt, though we live in Amman.

أصلا.gloss: anyway; in the first place; actually

meanings.en: anyway; in the first place; actually
meanings.note: Everyday conversational adverb meaning 'in the first place / anyway / to begin with'.

examples.trans: Does the attic even have a comfortable bed?
The wire needed adjusting anyway.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: أصلية, plural: أصليين).

examples.trans: The ceiling is solid oak wood.
All the old tilework is original.

meanings.note: Praises honest natural materials, authentic recipes, or trustworthy character.

examples.text: الخشب الأصيل بيعيش سنين طويلة لو اعتنينا فيه.
examples.trans: Honest solid wood lasts for decades when cared for.

examples.text: قائمة سلمى بسيطة وأصيلة من خيرات البلد.
examples.trans: Salma's menu is simple and authentic, made with local produce.

meanings.note: Form IV hollow verb (بضيف / ضفت). Used for adding an item to a box, list, or recipe.

examples.text: كل واحد بيضيف تذكار صغير للعلبة.
examples.trans: Everyone adds one small keepsake to the tin.
We added a little honey and orange zest.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of طويل ('tall, long').

examples.trans: You have grown taller than the piano!
The bridge route is two minutes longer.

meanings.note: Literally 'tastiest', the top Levantine Arabic compliment for food.

examples.text: هادي أطيب منسف أكلتها بحياتي، يسلمو إيديك!
examples.trans: This is the most delicious mansaf I've ever eaten in my life—bless your hands!

examples.text: قهوة الهيل الصبح أطيب إشي بالدنيا.
examples.trans: Cardamom coffee in the morning is the best thing in the world.

meanings.note: Form IV verb; in casual Jordanian speech often replaced by عاد, though نعيد is widely heard.

examples.text: إذا خربت الوصفة لازم نعيد الخبز من الأول.
examples.trans: If the recipe goes wrong we have to redo the baking from scratch.

examples.text: المعلم أعاد السؤال مرتين عشان الكل يفهم.
examples.trans: The teacher repeated the question twice so everyone would understand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعطي, بيعطي).

examples.trans: Did the shopkeeper give you a receipt?
Give me the breakfast bag, please.

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of غريب ('strange').

examples.trans: The story gets stranger every hour.
That is the strangest request I have heard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective; بالأغلب means 'mostly'.

examples.trans: Guests wake up early for the most part.
Most houses here are made of stone.

meanings.note: Feminine noun; the plural أغاني (aghaani) is the one you hear most.

examples.trans: This is an old song my grandmother loves.
We listen to songs in the car every morning.

meanings.note: Elative comparative/superlative of قديم (old); invariable across gender and number.

examples.text: هاي أقدم شجرة زيتون بالحارة كلها.
examples.trans: This is the oldest olive tree in the whole neighbourhood.

examples.text: الكتاب هادا أقدم من كل الكتب اللي عالرف.
examples.trans: This book is older than every other book on the shelf.

meanings.note: First person singular present tense of قرأ (qaraʾa).

examples.trans: I am reading a nice book.

examples.text: بحب أقرأ الجريدة الصبح مع فنجان قهوة.
examples.trans: I like to read the newspaper in the morning with a cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective; عالأقل means 'at least'.

examples.trans: At least the bread is ready in the oven.
We need less than ten minutes.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of أكثر ('more, most').

examples.trans: I liked working here much more.
Who knows the neighbourhood better than you?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باكل, بياكل).

examples.trans: The brothers are eating lemon cake in the courtyard.
We ate a hot breakfast in the morning.

meanings.note: Used to express certainty or agreement.

examples.trans: I will certainly come to the party.

examples.text: أكيد ما رح أنسى أجبلك الكتاب بكرة الصبح.
examples.trans: For sure I won't forget to bring you the book tomorrow morning.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of أكل (to eat), used as the everyday word for 'food'.

examples.text: الأكل اليوم ريحته واصلة لآخر الشارع.
examples.trans: The aroma of today's food reaches all the way down the street.

examples.text: لا تنسى تجيب أكل معك عالرحلة.
examples.trans: Don't forget to bring food with you on the trip.

meanings.note: In بحسب إلها ألف حساب ('counts a thousand accounts for her'), ألف intensifies caution: everyone thinks twice around her.

examples.trans: I thought about it a thousand times.
Thanks a thousand times.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلقي, بيلقي).

examples.trans: Let me take a look at the letter.
He took a quick look at the ledger.

meanings.note: Standard Jordanian way to answer or check a phone line.

examples.trans: Hello? Jasmine House, how may I help you?
Hello, can you hear me clearly?

meanings.note: With 1sg suffix أمي (ummi), affectionately means 'Mom' even when talking to a sibling ('our mom').

examples.text: أمي علمتني أعمل شوربة عدس بالليمون.
examples.trans: Mom taught me how to make lentil soup with lemon.

examples.text: كل جمعة بنزور بيت أمي بعمان.
examples.trans: Every Friday we visit my mom's house in Amman.

meanings.note: Relational adjective from أمام ('in front of'): الغرفة الأمامية / الباب الأمامي.

examples.text: علقنا اللوحة الجديدة جنب البوابة الأمامية.
examples.trans: We hung the new sign beside the front gate.
The front windows look straight out onto the lane.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Safety in the house is very important.
They arrived safely and securely.

meanings.note: Means something kept in trust for someone, and in Amman also names City Hall (أمانة عمان).

examples.trans: I have something entrusted for you from your grandfather.
We put the bag in the left-luggage closet.

meanings.note: Plural أوامر means 'orders / instructions' (أوزع أوامر 'hand out orders').

examples.text: الشيف سلمى جاهزة توزع أوامر عالفريق كله!
examples.trans: Chef Salma is ready to issue orders to the whole team!

examples.text: تحت أمرك يا معلم، الشيش صار جاهز للتركيب.
examples.trans: At your service, boss—the shutters are ready to mount.

meanings.note: Feminine singular agreement for the non-human plural أيدي, meaning 'trustworthy/safe'.

examples.text: لا تخاف، مفاتيح البيت بأيدي أمينة.
examples.trans: Don't worry, the house keys are in safe hands.

examples.text: أبو سامي زلمة أمين والكل بيثق فيه.
examples.trans: Abu Sami is an honest man and everyone trusts him.

meanings.note: First person singular pronoun.

examples.trans: I am from Jordan.

examples.text: أنا وإياك رح نخلص المشروع قبل يوم الخميس.
examples.trans: You and I will finish the project before Thursday.

meanings.note: Form IV verb meaning to complete a task cleanly or deliver on time.

examples.trans: We got all the orders done before sunset.

examples.text: بتنجزي الشغل أسرع لما تشتغلي بهدوء.
examples.trans: You finish the work faster when you work calmly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أنوف.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your nose now.
The air feels cold on my nose in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنقذ, بينقذ).

examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast!
You saved my whole trip.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization or confirmation in Jordanian conversation.

examples.text: أها! هلق فهمت ليش الباب ما كان يفتح.
examples.trans: Aha! Now I understand why the door would not open.

examples.text: أها، إنت اللي خبيت المفتاح تحت الصحن!
examples.trans: Aha, you are the one who hid the key under the plate!

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of هادي ('quiet, calm').

examples.trans: Jasmine House is the calmest place in Amman.
The street is much quieter at night.

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun meaning 'family/parents' or 'people of a place' (يا أهل شارع الياسمين 'friends/folks of Jasmine Street').

examples.trans: Welcome to the friends of Jasmine Street!
My family comes to visit me every Friday.

meanings.note: Warm greeting used alone (أهلا!), with فيك/فيكي ('welcome to you!'), or paired as أهلا وسهلا! ('you are most welcome!').

examples.trans: Hello, I am Tariq!
Welcome to Jasmine House!

meanings.note: Core Arabic welcome formula (literally 'you have come to family').

examples.text: أهلاً وسهلاً فيكم ببيتنا، نورتوا القعدة!
examples.trans: Welcome to our home—you've brightened the gathering!

examples.text: أهلاً يا خالتو، كيف صحتك اليوم؟
examples.trans: Hello auntie, how is your health today?

meanings.note: Elative form placed before a definite plural noun (أهم القيم 'the most important values').

examples.trans: This is the most important topic today.
Honesty is the most important thing.

meanings.note: Conjunction 'or' in statements and open questions.

examples.text: مكتوب عليها اسم أو رقم تليفون؟
examples.trans: Is there a name or phone number written on it?
We need two or three minutes.

meanings.note: Lighthearted exclamation after a small spill or slip.

examples.trans: Oops! A drop of juice landed on my tie!
Oops, I left the pen on the desk.

meanings.note: Feminine elative of وسط (middle), agreeing with نغمة for 'middle D'.

examples.text: الشرق الأوسط معروف بتاريخه العريق ومطبخه الغني.
examples.trans: The Middle East is known for its ancient history and rich cuisine.
The middle finger is the longest finger on the hand.

meanings.note: Elative comparative of واطي ('low'). Invariable for gender and number before or after nouns.

examples.trans: Put the chair on the lowest step.
This shelf is lower than the window.

meanings.note: Strong spoken Levantine warning word meaning 'mind you don't / never!'.

examples.text: أوعى تنسى تطفي الغاز قبل ما تطلع!
examples.trans: Don't you dare forget to turn off the stove before you leave!

examples.text: أوعك تحكي لحد عن المفاجأة لسه.
examples.trans: Mind you don't tell anyone about the surprise yet.

meanings.note: A sigh of dismay or tiredness, a little like English 'oof' or 'ugh'.

examples.trans: Oof, I forgot the key at home!
Ugh, it's hot today.

meanings.note: Musical interval of eight scale steps.

examples.text: مدام سعاد عزفت نفس اللحن أوكتاف أعلى.
examples.trans: Madam Suad played the same melody one octave higher.

examples.text: الأوكتاف الوسطاني بالبيانو بده دوزان بسيط.
examples.trans: The middle octave on the piano needs a light tuning.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Feminine of أول (awwal).

examples.text: هاي المرة الأولى اللي بزور فيها البتراء.
examples.trans: This is the first time I visit Petra.

examples.text: العيلة دايماً إلها الأولوية الأولى بحياتنا.
examples.trans: Family always has the first priority in our lives.

meanings.note: Exclamation of mild surprise or realization ('oh!').

examples.trans: Oh! My glasses are on my head!
Oh, look at the beauty of this ceiling!

meanings.note: Used as a question word or indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: Which car do you prefer?

examples.text: بأي ساعة رح يبلش الاجتماع اليوم؟
examples.trans: At what hour is the meeting going to start today?

meanings.note: Name of the month of May in the Levantine calendar.

examples.trans: My birthday is in the month of May.

examples.text: الطقس بشهر أيار بكون دافي ومناسب للرحلات.
examples.trans: The weather in May is warm and ideal for trips.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'when?'.

examples.trans: When does the hardware shop open?
When did the bus arrive at the station?

meanings.note: Warm spoken Levantine affirmation ('yes! / exactly!').

examples.text: أيوا، هاد هو اللحن اللي كنت أدور عليه!
examples.trans: Yes, that's the exact melody I was looking for!

examples.text: أيوا بالزبط، حط الكراسي جنب القوس.
examples.trans: Yes, right there—put the chairs beside the arch.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أباريق.

examples.trans: The teapot is hot on the table.
Pour the hot water into the teapot.

meanings.note: Used in تحت إبطي ('tucked under my arm') when carrying books or newspapers.

examples.text: مازن كان حامل الدفتر الأخضر تحت إبطه.
examples.trans: Mazen was carrying the green ledger under his arm.

examples.text: حط الجريدة تحت إبطه ومشي عالسوق.
examples.trans: He tucked the newspaper under his arm and walked to the market.

meanings.note: Core Jordanian everyday verb for 'to come' (إجا / بيجي).

examples.trans: You came ten minutes early.
I will come on Friday at noon.

meanings.note: Colloquial Jordanian pronunciation of أحد عشر; precedes singular nouns as إحدعشر in construct.

examples.trans: We arrived at the market at eleven in the morning.

examples.text: عدينا إحدعش خطوة من البوابة للدرج.
examples.trans: We counted eleven steps from the gate to the stairs.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun for 'we' (equivalent to formal نحن).

examples.trans: We respect all our guests.
We are ready for breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: Used constantly in the polite phrase عن إذنك ('excuse me / with your permission').

examples.trans: Excuse me, may I pass?
He asked permission before heading out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: I am very sorry for the disturbance.
There is no bother at all.

meanings.note: Soft cleaning sponge for washing windows or dishes.

examples.text: اعصري الإسفنجة منيح قبل ما تمسحي القزاز.
examples.trans: Wring the sponge out well before wiping the glass.
We bought two new sponges for the café kitchen.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from إسفنج (sponge); commonly describes light cakes.

examples.text: عملت سلمى كيكة إسفنجية خفيفة مع التوت.
examples.trans: Salma made a light sponge cake with berries.
Fresh bread has a soft and spongy texture.

meanings.note: Feminine noun used for traffic lights, hand gestures, and railway or stage signals.

examples.text: وقفنا عند أول إشارة بعد المحطة.
examples.trans: We stopped at the first traffic light after the station.

examples.text: اعطيني إشارة بإيدك بس يبدأ العزف.
examples.trans: Give me a hand signal as soon as the playing starts.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: إشعارات.

examples.trans: An official notice arrived in the mail.
I read the notice twice.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for a finger or toe; dual إصبعين ('two fingers'), broken plural أصابع.

examples.trans: Pull the paper out gently with two fingers.

examples.text: خلي أصابعك بعيدة عن الفرن السخن.
examples.trans: Keep your fingers away from the hot oven.

meanings.note: Standard and Jordanian noun for a picture frame (إطار الجوز 'walnut frame') or tyre. Plural: إطارات.

examples.text: حطينا الخريطة جوا إطار جوز حلو.
examples.trans: We placed the map inside a lovely walnut frame.
This wooden frame protects the drawing.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: إطلالات.

examples.trans: The room has a lovely view onto the courtyard.
This is the prettiest view in the house.

meanings.note: Form IV verbal noun from عاد, used for rehearsals, replays, and another try.

examples.text: هاي آخر إعادة للمشهد قبل العرض.
examples.trans: This is the last run-through of the scene before the show.

examples.text: بعد إعادة سريعة صارت الجملة واضحة.
examples.trans: After one quick repeat, the line became clear.

meanings.note: Verbal noun (masdar) of Form IV أعار; used in library phrases like رف الإعارة.

examples.text: هادا الكتاب موجود على رف الإعارة بالمكتبة.
examples.trans: This book is on the lending shelf in the library.
The loan period for the novel is only two weeks.

meanings.note: Feminine Arabic noun إقامة meaning 'stay/residence' with Suad's ending.

examples.text: إن شاء الله تكون إقامتك بعمان مريحة وحلوة.
examples.trans: Hopefully your stay in Amman is comfortable and pleasant.

examples.text: جدّدت تصريح الإقامة في دائرة الأحوال مبارح.
examples.trans: I renewed my residency permit at the civil affairs office yesterday.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine dative base taking pronoun endings: إلي (to me), إلك (to you), إلها (to her), إلنا (for us), إلهم (to them).

examples.trans: This book is for you.
Tell me the truth.

meanings.note: Means 'except / unless' (إلا إذا 'unless') and 'minutes to the hour' (اطنعش إلا خمسة 'five to twelve').

examples.trans: It is five minutes to twelve!

examples.text: ما حدا بيقيس الساحة إلا مهندس!
examples.trans: Nobody measures a courtyard except an engineer!

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian/Levantine form of أم ('mother'); إمي means 'my mother'.

examples.text: إمي بتعمل أطيب مربى مشمش بالصيف.
examples.trans: My mother makes the best apricot jam in summer.

examples.text: سلم على إمك لما ترجع عالبيت.
examples.trans: Say hello to your mother when you get home.

meanings.note: Introduces 'that'-clauses with pronoun suffixes (إنه 'that', إني 'that I', إنك 'that you', إنها 'that she/it') and appears in إن شاء الله ('if God wills').

examples.trans: Thank you for coming today.
Do you think that I am a hotel inspector?

meanings.note: Second person masculine singular pronoun.

examples.trans: Where do you live?

examples.text: إنت اللي رسمت الخريطة هاي بإيدك؟
examples.trans: Are you the one who drew this map by hand?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing two or more people.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
Hold the torch, both of you.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing one woman.

examples.trans: You must be Nour!
You are today's heroine, Nour.

meanings.note: Measurement unit.

examples.trans: The screen size is fifty inches.

examples.text: طول اللوح الخشبي أربعين إنش بالزبط.
examples.trans: The length of the wooden board is forty inches exactly.

meanings.note: إن (that) + ك (you).

examples.trans: I know that you are busy.

examples.text: فرحت كتير لما عرفت إنك نجحت بالامتحان.
examples.trans: I was so happy when I found out that you passed the exam.

meanings.note: إن (that) + كم (you plural).

examples.trans: I heard that you (all) are traveling.

examples.text: مبسوط إنكم جيتوا تزورونا بعطلة نهاية الأسبوع.
examples.trans: I'm glad that you all came to visit us over the weekend.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine conjunction introducing reported thoughts or clauses (MSA أن).

examples.text: حسّيت إنو الجو بلّش يبرد بالليل.
examples.trans: I felt that the weather started getting cold at night.

examples.text: المشكلة إنو المحل بسكر بكير يوم الجمعة.
examples.trans: The problem is that the shop closes early on Friday.

meanings.note: Warm spoken Levantine affirmative particle alongside آه and نعم.

examples.trans: He nodded his head yes.
Yes indeed, you are right.

meanings.note: Detached object carrier إيا- used when a verb already has a bound indirect object pronoun (-ك).

examples.text: الكتاب هاد كتير مفيد، رح أعطيك إياه بكرة.
examples.trans: This book is very useful; I'll give it to you tomorrow.

examples.text: الهدية جاهزة وبدي أبعتلك إياها مع أختي.
examples.trans: The gift is ready and I want to send it to you with my sister.

meanings.note: Independent object pronoun for the first person plural. Rare in spoken, mostly formal or specific expressions.

examples.trans: May God protect us and you.

examples.text: ربنا يحفظ إيانا وإياكم من كل سوء.
examples.trans: May God protect both us and you from every harm.

meanings.note: Carries the direct object pronoun after بدي ('want'): هاد اللي بدي إياه ('that is what I want').

examples.trans: That is exactly what I want.
I gave it to you this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: إيجارات.

examples.trans: The shop rent is paid until summer.
We signed the lease today.

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: Musical rhythm or tempo pattern.

examples.text: إيقاع الفالس خفيف وبيرقص متل الموج.
examples.trans: A waltz rhythm is light and swaying like waves.

examples.text: دقت سعاد الإيقاع بأصابعها على طرف الطاولة.
examples.trans: Suad tapped the rhythm with her fingers on the edge of the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine question word for 'when?' (alongside متى).

examples.text: إيمتى رح نعلق الشيش الأخضر عالشبابيك؟
examples.trans: When are we going to hang the green shutters on the windows?

examples.text: إيمتى بيجهز أول فوج خبز الصبح؟
examples.trans: When does the first batch of bread come out in the morning?

meanings.note: From ابتسم (to smile); everyday noun for a warm smile.

examples.text: استقبلتنا بابتسامة دافية أول ما فتحنا الباب.
examples.trans: She welcomed us with a warm smile as soon as we opened the door.

examples.text: ابتسامة صغيرة بتغيّر مزاج الواحد كل اليوم.
examples.trans: A small smile can change someone's mood for the whole day.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببتسم, بيبتسم).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
He smiled when he saw his brother.

meanings.note: Combines with عم ('paternal uncle') as ابن عمي ('my cousin').

examples.text: ابن عمي ساكن قريب من هون.
examples.trans: My cousin lives near here.
The boys are playing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Form VIII verb; frequently used in imperatives for following directions or clues.

examples.text: اتبعوا الخريطة خطوة بخطوة عشان ما تضيعوا.
examples.trans: Follow the map step by step so you do not get lost.

examples.text: دايما بنتبع البوصلة لما نمشي بالزقاق.
examples.trans: We always follow the compass when we walk through the alley.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of اتجه. With بـ, باتجاه means 'toward' (باتجاه الشباك 'toward the window').

examples.trans: He raised his cup toward the room's window.
He pointed us in the direction of the bus station.

اتسكّر.gloss: to close; shut; get locked up

meanings.en: to close; shut; get locked up
meanings.note: Form V passive/reflexive of سكّر in spoken Jordanian Arabic: to close up on its own or be closed for the day.

examples.trans: The door shut from the strong wind.
The bakery closes at ten at night.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتصل, بيتصل).

examples.trans: Call the lost-and-found office right away.
You called us on Tuesday.

meanings.note: Classic Levantine verb اتطلّع ('to look / gaze at'), slightly more attentive than شوف.

examples.text: اتطلّع من الشباك، المنظر عالجبل بياخد العقل!
examples.trans: Look out the window—the view over the hill is breathtaking!
She was looking at the old photos and laughing.

meanings.note: Used when reminding friends of what they agreed on (مش هيك الاتفاق 'that wasn't the deal').

examples.trans: That was our deal from the start.
We reached a clear agreement.

meanings.note: Said on its own, اتفقنا ('we agreed') is the everyday way to close a deal: 'deal!'.

examples.text: اتفقنا، بنلتقي الساعة تسعة عند الباب.
examples.trans: Agreed, we meet at nine at the door.

examples.text: اتفقت مع سلمى على كيكة الجمعة.
examples.trans: I agreed with Salma about the Friday cake.

meanings.note: Past tense Levantine passive verb meaning 'to be cancelled'.

examples.text: الحفل اتلغى بسبب المطر القوي مبارح.
examples.trans: The concert was cancelled because of the heavy rain yesterday.

examples.text: الموعد اتلغى ولسه ما حددوا يوم جديد.
examples.trans: The appointment got cancelled and they haven't set a new day yet.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian for 12. From eleven up, the counted noun stays singular: اتنعش فنجان 'twelve cups'.

examples.trans: We have twelve guests tonight.
It's twelve noon.

meanings.note: The number two. Often pronounced 'tnēn' in Jordanian.

examples.trans: I have two children.

examples.text: طلبنا فنجانين قهوة وكاستين شاي للاثنين.
examples.trans: We ordered two cups of coffee and two glasses of tea for the two of us.

meanings.note: Feminine verb form meaning 'to gather' or 'come together'.

examples.text: العيلة كلها اجتمعت عالغدا يوم الجمعة.
examples.trans: The whole family gathered for lunch on Friday.

examples.text: بكرا رح نجتمع بالمكتب عشان نرتب الخطة.
examples.trans: Tomorrow we'll meet at the office to organize the plan.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحتاج, بيحتاج).

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.
An old house needs steady care.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحترم, بيحترم).

examples.trans: We respect the Amman tourist guide!
Everyone respects Madam Suad.

meanings.note: Form VIII verb taking بـ for what is celebrated.

examples.text: رح نحتفل بافتتاح الكافيه مع كل الجيران.
examples.trans: We're going to celebrate the café opening with all the neighbours.

examples.text: احتفلنا لما خلص دهان الشيش قبل المغرب.
examples.trans: We celebrated when the shutter painting finished before dusk.

meanings.note: Often placed directly after a noun in Jordanian to mean 'spare' (مفتاح احتياط a spare key).

examples.trans: I have a spare key in the drawer.
We bought a spare valve for winter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بختار, بيختار).

examples.trans: I chose this quarter for a family reason.
They chose a table under the tree.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of Form VIII اختبر; covers taste tests, school exams, and trials.

examples.text: عملنا اختبار للكيكات قبل ما نقدمهم للضيوف.
examples.trans: We ran a test on the cakes before serving them to guests.

examples.text: عندهم اختبار عربي بكرة الصبح بالمدرسة.
examples.trans: They have an Arabic exam tomorrow morning at school.

meanings.note: Form VIII verb taking a direct object.

examples.text: لازم نختبر حرارة الفرن قبل ما ندخل الصينية.
examples.trans: We need to test the oven temperature before putting the tin in.

examples.text: مازن بختبر كل وصفة بدقة كبيرة.
examples.trans: Mazen tests every recipe with great precision.

meanings.note: Used in everyday speech for a shorter route as well as a shortened word.

examples.text: رامي دايما بلاقي اختصار سريع من ورا الساحة.
examples.trans: Rami always finds a quick shortcut behind the courtyard.

examples.text: بلاش نجرب أي اختصار واحنا مستعجلين.
examples.trans: Let us not try any shortcut while we are in a hurry.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: اختيارات.

examples.trans: A wonderful choice for breakfast!
That was our choice from the start.

meanings.note: Command to enter. In Jordanian, فوت (fūt) is more common.

examples.trans: Enter inside the house.

examples.text: تفضل ادخل عالصالون، الجو برا برد.
examples.trans: Please come into the living room; it's cold outside.

meanings.note: Conditional conjunction. Pronounced 'iza' in some dialects.

examples.trans: If you want, we can go together.

examples.text: اذا خلصت شغلك بكير، مرّ علينا نشرب شاي.
examples.trans: If you finish your work early, stop by our place for tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برتاح, بيرتاح).

examples.trans: Rest up after your journey, ma'am.
We rested in the courtyard with a glass of tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برتبك, بيرتبك).

examples.trans: I got flustered and rang the doorbell.
Do not get flustered; take your time speaking.

meanings.note: Form VIII verb meaning 'get a fright / panic'.

examples.text: لا ترتعبوا، هي بس لوية خفيفة مش كسر.
examples.trans: Don't panic—it's just a mild twist, not a break.

examples.text: ارتعبت لما سمعت صوت الصحن بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: I panicked when I heard the sound of the plate in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Form VIII verb used for rising motion, music, or levels.

examples.text: بترتفع المطرقة بهدوء لما تكبس المفتاح.
examples.trans: The hammer rises smoothly when you press the key.
The sound of laughter rose in the courtyard in the evening.

meanings.note: Command to go back.

examples.trans: Go back to your work.

examples.text: ارجع بكير عالبيت قبل ما تظلّم الدنيا.
examples.trans: Come back home early before it gets dark.

meanings.note: Command to a group to go back.

examples.trans: Return to your places.

examples.text: ارجعوا اقعدوا بأماكنكم عشان نبلش العرض.
examples.trans: Go back and sit in your seats so we can start the show.

meanings.note: Command to a female to lift something.

examples.trans: Raise your voice a little bit.

examples.text: ارفعي الستارة شوي عشان يفوت ضو الشمس.
examples.trans: Lift the curtain a little so the sunlight comes in.

meanings.note: Takes a direct object suffix (أستأذنك) or من (بتستأذني مني) for asking someone's permission.

examples.trans: I have to ask the teacher's permission.
I asked permission before leaving.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستاهل, بيستاهل).

examples.trans: Your welcome deserves ten out of ten!
The house is worth all this effort.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian Form X verb (بيستاهل / بتستاهل) meaning 'to deserve, be worth it'.

examples.trans: The ovens deserve a break after baking!

examples.text: انتي بتستاهلي كل خير يا سلمى.
examples.trans: You deserve every good thing, Salma.

meanings.note: Both a quiet personal breather (تاخدي استراحة) and school recess.

examples.trans: We have recess in the courtyard now.
Take a five-minute break.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستعجل, بيستعجل).

examples.trans: Hurry, the guests are coming down the stairs!
Do not rush to go upstairs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستعمل, بيستعمل).

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
I used the last valve in winter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The reception desk is beside the door.
Thank you for the warm welcome.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستقبل, بيستقبل).

examples.trans: Let us go down to welcome the new guest.
They welcomed us with a smile and hot tea.

meanings.note: Form VIII verb meaning both 'receive a delivery' and 'take over a station/duty'.

examples.text: زياد بيستلم قسم الشوربة وتقشير الخضار.
examples.trans: Ziad takes charge of the soup and vegetable-peeling station.

examples.text: استلمنا الطحين الطازة من الفرن الصبح.
examples.trans: We received the fresh flour from the bakery in the morning.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of Form X استنتج; denotes reasoning from clues.

examples.text: هاد استنتاج ذكي كتير من الأدلة الموجودة.
examples.trans: That is a very clever deduction from the available clues.

examples.text: وصلنا لاستنتاج واضح بعد ما قرأنا الكرت.
examples.trans: We reached a clear conclusion after reading the card.

meanings.note: A combination of استنوا (wait plural) and لسه (not yet / still).

examples.trans: Wait, we haven't finished yet.

examples.text: استنوالسه ما جهزنا الطاولات والكراسي بالصالة.
examples.trans: Wait, we still haven't set up the tables and chairs in the hall yet.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait just a minute.

examples.text: استنى شوي، أنا نازل معك هسه!
examples.trans: Wait a second—I'm coming down with you right now!

meanings.note: Command to a female to wait.

examples.trans: Wait here until I return.

examples.text: استني عند البوابة لبين ما أجيب المفتاح.
examples.trans: Wait by the gate until I bring the key.

meanings.note: Masculine singular loanword used in Arabic for a design or art studio.

examples.text: أخوي فتح استوديو تصوير صغير بجبل اللويبدة.
examples.trans: My brother opened a small photography studio in Jabal Al-Weibdeh.

examples.text: الشقة عبارة عن استوديو مريح وقريب عالجامعة.
examples.trans: The apartment is a cozy studio close to the university.

meanings.note: Often paired with مش قادرة ('I can't wrap my head around what happened').

examples.trans: I can't process the news.
Did you grasp the whole lesson?

meanings.note: Key Jordanian kitchen verb استوى meaning 'to become cooked/done' (for food) or 'ripe' (for fruit).

examples.text: خلي الرز عالنار الهادية لحد ما يستوي تمام.
examples.trans: Leave the rice on low heat until it cooks all the way through.

examples.text: التين استوى عالشجرة وصار حلو كتير.
examples.trans: The figs ripened on the tree and became super sweet.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for a person's or place's name; takes possessive endings directly (اسمي my name, اسمك your name).

examples.trans: What is your kind name?
My name is written here in the notebook.

meanings.note: Command to a group to listen.

examples.trans: Listen to what I want to say.

examples.text: اسمعوا يا جماعة، عندي خبر كتير حلو إلكم!
examples.trans: Listen everyone, I have some really great news for you!

meanings.note: Command to prop up or lean something.

examples.trans: Lean the ladder against the wall.

examples.text: اسند الباب بحجر عشان الهوا ما يسكره.
examples.trans: Prop the door open with a stone so the wind doesn't shut it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشتاق, بيشتاق).

examples.trans: I missed you so much over these three years.
We missed our Friday gatherings.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشتري, بيشتري).

examples.trans: Tell me exactly what to buy.
Buy both brass valves together.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشتغل, بيشتغل).

examples.trans: Look, the flame came on blue!
He works on heritage buildings in Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'thing' (شيء).

examples.trans: I want to buy something tasty.

examples.text: في اشي مهم لازم أحكيلك إياه اليوم.
examples.trans: There's something important I need to tell you today.

meanings.note: The color yellow.

examples.trans: The color of the flower is yellow.

examples.text: اشتريت دفتر اصفر عشان أكتب فيه الملاحظات.
examples.trans: I bought a yellow notebook to write notes in.

اضطر.gloss: to have to; be forced to

meanings.en: to have to; be forced to
meanings.note: Followed directly by a subjunctive verb ('have to do something').

examples.text: ما رح يضطر حدا يضيق عيونه عشان يقرأ اللوحة.
examples.trans: Nobody will have to squint to read the sign.

examples.text: اضطرينا ندهن الشيش جوا الممر بسبب المطر.
examples.trans: We had to paint the shutters inside the hallway because of the rain.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian verb taking على ('check on someone/something') or عن ('feel reassured').

examples.text: خليني أطلع عالدرج وأطمن عالشباك العلوي.
examples.trans: Let me step up the ladder and check on the upper transom.

examples.text: اطمنا لما شفنا سلمى بتحرك أصابع رجلها.
examples.trans: We felt relieved when we saw Salma wiggle her toes.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'twelve'; before a singular counted noun it takes -r: اطنعشر دقة ('twelve chimes').

examples.trans: The clock tower chimed twelve!
Here is twelve dinars change.

meanings.note: Construct form of اطنعش used directly before a singular noun.

examples.text: دقت الساعة اطنعشر دقة وقت الضهر.
examples.trans: The clock struck twelve chimes at noon.

examples.text: في اطنعشر كرسي حوالين طاولة الساحة.
examples.trans: There are twelve chairs around the courtyard table.

meanings.note: Command to fold clothes or paper.

examples.trans: Fold the paper in half.
Fold the clean laundry and put it in the closet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعتذر, بيعتذر).

examples.trans: I must apologize to you frankly.
He apologized for the mistake on the phone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعتمد, بيعتمد).

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading right out!
We rely on Nour at reception.

meanings.note: Official opening day or evening of a café, exhibition, or hall.

examples.text: افتتاح الكافيه رح يكون بآخر الأسبوع.
examples.trans: The café opening will take place at the end of the week.

examples.text: عزمنا كل الجيران على ليلة الافتتاح.
examples.trans: We invited all the neighbours to opening night.

meanings.note: Command to open.

examples.trans: Open the door quickly.

examples.text: افتح الشباك شوي عشان يتهوّى المكتب.
examples.trans: Open the window a little so the office airs out.

meanings.note: Used in conversational questions like تفتكري سمعت كل إشي؟ ('do you think she heard everything?').

examples.trans: Do you think she'll come today?
I thought you were in class.

meanings.note: Command to a female to read.

examples.trans: Read the lesson out loud.

examples.text: اقرأي البطاقة بصوت عالي عشان كلنا نسمع.
examples.trans: Read the card out loud so all of us can hear.

meanings.note: Same as اقرأي, orthographic variation.

examples.trans: Read the story to your brother.

examples.text: اقرئي الملاحظات اللي كتبتها على الورقة قبل الامتحان.
examples.trans: Read the notes I wrote on the paper before the exam.

اقرئيها.gloss: read it (feminine imperative, referring to feminine object)

meanings.en: read it (feminine imperative, referring to feminine object)
meanings.note: Command to a female to read a feminine object (like a story or paper).

examples.trans: Take the letter and read it.

examples.text: الجريدة وصلت الصبح، اقرئيها وأنتِ بتشربي القهوة.
examples.trans: The newspaper arrived this morning—read it while you drink your coffee.

meanings.note: Command to a female to flip something.

examples.trans: Turn the page so I can see.

examples.text: اقلبي الرغيف عالجهة التانية عشان يتحمّر منيح.
examples.trans: Flip the loaf to the other side so it browns nicely.

meanings.note: The color white with the definite article.

examples.trans: The white house is big.

examples.text: القميص الأبيض طلع مرتب كتير مع البدلة.
examples.trans: The white shirt looked very sharp with the suit.

meanings.note: First working day of the Jordanian week (pronounced il-ahad).

examples.text: يوم الأحد الصبح بنرتب جدول الأسبوع كله.
examples.trans: On Sunday morning we plan the schedule for the whole week.

examples.text: المدارس والمكاتب بعمان بتفتح يوم الأحد.
examples.trans: Schools and offices in Amman open on Sunday.

meanings.note: The color red with the definite article.

examples.trans: I like the red shirt.

examples.text: القلم الأحمر ضايع ومو لاقيه بالمكتب.
examples.trans: The red pen is missing and I can't find it in the office.

meanings.note: The color green with the definite article.

examples.trans: The green line means go.

examples.text: الشاي الأخضر مع النعنع خفيف ومنعش بعد الغدا.
examples.trans: Green tea with mint is light and refreshing after lunch.

meanings.note: Definite plural for proof/evidence.

examples.trans: The evidence is not enough for the court.

examples.text: فحصنا الأدلة الموجودة بالملف وحدة وحدة.
examples.trans: We examined the evidence in the file one by one.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The guest arrived Wednesday night.
We meet on Wednesday morning.

meanings.note: The number four with the definite article.

examples.trans: The four boys went to school.

examples.text: الأصدقاء الأربعة اتفقوا يلتقوا بالمقهى يوم السبت.
examples.trans: The four friends agreed to meet at the café on Saturday.

meanings.note: Refers to a way of doing things or way of speaking.

examples.trans: I don't like this style of speaking.

examples.text: الأسلوب اللطيف بالحوار بحل أكبر المشاكل.
examples.trans: A gentle manner in conversation solves the biggest problems.

meanings.note: Feminine definite form of original, used for things that are authentic.

examples.text: هاي هي القطعة الأصلية مش تقليد.
examples.trans: This is the original piece, not a fake.

examples.text: النسخة الأصلية من العقد محفوظة بالملف الأزرق.
examples.trans: The original copy of the contract is kept in the blue folder.

meanings.note: Feminine definite form of first, commonly used to describe the first instance of a feminine noun.

examples.text: هي المرة الأولى اللي بزور فيها البتراء.
examples.trans: This is the first time I visit Petra.

examples.text: المرة الأولى اللي بعزف فيها قدام جمهور كانت بتخوّف.
examples.trans: The first time I played in front of an audience was scary.

meanings.note: Can refer to a sewing needle or a medical syringe in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: The doctor gave him the injection so he would rest.

examples.text: لضمت الخيط بالإبرة عشان ترقّع المفرش المشقوق.
examples.trans: She threaded the needle to mend the torn tablecloth.

meanings.note: Refers to the day of the week (Monday) or the number two.

examples.trans: I will see you next Monday.

examples.text: اجتماعنا الجاي رح يكون يوم الاثنين الصبح.
examples.trans: Our next meeting will be on Monday morning.

meanings.note: Used for the planet Earth, a piece of land, or the floor of a room.

examples.text: لا تقعد على الارض لأنها باردة.
examples.trans: Don't sit on the floor because it's cold.

examples.text: مسحنا بلاط الارض كله قبل ما نفرش السجاد.
examples.trans: We mopped the entire floor before laying out the carpets.

meanings.note: Refers to a reception area in a hotel or hospital, or the act of welcoming.

examples.trans: Let's wait in the reception hall.

examples.text: سألت موظف الاستقبال عن رقم الغرفة والمفتاح.
examples.trans: I asked the reception clerk for the room number and the key.

meanings.note: Collective noun for biscuits or cookies.

examples.trans: The kids ate all the biscuits.

examples.text: حطّيت صحن البسكوت والشاي عالطاولة للضيوف.
examples.trans: I put the plate of biscuits and tea on the table for the guests.

meanings.note: Plural of card, used for ID cards, bank cards, or tickets.

examples.trans: I forgot the cards at home.

examples.text: رتّبنا البطاقات البريدية كلها جوا الصندوق الخشبي.
examples.trans: We organized all the postcards inside the wooden box.

meanings.note: Singular of cards, refers to any physical card or ticket.

examples.trans: Give me your ID card, please.

examples.text: لا تنسى تاخد البطاقة البنكية معك قبل ما تطلع.
examples.trans: Don't forget to take your bank card with you before leaving.

meanings.note: Refers to a large gate or portal, physical or digital.

examples.trans: Wait for me at the main gate.

examples.text: تلاقينا قدام البوابة الغربية للجامعة الساعة عشرة.
examples.trans: We met in front of the university's west gate at ten o'clock.

meanings.note: Navigation tool, sometimes used metaphorically for guidance.

examples.trans: They got lost in the desert because they forgot the compass.

examples.text: البوصلة القديمة بتشير دايماً لجهة الشمال.
examples.trans: The old compass always points toward the north.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian pronunciation of the ordinal number third.

examples.trans: He lives on the third floor.

examples.text: مكتب المحامي موجود بالطابق التالت عاليمين.
examples.trans: The lawyer's office is on the third floor on the right.

meanings.note: Commonly means a comment on social media or sports commentary.

examples.text: قرأت التعليق اللي كتبته على الفيسبوك.
examples.trans: I read the comment you wrote on Facebook.

examples.text: شكراً على التعليق اللطيف اللي كتبته تحت الصورة.
examples.trans: Thanks for the kind comment you wrote under the photo.

meanings.note: Guidelines or rules to be followed.

examples.trans: You must follow the written instructions.

examples.text: اقرا التعليمات اللي عالعلبة قبل ما تفتح الجهاز.
examples.trans: Read the instructions on the box before opening the device.

meanings.note: Form VIII defective verb; used both for people meeting and lines/corners meeting.

examples.text: الزوايا الأربعة بتلتقي بنقطة واحدة بالنص.
examples.trans: The four corners meet at a single point in the middle.

examples.text: التقينا عند برج الساعة قبل الغروب.
examples.trans: We met by the clock tower before sunset.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: He called us on Tuesday.
The corner shop is open every Tuesday.

meanings.note: Peeking or spying on others in a sneaky way.

examples.trans: Stop snooping on the neighbors.

examples.text: التلصص على خصوصيات الناس عادة سيئة كتير.
examples.trans: Snooping into people's private affairs is a very bad habit.

meanings.note: A concatenated transcription error from a corpus, merging 'the two' and 'tell us'.

examples.text: الساعة التنتين احكيلنا شو صار معك.
examples.trans: At two o'clock, tell us what happened with you.

examples.text: الساعة التنتين احكيلنا شو طلع معك بالاجتماع.
examples.trans: At two o'clock, tell us what came out of the meeting.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of الاثنين ('Monday', and with ال also 'both / the two').

examples.trans: I started work on Monday morning.
Monday's bus arrived at seven.

meanings.note: Another concatenated corpus error, combining 'Monday/two' and 'o'clock/hour'.

examples.trans: On Monday at five o'clock we will meet.

examples.text: موعدنا يوم التنين الساعة تلاتة بعد الضهر.
examples.trans: Our appointment is on Monday at three in the afternoon.

meanings.note: Commonly refers to mulberries, which are popular in Jordan, or any berry.

examples.trans: Mulberry juice is very delicious in the summer.

examples.text: شجرة التوت بالحديقة صارت مليانة حبات سودة حلوة.
examples.trans: The mulberry tree in the garden is full of sweet dark berries now.

meanings.note: Formal or semi-formal pronunciation of 'third' with the 'th' sound.

examples.text: هذا هو الفوز الثالث على التوالي.
examples.trans: This is the third win in a row.

examples.text: الفصل الثالث من الكتاب بحكي عن تاريخ المدينة.
examples.trans: The third chapter of the book talks about the city's history.

الثانية.gloss: the second (unit of time) / the second (f)

meanings.en: the second (unit of time) / the second (f)
meanings.note: Can mean the feminine ordinal 'second' or the time unit 'second'.

examples.trans: Wait for me a minute, or not even a second.

examples.text: استنى ثانية وحدة بس، جاي علطول!
examples.trans: Wait just one second, I'm coming right now!

meanings.note: Plural referring to other people or items in a group.

examples.trans: Where are the other guys?

examples.text: أصحابي الثانيين وصلوا القهوة قبلنا بنص ساعة.
examples.trans: My other friends got to the cafe half an hour before us.

meanings.note: Heavy in weight, or sometimes heavy-blooded (annoying/dull person).

examples.text: هذا الصندوق الثقيل ما بقدر أرفعه.
examples.trans: I cannot lift this heavy box.

examples.text: هالكرسي الحديد الثقيل بده اتنين يحملوه.
examples.trans: This heavy iron chair takes two people to carry it.

meanings.note: The number eight.

examples.trans: At eight o'clock at night we will have dinner.

examples.text: الباص بطلع على المفرق الساعة الثمانية تماماً.
examples.trans: The bus leaves for Mafraq at eight o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: The holy day in Islam and the weekend in Jordan.

examples.trans: On Friday, the whole family gathers.

examples.text: بنزور ستي كل يوم الجمعة بعد صلاة الظهر.
examples.trans: We visit my grandmother every Friday after the noon prayer.

meanings.note: Plural of 'jaanib', referring to physical sides or metaphorical aspects.

examples.text: لازم ندرس الموضوع من كل الجوانب.
examples.trans: We must study the issue from all aspects.

examples.text: فحصنا الخطة من جميع الجوانب قبل ما نوقع العقد.
examples.trans: We examined the plan from every angle before signing the contract.

الجوز.gloss: the walnuts / the husband / the pair

meanings.en: the walnuts / the husband / the pair
meanings.note: Depending on context, it means walnuts, a husband (from zoj), or a pair.

examples.trans: I put some walnuts on the cake.

examples.text: أمي بتحشي المعمول بالتمر أو الجوز في العيد.
examples.trans: My mom stuffs the maamoul pastries with dates or walnuts for Eid.

meanings.note: Plural for neighbors. Highly important in Jordanian culture.

examples.trans: The neighbors invited us for lunch.

examples.text: سلمت على الجيران الجداد اللي سكنوا بالطابق التالت.
examples.trans: I greeted the new neighbors who moved into the third floor.

meanings.note: Colloquial plural form of 'stone' (hajar).

examples.trans: The kids were throwing stones in the street.

examples.text: العمال صفوا الحجار البيضا عشان يبنوا السور.
examples.trans: The workers stacked the white stones to build the wall.

meanings.note: Another plural form for stone, slightly more formal than 'hjaar'.

examples.trans: The house is built from old stones.

examples.text: البيوت في وسط البلد مبنية من الحجارة الصفرا.
examples.trans: The houses in downtown are built out of yellow limestone.

meanings.note: Means stone, but recently widely used for quarantine (Hajar siHHi).

examples.trans: This stone is very heavy.

examples.text: حطينا الحجر الكبير تحت العجل عشان ما ترجع السيارة.
examples.trans: We put the big rock under the tire so the car wouldn't roll back.

الحديدة.gloss: the piece of iron / the metal bar

meanings.en: the piece of iron / the metal bar
meanings.note: Singulative form referring to a specific iron bar, tool, or piece.

examples.trans: Strike the iron piece while it is hot.

examples.text: الحديدة اللي ماسكة الباب انكسرت من الهوا القوي.
examples.trans: The iron bracket holding the door snapped from the strong wind.

الحلو.gloss: the sweet / the beautiful / the dessert

meanings.en: the sweet / the beautiful / the dessert
meanings.note: Can refer to a handsome person, something nice, or sweet desserts.

examples.text: جاب معاه بوكس الحلو بعد الشغل.
examples.trans: He brought a box of dessert with him after work.

examples.text: وزعنا الحلو على المعازيم بنهاية الحفلة.
examples.trans: We handed out the sweets to the guests at the end of the party.

meanings.note: Usually heard in the phrase 'Alhamdulillah' (Praise be to God).

examples.trans: Praise be to God for your safety.

examples.text: كل الناس بقولوا الحمد لله لما يسمعوا خبر منيح.
examples.trans: Everyone says praise be to God when they hear good news.

meanings.note: Colloquial pronunciation of 'hamraa', designating the feminine color red.

examples.trans: The red car parked in front of the house.

examples.text: الكنزة الحمرا بتلبقلك أكثر من الزرقا.
examples.trans: The red sweater suits you better than the blue one.

meanings.note: The staple food in Jordan, often a symbol of livelihood.

examples.trans: I bought the bread from the bakery in the morning.

examples.text: ريحة الخبز السخن طالعة من الفرن على الشارع.
examples.trans: The smell of warm bread is wafting out of the bakery onto the street.

meanings.note: Colloquial plural for 'khareeta' (map).

examples.trans: We used the maps to find the way.

examples.text: فتحت الخرايط على التلفون عشان أشوف الأزمة وين.
examples.trans: I opened the maps on my phone to see where the traffic jam is.

meanings.note: Collective noun for wood material or timber.

examples.text: الطاولة هاي مصنوعة من الخشب الزان.
examples.trans: This table is made of beech wood.

examples.text: النجار قص الخشب وزبط القياسات للخزانة.
examples.trans: The carpenter cut the wood and adjusted the measurements for the closet.

meanings.note: Name of the fifth day of the traditional Arabic week ('Thursday', related to خمسة 'five').

examples.text: السوق الشعبي بيفتح يوم الخميس بعد الظهر.
examples.trans: The neighbourhood market opens on Thursday afternoon.

examples.text: رح نستلم الطاولات يوم الخميس الجاي.
examples.trans: We will receive the tables next Thursday.

meanings.note: Goodness, kindness, or general prosperity/wealth.

examples.text: يعطيك ألف عافية، كتر الله من الخير.
examples.trans: May God give you health, may God increase the good/wealth.

examples.text: إن شاء الله السنة الجديدة بتجيب الخير للجميع.
examples.trans: Hopefully the new year brings goodness and blessings to everyone.

meanings.note: Refers to sewing thread or any thin string/cord.

examples.text: بدي الخيط والإبرة عشان أصلح القميص.
examples.trans: I need the thread and the needle to fix the shirt.

examples.text: لضمت الخيط بالإبرة ورتقت الجاكيت الممزع.
examples.trans: I threaded the needle and mended the torn jacket.

meanings.note: Precious metal, culturally significant for weddings in Jordan.

examples.trans: They bought the gold for my brother's engagement.

examples.text: أسعار الذهب طلعت هالأيام بسوق الصاغة.
examples.trans: Gold prices went up these days in the goldsmiths' market.

meanings.note: Used for main streets, main gates, or main issues.

examples.trans: The street is closed at the main traffic light.

examples.text: البوابة الرئيسية للجامعة بتسكر الساعة عشرة بالليل.
examples.trans: The main gate of the university closes at ten at night.

meanings.note: Can refer to a physical letter, an SMS/WhatsApp message, or an academic thesis.

examples.trans: I received the message from you in the morning.

examples.text: بعتتلك الرسالة على الواتساب بس ما رديت علي.
examples.trans: I sent you the message on WhatsApp, but you didn't reply to me.

meanings.note: A specific piece of artwork or a sketch.

examples.trans: The drawing you drew is very beautiful.

examples.text: بنتي علقت الرسمة تبعتها على باب التلاجة.
examples.trans: My daughter hung her drawing up on the fridge door.

meanings.note: Usually used to describe bright, cheerful colors.

examples.trans: I like to wear bright colors in the summer.

examples.text: الورود الزاهية فتحت بالحديقة من أول الربيع.
examples.trans: The bright flowers bloomed in the garden since early spring.

meanings.note: Physical corner of a room/street, or a geometric angle.

examples.trans: I put the sofa in the corner.

examples.text: الدكان الصغير موجود على الزاوية عند آخر الدخلة.
examples.trans: The small grocery shop is on the corner at the end of the alley.

meanings.note: Plural of zaawiya (corner/angle).

examples.trans: We must clean all the corners in the room.

examples.text: مسحنا الزوايا والرفوف قبل ما نرجع الكتب مكانها.
examples.trans: We wiped down the corners and shelves before putting the books back.

meanings.note: Most commonly refers to olive oil (zeit zaytoun) in Jordan, or motor oil.

examples.text: جيب معاك تنكة الزيت من البلد.
examples.trans: Bring the tin of oil with you from the village.

examples.text: سخنت الزيت بالمقلاية عشان أقلي البطاطا.
examples.trans: I heated the oil in the pan to fry the potatoes.

الساحة.gloss: the square / the courtyard / the arena

meanings.en: the square / the courtyard / the arena
meanings.note: An open space, public square, or schoolyard.

examples.trans: The students were playing in the courtyard.

examples.text: الناس اتجمعوا في الساحة الهاشمية يوم المهرجان.
examples.trans: People gathered in the Hashemite Plaza on the day of the festival.

meanings.note: A concatenated corpus error, likely merging 'the square/arena' and 'written'.

examples.text: قصة الساحة مكتوبة في كتب التاريخ.
examples.trans: The story of the square is written in history books.

examples.text: كانت يافطة الساحة مكتوبة بخط واضح وكبير.
examples.trans: The plaza's sign was written in clear, large lettering.

meanings.note: The day of the week, Saturday.

examples.trans: Our weekend is on Saturday.

examples.text: يوم السبت الصبح دايماً بنروح نجيب خضرة من السوق.
examples.trans: On Saturday morning we always go buy vegetables from the market.

meanings.note: Used to describe something at the bottom.

examples.trans: The lower floor is cold.

examples.text: خزنا المونة بالرف السفلي عشان يضل بارد.
examples.trans: We stored the pantry provisions on the bottom shelf so they stay cool.

meanings.note: Commonly used for a young guy or youth.

examples.trans: The young man helped me a lot.

examples.text: الشاب اللي واقف عالباب بستنى طلب التوصيل.
examples.trans: The young man standing by the door is waiting for the delivery order.

meanings.note: The standard word for a window in a house.

examples.trans: Open the window a little.

examples.text: سكرت الشباك عشان الغبرة ما تفوت عالصالون.
examples.trans: I closed the window so the dust wouldn't get into the living room.

meanings.note: Can mean either the season of winter or the rain itself in Jordanian.

examples.trans: The rain started falling.

examples.text: بالشتا بنشغل الصوبة وبنشرب سحلب سخن.
examples.trans: In winter we turn on the heater and drink hot sahlab.

meanings.note: Collective noun for trees.

examples.trans: The trees in the garden are beautiful.

examples.text: ورق الشجر بلش يصفر ويوقع بشهر تشرين.
examples.trans: The tree leaves started turning yellow and falling in October.

meanings.note: Refers to personal or family honor.

examples.trans: Honor is precious to us.

examples.text: إلنا الشرف نرحب فيكم ببيتنا بأي وقت.
examples.trans: We have the honor of welcoming you into our home anytime.

meanings.note: Means either left direction or the geographical north.

examples.trans: Turn to the left.

examples.text: إربد وعجلون موجودات في منطقة الشمال بالأردن.
examples.trans: Irbid and Ajloun are located in the northern region of Jordan.

meanings.note: Collective noun for wax or candles.

examples.trans: Light the candles because the electricity went out.

examples.text: حطينا الشمع على الطاولة وزينا الغرفة لعيد الميلاد.
examples.trans: We put the candles on the table and decorated the room for the birthday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for morning time.

examples.trans: I wake up early in the morning.

examples.text: بشرب فنجان قهوة كل يوم الصبح قبل ما أطلع عالشغل.
examples.trans: I drink a cup of coffee every morning before heading out to work.

meanings.note: Depending on context, means seashells or plural of coincidence.

examples.trans: We found seashells at the beach.

examples.text: الأولاد جمعوا الصدف من شط العقبة وحطوه بكيس.
examples.trans: The kids collected seashells from the Aqaba shore and put them in a bag.

meanings.note: Used for small objects or young people.

examples.trans: My little brother is studying.

examples.text: الولد الصغير ركض ورا الكرة بالملعب.
examples.trans: The little boy chased after the ball on the field.

meanings.note: Feminine form of small.

examples.trans: The small car is faster.

examples.text: اختي الصغيرة بلشت صف أول هاي السنة.
examples.trans: My little sister started first grade this year.

meanings.note: Often refers to corrugated iron or tin sheets.

examples.trans: The roof is made of sheet metal.

examples.text: زمان كانوا يعبوا الزيت بتتنك من الصفيح.
examples.trans: Back in the day they used to fill oil in cans made of tinplate.

meanings.note: Relating to the summer.

examples.trans: I bought the summer clothes.

examples.text: الشمس بتحرق بالجو الصيفي بنص النهار.
examples.trans: The sun burns in the summer weather at midday.

meanings.note: Refers to the floor of a building.

examples.trans: My house is on the second floor.

examples.text: المصعد عطلان فطلعنا على الطابق الرابع مشي.
examples.trans: The elevator is out of order, so we walked up to the fourth floor.

meanings.note: The universal word for table.

examples.trans: Put the food on the table.

examples.text: حطينا الشاي والقهوة على الطاولة بالنص.
examples.trans: We put the tea and coffee on the table in the middle.

meanings.note: Edge of a table, side of a town, or a party in a conflict.

examples.trans: Sit on the edge.

examples.text: لا تترك الكاسة على الطرف عشان ما توقع وتنكسر.
examples.trans: Don't leave the glass on the edge so it doesn't fall and break.

meanings.note: Very common for a dent in a car or a bent piece of metal.

examples.trans: There is a dent in the car.

examples.text: البودي فيه شوية شغل عشان نصلح الطعجة بالباب.
examples.trans: The bodywork needs a bit of fixing to take out the dent in the door.

meanings.note: Used for shade from the sun.

examples.trans: Let's sit in the shade.

examples.text: صفينا السيارة تحت الشجرة عشان تضل في الظل.
examples.trans: We parked the car under the tree so it would stay in the shade.

meanings.note: General word for a small box, tin, or can.

examples.trans: Where is the empty box?

examples.text: خبي البسكوت جوا العلبة المسكرة عشان ما يطرا.
examples.trans: Keep the biscuits inside the sealed box so they don't go soft.

meanings.note: Refers to Eid holidays (Fitr/Adha) or any festive holiday.

examples.text: كل عام وانت بخير بمناسبة العيد.
examples.trans: Happy holiday (Eid greetings).

examples.text: الأولاد بلبسوا أواعيهم الجديدة صبيحة العيد.
examples.trans: The children put on their new clothes on the morning of Eid.

meanings.note: The main meal of the day, usually eaten in the afternoon.

examples.trans: Please join us for lunch.

examples.text: سخنا المنسف عشان يكون الغدا جاهز على التنتين.
examples.trans: We heated up the mansaf so lunch would be ready at two o'clock.

meanings.note: Plural of room.

examples.trans: I cleaned all the rooms.

examples.text: دهنا كل الغرف بالبيت لون أبيض قبل العرس.
examples.trans: We painted all the rooms in the house white before the wedding.

meanings.note: Used for a pot lid or a blanket.

examples.trans: Close the pot with the lid.

examples.text: مش لاقي الغطا تبع المطرة اللي خدتها عالنادي.
examples.trans: I can't find the lid for the water bottle I took to the gym.

meanings.note: Usually refers to a traditional or Ramadan lantern.

examples.trans: We hung the lantern for Ramadan.

examples.text: الأطفال فرحوا بالفانوس المضيء بأول يوم رمضان.
examples.trans: The children were thrilled with the lit lantern on the first day of Ramadan.

meanings.note: Used primarily for grilling or for water pipes (argileh).

examples.trans: Light the charcoal so we can grill.

examples.text: شغلنا الفحم على البلكونة عشان نعمل مشاوي.
examples.trans: We lit the charcoal on the balcony to make grilled meats.

meanings.note: Describes something situated above or on an upper level.

examples.trans: The upstairs neighbor is annoying.

examples.text: الدرج الفوقاني بده تنظيف وشطف من الغبرة.
examples.trans: The upper staircase needs cleaning and mopping from the dust.

meanings.note: Used for old objects, not usually people.

examples.trans: The old phone broke.

examples.text: جدي لسه محتفظ بالراديو القديم بغرفته.
examples.trans: My grandfather still keeps the old radio in his room.

meanings.note: Feminine form of old.

examples.trans: The old car still runs.

examples.text: البيوت القديمة بجبل اللويبدة إلها طابع خاص.
examples.trans: The old houses in Jabal Al-Weibdeh have a special character.

meanings.note: Used almost exclusively to mean aluminum foil in the kitchen.

examples.trans: Wrap the food in tin foil.

examples.text: غطيت صينية الدجاج بالقصدير قبل ما أدخلها الفرن.
examples.trans: I covered the chicken tray with aluminum foil before putting it in the oven.

meanings.note: Material for making clothes or upholstery.

examples.trans: This fabric is soft.

examples.text: اشترت مترين من القماش عشان تفصل فستان.
examples.trans: She bought two meters of fabric to tailor a dress.

meanings.note: Refers to linen fabric or flax seeds.

examples.trans: The linen shirt is comfortable in summer.

examples.text: البنطلون الكتان بارد ومريح بشوب شهر تموز.
examples.trans: Linen pants are cool and comfortable in the heat of July.

meanings.note: Plural of book.

examples.trans: Put the books in the bag.

examples.text: رتبت كل الكتب على الرف حسب التخصص.
examples.trans: I arranged all the books on the shelf by subject.

meanings.note: Plural of chair.

examples.trans: Bring the chairs for the guests.

examples.text: صفينا الكراسي بالحديقة عشان عزومة بكرا.
examples.trans: We lined up the chairs in the garden for tomorrow's gathering.

meanings.note: Can mean a business card, playing card, or SIM/recharge card.

examples.trans: Do you have my card?

examples.text: شحنت الكرت تبع الباص عند السوبرماركت الصبح.
examples.trans: I topped up the bus card at the supermarket this morning.

meanings.note: Used for food textures or colors (off-white).

examples.trans: The creamy soup is delicious.

examples.text: الصلصة الكريمية مع الباستا طلعت طعمها خيالي.
examples.trans: The creamy sauce with the pasta turned out tasting amazing.

meanings.note: Literal treasure or used metaphorically for something valuable.

examples.trans: They found the treasure on the map.

examples.text: القصة بتحكي عن شباب بدوروا على الكنز المخبي بالمغارة.
examples.trans: The story is about young people searching for the treasure hidden in the cave.

meanings.note: Likely a typographical error or compound (e.g. whose treasure). Treated here as an odd plural/dual or typo.

examples.trans: The treasures (or sweaters) are unknown.

examples.text: سألت الشباب عن الكنزمين بس ولا واحد عرف معناها.
examples.trans: I asked the guys about that odd word, yet not one of them knew what it meant.

meanings.note: Combines with الحمد as a natural everyday expression of relief.

examples.text: الحمد لله خلصنا كل الترتيبات قبل ما يوصلوا الضيوف.
examples.trans: Thank God we finished all the arrangements before the guests arrived.
