examples.text: الله يعطيك العافية على الشغل الحلو هاد.
examples.trans: May God give you strength for this wonderful work.

meanings.note: Almonds, also used metaphorically to mean 'perfect' or 'excellent'.

examples.trans: The situation is perfect (lit. almonds).

examples.text: حمصنا اللوز بشوية سمنة وحطيناه فوق الأرز.
examples.trans: We toasted the almonds in a little ghee and put them on top of the rice.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: The man who I saw yesterday.

examples.text: هذا المحل اللي اشترينا منه الكنافة الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: This is the shop where we bought the kunafa last week.

meanings.note: Describes rainy weather.

examples.trans: The rainy weather makes one sleep.

examples.text: الجو الماطر بخلي الواحد يفضل القعدة بالبيت.
examples.trans: Rainy weather makes a person prefer staying home.

meanings.note: Someone who is retired.

examples.trans: My retired father enjoys relaxing.

examples.text: عمي المتقاعد بقضي الصبح بقراءة الجريدة والقهوة.
examples.trans: My retired uncle spends the morning reading the newspaper and drinking coffee.

meanings.note: Everyday word for facial tissues or handkerchiefs.

examples.trans: Give me the box of tissues.

examples.text: ناولتني اختي ورقة من علبة المحارم اللي عالطاولة.
examples.trans: My sister handed me a tissue from the tissue box on the table.

meanings.note: Passive participle meaning something that has been painted.

examples.trans: The painted wall is still wet.

examples.text: انتبه لا تلمس الباب المدهون لأنه لسه ما نشف.
examples.trans: Be careful not to touch the painted door because it hasn't dried yet.

meanings.note: Describes a square shape or sometimes a sturdy build.

examples.trans: The square table takes up space.

examples.text: حطينا الصينية المربعة على السفرة بنص الصالة.
examples.trans: We placed the square tray on the dining spread in the middle of the hall.

meanings.note: Can mean a tidy female/object, or a mattress (though 'farshe' is more common for mattress in Jordan).

examples.trans: I like the neat girl.

examples.text: الغرفة المرتبة بتفتح النفس للدراسة والشغل.
examples.trans: A tidy room makes you feel ready to study and work.

meanings.note: Passive participle for something drawn.

examples.trans: The drawn painting is beautiful.

examples.text: الوردة المرسومة على الفنجان شغل يدوي دقيق.
examples.trans: The flower painted on the cup is delicate handmade work.

meanings.note: Universal term for a female school teacher in Jordan.

examples.trans: The teacher told us to study.

examples.text: المس وزعت أوراق الامتحان على الطلاب بالصف.
examples.trans: The female teacher handed out the exam papers to the students in class.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a flat surface (masculine).

examples.trans: The flat surface is better for building.

examples.text: الشاش الموجود بالجهاز الجديد هو المسطح مش المنحني.
examples.trans: The screen on the new device is the flat one, not the curved one.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a flat surface (feminine).

examples.trans: The flat ground is comfortable for walking.

examples.text: الصحون المسطحة بتناسب التقديم على السفرة الكبيرة.
examples.trans: Flat plates work well for serving on the large dining spread.

meanings.note: Standard word for kitchen.

examples.trans: The kitchen is clean today.

examples.text: أمي واقفة في المطبخ بتجهز الأكل للضيوف.
examples.trans: My mom is standing in the kitchen preparing food for the guests.

meanings.note: Printed (feminine) or a printout document.

examples.trans: The printed paper is on the table.

examples.text: أخدنا النسخة المطبوعة من المعاملة عشان نقدمها بالبنك.
examples.trans: We took the printed copy of the paperwork to submit it at the bank.

meanings.note: Open (feminine).

examples.trans: The open room lets air in.

examples.text: سكر الشبابيك المفتوحة قبل ما نطلع من البيت.
examples.trans: Close the open windows before we leave the house.

meanings.note: Favorite (masculine).

examples.trans: This is my favorite restaurant.

examples.text: المقلوبة هي الطبق المفضل عندي يوم الجمعة.
examples.trans: Maqluba is my favorite dish on Fridays.

meanings.note: Can mean a written thing or commonly a physical letter.

examples.trans: I received the letter from my friend.

examples.text: زمان كان المرسال يوصل المكتوب على البسكليت.
examples.trans: In the old days the mail carrier used to deliver the letter by bicycle.

meanings.note: Written (feminine).

examples.trans: The written word lasts forever.

examples.text: راجعت الملاحظات المكتوبة بالدفتر قبل الاجتماع.
examples.trans: I reviewed the notes written in the notebook before the meeting.

meanings.note: A sticker or a poster.

examples.trans: Put the poster on the wall.

examples.text: الولد لزق الملصق على دفتر العلوم الجديد.
examples.trans: The boy stuck the sticker onto his new science notebook.

meanings.note: Cabbage, or something wrapped/rolled.

examples.trans: We ate stuffed cabbage yesterday.

examples.text: سلقت أوراق الملفوف عشان ألفهم بالرز واللحمة.
examples.trans: I boiled the cabbage leaves to roll them with rice and meat.

meanings.note: Full (feminine).

examples.trans: The full bottle is very heavy.

examples.text: شلت الكيسة المليانة أغراض من السيارة للمطبخ.
examples.trans: I carried the bag full of groceries from the car to the kitchen.

meanings.note: Star.

examples.trans: The star shines in the sky.

examples.text: البنت لقت النجمة اللامعة بالسما ورتها لأخوها.
examples.trans: The girl spotted the bright star in the sky and showed it to her brother.

meanings.note: Copper or brass.

examples.trans: This tray is made of authentic copper.

examples.text: غسلت إبريق القهوة النحاس بالليمون والملح عشان يلمع.
examples.trans: I washed the copper coffee pot with lemon and salt so it shines.

meanings.note: Made of copper (feminine).

examples.trans: The copper pot makes delicious coffee.

examples.text: مسكت اليد النحاسية للباب اللي برن جرسها قديم.
examples.trans: I grabbed the brass doorknob whose bell sounds vintage.

meanings.note: Bees (collective).

examples.trans: Bees make beneficial honey.

examples.text: جدي بربي النحل بالأغوار وبطلع عسل صافي.
examples.trans: My grandfather keeps bees in the Jordan Valley and harvests pure honey.

meanings.note: Can mean 'the half' (an-noSS) or 'the text' (an-naSS). Both meanings are extremely common.

examples.trans: I ate half and left the rest.

examples.text: قسمنا الرغيف بالنص وأكل كل واحد شقفة.
examples.trans: We split the loaf in half and each person ate a piece.

meanings.note: Margin of a page or margin of a society.

examples.trans: Write your notes on the margin.

examples.text: الدكتور كتب تعليقه على الهامش بقلم أحمر.
examples.trans: The professor wrote his comment in the margin with a red pen.

meanings.note: Front or facade of a building.

examples.trans: The building's facade is fully glass.

examples.text: نظفوا الواجهة القزاز للمحل قبل الافتتاح.
examples.trans: They cleaned the shop's glass storefront before the opening.

meanings.note: Clear, obvious (masculine).

examples.trans: An obvious thing does not need explanation.

examples.text: الحكي الواضح بريح الطرفين من أي سوء فهم.
examples.trans: Clear talk saves both sides from any misunderstanding.

meanings.note: Paper or leaves (collective).

examples.text: جيب معك شوية الورق عشان نكتب.
examples.trans: Bring some paper with you so we can write.

examples.text: خلص الورق من الطابعة ولازم نجيب رزمة جديدة.
examples.trans: The printer ran out of paper and we need to get a new ream.

meanings.note: A single piece of paper or leaf.

examples.trans: Write your name on this piece of paper.

examples.text: وقع الموظف على الورقة وختمها بالختم الرسمي.
examples.trans: The clerk signed the sheet of paper and stamped it with the official seal.

meanings.note: Made of paper or relating to paper.

examples.trans: The paper bag is better for the environment.

examples.text: بحب أقرأ الكتاب الورقي أكثر من النسخة الإلكترونية.
examples.trans: I prefer reading a paper book rather than the electronic copy.

meanings.note: Recipe or medical prescription.

examples.trans: This recipe for making knafeh is wonderful.

examples.text: أعطاني الصيدلاني الدوا حسب الوصفة اللي كتبها الدكتور.
examples.trans: The pharmacist gave me the medicine according to the prescription the doctor wrote.

meanings.note: Name of the historic Amman street where the guesthouse stands (Jasmine Street).

examples.text: شجرة الياسمين عالمدخل معبية الدنيا ريحة بتجنن.
examples.trans: The jasmine tree by the entrance fills the air with an incredible scent.

examples.text: مقهى بيت الياسمين موجود بشارع الياسمين القديم.
examples.trans: Bayt Al-Yasmin café is located on old Jasmine Street.

meanings.note: The left direction or side.

examples.trans: Turn left after the traffic light.

examples.text: باب الصيدلية على إيدك اليسار أول ما تفوت المجمع.
examples.trans: The pharmacy door is on your left as soon as you enter the complex.

meanings.note: The right direction or side.

examples.trans: Keep to the right while driving.

examples.text: خود أقصى اليمين قبل الدوار عشان تفوت عالنفق.
examples.trans: Take the far right lane before the roundabout to enter the tunnel.

meanings.note: Today (literally: the day).

examples.trans: Today the weather is very nice.

examples.text: اليوم عنا شغل كتير بالمكتب وما رح نروح بدري.
examples.trans: Today we have a lot of work at the office and won't head home early.

meanings.note: Form VIII geminate verb.

examples.text: الورق القديم امتص ريحة العسل والبرتقال.
examples.trans: The old paper absorbed the scent of honey and orange.
The blotter absorbs excess ink quickly.

meanings.note: I extend or stretch out.

examples.text: لازم امد إيدي عشان أطول الكتاب.
examples.trans: I have to reach out my hand to get the book.

examples.text: بحاول امد رجلي شوي بعد القعدة الطويلة بالسيارة.
examples.trans: I'm trying to stretch my legs out a bit after sitting so long in the car.

meanings.note: Walk! (directed to a group).

examples.trans: Walk quickly so we don't get late.

examples.text: امشوا شوي شوي عالدرج عشان ما تزحلقوا.
examples.trans: Walk slowly on the stairs so you do not slip.

meanings.note: Form VII colloquial passive of باع (to sell).

examples.text: العسل البلدي بنباع بسوق السبت الصبح.
examples.trans: Local honey is sold at the Saturday morning market.

examples.text: كل الكتب المستعملة انباعت خلال ساعة.
examples.trans: All the second-hand books were sold within an hour.

meanings.note: Plural Jordanian Arabic verb meaning 'to be thrilled' or 'have a wonderful time'.

examples.trans: We really enjoyed hanging out with you tonight.

examples.text: الأولاد رح ينبسطوا بس يشوفوا الكيكة.
examples.trans: The kids are going to be thrilled when they see the cake.

meanings.note: Frequently paired with لفت ('caught my attention': لفت انتباهي).

examples.trans: This question caught my attention.
Thank you for your attention.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنتبه, بينتبه).

examples.text: انتبه على راسك من الخشب الواطي.
examples.trans: Watch your head on the low beam.
Be careful of the corner chair.

meanings.note: Common Arabic verb meaning 'to spread', with the spoken Levantine b- prefix.

examples.text: ريحة القهوة المحمّصة بتنتشر بكل الحارة الصبح.
examples.trans: The aroma of roasted coffee spreads through the whole neighborhood in the morning.
The news spread quickly among the neighbors.

meanings.note: Frequently used with بـ as بانتظام (neatly, regularly).

examples.trans: Arrange the trays neatly on the table.
Suad waters the flowers in the garden regularly.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of انتقل (to move/transition), used here for a musical passage.

examples.text: الانتقال من المقطوعة الهادية للسريعة كان كتير سلس.
examples.trans: The transition from the quiet piece to the fast one was super smooth.

examples.text: موضوع الانتقال لبيت جديد بده ترتيب كتير.
examples.trans: Moving to a new house takes a lot of organizing.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنتهي, بينتهي).

examples.trans: The problem ended well.
We thought everything was over.

meanings.note: You all (subject pronoun).

examples.trans: Where are you all going tonight?
Are you all ready for us to start tasting the cakes?

meanings.note: You all (alternative spelling).

examples.trans: You all are the best people I have known.

examples.text: انتوا التنتين عملتوا شغل ممتاز اليوم.
examples.trans: You two did an excellent job today.

meanings.note: Form VII passive/inchoative of حرق.

examples.text: انتبهي عالفرن عشان الكيكة ما تنحرق!
examples.trans: Watch the oven so the cake does not burn!

examples.text: شامة ريحة إشي عم ينحرق بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: I smell something burning in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Levantine passive Form VII of حط ('to put/place').

examples.trans: The new tables were placed under the arch.
The green ledger was put away in the attic chest.

انحل.gloss: to dissolve; come untied; be solved

meanings.en: to dissolve (in water); to be solved or untied
meanings.note: Form VII medio-passive of حل ('to untie / solve'). Used for ink running in water or a knot coming undone.

examples.trans: Blue ink dissolves quickly in water.
The problem was solved calmly.

meanings.note: Form VII passive/reflexive of حلّ (to solve), meaning 'it got resolved'.

examples.text: الحمد لله المشكلة انحلّت قبل ما تكبر.
examples.trans: Thank goodness the problem got solved before it grew bigger.

examples.text: العقدة بالخيط انحلّت بسهولة بس سحبتها.
examples.trans: The knot in the thread came undone easily once I pulled it.

meanings.note: Common Arabic verb meaning 'to bow down' or take a theatrical bow.

examples.text: العازفة انحنت للجمهور بعد ما خلصت المعزوفة.
examples.trans: The musician bowed to the audience after finishing the piece.

examples.text: الغصن انحنى من كتر التلج اللي تراكم عليه.
examples.trans: The branch bent down from all the snow that piled up on it.

meanings.note: Form VII passive of خبز ('to bake'): describes bread or pastries baking in the oven.

examples.text: الكعكة بتحتاج ربع ساعة لتنخبز منيح.
examples.trans: The cake needs a quarter of an hour to bake properly.
The bread was baked this morning and is still warm.

meanings.note: Form VII Medio-passive of دفع ('to pay'): اندفع حقه means 'its price has been paid'.

examples.trans: The bill was paid in cash at the desk.
Everything was paid for at the market.

meanings.note: Form VII verb used for colours, ink, or groups blending smoothly together.

examples.trans: The colours blended together with the rain.
The guests mingled quickly at the party.

meanings.note: Form VII verb انساب describes water or music flowing smoothly and gracefully.

examples.text: المي بتنساب بين الصخور بصوت هادي ومريح.
examples.trans: The water flows smoothly between the rocks with a calm, soothing sound.

examples.text: اللحن انساب بالصالة وخلى الكل ساكت وبسمع.
examples.trans: The melody drifted effortlessly through the hall, leaving everyone quiet and listening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنسحب, بينسحب).

examples.trans: I shall retreat to my office with dignity!
He quietly stepped out of the room.

meanings.note: Was removed or lifted.

examples.trans: The chair was removed from its place.

examples.text: الغطا انشال عن الصينية قبل ما تبرد.
examples.trans: The cover was lifted off the tray before it cooled.

meanings.note: Relative clause without اللي after an indefinite noun ('chairs that fold').

examples.text: جبنا كراسي بتطوى عشان نقدر نخبيها بالمخزن.
examples.trans: We brought chairs that fold so we can store them in the closet.
The old map was folded up and placed inside the envelope.

meanings.note: Form VII passive of عقد ('to tie a knot'). Spoken Jordanian uses it for cords getting knotted.

examples.trans: The rope got knotted tight from the wind.
The thread knots up if you pull it fast.

meanings.note: The n-pattern of فتح: the thing opens by itself, nobody is named (الباب انفتح 'the door came open').

examples.trans: The window blew open by itself in the wind.
The old lock does not open easily.

meanings.note: Form VII verb from فلت ('to slip away'). Common for latches, hooks, or papers escaping.

examples.trans: The first lantern slipped free from the wire.
Tie it well so it does not come loose.

meanings.note: Passive Levantine Arabic verb from قرا ('to read'), meaning 'to be readable'.

examples.text: الخط كتير صغير لدرجة إنه ما بينقرأ من بعيد.
examples.trans: The handwriting is so small that it can't be read from a distance.
The letter was read aloud in front of everyone at the celebration.

meanings.note: Used for electricity, water, etc.

examples.trans: The electricity cuts off a lot in the summer.
The water got cut off this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنكتب, بينكتب).

examples.trans: Your name will be written in the big ledger!
The address was written in clear handwriting.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنكسر, بينكسر).

examples.trans: The brass pressure valve broke.
Not a single glass broke in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Form VII passive of لف ('to wrap, turn'), common for parcels and fragile dishes.

examples.trans: The cups were wrapped well in newspaper.

examples.text: الخبز السخن ما بينلف بكيس مسكر.
examples.trans: Hot bread is not wrapped in a closed bag.

meanings.note: Form VII intransitive/passive of مزع ('to tear, rip') in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: انتبه عشان ما تنمزع الورقة القديمة.
examples.trans: Be careful so the old sheet of paper does not tear.

examples.text: انمزع الكيس الورق من تقل الليمون.
examples.trans: The paper bag tore from the weight of the lemons.

meanings.note: Everyday casual 'yes' in Amman speech, softer and more informal than نعم.

examples.trans: Yeah, I'm coming with you.
Yeah, of course I know her.

اهتم.gloss: to take care of; look after

meanings.en: to take care of; look after
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بهتم, بيهتم).

examples.trans: Someone has to look after the courtyard plants.
They looked after the guests like family.

meanings.note: Or (conjunction).

examples.trans: Do you want tea or coffee?

examples.text: بتحب العسل الدافي او كريمة الليمون؟
examples.trans: Do you prefer warm honey or lemon icing?

meanings.note: Expression of surprise, realization, or reaction.

examples.trans: Oh, I forgot the keys in the car!
Oh, we forgot to get the honey jar ready!

meanings.note: My hand.

examples.trans: My hand hurts from work.

examples.text: مسكت الكتاب بإيدي التنتين عشان ما يوقع.
examples.trans: I held the book with both my hands so it would not drop.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ب- before nouns ('in/with'); with pronoun suffixes in Levantine it takes the stem في-: فيي ('in me'), فيك ('in/to you m.'), فيكي ('in/to you f.'), فيه ('in him/it'), فيها ('in her/it'), فينا ('in us'), فيهم ('in them').

examples.trans: Welcome to Jasmine House!
My suitcase has a red ribbon in it.

meanings.note: By or with four, or for four (e.g. in currency).

examples.trans: I bought this item for four dinars.
We finished decorating the trays in four colours.

meanings.note: With or by a thumb.

examples.trans: He fingerprinted with his right thumb.
He held the card steady at the corner with his thumb.

بإيدي.gloss: with my hand / in my hand

meanings.en: with my hand / in my hand
meanings.note: In my hand or with my hand.

examples.trans: I made this food with my own hands.

examples.text: عجنت خليط اللوز بإيدي اليوم الصبح.
examples.trans: I mixed the almond batter by hand this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بواب.

examples.trans: The wooden door is open now.
Someone knocked on the door.

meanings.note: Uncountable herbal noun; شاي بابونج ('chamomile tea') is a beloved soothing Levantine infusion.

examples.text: غليت إبريق بابونج دافي عشان ترتاح سلمى.
examples.trans: I brewed a warm pot of chamomile tea so Salma could relax.

examples.text: ريحة البابونج مع العسل بتهدي الأعصاب بالليل.
examples.trans: The scent of chamomile with honey calms the nerves at night.

meanings.note: In four or with four (masculine form modifying feminine nouns).

examples.trans: I finished the work in four hours.

examples.text: زين الكيكة باربع حبات توت كبار.
examples.trans: He decorated the cake with four big berries.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: باردة, plural: باردين).

examples.trans: Here, drink a glass of cold water.
My hands were cold from the rain.

meanings.note: Form III verb from ب-ر-ك; باركلي means 'congratulate me!' (related to مبروك 'congratulations!').

examples.trans: Congratulate me—I found the lost key in the drawer!

examples.text: كل الجيران إجوا يباركوا لنور عالشغل الجديد.
examples.trans: All the neighbours came to congratulate Nour on the new job.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: باصات.

examples.trans: The bus station is close to here.
The bus trip was comfortable.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببيع, بيبيع).

examples.trans: The hardware shop sells this size.
I thought it was lost when we sold the house!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بواقي.

examples.trans: Here you go, here is five dinars change.
I counted the change on the table.

meanings.note: Used in core Jordanian idioms like طول بالك ('be patient'), هدي بالك ('calm down'), and جاي على بالي ('I feel like').

examples.trans: Be patient a moment, everything is fine.

examples.text: جاي على بالي كاسة شاي بالنعنع.
examples.trans: I feel like having a glass of mint tea.

meanings.note: Manually, by hand.

examples.trans: Washing by hand is very tiring.
We whipped the cream by hand without a mixer.

meanings.note: Equally or evenly.

examples.trans: We divided the cake equally.

examples.text: وزعنا التوت بالتساوي على التلات صواني.
examples.trans: We distributed the berries evenly across the three tins.

meanings.note: In or at the university.

examples.trans: I study at the University of Jordan.

examples.text: كان يدرس الخرايط بالجامعة قبل عشر سنين.
examples.trans: He used to study maps at university ten years ago.

meanings.note: Written in ink.

examples.trans: You must sign the paper in blue ink.
The recipe is written in old blue ink.

meanings.note: In the degree, grade, level, or step.

examples.trans: He succeeded with the first degree (top of the class).
He passed with first-class honours in the kitchen.

meanings.note: By drawing or in the field of drawing.

examples.trans: He is very good at drawing.
She is very skilled at drawing and watercolour painting.

meanings.note: In the corner.

examples.trans: The chair is placed in the corner.
There is a number written in pencil in the corner.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.
Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: In the courtyard, yard, or public square.

examples.trans: The boys are playing in the yard.
We drank tea in the courtyard under the tree.

meanings.note: With wax.

examples.trans: We stuck the paper with wax.
The envelope is sealed with red wax.

meanings.note: Exactly, precisely.

examples.text: هذا اللي كنت بدي أحكيه بالضبط.
examples.trans: This is exactly what I wanted to say.
We arrived at nine o'clock sharp.

بالعلبة.gloss: in the box / in the can

meanings.en: in the box / in the can
meanings.note: In the box or the can.

examples.trans: The items are still in the box.
We found the square cards in the metal tin.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian expression for doing something accidentally.

examples.trans: I called you by mistake.
He ate a hot chili pepper by mistake!

meanings.note: Used mostly when referring to grilling or making tea on charcoal.

examples.trans: We made tea on charcoal.
He drew the lines on the paper with black charcoal.

meanings.note: Often used in expressions like 'shū bālak' (what do you think) or 'dir bālak' (take care).

examples.trans: Take care of yourself (literally: turn your mind to yourself).
Keep your mind on the cake while it is in the oven.

meanings.note: Used to describe a location inside a hotel or building lobby.

examples.trans: I am waiting for you in the hotel lobby.
The guests are waiting in the lobby next to reception.

meanings.note: Colloquial Levantine adverbial phrase meaning 'at all' in negatives (ما شفته بالمرة) or 'altogether / completely'.

examples.trans: I did not rush the playing at all today.

examples.text: الموضوع هاد عملي بدون عاطفة بالمرة.
examples.trans: This matter is practical with zero sentiment at all.

meanings.note: Used to indicate the center of something or splitting something equally.

examples.trans: Split the apple in half.
Tin Two is placed right in the middle.

meanings.note: Often used to describe arriving safely or living without danger.

examples.trans: We arrived home safely.
We came down the stairs safely and reached the kitchen.

meanings.note: Hollow verb (long aa in the past, ii in the subjunctive/present). Often used in the sense 'to look/seem'.

examples.text: الألوان بتبان أحلى تحت ضوء الشمس.
examples.trans: The colours look prettier in the sunlight.
After two minutes the true story became clear.

meanings.note: Used to describe colors that have lost their brightness or people looking pale.

examples.text: لون القميص صار باهت من الغسيل.
examples.trans: The shirt's color became faded from washing.
The book cover has a faded green colour.

meanings.note: Used to describe doing something manually or holding something.

examples.trans: I made the cake by hand.

examples.text: دق عالباب بايد الخشب يا طارق.
examples.trans: Tap on the door with the wooden handle, Tariq.

meanings.note: Directing speech to a female, meaning she holds responsibility or literal items in her hands.

examples.trans: The decision is in your hands now.
Hold the tin with both of your hands.

meanings.note: Describes doing an action without rushing.

examples.trans: The car was moving very slowly.

examples.text: عم يمضغ اللقمة ببطء وهو بفكر.
examples.trans: He is chewing the bite slowly while thinking.

meanings.note: Jordanian and Levantine 'for free', built from ب + بلاش ('with nothing').

examples.trans: Tea is free with breakfast.
I got the chair for free from the neighbours.

meanings.note: Very common verb meaning to become visible or clear.

examples.trans: Tiredness shows on him.

examples.text: هادا الكرت ببين قديم كتير ومكتوب بقلم حبر.
examples.trans: This card looks very old and is written in fountain pen.

meanings.note: Used when referring to pointing at something with a finger or signaling.

examples.trans: Why are you pointing at me?
Salma is pointing at the red star on the balcony.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for beginning an action or event.

examples.trans: The party starts at eight o'clock.
The competition starts in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Means to slacken, loosen a grip, or relax tension.

examples.trans: You need to loosen the rope a bit.

examples.text: المي الدافية بترخي العجين وبتسهّل فرده.
examples.trans: Warm water relaxes the dough and makes it easy to roll out.

meanings.note: Used to state similarity between people or things.

examples.trans: The girl resembles her mother a lot.

examples.text: نكهة المليسة بتشبه قشر الليمون الطازج.
examples.trans: The flavour of lemon balm resembles fresh lemon peel.

meanings.note: Commonly used for pouring liquids like water, coffee, or tea.

examples.trans: Can you pour me a glass of water?

examples.text: سلمى بتصب العسل الدافي فوق اللوز المحمص.
examples.trans: Salma pours the warm honey over the toasted almonds.

meanings.note: Fundamental verb for having knowledge or acquaintance with something or someone.

examples.trans: Do you know where the bus station is?

examples.text: بتعرف مين كتب الملاحظة على ظهر الخريطة؟
examples.trans: Do you know who wrote the note on the back of the map?

meanings.note: Used for opening doors, windows, businesses, or even turning on devices sometimes.

examples.trans: The supermarket opens early.

examples.text: المكتبة بتفتح أبوابها الساعة تمانية الصبح.
examples.trans: The library opens its doors at eight in the morning.

بتلف.gloss: you turn / she turns / you wrap

meanings.en: you turn / she turns / you wrap
meanings.note: Used for taking a turn while driving or walking, and for wrapping items like gifts or sandwiches.

examples.trans: You turn right at the traffic light.

examples.text: بعد الشجرة الكبيرة بتلف يمين عالزقاق الضيق.
examples.trans: After the big tree you turn right into the narrow alley.

meanings.note: Used as a material noun after خشب ('birch wood') or ملقط ('birch clothespin').

examples.trans: Birch wood is smooth and light in colour.
We have clean birch clothespins.

meanings.note: Used to indicate that something will happen very quickly.

examples.trans: I will finish the work in a second.

examples.text: حل مازن اللغز بثانية أول ما شاف الرقم.
examples.trans: Mazen solved the riddle in a second as soon as he saw the number.

meanings.note: Refers to something being inside a sock or a small pouch/bag.

examples.trans: I put the money in a sock.

examples.text: خبينا المفتاح الصغير بجراب صوف دافي.
examples.trans: We hid the small key inside a warm wool sock.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بجعات.

examples.trans: We saw a white swan on the water.
The drawing of the swan is very pretty.

meanings.note: Used when talking about items kept in one's clothing pocket.

examples.trans: My phone is in my pocket.

examples.text: خليت بطاقة الدخول بجيبي عشان ما تضيع.
examples.trans: I kept the entry card in my pocket so it would not get lost.

meanings.note: Refers to writing or drawing done specifically using ink rather than a pencil.

examples.trans: I signed the paper with blue ink.

examples.text: العنوان مكتوب بحبر أزرق غامق على المغلف.
examples.trans: The address is written in dark blue ink on the envelope.

meanings.note: Used to express necessity or a requirement.

examples.trans: I need help with this matter.

examples.text: الشاي المغلي بحتاج خمس دقايق عشان يتخمر.
examples.trans: Boiling tea needs five minutes to steep properly.

meanings.note: Both academic/historical research and physical searching.

examples.text: هادا البحث التاريخي أخد منا وقت طويل.
examples.trans: This historical research took us a long time.

examples.text: بعد بحث طويل لقينا الكرت جوا الكتاب.
examples.trans: After a long search we found the card inside the book.

meanings.note: Used in ملح بحر ('sea salt') as well as for the Mediterranean or Dead Sea.

examples.text: حطيت رشة صغيرة من ملح البحر فوق العجينة.
examples.trans: I put a tiny pinch of sea salt on top of the dough.

examples.text: هوا البحر بيجي لطيف ومنعش آخر النهار.
examples.trans: The sea breeze comes in gentle and refreshing late in the afternoon.

meanings.en: nautical; marine; relating to the sea
meanings.note: Nisba adjective from بحر ('sea'). Adverbial form بحريا means 'nautically'.

examples.trans: This rope knot is tied in a nautical style.
The shirt colour is navy blue.

meanings.note: Expresses placing or setting down a feminine object.

examples.trans: Where do I put the books?

examples.text: كل ما ألاقي ورقة قديمة بحطها جوا الدفتر.
examples.trans: Whenever I find an old sheet I put it inside the notebook.

meanings.note: Noun for steam or vapour.

examples.text: البخار طالع من طنجرة الشوربة ومغبّش الشباك.
examples.trans: Steam is rising from the soup pot and fogging up the window.

examples.text: عملت بخار لقميصي قبل المقابلة عشان يطلع مرتب.
examples.trans: I steamed my shirt before the interview so it would look neat.

meanings.note: Used to describe an action done gently, quickly, or with agility.

examples.trans: He jumped over the wall nimbly.

examples.text: شال الغطا عن الصينية بخفة بدون ما يعمل صوت.
examples.trans: He lifted the lid off the tin lightly without making a sound.

meanings.note: Refers to sewing or tying something using a piece of thread.

examples.trans: I sewed the button with black thread.

examples.text: العلبة الخشب مربوطة بخيط قنب متين.
examples.trans: The wooden box is tied with sturdy hemp string.

meanings.note: Core Levantine word for 'want', inflected with pronoun suffixes rather than verb prefixes.

examples.text: بدك تشرب قهوة سادة ولا وسط؟
examples.trans: Do you want to drink plain black coffee or medium-sweet?

examples.text: بدنا نطلع بكير عشان ما نعلق بالأزمة.
examples.trans: We want to leave early so we don't get stuck in traffic.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببدا, بيبدا).

examples.trans: Start with three short sentences.
The day began lively and bright.

meanings.note: Opening section of a song, book, or week.

examples.trans: The opening of the song is gentle and lifts the heart.

examples.text: من بداية الربيع، الساحة بتتعبى ورد.
examples.trans: From the start of spring, the courtyard fills with blossoms.

meanings.note: Commonly used regarding time, indicating morning hours or ahead of schedule.

examples.trans: I woke up early today.

examples.text: طلعنا من البيت بدري قبل زحمة السوق.
examples.trans: We left the house early before the market crowd.

meanings.note: Used directly before nouns or pronouns (بدل ستة 'instead of six') and before ما + verb (بدل ما تستنى 'instead of waiting').

examples.text: اشرب شاي سخن بالنعنع بدل القهوة بالليل.
examples.trans: Drink hot mint tea instead of coffee at night.

examples.text: ضل معنا تلات أيام بس بدل أسبوع كامل.
examples.trans: We only have three days left instead of a whole week.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'want / need', inflected with pronoun suffixes: بدي (I want), بدك (you want), بده (he/it wants), بدها (she/it wants), بدنا (we want), بدكم (you pl. want), بدهم (they want).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Jam bread needs unsalted butter.

meanings.note: The most common way to express 'they want' in Jordanian and Palestinian dialects.

examples.trans: They want to go to the cinema.

examples.text: الضيوف بدهم يذوقوا الكيكة التالتة كمان.
examples.trans: The guests want to taste the third cake as well.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'without', used identically to MSA.

examples.trans: I like coffee without sugar.

examples.text: شرب القهوة بدون سكر مع قطعة بقلاوة.
examples.trans: He drank the coffee without sugar alongside a piece of baklava.

meanings.note: Levantine colloquial pronunciation of بدأ (bada'), conjugated like a defective verb (بديت، بدينا).

examples.text: رجعنا لنفس البوابة اللي بدينا منها.
examples.trans: We came back to the exact gate we started from.

examples.text: العرض رح يبدا الساعة ستة بالزبط.
examples.trans: The show will start at six o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Form II verb from بدل. Used for alternating colours or swapping items.

examples.trans: We alternated between gold and white.
I need to swap out the wet bag.

meanings.note: Refers to being outdoors or outside a specific location.

examples.trans: The kids are playing outside.

examples.text: الأولاد بلعبوا برا بالساحة جنب الشجر.
examples.trans: The children are playing outside in the courtyard beside the trees.

meanings.note: Commonly heard in Amman to applaud music, baking, or a clever idea. Followed by عليك/عليكي for 'well done to you!'.

examples.trans: Bravo! The piano playing was wonderful!

examples.text: برافو عليكي يا نور، الخطة ممتازة.
examples.trans: Well done, Nour, the plan is excellent.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: برتقالات.

examples.trans: The fresh orange juice is cold.
We bought oranges and apples from the market.

meanings.note: Can refer to a physical tower, a skyscraper, or an astrological sign.

examples.trans: This is the highest tower in the city.

examples.text: برج الساعة القديم مبين من فوق السطوح.
examples.trans: The old clock tower is visible from the rooftop.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببرد, بيبرد).

examples.trans: The cake is cooling on the rack right now.
The radiator is starting to get cold at the bottom.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of برتقال (collective noun; unit noun بردقانة 'one orange').

examples.trans: Fresh orange juice is nicest in the morning.

examples.text: جيب معك كيلو بردقان من السوق.
examples.trans: Bring a kilo of oranges with you from the market.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of برش ('to grate'). Used in baking for citrus zest (برش البرتقال 'orange zest', برش الليمون 'lemon zest').

examples.text: برش البرتقال بيعطي الكيكة ريحة حلوة.
examples.trans: Orange zest gives the cake a lovely aroma.
We added one teaspoon of lemon zest.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word (from Turkish burgu) for a metal screw.

examples.trans: I tightened the screw with the small screwdriver.
The chair needs a new screw.

meanings.note: Used for lifting objects, raising volume, or increasing prices.

examples.trans: I lift the heavy box.

examples.text: كل يوم الصبح برفع الغطا عن العجين.
examples.trans: Every morning he lifts the cover off the dough.

meanings.note: Flash of lightning in a storm, often paired with رعد ('thunder').

examples.text: شفنا برق قوي ورا قزاز الباب.
examples.trans: We saw bright lightning behind the door glass.

examples.text: بعد البرق بثواني، سمعنا صوت الرعد.
examples.trans: Seconds after the lightning, we heard the roll of thunder.

meanings.note: Feminine noun from برق ('lightning'), referring to a telegraphed or urgent written dispatch.

examples.text: وصلت برقية عاجلة من المحطة الصبح.
examples.trans: An urgent telegram arrived from the station this morning.

examples.text: زمان كانوا يبعتوا البرقيات للأخبار المهمة.
examples.trans: In the old days they used to send telegrams for important news.

meanings.note: Masculine noun with broken plural برامج (baraamij).

examples.text: برنامج الحفلة مطبوع على ورق أبيض.
examples.trans: The concert programme is printed on white paper.
What is our schedule for Saturday?

meanings.note: Borrowed from Italian prova; used across Arabic for music rehearsals, theatre runs, and tailoring fittings.

examples.text: عندنا بروفة الساعة خمسة في القاعة.
examples.trans: We have a rehearsal at five in the hall.

examples.text: بعد تلت بروفات صارت الفرقة جاهزة.
examples.trans: After three rehearsals the band was ready.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A postcard arrived in the morning.
The postman rang the bell.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from بريد (mail); بطاقة بريدية means 'postcard'.

examples.text: بعتتلي بطاقة بريدية حلوة من العقبة.
examples.trans: She sent me a lovely postcard from Aqaba.

examples.text: الطرد البريدي وصل خلال تلات أيام.
examples.trans: The postal parcel arrived within three days.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Refers to an outdoor area belonging to a home or building owned by the speakers.

examples.trans: We planted a tree in our courtyard.
There is a large lemon tree in our courtyard.

meanings.note: Similar to 'b-sāḥitnā' but referring to a space belonging specifically to the speaker.

examples.trans: I like to drink coffee in my yard.

examples.text: أزهار الياسمين مفتحة بساحتي كل صيف.
examples.trans: The jasmine flowers bloom in my yard every summer.

meanings.note: Commonly used to describe going on trips, usually international or long-distance.

examples.trans: Every summer I travel to Aqaba.

examples.text: خالي بسافر على العقبة كل شهر مرة.
examples.trans: My uncle travels to Aqaba once every month.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بسطات.

examples.trans: Turn left at the stair landing.
The landing is wide and bright.

meanings.note: General term for any kind of sweet, dry baked good like a cookie or biscuit.

examples.trans: I ate biscuits with tea.
We baked sesame and anise biscuits for the guests.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بسيطة, plural: بسيطين).

examples.trans: Explain the matter to me in simple words.
The problem is minor and easy to fix.

meanings.note: Indicates location within a street or on a specific road.

examples.trans: I saw you on University Street.

examples.text: المكتبة بشارع هادي قريب من الساحة.
examples.trans: The library is on a quiet street near the square.

بشكل.gloss: in a way / in a shape

meanings.en: in a way / in a shape
meanings.note: Often used as a prefix for adverbs, e.g., 'bi-shakil ʿām' (generally).

examples.trans: We need to work in a faster way.
The ingredients are mixed in a completely even way.

meanings.note: Collective noun for onions; a single onion is بصلة.

examples.text: قطّع البصل ناعم وحطّه بالزيت الساخن.
examples.trans: Chop the onions finely and put them in the hot oil.

examples.text: جبت كيلو بصل أحمر من السوق.
examples.trans: I brought a kilo of red onions from the market.

meanings.note: Refers to vocalization, often used in phrases like 'b-ṣōt ʿālī' (with a loud voice).

examples.trans: Don't speak with a loud voice.

examples.text: قرأ الرسالة بصوت واطي عشان ما حدا يسمع.
examples.trans: He read the letter in a low voice so no one would hear.

meanings.note: Plural of 'biṭāqa', can mean playing cards, identity cards, or event tickets.

examples.trans: I bought tickets for the match.

examples.text: وزعنا بطاقات التذوق على كل الطاولات.
examples.trans: We handed out the tasting cards across all the tables.

meanings.note: Singular form for any type of card (ID, credit, ticket, etc.).

examples.trans: My bank card is lost.

examples.text: كل بطاقة عليها رقم ورمز مرسوم بالحبر.
examples.trans: Each card has a number and a symbol drawn in ink.

meanings.note: Most often heard in understated Jordanian praise: مش بطال ('not bad at all!').

examples.trans: Not bad for a first week of work!
The weather today is not bad at all.

meanings.note: Inner lining of a coat or the tiny wool-felt bushing inside a piano hinge.

examples.text: بطانة اللباد جوا المفصلة بدها تبديل بسيط.
examples.trans: The felt bushing inside the hinge just needs a small adjustment.

examples.text: هاد المعطف الشتوي إله بطانة صوف دافية.
examples.trans: This winter coat has a warm wool lining.

بطاولة.gloss: at a table / with a table

meanings.en: at a table / with a table
meanings.note: Indicates physical interaction or location relative to a table.

examples.trans: I bumped my leg against a table.

examples.text: حطينا العلبة بطاولة المطبخ جنب الشباك.
examples.trans: We set the tin on the kitchen table beside the window.

meanings.note: Form II verb (battal) used in imperatives like بطلي حركاتك ('cut out your antics').

examples.trans: Stop talking like that.
We stopped going there.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بطلات.

examples.trans: You are the heroine of the kitchen today!
She ran fast like a champion.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بطيئة, plural: بطيئين).

examples.trans: Downtown traffic at noon is slow.
A slow step is better than rushing.

بطّل.gloss: to stop (doing); no longer be able

meanings.en: to stop (doing); no longer be able
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببطل, بيبطل).

examples.trans: My knees stopped holding me up from the shock!
The rain stopped falling in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببعت, بيبعت).

examples.trans: Last week I sent him a postcard.
She sent a kind thank-you note.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'then, next, afterwards' (وبعدين 'and then').

examples.trans: Lift the handle first, and then push.
Have some tea and then we will talk.

meanings.note: The most fundamental way to state personal knowledge or awareness.

examples.trans: I know what happened.

examples.text: أنا بعرف هادا المخبز من أيام الطفولة.
examples.trans: I have known this bakery since childhood days.

meanings.note: After a plural verb, بعض means 'each other' (بننادي بعض 'we call each other').

examples.trans: We call each other by first name here.

examples.text: ما حكينا مع بعض من زمان.
examples.trans: We have not spoken with each other in a long time.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بعيدة, plural: بعاد).

examples.trans: The shop is not far from the gate.

examples.text: الطاولة تحت الشجرة بعيد عن الباب.
examples.trans: The table is under the tree away from the door.

meanings.note: Specifies location inside a room of a building.

examples.trans: The boy is sleeping in the guest room.
We found the map in my grandfather's old room.

بغطا.gloss: with a cover / in a cover

meanings.en: with a cover / in a cover
meanings.note: Refers to a lid, cap, or a blanket covering something.

examples.trans: Close the pot with a lid.
We sealed the jar with a tight brass lid.

meanings.note: A highly versatile prefix used as a preposition of place or instrument.

examples.trans: We went to work by car.

examples.text: اكتب اسمك بـ قلم الحبر على البطاقة.
examples.trans: Write your name with the fountain pen on the card.

meanings.note: Expresses the action of astonishing or surprising someone.

examples.trans: I always surprise my friends on their birthdays.

examples.text: طارق دايما بفاجئ أهله بوصفات جديدة.
examples.trans: Tariq always surprises his family with new recipes.

meanings.note: Refers to the lowest part of a container, the sea, or any deep object.

examples.trans: The key fell at the bottom of the pool.

examples.text: ضل شوية سكر بقاع كاسة الشاي.
examples.trans: A little sugar stayed at the bottom of the teacup.

meanings.note: Used to indicate something is rhymed.

examples.trans: He wrote the poem with a nice rhyme.

examples.text: البيت الشعري مكتوب بقافية حلوة وموزونة.
examples.trans: The verse is written with a lovely, balanced rhyme.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for parsley.

examples.text: رشّ شوية بقدونس مفروم على وجه التبولة.
examples.trans: Sprinkle a little chopped parsley on top of the tabbouleh.

examples.text: لا تنسى تجيب ضمة بقدونس طازة معك.
examples.trans: Don't forget to bring a bunch of fresh parsley with you.

meanings.note: Used to indicate authorship or the instrument used.

examples.trans: This article is by a famous writer.

examples.text: سلمى سجلت النتايج بقلم رصاص ناعم.
examples.trans: Salma recorded the results with a soft pencil.

meanings.note: Used to refer to something made of or covered with fabric.

examples.trans: He covered the table with a red cloth.

examples.text: غطينا سلة الخبز بقماش كتان أبيض.
examples.trans: We covered the bread basket with white linen cloth.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'tomorrow' (بكرا الصبح 'tomorrow morning').

examples.text: بكرا الصبح رح نسبق المي الباردة!
examples.trans: Tomorrow morning we will beat the cold water!
We booked a quiet dinner — will you join us tomorrow?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'tomorrow' (أشوفك بكرة! 'See you tomorrow!').

examples.trans: We have an exam tomorrow morning.
See you tomorrow at school!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for expressing the price or cost of an item or service.

examples.trans: This project costs a lot of money.

examples.text: هادا المكون النادر بكلف وقت ومجهود كتير.
examples.trans: This rare ingredient costs a lot of time and effort.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببكي, بيبكي).

examples.trans: The poor gentleman looks about to cry.
We laughed and nobody cried in the end.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'early'.

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
We wake up early every day.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine preposition meaning 'without' or 'let's skip / no…' (قهوة بلا سكر 'coffee without sugar').

examples.text: بشرب الشاي بنعنع وبلا سكر لو سمحت.
examples.trans: I drink mint tea without sugar, please.

examples.text: بلا عجلة، قدامنا تلات أيام كاملة.
examples.trans: No rush—we have three full days ahead of us.

meanings.note: Everyday masculine loanword for plastic wrap, sleeves, or containers.

examples.text: غلّفت الوصفة ببلاستيك عشان ما تتبلل.
examples.trans: She sealed the recipe in plastic so it would not get wet.

examples.text: ما بنحب نحط الشاي بكاسات بلاستيك.
examples.trans: We do not like serving tea in plastic cups.

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for stone, ceramic, or courtyard tiles; single tile is بلاطة.

examples.trans: We wiped the courtyard tiles with water this morning.

examples.text: بلاط المطبخ بارد على الرجلين بالشتاء.
examples.trans: The kitchen tile is cold on the feet in winter.

meanings.note: Plural of بلاطة, the everyday Arabic word for a paving stone or floor tile.

examples.text: في بلاطة مكسورة عند مدخل الحوش لازم نبدلها.
examples.trans: There is a cracked tile at the courtyard entrance that we need to replace.

examples.text: بلاطات الحوش الحجرية بتضل باردة حتى بالصيف.
examples.trans: The stone courtyard flagstones stay cool even in summer.

meanings.note: In Amman, وسط البلد or simply البلد refers to downtown Amman.

examples.trans: We went down to downtown in the morning.
Town is quiet on Friday.

meanings.note: From بلد ('country, town'); prized on Jordanian market stalls for local olive oil, honey, lemons, and thyme.

examples.text: عسل بلدي من جبال عجلون ريحته بتشهي.
examples.trans: Local honey from the Ajloun hills smells delicious.
We bought yellow local lemons for tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بلديات.

examples.trans: He works in the contracts office at the municipality.
The municipal building is next to the square.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine verb for starting something or starting a fight (هي اللي بلشت 'she's the one who started it').

examples.trans: Class started a little while ago.
Who started the problem?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian noun for a balcony or veranda.

examples.text: شربنا القهوة عالبلكونة الخشب الطابق التاني.
examples.trans: We drank coffee on the wooden balcony on the second floor.
The balcony of Jasmine House overlooks the courtyard.

meanings.note: Very common Jordanian/Levantine modal adverb expressing hope or possibility.

examples.text: بلكي نلاقي الكرت التاني جوا العلبة.
examples.trans: Maybe we will find the second card inside the tin.

examples.text: استنى شوي، بلكي سلمى ترجع بعد دقايق.
examples.trans: Wait a moment, perhaps Salma will come back in a few minutes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The table is made of oak wood.
Oak trees are old and strong.

meanings.note: Loanword used for urban street blocks as well as building bricks.

examples.text: المكتبة بعيدة تلات بلوكات لفوق بالشارع.
examples.trans: The library is three blocks up the street.

examples.text: بنينا الحيط الصغير من حجر البلوك.
examples.trans: We built the low wall out of concrete blocks.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببلش, بيبلش).

examples.trans: The brass pipe started heating up right away!
The clock tower started chiming twelve.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببلغ, بيبلغ).

examples.text: في حدا بلغ عن شنتة زرقا؟
examples.trans: Has anyone reported a blue suitcase?
We gave the office the phone number.

meanings.note: Indicates a location or a specific spot.

examples.trans: I put it in a safe place.

examples.text: خبوا الصندوق بمكان آمن تحت الدرج.
examples.trans: They hid the box in a safe place under the stairs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بنايات.

examples.trans: The stone building is eighty years old.
The building owner sent a letter.

meanings.note: Singular بنت, definite البنت, plural بنات / البنات ('AlRawabi School for Girls' = مدرسة الروابي للبنات).

examples.trans: She is a very bright girl.
The girls are standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بنود.

examples.trans: Read clause four in the contract.
This clause protects the tenant.

meanings.note: Standard Levantine collective word for tomatoes (from Italian pomodoro).

examples.trans: The roasted tomato soup smells mouthwatering.

examples.text: اشترينا كيلو بندورة حمرا من سوق السبت.
examples.trans: We bought a kilo of ripe red tomatoes at the Saturday market.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببنشر, بيبنشر).

examples.trans: The dairy van got a flat tyre outside town.
The tyre went flat on the road this morning.

meanings.note: Reflexive pronoun used for second person plural.

examples.trans: You must do this thing by yourselves.

examples.text: جربوا تذوقوا العسل بنفسكم عشان تفرقوا الطعم.
examples.trans: Try tasting the honey yourselves so you can tell the flavour apart.

meanings.note: Commonly used in Jordanian Arabic to mean "it is acceptable" or "it works".

examples.trans: This solution works for us.

examples.text: بنفع نستعمل زبدة بلدية بدل الزيت بالوصفة؟
examples.trans: Does it work to use local butter instead of oil in the recipe?

meanings.note: Used to say "we are walking" or "let us go".

examples.trans: Come on, let's walk now.

examples.text: كل يوم المسا بنمشي سوا بالحديقة.
examples.trans: Every evening we walk together in the garden.

meanings.note: Everyday verb بنى (to build).

examples.text: جدي بنى هاد البيت الحجري قبل ستين سنة.
examples.trans: My grandfather built this stone house sixty years ago.

examples.text: بدنا نبني غرفة جديدة عالسطح السنة الجاية.
examples.trans: We want to build a new room on the roof next year.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بنية, plural: بنيين).

examples.trans: The brown leather notebook is on the desk.
A clean pair of men's brown shoes.

meanings.note: Used in Levantine dialects to mean "like this" or "with this kind of".

examples.trans: In such a case, we must be careful.

examples.text: بهيك حالة لازم نعيد قراءة التعليمات.
examples.trans: In such a case we need to re-read the instructions.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.
The taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Refers to a gate belonging to a group (us).

examples.trans: Our gate is closed today.

examples.text: بوابتنا الخشب بتطل مباشرة عالساحة القديمة.
examples.trans: Our wooden gate looks directly out onto the old courtyard.

meanings.note: Used for navigation or metaphorically for direction.

examples.text: ضاع بالصحراء لأنه ما كان معه بوصلة.
examples.trans: He got lost in the desert because he didn't have a compass.

examples.text: اتبعنا إبرة البوصلة لحد ما وصلنا الشرق.
examples.trans: We followed the compass needle until we reached the east.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بياعين.

examples.trans: The shopkeeper gave me a receipt and change.
I asked the clerk about the size.

meanings.note: The musical instrument.

examples.trans: He plays the piano every day.
The black piano is placed in the corner of the parlour.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: Describes the action of baking bread or pastries.

examples.text: هو بيخبز خبز طازج كل الصبح.
examples.trans: He bakes fresh bread every morning.

examples.text: الفران بيخبز الخبز الطازج قبل الفجر.
examples.trans: The baker bakes fresh bread before dawn.

meanings.note: Feminine/masculine noun used in the beloved Levantine proverb سرك ببير ('your secret is in a well' = safe with me).

examples.trans: Do not worry, your secret is safe with me.
Well water is cold in summer.

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'bass', referring to the bass line, bass guitar, or upright bass.

examples.text: خط البيز هو اللي بيمسك إيقاع الأغنية.
examples.trans: The bass line is what holds the rhythm of the song.

examples.text: صوت البيز كان واطي شوي بالبروفة.
examples.trans: The bass sound was a bit low in the rehearsal.

meanings.note: Collective plural بيض ('eggs'), singulative بيضة ('one egg'), dual بيضتين ('two eggs').

examples.trans: I fried two eggs for breakfast.
Hot eggs are delicious with bread.

meanings.note: Plural form of egg, commonly used when counting eggs.

examples.trans: I bought five eggs from the shop.

examples.text: استعملنا تلات بيضات طازجة للكيكة الإسفنجية.
examples.trans: We used three fresh eggs for the sponge cake.

meanings.note: Describes a group of people laughing.

examples.trans: The boys are laughing loudly.
The children are laughing as they look for the treasure.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The building is not up for sale.
The bill of sale is ready in the office.

meanings.note: Used to explain or clarify a point.

examples.text: هذا الاشي بيعني انه احنا خلصنا.
examples.trans: This thing means that we are finished.

examples.text: هادا الرمز بيعني إنه الغرفة مسكرة من جوا.
examples.trans: This symbol means that the room is locked from inside.

meanings.note: Preposition 'between, among'.

examples.trans: Today you are mending things between two brothers!
The table is between the window and the door.

meanings.note: Used to contrast two different situations or actions happening at the same time.

examples.text: هو كان بدرس بينما أنا كنت بلعب.
examples.trans: He was studying while I was playing.

examples.text: كنت بحضر الشاي بينما سلمى بتقطع الكيكة.
examples.trans: I was preparing the tea while Salma was slicing the cake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببين, بيبين).

examples.text: لما بدهم يبينوا هاديين بيتأخروا دقيقتين.
examples.trans: When they want to play it cool, they arrive two minutes late.
The truth came out at the end of the week.

meanings.note: Imperative ابعدوا ('step back!'); distinct from preposition بعد ('after').

examples.trans: Step back from the window, all of you!
He moved the chair slightly away from the door.

meanings.note: As a noun after على (على بعد عشر أمتار 'at a distance of ten metres'); distinct from preposition بعد ('after').

examples.trans: The shop is five minutes away.
The stop is a hundred metres away.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتأخر, بيتأخر).

examples.trans: Tell me I am not late for the lesson!
The bus was not even a minute late.

meanings.note: Past tense Arabic verb meaning 'to make sure' or 'verify', conjugated for a woman.

examples.text: تأكدتي إنو الباب تسكّر منيح قبل ما تطلعي؟
examples.trans: Did you make sure the door was locked properly before you left?

examples.text: لازم نتأكد من الموعد قبل ما نحجز التذاكر.
examples.trans: We need to verify the appointment before booking the tickets.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتأكد, بيتأكد).

examples.trans: I am just checking safety.
Make sure the size is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تابلتات.

examples.trans: The tablet screen is clear and large.
I left the tablet on the desk.

meanings.note: Baked fruit or custard tart, especially تارت الليمون ('lemon tart').

examples.text: تارت الليمون بقشرة اللوز طلع أطيب واحد.
examples.trans: The lemon tart with the almond crust turned out to be the tastiest one.

examples.text: خلينا قطعة تارت صغيرة لطارق بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: We saved a small slice of tart for Tariq in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Means both a calendar 'date' (تاريخ البطاقة 'the date on the card') and 'history'.

examples.trans: Write today's date at the top of the page.

examples.text: هاد البيت القديم إله تاريخ حلو بعمان.
examples.trans: This old house has a lovely history in Amman.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from تاريخ (history), agreeing with الساحة.

examples.text: وسط البلد فيه مباني تاريخية عمرها أكتر من مية سنة.
examples.trans: Downtown has historic buildings that are over a hundred years old.

examples.text: المدرج الروماني معلم تاريخي مهم بعمان.
examples.trans: The Roman Theater is an important historic landmark in Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تاسعة, plural: تاسعين).

examples.trans: We found a ninth brass key in the box.

examples.text: الباب التاسع كان مخفي ورا الحيط.
examples.trans: The ninth door was hidden behind the wall.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تكاسي.

examples.trans: A yellow taxi pulled up at the pavement.
We took a taxi to the bus station.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تالتة, plural: تالتين).

examples.trans: The attic room is on the third floor.
He used to sit on the third step.

meanings.note: Active participle of the geminate verb تمّ.

examples.text: التذوق المضبوط بده هدوء تام بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: A proper tasting requires complete silence in the kitchen.

examples.text: كلامك إله معنى تام ومقنع كتير.
examples.trans: Your words make total sense and are very convincing.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Refers to making a substitution or changing something.

examples.trans: We need to do a changing of clothes.

examples.text: احتجنا تبديل الصواني عشان تنخبز بالتساوي.
examples.trans: We needed to swap the trays so they bake evenly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتبدل, بيتبدل).

examples.trans: A blue suitcase got swapped at the bus station.
The keys were never mixed up.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of برّد (to cool down).

examples.text: التبريد بالمخزن شغال منيح عشان الخضرة ما تخرب.
examples.trans: The cooling in the storeroom is working well so the vegetables don't spoil.

examples.text: سيب الكيكة تبرد عالرف، التبريد بياخد نص ساعة.
examples.trans: Let the cake cool on the rack; cooling takes half an hour.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian and Levantine word used as a possessive marker, similar to "of" or "'s".

examples.trans: My brother's car is broken.
Where is the key belonging to the kitchen cupboard?

meanings.note: The feminine form of the Levantine possessive marker.

examples.trans: Reem's bag is lost.

examples.text: العلبة تبعت الشاي الأخضر عالرف التاني.
examples.trans: The green tea tin is on the second shelf.

meanings.note: Used to indicate first-person possession.

examples.trans: This book is mine, not yours.
My notebook is still open on the table.

meanings.note: Form V intransitive verb meaning 'get wet / soaked in the rain'.

examples.text: دخلنا الشيش جوا قبل ما يتبلل الخشب.
examples.trans: We brought the shutters inside before the wood got soaked.
My sleeves got a little wet from the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تجارية, plural: تجاريين).

examples.trans: Converting the house into commercial offices is forbidden.
This is a residential street, not commercial.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: تجارب.

examples.trans: The trial week went by fast.
It was a very sweet experience.

meanings.note: Formed from تجريد ('abstraction'). Feminine singular: تجريدية.

examples.trans: Abstract art has bold colours.
This painting is very abstract.

meanings.note: Often a colloquial pronunciation or a typo of "تجبري" (tijibri), meaning to force someone or set a broken bone.

examples.text: ما بتقدري تجيبري حدا على شي ما بده ياه.
examples.trans: You cannot force anyone into something they don't want.

examples.text: لا تجيبري الضيوف ياكلوا إذا شبعانين.
examples.trans: Do not force the guests to eat if they are full.

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: The cat is hiding under the table.

examples.text: لقينا البطاقة التانية تحت الصحن الأبيض.
examples.trans: We found the second card under the white plate.

meanings.note: Levantine relational adjective formed from تحت ('under/below') + -aani; opposite of فوقاني.

examples.trans: The tuning wrench is in the bottom drawer.

examples.text: نور مسحت الألواح التحتانية للشباك الكبير.
examples.trans: Nour wiped the lower panes of the tall window.

meanings.note: Preposition with the third-person masculine singular suffix attached.

examples.trans: The box has something under it.

examples.text: ارفعي الدفتر، في خريطة مطوية تحته.
examples.trans: Lift the notebook; there is a folded map underneath it.

meanings.note: Preposition with the third-person feminine singular suffix attached.

examples.trans: The carpet has money under it.

examples.text: الشجرة كبيرة وفي مقعد خشب تحتها.
examples.trans: The tree is big and there is a wooden bench beneath it.

meanings.note: With progressive عم (عم بتتحديني؟), Layan asks 'are you challenging me right now?'.

examples.trans: Nobody challenges her at school.
Are you challenging me?

meanings.note: Describes the action of protecting or guarding a place.

examples.trans: She guards the building at night.

examples.text: القطة قاعدة عند البوابة كأنها بتحرس الحديقة.
examples.trans: The cat is sitting by the gate as if guarding the garden.

meanings.note: Intransitive 'move': ما بتتحرك خطوة بدونهم ('she doesn't move a step without them').

examples.trans: The bus started moving.
Move over a little, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتحرك, بيتحرك).

examples.text: في قطعة معدن تحركت جوا الصندوق!
examples.trans: A piece of metal shifted inside the box!
The car pulled away from the door.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of حضّر ('to prepare'). Plural: تحضيرات.

examples.trans: Coffee prep takes ten minutes.
All preparations for the party are ready.

meanings.note: Everyday praise word for anything beautifully crafted (تحفة فنية 'a work of art'). Plural: تحف.

examples.trans: Your lettering on paper is a work of art!
This old chair is a real treasure.

meanings.note: Construes with بـ or في: بتحكموا فينا ('you boss us around / control us').

examples.trans: I don't like anyone bossing me around.
Try to control your nerves.

meanings.note: Covers enduring mistreatment (يتحمل الظلم) and taking responsibility (نتحمل المسؤولية).

examples.text: ما بقدر أتحمل أكتر من هيك.
examples.trans: I can't put up with more than this.
We must take responsibility.

meanings.note: Form V verb (بيتحمّل / تحمّلت). Used for enduring stress, weight, or a surprise inspection.

examples.text: قلبي ما بيتحمّل تفتيش تاني اليوم!
examples.trans: My heart cannot survive another inspection today!
This brick endures rain and heavy weight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تحويلات.

examples.trans: Converting the building into offices is prohibited.
We read the conversion request in the morning.

meanings.note: Feminine noun from حوّل ('to divert/turn'): a side turn in a road or trail, or a call extension.

examples.text: خد التحويلة اللي على إيدك اليمين.
examples.trans: Take the turnoff on your right-hand side.

examples.text: في تحويلة جديدة على طريق المطار.
examples.trans: There is a new detour on the airport road.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: تحيات.

examples.trans: Here is to all our kind neighbours!
He returned the greeting with a warm smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتخانق, بيتخانق).

examples.trans: We used to argue over the corner piece!
We fell out over selling the old house.

meanings.note: Used for the action of concealing something.

examples.trans: Why are you hiding the truth?

examples.text: حاولت تخبي المفاجأة عن أخوها ليوم العيد.
examples.trans: She tried to hide the surprise from her brother until the feast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتخبى, بيتخبى).

examples.trans: Why did you hide behind a mysterious note?

examples.text: القطة تخبت تحت الطاولة من المطر.
examples.trans: The cat hid under the table from the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for a bed (from Persian takht).

examples.trans: The wooden bed is very comfortable.
I put the clean sheet on the bed.

meanings.note: Often used to refer to dough rising due to yeast.

examples.trans: The dough fermented and became ready for baking.

examples.text: تركنا العجينة ساعة كاملة عشان تخمر منيح.
examples.trans: We left the dough a full hour so it would rise well.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتخيل, بيتخيل).

examples.trans: Imagine how the whole story started!
I never imagined finding the train here.

meanings.note: Form V verb تدرّب (to practise/rehearse), pairing with على before the thing practised.

examples.text: الفرقة عم تتدرّب عالأغنية الجديدة كل يوم المسا.
examples.trans: The band is rehearsing the new song every evening.

examples.text: تدرّبت على العزف ساعة كاملة قبل الامتحان.
examples.trans: I practiced playing for a full hour before the exam.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: The heating is working in all the rooms.
The heating pipe is warm now.

meanings.note: Masculine noun for a memento or keepsake (plural: تذكارات). From the same root as تذكّر ('remember').

examples.text: كل واحد حط تذكار صغير بالعلبة.
examples.trans: Everyone put one small keepsake in the tin.

examples.text: هاي الخريطة أحلى تذكار من أستاذنا.
examples.trans: This map is the loveliest keepsake from our teacher.

meanings.note: Train, bus, or concert ticket.

examples.text: حجزت تذكرة قطار ليوم السبت الصبح.
examples.trans: I booked a train ticket for Saturday morning.

examples.text: حطيت التذاكر بجيبتي عشان ما تضيع.
examples.trans: I put the tickets in my pocket so they wouldn't get lost.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتذكر, بيتذكر).

examples.trans: Remember your three simple sentences.
I can remember them easily.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of Form V تذوق.

examples.text: اليوم عندنا تذوق لتلات كيكات مختلفة.
examples.trans: Today we have a tasting of three different cakes.

examples.text: التذوق المضبوط محتاج كاسة مي وشاي.
examples.trans: A proper tasting needs a glass of water and tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Heritage law protects old houses.
Amman has beautiful architectural heritage.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تراثية, plural: تراثيين).

examples.trans: He works on restoring heritage buildings in Amman.

examples.text: هاد بيت تراثي عمره تمانين سنة.
examples.trans: This is a historic house eighty years old.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of رتّب ('to tidy, arrange'); بترتيب means 'neatly, in neat order'.

examples.trans: We lined the chairs up neatly beside the wall.

examples.text: ترتيب الطاولات بالساحة ما أخد عشر دقايق.
examples.trans: Arranging the tables in the courtyard did not take ten minutes.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of رحّب (to welcome), central to Jordanian hospitality.

examples.text: أهل البيت استقبلونا بترحيب حار وضيافة بتشرح القلب.
examples.trans: The hosts received us with a warm welcome and heartwarming hospitality.

examples.text: كلمة الترحيب بالبداية كانت قصيرة ولطيفة.
examples.trans: The welcoming speech at the start was short and lovely.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from ترحيب ('welcoming'). Feminine: ترحيبية (لوحة ترحيبية 'welcome sign').

examples.text: كتبنا لوحة ترحيبية للضيف قبل ما يوصل.
examples.trans: We wrote a welcome sign for the guest before he arrived.
A welcoming smile is the most important thing at the front desk.

meanings.note: Form V verb meaning 'be promoted to a higher post or role'.

examples.text: نور ترقت وصارت موظفة استقبال رسمية.
examples.trans: Nour got promoted to permanent receptionist.
We got promoted today to café taste testers!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بترك, بيترك).

examples.text: مين ترك هاد المغلف جنب الجرس؟
examples.trans: Who left this envelope by the bell?
Thank you for not leaving me in the rain.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of رمّم, standard term for architectural restoration of heritage buildings.

examples.text: ترميم البيوت التراثية بجبل عمان أخد شهور طويلة.
examples.trans: Restoring the heritage houses in Jabal Amman took many months.

examples.text: المتحف مسكّر هاد الشهر عشان أعمال الترميم.
examples.trans: The museum is closed this month for restoration work.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for waiting for someone or something.

examples.trans: You must wait your turn in line.

examples.text: لازم تستنى شوي قبل ما تقطع الكيكة السخنة.
examples.trans: You have to wait a little before slicing the hot cake.

meanings.note: The number 9.

examples.trans: I have nine books on the shelf.

examples.text: الساعة تسعة الصبح رح نلتقي عند النافورة.
examples.trans: At nine in the morning we will meet by the fountain.

meanings.note: Colloquial Jordanian numeral for 19 (also تسعطعشر before singular nouns).

examples.text: عدينا تسعطعش خطوة لحد زاوية الحيط.
examples.trans: We counted nineteen steps up to the corner of the wall.
He is nineteen years old and works at the bakery.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'nineteen' before a counted noun.

examples.trans: I wrote nineteen reasons on the sheet!
He is nineteen years old.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتشرف, بيتشرف).

examples.trans: Lovely to meet you, Salma!
I am honoured to have met you all.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of Form II شطّب; used for interior finishing and culinary final touches.

examples.text: دهنة العسل هي أحلى تشطيب للكيكة.
examples.trans: A honey glaze is the nicest finish for the cake.

examples.text: خلصوا تشطيب الشقة قبل نهاية الشهر.
examples.trans: They finished the apartment's finishing work before month's end.

meanings.note: Colloquial Form II verbal noun coined from Arabicized شيّك ('to check', from English). Used for quick safety or list checks.

examples.text: نعمل تشييك سريع عالأغراض قبل ما نطلع.
examples.trans: Let's do a quick check on the things before we head out.

examples.text: تشييك الكهربا أخد خمس دقايق بس.
examples.trans: The electrical check took only five minutes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتصالح, بيتصالح).

examples.trans: Thank goodness the two brothers finally made peace!
We reconciled and drank tea together.

meanings.note: Used with manner phrases like بشكل طبيعي ('in a normal way') or بطبيعتك ('naturally').

examples.trans: I acted calmly in front of everyone.
Act naturally.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun from صلّح ('to repair'). Plural تصليحات refers to repair jobs.

examples.text: السكة محتاجة تصليح بسيط قبل الظهر.
examples.trans: The track needs a small repair before noon.
We took the radio to the repair shop.

meanings.note: Standard Arabic noun for 'design', derived from صمّم ('to design').

examples.text: تصميم القاعة الجديدة بيدمج بين الحجر القديم والخشب.
examples.trans: The design of the new hall blends old stone with wood.

examples.text: أختي بتشتغل بمجال التصميم الداخلي بعمان.
examples.trans: My sister works in interior design in Amman.

meanings.note: Used to say stay, remain, or keep doing something.

examples.trans: You must stay here and not move.

examples.text: حطينا العلبة بالظل عشان تضل المكونات باردة.
examples.trans: We put the tin in the shade so the ingredients stay cool.

meanings.note: Core Levantine verb for 'look (at)' taking على or في.

examples.text: تطلعي من الشباك شوفي لون الشيش الأخضر!
examples.trans: Look out the window and see the green colour of the shutters!

examples.text: ليش بتطلعوا علي هيك؟ هلا بمسح الدهان!
examples.trans: Why are you staring at me like that? I'll wipe the paint right now!

meanings.note: Refers to moving upwards, outside, or appearing.

examples.trans: I want you (pl.) to go outside.

examples.text: قبل ما تطلعوا عالبلكونة تأكدوا من المفتاح.
examples.trans: Before you all go out onto the balcony check the key.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تطورات.

examples.trans: That is excellent progress at work.
We heard the latest developments in the morning.

meanings.note: An imperative-only word: تعال to a man, تعالي to a woman, تعالوا to a group. Other tenses use إجا.

examples.trans: Come and sit next to me.
Come to the kitchen, all of you!

meanings.note: Imperative command telling a group of people to come over.

examples.trans: Come, let's visit my grandfather's house.

examples.text: تعالوا شوفوا شو لقينا ورا الكتاب القديم!
examples.trans: Come look at what we found behind the old book!

meanings.note: Universal everyday Jordanian adjective for 'tired' (feminine: تعبانة, plural: تعبانين).

examples.text: أنا تعبان شوي من رحلة الباص الطويلة.
examples.trans: I am a little tired from the long bus trip.

examples.text: صوتي تعبان اليوم، بس قلبي فرحان.
examples.trans: My voice is tired today, but my heart is glad.

meanings.note: Past tense Levantine Arabic verb meaning 'to get filled up'.

examples.text: المكان تعبّى ناس قبل ما يبلش العرض بنص ساعة.
examples.trans: The place filled up with people half an hour before the show started.

examples.text: الخزان تعبّى مي عالآخر والحمد لله.
examples.trans: The water tank filled all the way up, thank goodness.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تعديلات.

examples.trans: The old wire needs a small adjustment.
We made a small adjustment to the schedule.

meanings.note: Wooden or iron garden trellis supporting climbing jasmine, grapevines, or ivy.

examples.text: رفعنا عرق اللبلاب شوي شوي عالتعريشة.
examples.trans: We lifted the ivy vine gently onto the trellis.

examples.text: القعدة تحت تعريشة الياسمين بالصيف بترد الروح.
examples.trans: Sitting under the jasmine trellis in summer refreshes the soul.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتعرف, بيتعرف).

examples.text: هادي كانت خطتي قبل ما أتعرف عليكم.
examples.trans: That was my plan before I got to know you all.
We met kind neighbours in the quarter.

meanings.note: Feminine noun from علّق ('to hang'): a wall peg, hook, or hanging tag.

examples.text: المفتاح معلق على أول تعليقة جنب الباب.
examples.trans: The key is hanging on the first hook beside the door.
Put the apron on the hook once you finish.

meanings.note: Plural تعليمات (f. pl.) means instructions.

examples.trans: Follow the baking instructions written on the card.
The teaching at this school is very good.

meanings.note: Form V passive/intransitive counterpart to علّق ('to hang something up').

examples.trans: The lantern will hang above the door.
The sign was hung in the hall.

meanings.note: Form V reflexive of علّم ('to teach').

examples.text: نور بتتعلم شغل الاستقبال بسرعة كبيرة.
examples.trans: Nour is learning the front-desk work very quickly.
I learned to play the piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of عيّن ('to appoint, hire to a post').

examples.text: فرحنا كتير بخبر تعيين نور بالنزل.
examples.trans: We were delighted at the news of Nour's permanent appointment at the inn.
The manager signed the appointment letter in the morning.

meanings.note: Form V defective verb from غداء ('lunch'). Past uses -ee- before consonant endings (تغديت).

examples.trans: We are going to have lunch in the garden under the tree.
Did you have lunch or are you still waiting for Tariq?

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of غلّف ('to wrap/package'). ورق تغليف means 'wrapping paper'.

examples.text: فكينا ورق التغليف البني عن اللوحة.
examples.trans: We removed the brown wrapping paper from the painting.
Good wrapping keeps cake fresh.
