meanings.note: Form V intransitive counterpart to غيّر ('to change something').

examples.trans: The appointment changed a moment ago.
The weather changes quickly in spring.

meanings.note: Expresses being caught off guard (بدل ما أتفاجأ هيك 'instead of being surprised like this').

examples.trans: I was surprised when I saw you here.
Don't be surprised by the news.

meanings.note: Collective تفاح ('apples'), singulative تفاحة ('an apple').

examples.trans: I bought red apples from the shop.
Apple jam is delicious at breakfast.

meanings.note: Action of opening a door, book, or shop.

examples.trans: Can you open the window a little bit?

examples.text: استنينا البوابة تفتح عشان ندخل الساحة.
examples.trans: We waited for the gate to open so we could enter the courtyard.

meanings.note: Action of a group of people opening something.

examples.trans: Do not open the door for a stranger.

examples.text: قبل ما تفتحوا الصندوق اقراوا التعليمات منيح.
examples.trans: Before you open the chest, read the instructions carefully.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of فتّش ('to inspect, check officially').

examples.text: لجنة التفتيش من البلدية جاية يوم الأربعا.
examples.trans: The inspection team from City Hall is coming on Wednesday.
The whole kitchen is clean and ready for inspection.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتفرج, بيتفرج).

examples.trans: Nobody gawks at the guests here!

examples.text: كنت ناوي تتفرج من الشارع المقابل؟
examples.trans: Were you planning to watch from across the street?

meanings.note: Used as a polite offering, invitation to enter, or handing something to a female.

examples.trans: Here you go, the coffee is ready.

examples.text: تفضلي كاسة شاي بالنعناع يا خالتي.
examples.trans: Please have a glass of mint tea, auntie.

تفضّل.gloss: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are

meanings.en: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are
meanings.note: Essential Jordanian hospitality verb used mostly in the imperative: تفضل (to a man), تفضلي (to a woman), تفضلوا (plural).

examples.trans: Please have a seat, ma'am!
Here you go, hot mint tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتفقد, بيتفقد).

examples.text: أنا بس بتفقد الطقس من الشباك!
examples.trans: I am just checking the weather from the window!
Tariq checked on the heater in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Quick thinking solved the problem.
That is smart, logical thinking.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Add the green mint right before serving.
The presentation is neat and lovely.

meanings.note: Form V verb; passive/reflexive of قدّم ('serve food/drink').

examples.text: الشوربة السخنة بتتقدم مع خبز محمص.
examples.trans: The hot soup is served with toasted bread.

examples.text: قهوة الصبح بتتقدم بالساحة الساعة تمانية.
examples.trans: Morning coffee is served in the courtyard at eight.

meanings.note: Adverbial accusative of تقريب (approximation).

examples.text: صارت الساعة الضهر تقريبا، خلينا نرتاح.
examples.trans: It is almost noon now, let us take a rest.

examples.text: الكيكة جاهزة تقريبا، ضايل لها خمس دقايق.
examples.trans: The cake is almost ready; five minutes are left.

meanings.note: Everyday masculine noun for a written or official report (تقرير التراث 'the heritage report'). Plural: تقارير.

examples.text: تقرير البلدية مدح ساحتنا يوم الأربعا.
examples.trans: The city report praised our courtyard on Wednesday.

examples.text: كتبت تقرير مختصر عن حالة المبنى.
examples.trans: I wrote a brief report on the condition of the building.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of قسم; تقسيم الغرف refers to the school-trip room assignments.

examples.trans: I didn't like the group assignments.
The room assignment list is ready.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of قطّع (to chop into pieces); لوح تقطيع is a cutting board.

examples.text: تقطيع البندورة والخيار بياخد عشر دقايق بس.
examples.trans: Chopping the tomatoes and cucumbers only takes ten minutes.

examples.text: لوح التقطيع الخشبي محطوط جنب المجلى.
examples.trans: The wooden cutting board is placed next to the sink.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تقيلة, plural: تقال).

examples.trans: This suitcase is very heavy today.
Take off your heavy coat and sit down to rest.

meanings.note: Used to describe a heavy object or a burdensome person.

examples.trans: This bag is very heavy for me.

examples.text: الصينية الحديد تقيلة كتير لما تكون مليانة.
examples.trans: The iron tray is very heavy when it is full.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تقييمات.

examples.trans: The guests wrote an excellent review.
We read all the reviews on the page.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian Form II verb from تقيل ('heavy'), matching Classical ثقّل.

examples.trans: Do not weigh the basket down with items.
Water weighs cloth down a lot.

meanings.note: The number 3 when followed by a counted noun.

examples.trans: I have three cars in the garage.

examples.text: مشينا تلات دقايق وبعدين وصلنا عالبوابة.
examples.trans: We walked three minutes and then reached the gate.

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Count to ten: one, two, three.

examples.text: رتبنا الصحون واحد تنين تلاتة عالطاولة.
examples.trans: We lined up the plates one, two, three on the table.

meanings.note: The number 30.

examples.trans: His age is now thirty years.

examples.text: ضلينا تلاتين دقيقة بنستنى الكيكة تبرد.
examples.trans: We spent thirty minutes waiting for the cake to cool.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: تلاجات.

examples.trans: The cold milk is inside the fridge.
Open the fridge and check the butter.

meanings.note: Small hill (plural تلال tilaal); familiar across hilly Amman.

examples.text: عمان مبنية على تلال حلوة بتطل عالسما.
examples.trans: Amman is built across lovely hills looking out at the sky.

examples.text: لما نقسم الشغل الكبير لتلال صغيرة بصير سهل.
examples.trans: When we break a big job into small hills, it becomes easy.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian construct numeral for 'three' before plural nouns (تلت بيضات 'three eggs'), and also 'one third' (ساعة وتلت 'twenty past').

examples.trans: The recipe needs three large eggs.
It is twenty past three right now.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تلوج.

examples.trans: The water is cold as ice.
Snow fell on the hills of Amman.

تلخبط.gloss: to get mixed up; get confused

meanings.en: to get mixed up; get confused
meanings.note: Colloquial quadriliteral reflexive verb meaning to become jumbled, tangled, or confused.

examples.text: تلخبطت الأوراق لما فات الهوا من الشباك.
examples.trans: The papers got mixed up when the wind came through the window.

examples.text: ما تتلخبط بالأرقام، اكتبها وحدة وحدة.
examples.trans: Don't get confused with the numbers—write them down one by one.

meanings.note: Noun of instance (ism marra) from لطّخ (to smudge).

examples.text: في تلطيخة حبر أزرق عالسطر التحتاني.
examples.trans: There is a blue ink smudge on the bottom line.
The smear of honey on the table sticks to your hand.

meanings.note: Spoken contraction of على التلفون ('on the telephone').

examples.text: رنّ عليّ التلفون وأنا بالطريق عالشغل.
examples.trans: My phone rang while I was on the way to work.

examples.text: حكيت مع خالتي عالتلفون واتفقنا نتلاقى العصر.
examples.trans: I talked to my aunt on the phone and we agreed to meet in the afternoon.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of لمّع ('to polish wood, brass, or shoes').

examples.text: بقي بس تلميع دواسات النحاس بقماشة ناعمة.
examples.trans: All that's left is polishing the brass pedals with a soft cloth.

examples.text: بعد التلميع رجع خشب الجوز يلمع زي المراية.
examples.trans: After polishing, the walnut wood shone like a mirror again.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تليفونات.

examples.trans: The phone rang on the reception desk.
I wrote the phone number in the notebook.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for mouth, or the pouring spout of a pitcher/teapot.

examples.trans: The pitcher's spout is a little wide.
He laughed wholeheartedly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian all-purpose word for 'all set, fine, spot-on!'.

examples.trans: Everything has to be spot-on!
Alright, I can remember the sentences.

meanings.note: Used to emphasize absolute completion or exactness.

examples.trans: I agree with you completely.

examples.text: النتيجة طلعت متل ما توقعنا تماما.
examples.trans: The result turned out exactly as we expected.

meanings.note: Adverbial form of تمام meaning 'precisely' or 'completely'.

examples.text: البيت طلع متل ما تخيلناه تماماً!
examples.trans: The house turned out exactly as we imagined it!

examples.text: فهمت قصدك تماماً، ما في داعي تشرح أكتر.
examples.trans: I understood what you mean completely; there's no need to explain more.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eighty'.

examples.text: خشب بلوط أصلي عمره تمانين سنة.
examples.trans: Solid oak wood eighty years old.
This house has lived through eighty winters!

meanings.en: to sway back and forth gently
meanings.note: Form VI verb from مال ('to lean / tilt'), expressing gentle rhythmic swaying.

examples.trans: The branches sway with the breeze.
The lanterns are swaying calmly.

meanings.note: Form V verb taking على for practicing music or a craft.

examples.trans: Can I practice the whole song on the piano?

examples.text: مدام سعاد تمرنت ساعة كاملة قبل شاي المساء.
examples.trans: Madam Suad practiced for a full hour before evening tea.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of مرّن ('to train / practice'). Plural: تمارين.

examples.trans: We have piano rehearsal at four o'clock.
This exercise is easy and useful.

meanings.note: Followed directly by a subjunctive verb without أن in spoken Arabic (بتتمنى تكون 'wishes to be').

examples.trans: I hope we'll be in the same class.
Every girl wishes to succeed.

meanings.note: Colloquial Jordanian form of ثمانية with interdental th > t shift.

examples.text: رسام الخرايط ساكن بغرفة رقم تمنية.
examples.trans: The mapmaker lives in Room Number Eight.
The party starts at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتمنى, بيتمنى).

examples.trans: We hope every guest feels comfortable with us.
We wished them a happy trip.

meanings.note: Formal administrative verb تمّ used with verbal nouns like الموافقة to mean 'approved!'.

examples.text: الحمد لله تمّ توقيع العقد اليوم الصبح.
examples.trans: Thankfully the contract was signed this morning.

examples.text: تمّت الموافقة على المشروع بعد المراجعة.
examples.trans: Approval for the project was granted after the review.

meanings.en: harmony; moving or sounding in unison
meanings.note: Built from نغمة ('musical note / tone'). Used for music, colours, or coordinated motion.

examples.trans: The lanterns move in lovely harmony.
There is clear harmony in the playing.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun from نبّه ('to alert/warn'). Used for announcements, reminders, and warning signs.

examples.text: شكرا عالتنبيه، لحقنا نرتب كل شي.
examples.trans: Thanks for the notice—we managed to sort everything out.

examples.text: حطوا ورقة تنبيه على باب المطبخ.
examples.trans: They put a reminder notice on the kitchen door.

meanings.note: Form V verb from نفس ('breath').

examples.text: فتحت الشباك عشان أتنفس هوا نضيف.
examples.trans: I opened the window to breathe fresh air.

examples.text: بعد ما رتبنا القائمة، قدرت أتنفس براحة.
examples.trans: Once we organized the list, I could breathe easily.

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.trans: I only want two pieces, two are enough.

examples.text: جبنا كتابين تنين من رف الإعارة.
examples.trans: We brought two books from the lending shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: توائم.

examples.trans: The two suitcases are just like twins.
His twin brother lives next to him.

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for berries/mulberries (singulative توتة 'one berry').

examples.trans: The berry and almond cake turned out delicious!
We have an old mulberry tree in the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتوتر, بيتوتر).

examples.trans: When I get nervous, my sentences turn long!

examples.text: لا تتوتر، كل شي رح يمشي تمام.
examples.trans: Do not get nervous, everything will go fine.

meanings.note: Loanword from English, for toasted sliced bread.

examples.trans: Do you want toast with the cheese?
The toast burned a little.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of وصّل ('to deliver, drop off; connect wires'); سيارة توصيل means 'delivery van'.

examples.trans: The delivery van pulled up in front of the gate.

examples.text: التوصيل للبيت مجاني إذا طلبنا دزينة.
examples.trans: Home delivery is free if we order a dozen.

meanings.note: Verbal noun from و-ف-ق; بالتوفيق! is the everyday Arabic way to say 'good luck!'.

examples.trans: Good luck in your new job, Nour!
Wish us luck before the municipality visit.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتوفى, بيتوفى).

examples.trans: My grandfather passed away three years ago.

examples.text: ترك ذكرى طيبة بعد ما توفى.
examples.trans: He left warm memories after passing away.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تواقيع.

examples.text: الورقة ما عليها اسم ولا توقيع.
examples.trans: The paper has neither name nor signature.
The postman asked for my signature.

meanings.note: Common Levantine Arabic verb meaning 'to expect', with feminine ending -i.

examples.trans: Do you think it's going to rain tomorrow?

examples.text: ما توقّعت أبداً أشوفك هون اليوم!
examples.trans: I never expected to see you here today!

meanings.note: Affectionate Levantine family word for 'grandmother' (often used directly without a possessive suffix).

examples.text: وصفة شوربة العدس هاي تعلمتها من تيتا.
examples.trans: I learned this lentil soup recipe from my grandma.

examples.text: تيتا دايما بتحط قشر ليمون طازة مع الكيك.
examples.trans: Grandma always puts fresh lemon zest into her cakes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ثابتة, plural: ثابتين).

examples.trans: Hold the torch steady on the pipe.
The flame's color is steady blue.

meanings.note: A unit of time or the feminine ordinal for second.

examples.trans: Wait for me just one second.

examples.text: كل ثانية بالسباق مهمة كتير للفريق.
examples.trans: Every second in the race matters a lot to the team.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بثبت, بيثبت).

examples.trans: Hold still a moment and listen to that sound!

examples.text: الكرسي ثبت بعد ما شدينا البرغي.
examples.trans: The chair held firm once we tightened the screw.

ثبّت.gloss: to fasten; seat firmly; fix in place

meanings.en: to fasten; seat firmly; fix in place
meanings.note: Form II verb meaning 'seat securely / hold steady'.

examples.text: طارق ثبت اللوحة النحاس ببراغي صغار.
examples.trans: Tariq fastened the brass plate with small screws.

examples.text: امسك السلم من تحت وثبته منيح.
examples.trans: Hold the ladder at the bottom and steady it well.

meanings.note: Refers to a large amount of money or resources.

examples.trans: He amassed a large wealth from his work.

examples.text: الجد ساب لهم ثروة من الكتب والخرايط.
examples.trans: Grandfather left them a treasure trove of books and maps.

meanings.note: Used for heavy weight or metaphorically for a dull person.

examples.text: هذا الصندوق ثقيل ما بقدر أرفعه.
examples.trans: This box is heavy, I can't lift it.

examples.text: الحجر المنحوت كان ثقيل على اتنين يشيلوه.
examples.trans: The carved stone was too heavy for two people to lift.

meanings.note: The standard or rural/Bedouin pronunciation of the number 3.

examples.trans: I have three children.

examples.text: اقراوا الأسئلة الثلاثة بتركيز قبل الجواب.
examples.trans: Read the three questions carefully before answering.

meanings.note: The number 30 with the "th" sound preserved.

examples.trans: He paid thirty dinars for the ticket.

examples.text: الدفتر مكتوب قبل ثلاثين سنة تقريبا.
examples.trans: The notebook was written roughly thirty years ago.

meanings.note: The number 8.

examples.trans: The time became eight in the evening.
The lecture begins at eight-thirty.

meanings.note: Colloquial Jordanian numeral for 18 (also تمنطعش).

examples.trans: We walked eighteen paces and then stopped.

examples.text: عنده ثمنطعش كتاب عن النباتات والأعشاب.
examples.trans: He has eighteen books on plants and herbs.

meanings.note: From ثنائي (two-part/duo), used in music for duets.

examples.text: البيانو والعود عملوا ثنائي رائع بالحفلة.
examples.trans: The piano and the oud made a wonderful duet at the concert.

examples.text: عزفوا مقطوعة ثنائية كل الناس صفقولها.
examples.trans: They played a duet piece that everyone applauded for.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجيب, بيجيب).

examples.text: رح أجيب شراشف نظيفة من الخزانة.
examples.trans: I will bring clean sheets from the closet.

examples.text: أي علبة زبدة جبتي يا نور؟
examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring, Nour?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جيران.

examples.trans: All the neighbours on the street are kind.
Good morning, dear neighbour.

meanings.note: Describes dry air, dry ingredients, or seasoned dry timber.

examples.text: خلينا نخلي كل المكونات الجافة عالرف العالي.
examples.trans: Let's keep all the dry ingredients on the upper shelf.

examples.text: المفصل بعد ما تدهنه زيت ما بيعود جاف.
examples.trans: Once you oil the hinge, it won't be dry anymore.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جاكيتات.

examples.trans: The key is in the right jacket pocket.

examples.text: البس جاكيت دافي قبل ما تطلع.
examples.trans: Put on a warm jacket before you go out.

meanings.note: Feminine plural جامدات also appears in Jordanian speech for firm fruit (متل ليمونات جامدات).

examples.text: نقي ليمونات صفر وجامدات عشان تارت الليمون.
examples.trans: Pick firm yellow lemons for the lemon tarts.

examples.text: الكريمة بردت بالبراد وصارت جامدة ومتماسكة.
examples.trans: The curd chilled in the fridge and turned firm and set.

meanings.note: Feminine noun from جمع ('to gather'), standard throughout the Arab world for university.

examples.trans: My sister studies engineering at the University of Jordan.

examples.text: الطلاب راجعين من الجامعة الساعة تلاتة.
examples.trans: The students are coming back from university at three.

meanings.note: Relative adjective (nisba) from جانب ('side'), e.g. الباب الجانبي ('the side door'), القفل الجانبي ('the side latch').

examples.text: افتح الشباك الجانبي عشان يفوت الهوا.
examples.trans: Open the side window so fresh air comes in.

examples.text: في ممر جانبي صغير ورا المطبخ.
examples.trans: There is a small side passage behind the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جاهزة, plural: جاهزين).

examples.trans: The desk is clean and the keys are ready.
Breakfast is ready in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Active participle of إجا ('to come'): means 'on the way / arriving' (جايين 'they are coming') and after a time noun 'next' (الأسبوع الجاي 'next week').

examples.trans: The guests are coming down the stairs now.
We will see you next week!

meanings.note: Active participle of جاب (to bring); Jordanian Arabic prefers participles for ongoing or resultant states.

examples.text: شو جايب معك بالكيس يا زيد؟
examples.trans: What have you got in the bag, Zaid?

examples.text: أمي جايبة كعك بالتمر من عند الجيران.
examples.trans: My mom is bringing date cookies over from the neighbors'.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جبانة, plural: جبناء).

examples.trans: It was a cowardly plan of mine.
Do not be timid, speak honestly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb meaning to bring something. Can also mean 'you (m) brought'.

examples.trans: I brought a gift with me for you.

examples.text: جبت معي مرطبان عسل وزبدة بلدية.
examples.trans: I brought a jar of honey and local butter with me.

meanings.note: Means 'mountain' and also names Amman's historic hilltop quarters (جبل اللويبدة, جبل عمان).

examples.text: الهوا على راس الجبل دايما نضيف ومنعش.
examples.trans: The air on top of the mountain is always clean and crisp.

examples.text: بيت الياسمين قريب من درج الجبل القديم.
examples.trans: Jasmine Courtyard House is near the old Jabal stairway.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from جبل ('mountain'); عسل جبلي ('mountain honey') is dark, aromatic wildflower honey.

examples.text: العسل الجبلي لونه غامق وطعمه غني.
examples.trans: Mountain honey has a dark colour and a rich taste.
The mountain air in Amman cools down at night.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: أجبان.

examples.trans: White cheese is tasty with mint.
We bought cheese and olives for breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أجبنة.

examples.trans: Your glasses are pushed up on your forehead!
He wiped the rain off his forehead.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian expression to express surprise or ask for confirmation, like 'really?' or 'seriously!'.

examples.trans: Are you talking seriously?

examples.text: جد؟ لقيتوا المفتاح الضاع جوا المطبخ؟
examples.trans: Seriously? Did you find the lost key inside the kitchen?

meanings.note: Feminine counterpart of جد (grandfather); plural جدات.

examples.text: جداتنا كانوا يخبزوا بعسل وزبدة بلدية.
examples.trans: Our grandmothers used to bake with honey and local butter.

examples.text: رح نزور جدتي يوم الجمعة بعد الغدا.
examples.trans: We will visit my grandmother on Friday after lunch.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جداول.

examples.trans: I read the bus timetable at the station.
The week's schedule is neat and clear.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جديدة, plural: جداد).

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I installed a new lightbulb last week.

meanings.note: Standard noun used in Jordanian for tree trunks and stems.

examples.text: في حلقة حديد معلقة على جذع الشجرة.
examples.trans: There is an iron ring hanging on the tree trunk.

examples.text: جذع شجرة البلوط قديم وعريض كتير.
examples.trans: The trunk of the oak tree is very old and wide.

meanings.note: Imperative form of 'try' addressed to a single female.

examples.trans: Try this food, it's very delicious.

examples.text: جربي قطعة من الكيكة التانية مع الشاي.
examples.trans: Try a piece of the second cake with tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أجراس.

examples.trans: The gate bell rang twice.
Listen to the sound of the bell in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جريئة, plural: جريئين).

examples.text: الأخ الكبير كان جريء وصوته عالي.
examples.trans: The older brother was bold and loud-voiced.
A bold and excellent idea!

meanings.note: Everyday word for a newspaper; broken plural in spoken Levantine is جرايد (jaraayid).

examples.text: عمي بيقرا الجريدة مع فنجان قهوة كل صبح.
examples.trans: My uncle reads the newspaper with a cup of coffee every morning.

examples.text: لف البياع الصحون بورق جرايد قديم.
examples.trans: The seller wrapped the plates in old newspaper.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجرب, بيجرب).

examples.trans: This sweater is clean and new — try it on.
We tried the new recipe and it turned out delicious.

meanings.note: Standard word used in Jordanian Arabic for a part, portion, or section of something.

examples.trans: This is part of the problem.

examples.text: كل جزء من الخريطة مرسوم بدقة عجيبة.
examples.trans: Each part of the map is drawn with remarkable precision.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a wallet or handbag/purse.

examples.text: خدي جزدانك يا نور وانزلي عالدكانة.
examples.trans: Grab your purse, Nour, and run down to the shop.
I left my wallet on the table by the door.

meanings.note: Collective noun جزر ('carrots') with singulative جزرة ('one carrot').

examples.text: فرمنا الجزر والبصل لمكعبات صغيرة ومتساوية.
examples.trans: We diced the carrots and onions into small, even cubes.

examples.text: الجزر المشوي بيعطي الشوربة حلاوة طبيعية.
examples.trans: Roasted carrots give the soup a natural sweetness.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جسور.

examples.trans: Cross the overpass toward downtown.
The old shop is past the overpass.

meanings.note: Verbal/abstract noun from جف ('become dry').

examples.text: الخشب بالبيانو بيحب جو معتدل ومش رطوبة شديدة.
examples.trans: Piano wood likes moderate air rather than extreme dampness or dryness.

examples.text: جفاف الهوا بعمان بيساعد الدهان ينشف بسرعة.
examples.trans: The dryness of Amman's air helps the paint dry fast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جلود.

examples.trans: This is a small brown leather notebook.
The leather bag is heavy and sturdy.

meanings.note: Craftsman's term for a small protective felt, rubber, or leather ring/bushing inside hardware or instruments.

examples.text: غيرنا جلدة اللباد الصغيرة تحت المفتاح فاختفت الطقة.
examples.trans: We replaced the tiny felt bushing under the key and the click vanished.

examples.text: شديت الصامولة بعد ما ركبت جلدة جديدة.
examples.trans: I tightened the nut after fitting a new washer.

meanings.note: Used to address a group of people informally, like 'guys' or 'folks' ('ya jamaa'a').

examples.trans: Hey guys, let's go.

examples.text: يا جماعة الخير، التذوق رح يبلش هلق.
examples.trans: Everyone, the tasting is about to begin right now.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Look at the beauty of the wooden ceiling!
The beauty of old stone rests the eye.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجمع, بيجمع).

examples.trans: Today our courtyard brings a family together!
We gathered the chairs under the tree.

meanings.note: Day of the week Friday, literally 'gathering day'.

examples.text: كل جمعة بنجتمع عند تيتا على الغدا.
examples.trans: Every Friday we gather at Grandma's for lunch.

examples.text: الجمعة الجاية رح نطلع رحلة ععجلون.
examples.trans: Next Friday we're going on a trip to Ajloun.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: جمل.

examples.trans: Start with three short, simple sentences.
Write this sentence in the notebook.

meanings.note: Commonly used preposition for indicating proximity, next to, or beside.

examples.trans: Sit next to your brother.
We set the trays next to the fountain in the shade.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The guests arrived from the south in the morning.
The weather is warm in the south today.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of جنّ; often used hyperbolically in speech for something absurd or crazy.

examples.text: نترك الكيكة تبرد واحنا بنشم ورق؟ هادا جنون!
examples.trans: Leave the cake to cool while we smell paper? That is madness!

examples.text: السواقة بهالزحمة بدون صبر جنون رسمي.
examples.trans: Driving in this traffic without patience is pure madness.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for a garden or yard; a small one is a جنينة, the formal word is حديقة.

examples.trans: We have a small garden behind the house.
The children are playing in the garden.

جنّن.gloss: to amaze; drive wild; look or taste wonderful

meanings.en: to amaze; drive wild; look or taste wonderful
meanings.note: Form II geminate verb. In Levantine speech, بيجنن ('it drives one crazy') is one of the warmest compliments for food, music, or places.

examples.trans: The smell of pastries from the morning is amazing!

examples.text: العزف اليوم جنن كل اللي قاعدين.
examples.trans: Today's playing amazed everyone sitting there.

meanings.note: Used with right and left: الجهة اليمين 'the right side', من هاي الجهة 'from this side'.

examples.trans: The kitchen is on the other side.
Walk this way, it is closer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجهز, بيجهز).

examples.trans: We prepared the quiet attic room for you.
Salma got breakfast ready early.

meanings.note: Refers to both weather and the emotional vibe of a room (ألطف الجو 'lighten the mood').

examples.trans: The mood is a bit tense today.
The weather is nice in the courtyard.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine Arabic word for 'inside' or 'inwards'.

examples.trans: Go inside the house, the weather is cold.
The metal tin is hidden inside the cupboard.

meanings.note: Everyday masculine noun for an answer or musical response (plural: أجوبة).

examples.trans: A breath first and a second answer on the key.
We are waiting for an answer from City Hall tomorrow.

meanings.note: Collective noun for walnuts; خشب جوز is walnut wood. (Not to be confused with جوز 'husband; pair', a different everyday sense.)

examples.trans: I bought a kilo of walnuts at the market.
The cake has walnuts and honey in it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جوعانة, plural: جوعانين).

examples.trans: Eight hungry guests are coming down to breakfast.
Come eat, you look hungry.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (plural: جيوب). Also homographic with imperative جيب ('bring!') from جاب.

examples.trans: The key is inside the jacket pocket.
I put the small watch in my pocket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: جيب.

examples.trans: Put the key in the coat pocket.
The paper is in my right pocket.

meanings.note: Masculine noun meaning the physical side of an object or person (distinct from the preposition جنب 'beside').

examples.text: امسح جنب الصينية قبل ما تفوتها الفرن.
examples.trans: Wipe the side of the tin before you put it in the oven.

examples.text: قعدت على جنب الطريق أستنى الباص.
examples.trans: I sat on the side of the road waiting for the bus.

meanings.note: Active participle of حب used for polite wishes; with كنت (كنت حابة هيك) it means 'I would have loved that'.

examples.trans: I would have loved to sit with you.
I really like the idea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حواجب.

examples.trans: Why did you knit your eyebrows like that?
He raised his eyebrow in surprise.

meanings.note: Feminine noun for an incident or mishap (حادثة الملصق المبلول 'the soggy poster accident'). Plural: حوادث.

examples.text: حتى حادثة الملصق صارت موضة بالشارع!
examples.trans: Even the poster accident became a street trend!

examples.text: هاي حادثة صغيرة وخلصت على خير.
examples.trans: That was a small mishap and ended well.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: حارات.

examples.trans: The shop is right here in our neighbourhood.
Old Amman neighbourhoods are peaceful.

meanings.note: Form III verb from حساب: رح نحاسبهم ('we will make them answer for what they did').

examples.trans: The principal will hold everyone accountable.
We must hold them accountable for their mistake.

meanings.note: Active participle of حس ('to feel'), used in spoken Jordanian for present state ('I feel').

examples.trans: I feel I will sleep well tonight.

examples.text: حاسس إنه اليوم رح يكون حلو.
examples.trans: I have a feeling today will be lovely.

meanings.note: Active participle of feeling, commonly used to describe a present feeling or intuition about something feminine or a situation.

examples.trans: I feel (it) like it's going to rain today.

examples.text: حاسيتها رح تمطر قبل ما نوصل البيت.
examples.trans: I feel like it is going to rain before we get home.

meanings.note: Active participle of حسّ (to feel); Arabic uses participles for current sensations.

examples.text: حاسة حالي تعبانة شوي بعد المشوار الطويل.
examples.trans: I'm feeling a bit tired after the long walk.

examples.text: حاسّ إنو في إشي حلو رح يصير اليوم.
examples.trans: I have a feeling something nice is going to happen today.

meanings.note: Polite everyday reply meaning 'yes / at your service / right away'.

examples.text: حاضر يا ستي، دقيقتين وبجيبلك كاسة المي.
examples.trans: Right away, ma'am—two minutes and I'll bring you a glass of water.

examples.text: لا تشيل هم، حاضر، بمر عالبنك عنك.
examples.trans: Don't worry—consider it done, I'll stop by the bank for you.

meanings.note: Active participle of حط ('to put, place').

examples.trans: Mazen has put old boxes on the stairs.
What have you packed inside this suitcase?

meanings.note: Feminine noun for the rim of a tin or the edge of a paving stone (الحافة الشمالية 'the north edge'). Plural: حواف.

examples.trans: We wrapped white tape around the rim of the tin.
Lower the north edge first gently.

meanings.note: With possessive endings, حال acts as 'myself/yourself/itself' (لحاله by itself, لا تغلبي حالك don't tire yourself).

examples.trans: The door opened by itself from the wind.
How are you doing today?

meanings.note: Commonly used in expressions like حالة طوارئ (emergency).

examples.text: عسل المونة خلص، وهاي حالة طوارئ بالمطبخ!
examples.trans: The pantry honey ran out, and this is a kitchen emergency!

examples.text: حالة الطقس بكرة رح تكون دافية وصافية.
examples.trans: Tomorrow's weather condition will be warm and clear.

meanings.note: Adverb 'at the moment, for now'.

examples.trans: For now, the suitcase is safe and sound in the closet.
Currently the tables serve the inn's guests.

meanings.note: Describes citrus, yogurt, or tart flavours.

examples.text: كريمة الليمون طلعت حامضة زيادة عن اللزوم.
examples.trans: The lemon icing turned out too sour.

examples.text: التوت الأخضر بعده حامض قبل ما يستوي.
examples.trans: Green berries are still tart before they ripen.

meanings.note: From ح-م-ل ('to carry, hold'); names a music stand (حامل النوتة) or lamp/book holder.

examples.text: حطينا الورقة على حامل النوتة الخشب.
examples.trans: We set the sheet on the wooden music stand.

examples.text: حامل المفاتيح معلق ورا مكتب الاستقبال.
examples.trans: The key rack hangs behind the reception desk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحاول, بيحاول).

examples.trans: I tried to smile as hard as I could!
We tried to find a quick solution.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحب, بيحب).

examples.trans: I liked working here so much more!
Would you like coffee or black tea?

meanings.note: Everyday counting unit for rolls of bread, fruit, lemons, or pills (خدي حبة take a piece; ست حبات ليمون six lemons).

examples.trans: Take a bread roll while it is hot.
I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Standard Arabic and colloquial term for ink used in pens.

examples.trans: The pen ran out of ink.

examples.text: الحبر الأزرق نشف بسرعة عالورق السميك.
examples.trans: The blue ink dried quickly on the thick paper.

meanings.note: Form I verb (بحبس / حبس). Used literally for confining or playfully when rain traps someone indoors.

examples.text: أسبوع شتا حبس المسافر بغرفة تمانية.
examples.trans: A rainy week trapped the traveller in Room Eight.

examples.text: المطر حبسنا جوا القاعة طول الصبح.
examples.trans: The rain kept us inside the hall all morning.

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural حبال (hibaal).

examples.trans: Pull the rope tight on the tree.
We tied the lanterns with a sturdy cord.

meanings.note: Used warmly across ages in Jordan: يا حبيبي (to a boy/man, or as 'my goodness!') and يا حبيبتي (to a girl/woman).

examples.trans: Good morning, my dear.
A warm welcome to dear friends.

meanings.note: Seems to be a typo or portmanteau of 'habibti fi' (my love/dear in). Often used as a term of endearment.

examples.trans: My love is in the house.

examples.text: حبيبتي في المطبخ عم تجهز العسل واللوز.
examples.trans: My dear is in the kitchen preparing the honey and almonds.

meanings.note: Polite offer opener بتحب ('would you like to...?'), from حبّ (to love/like).

examples.text: بتحب تجرب قطعة من الكعك السخن؟
examples.trans: Would you like to try a piece of the warm cake?

examples.text: أختي بتحب تقرأ روايات بالبلكونة العصر.
examples.trans: My sister loves reading novels on the balcony in the afternoon.

meanings.note: Used to mean 'even' (e.g., even he went) or 'until' (e.g., until tomorrow).

examples.text: ما أكلت ولا إشي، حتى تفاحة.
examples.trans: I didn't eat anything, not even an apple.

examples.text: ما فتحنا الصندوق حتى قرأنا كل البطاقات.
examples.trans: We did not open the box until we read all the cards.

meanings.note: Plural of stone, widely used in rural and urban Jordanian contexts for rocks or building stones.

examples.trans: The boy is throwing stones at the trees.

examples.text: بنينا سور صغير من حجار بيضا وحمرا.
examples.trans: We built a low wall from white and red stones.

meanings.note: Standard word for a stone or rock, singular form.

examples.trans: We found a strange stone in the garden.

examples.text: لقينا حجر منحوت عليه نجمة صغيرة.
examples.trans: We found a stone with a small star carved on it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: حجرية, plural: حجريين).

examples.trans: Go down the stone stairs to downtown.
She stood beside the stone fountain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حجوزات.

examples.trans: I have a booking for a double room.
I read the booking ledger in the morning.

meanings.note: Can mean 'border' or 'limit'. Can also be a shortened form of 'hada' meaning 'someone'.

examples.trans: Everything has a limit.

examples.text: وقفنا عند حد الحديقة قبل الزقاق.
examples.trans: We stopped at the boundary of the garden before the alley.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine colloquial word for 'someone' or 'anyone' (in negative sentences).

examples.trans: Is anyone here?

examples.text: في حدا بعرف وين نحفظت الخريطة؟
examples.trans: Does anyone know where the map was stored?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eleven' (حدعش وتلت 'twenty past eleven').

examples.trans: It is twenty past eleven now.
We counted ten, eleven, twelve.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: حديثة, plural: حديثين).

examples.trans: We installed a modern hot-water system.
The building is old, yet the service is modern.

meanings.note: The metal iron. Used commonly in construction contexts or metaphorically for strength.

examples.trans: This door is made of iron.

examples.text: قفل البوابة مصنوع من حديد قديم وتقيل.
examples.trans: The gate lock is made of old, heavy iron.

meanings.note: Standard and Jordanian feminine noun for a public park or walled garden (حدائق 'parks').

examples.trans: The park bench is painted beside the arch.

examples.text: بنتمشى بالحديقة كل يوم جمعة العصر.
examples.trans: We walk in the park every Friday afternoon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أحذية.

examples.trans: Take off your shoes by the door.
Inside the bag are two pairs of men's shoes.

meanings.note: Feminine noun sharing its root with حذاء ('shoe'). Plural: حذوات.

examples.trans: An iron horseshoe is very heavy.

examples.text: علقوا حذوة قديمة فوق باب الورشة.
examples.trans: They hung an old horseshoe above the workshop door.

meanings.note: From ح-ر-ر ('hot, warm'); describes warmth retained by clay cups or weather temperature.

examples.text: الفخار السميك بيحفظ حرارة الشاي وقت طويل.
examples.trans: Thick pottery holds the heat of the tea for a long time.
The oven temperature is ideal for morning bread.

meanings.note: In Jordanian household speech, حرام (plural حرامات) is the everyday word for a warm bed blanket.

examples.trans: I have a warm wool blanket on the bed.
We brought clean blankets from the closet.

meanings.note: Colloquial noun widely used across Jordanian and Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ليش بتركضي هيك، عم تلحقي حرامي؟
examples.trans: Why are you running like that, are you chasing a thief?

examples.text: الحرامي هرب قبل ما يجي الحارس.
examples.trans: The thief fled before the guard arrived.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حروف.

examples.trans: Two small letters are written on the corner.
The letters of her name are clear on the zip.

meanings.note: Feminine noun for an artisanal craft or profession. Plural: حرف (حرف يدوية 'handicrafts').

examples.text: بالمهرجان في طاولات حرف يدوية حلوة.
examples.trans: At the festival there are lovely local craft tables.

examples.text: رسم الخرايط حرفة بدها صبر ودقة.
examples.trans: Mapmaking is a craft that requires patience and precision.

حرق.gloss: to burn; scald; be piping hot

meanings.en: to burn; scald; be piping hot
meanings.note: Form I transitive verb; in everyday speech بتحرق also describes food or pans that are scorching hot.

examples.trans: Careful, the coffee is still hot and will burn!
He forgot the bread in the oven and burnt the edges.

meanings.note: Transitive Form II verb ('move furniture, stir a pot, wiggle toes').

examples.text: حركنا البيانو خطوتين لورا بعيد عن الشباك.
examples.trans: We moved the piano two steps back away from the window.

examples.text: حركي الشوربة بملعقة خشب كل خمس دقايق.
examples.trans: Stir the soup with a wooden spoon every five minutes.

meanings.note: In the plural حركات, often means 'attitude / games / antics' (بطلي حركاتك الباردة).

examples.trans: I don't like these antics.
I noticed every move she made.

meanings.note: Form II verb حرّك means 'to move' or 'to stir' ingredients.

examples.text: حرّك الشوربة منيح عشان ما تلزق بقاع الطنجرة.
examples.trans: Stir the soup well so it doesn't stick to the bottom of the pot.

examples.text: لا تحرّك الطاولة وأنا عم بلزق الورق.
examples.trans: Don't move the table while I'm gluing the paper.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحزر, بيحزر).

examples.trans: Let me guess what happened!
She guessed the answer on the first try.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحس, بيحس).

examples.text: نتمنى كل ضيف يحس بالراحة هون.
examples.trans: We hope every guest feels at home here.
I felt the warmth the moment I walked in.

meanings.note: Also used in the warm hospitality phrase على حسابنا ('on our tab / on the house').

examples.trans: The bill is thirty-eight dinars.
The first coffee today is on the house!

meanings.note: Refers to personal calculations, accounts, or expectations about a situation.

examples.trans: The matter went beyond my calculations.

examples.text: حسب حساباتي، الكيكة بتطلع من الفرن بعد دقيقتين.
examples.trans: According to my calculations, the cake comes out of the oven in two minutes.

meanings.note: Used idiomatically in بحسب إلها ألف حساب ('takes her very seriously / fears crossing her').

examples.trans: We calculated the time exactly.
Count me in with you.

meanings.note: Masculine abstract noun used especially in expressions like لحسن الحظ ('fortunately', literally 'for the goodness of luck').

examples.text: لحسن الحظ لقينا القطار لسه واقف.
examples.trans: Fortunately, we found the train still standing.

examples.text: حسن الضيافة معروف عند أهل البلد.
examples.trans: Goodness of hospitality is well known among the local people.

meanings.note: Form II causative of حس ('to feel'). حسّسني بدفا means 'made me feel warm'.

examples.text: ولا مكان حسّسني بدفا أكتر من هون.
examples.trans: No place ever made me feel warmer than here.
Your kind words made me feel at ease.

meanings.note: Everyday Arabic word for horse. Plural: أحصنة or خيل.

examples.trans: The horse runs fast across the plain.
We drew a small horse on the paper.

meanings.note: Formal honorific title meaning 'Your/Esteemed Presence', used in official speeches.

examples.text: نرحب بحضرة المدير العام وبكل الضيوف الكرام.
examples.trans: We welcome the esteemed General Director and all our honored guests.
Have you (formal) been working in this building for a long time?

meanings.note: Respectful Jordanian way to say 'you' to a guest or elder (hadritak to a man, hadritik to a woman).

examples.trans: You must be Mr. Rami.
Please, what would you like to drink?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحط, بيحط).

examples.trans: Where should I put the spoons and napkins?
I put the suitcase beside the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine verb حطّ ('to put/place').

examples.text: حطّ الأغراض عالمطبخ وتعال اقعد معنا.
examples.trans: Put the groceries in the kitchen and come sit with us.

examples.text: وين حطّيت مفاتيح السيارة مبارح بالليل؟
examples.trans: Where did you put the car keys last night?

meanings.note: Everyday masculine noun (حظ حلو 'good luck'). Plural: حظوظ.

examples.text: دق الحجرة دقة وحدة عشان الحظ الحلو!
examples.trans: Tap the stone once for good luck!

examples.text: من حسن الحظ لقينا المفتاح بدرج المكتب.
examples.trans: By good luck we found the key in the desk drawer.

meanings.note: Used to refer to the edge of a table, cliff, or any physical boundary.

examples.text: دير بالك، الكاسة على حفة الطاولة.
examples.trans: Watch out, the cup is on the edge of the table.

examples.text: لا تحطي الفنجان على حفة الطاولة عشان ما يوقع.
examples.trans: Do not set the cup on the edge of the table so it does not fall.

meanings.note: 'Edge' combined with the third-person masculine possessive pronoun.

examples.trans: Hold its edge well.

examples.text: حفته محززة ومكتوب عليها رقم تمنية.
examples.trans: Its edge is notched and has the number eight written on it.

حفر.gloss: to carve; wear a groove in

meanings.en: to carve; wear a groove in
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحفر, بيحفر).

examples.text: احكي معه قبل ما يحفر خشب الأرضية!
examples.trans: Talk to him before he wears a groove in the floorboards!
My grandfather carved the wooden train by hand.

meanings.note: Past tense verb in the second-person plural, indicating the action of digging.

examples.trans: Where did you (pl) dig the hole?

examples.text: وين حفرتوا تحت شجرة الزيزفون بالزبط؟
examples.trans: Where exactly did you dig under the linden tree?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The suitcase is safe and sound in the closet.
Preserving heritage is everyone's responsibility.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: حفلات.

examples.trans: He designs concert halls.
We attended a lovely music concert.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أحفاد.

examples.trans: The grandfather sat with his grandchildren in the courtyard.
His young grandson loves trains.

meanings.note: Used in معك حق ('you are right / you have a point').

examples.trans: You are right, the weather is cold today.
Everyone has a right to rest.

meanings.note: Form II verb in the past tense. Can mean 'she achieved' or 'I achieved' depending on the vowel.

examples.trans: She finally achieved her dream.

examples.text: سلمى حققت حلمها وفتحت مخبز العسل.
examples.trans: Salma achieved her dream and opened the honey bakery.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: حقائق.

examples.trans: I have to tell you the whole truth.
Honestly, that is the truth.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: حقيقية, plural: حقيقيين).

examples.trans: Did you book the room under your real name?
Let me show you my real work.

meanings.note: Geminate verb meaning both 'itch' (أنفي بيحكني 'my nose itches') and 'scratch/rub'.

examples.text: استنوا لحظة، أنفي بيحكني وإيدي فيها دهان!
examples.trans: Wait a second—my nose itches and my hand has paint on it!

examples.text: مازن حك جبينه بطرف الفرشاية بالغلط.
examples.trans: Mazen scratched his forehead with the tip of the brush by mistake.

meanings.note: Very common Levantine combination of the verb 'haka' (to speak/tell) and the preposition 'la' with a first-person suffix.

examples.trans: My friend told me the story.

examples.text: جدي حكالي قصة الخريطة واحنا صغار.
examples.trans: My grandfather told me the story of the map when we were young.

meanings.note: Used in قبل ما تحكم ('before she judges').

examples.trans: Don't judge people quickly.
Hear the story before you judge.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to speak, talk, tell' (بحكي / حكى).

examples.trans: Salma chats with all the neighbours.
Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Save the formal talk for later.
That is kind, honest talk.

meanings.note: Describes a wise person or a smart, prudent choice (قرار حكيم).

examples.text: الراحة الليلة قرار حكيم عشان تطيب رجلك.
examples.trans: Resting tonight is a wise decision so your foot heals.

examples.text: أبو طارق معروف بالحارة برأيه الهادئ والحكيم.
examples.trans: Abu Tariq is known down the lane for his calm, wise advice.

meanings.note: Geminate Form I verb; used for solving problems and untying knots.

examples.text: كيف رح نحل مشكلة الحبر الملطخ عالكرت؟
examples.trans: How are we going to solve the smudged ink problem on the card?
Tariq untied the knot quickly with his hand.

meanings.note: Appears in the vivid Jordanian idiom ضبي لسانك جوا حلقك ('tuck your tongue inside your throat' = keep quiet).

examples.trans: My throat hurt from talking.
Keep your tongue inside your mouth for a bit.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: حلقات.

examples.trans: The brass ring is twenty millimetres wide.
We fitted a new washer on the pipe.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أحلام.

examples.text: هاد كان حلم حياتي من زمان.
examples.trans: That was my lifelong dream.
At last our dreams came true.

meanings.note: Past tense verb indicating dreaming, for a third-person plural subject.

examples.trans: They dreamt of a better future.

examples.text: الأولاد حلموا يلاقوا الكنز قبل نهاية اليوم.
examples.trans: The children dreamed of finding the treasure before the day ended.

meanings.note: One of the most frequently used adjectives in Jordanian Arabic to mean beautiful, sweet, nice, or good.

examples.trans: This dress is very beautiful on you.

examples.text: طعم العسل مع قشر البرتقال حلو ومتوازن.
examples.trans: The taste of honey with orange peel is sweet and balanced.

meanings.note: Verb حلي means 'to become sweet' (used for caramelizing onions and carrots).

examples.text: البصل بس ينطبخ على نار هادية بحلى وبطلع طعمه روعة.
examples.trans: When onions cook on low heat, they turn sweet and taste amazing.
The oranges got really sweet toward the end of winter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: I would like coffee with hot milk.
We bought three bottles of milk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حمامات.

examples.trans: The small bathroom beside the room is clean.
The bathroom light works fine.

meanings.note: Abstract noun from حمى, to protect; in the construct state it is pronounced himaayit (حماية التراث heritage protection).

examples.trans: This cream is protection from the sun.
Protection matters for old houses.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; الحمد لله means 'thank goodness'.

examples.trans: Thank goodness everything is fine!
We arrived safely, thank goodness.

meanings.note: Plural form of the color red, used to describe plural nouns.

examples.trans: I bought red apples.

examples.text: قطفنا حبات توت حمر وطازجة من الحديقة.
examples.trans: We picked fresh red berries from the garden.

meanings.note: Form I verb; often describes honey, milk, or dough turning sour.

examples.text: العسل الدافي بضل طري بدون ما يحمض.
examples.trans: Warm honey stays soft without turning sour.

examples.text: إذا تركتي الحليب برا التلاجة رح يحمض.
examples.trans: If you leave the milk outside the fridge it will go sour.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحمل, بيحمل).

examples.text: بتحمل مفك بكل مكان يا طارق!
examples.trans: You carry a screwdriver everywhere, Tariq!
He picked up the wrong blue bag at the station.

meanings.note: Feminine noun; covers expeditions, cleaning drives, and campaigns.

examples.text: قود الحملة يا كابتن واحنا وراك بالخريطة.
examples.trans: Lead the expedition, captain, and we are right behind you with the map.

examples.text: الحارة عملت حملة تنظيف للساحة يوم السبت.
examples.trans: The neighbourhood organized a cleanup campaign for the square on Saturday.

meanings.note: Form II defective verb meaning to preheat an oven, pan, or food.

examples.trans: Preheat the oven ten minutes beforehand.
Suad warmed up the soup on a low flame.

meanings.note: Plural noun for eyebrows, with a second-person possessive suffix.

examples.trans: Your eyebrows are neat today.

examples.text: رفعت حواجبك باستغراب أول ما شفت الخريطة!
examples.trans: You raised your eyebrows in astonishment as soon as you saw the map!

meanings.note: Spatial and approximate preposition.

examples.text: امشي حوالي الجهة الناشفة من النافورة.
examples.trans: Walk around the dry side of the fountain.

examples.text: في حوالي عشرين كتاب قديم عالرف.
examples.trans: There are around twenty old books on the shelf.

meanings.note: A very common preposition denoting physical surrounding or approximation of time/quantity.

examples.trans: There are many people around the roundabout.

examples.text: جمعنا الكراسي حوالين الطاولة الكبيرة بالساحة.
examples.trans: We gathered the chairs around the big table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural أحواض. Used for courtyard fountain basins, flowerbeds, and sinks.

examples.trans: The paper landed in the middle of the fountain basin.
There is a planter basin of green mint in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحول, بيحول).

examples.trans: They want to turn our guesthouse into offices?
We turned the attic into a cozy guest room.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أحياء.

examples.trans: The old quarter in Amman is calm and beautiful.
The district law protects courtyards.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: Life is sweet with kind people.
Never in my life have I seen a prettier view.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حيطان.

examples.trans: We hung the mirror on the wall.
Stone walls keep the coolness in summer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحجز, بيحجز).

examples.trans: I booked room seven on the phone yesterday.
We booked a quiet dinner at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Form I verbal noun from حمل ('to carry'), meaning the act of carrying or a heavy load.

examples.text: حمل الشناتي التقيلة بده شوية حذر.
examples.trans: Carrying the heavy bags needs a little care.
Help me carry the trays to the table.

meanings.note: Vocalized with fatha-shadda to distinguish adjective حَيّ ('live/living') from noun حي ('neighbourhood').

examples.text: يوم الجمعة رح يكون عنا شاي وموسيقى حية عالبيانو.
examples.trans: On Fridays we'll have tea and live music on the piano.

examples.text: الساحة صارت حية ودافية بوجود الجيران.
examples.trans: The courtyard came alive and warm with the neighbours there.

حِفِظ.gloss: to keep safe; hold onto; preserve

meanings.en: to keep safe; hold onto; preserve
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحفظ, بيحفظ).

examples.trans: Old stone holds the warmth until morning.

examples.text: شكرا لأنك حفظت الشنتة طول الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Thank you for keeping the bag safe all week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحلم, بيحلم).

examples.trans: Am I dreaming or awake?
She dreamed of a small café in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Describes outer shutters, doors, or walls facing the courtyard or street.

examples.text: رح ندهن الشيش الخارجي بلون أخضر دافي.
examples.trans: We are going to paint the outside shutters a warm green.

examples.text: الباب الخارجي بيفتح مباشرة على شارع الياسمين.
examples.trans: The exterior gate opens straight onto Jasmine Street.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خاصة, plural: خاصين).

examples.trans: Converting the house into private offices is forbidden.

examples.text: هادي وصفة خاصة من مطبخ سلمى.
examples.trans: This is a special recipe from Salma's kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخاف, بيخاف).

examples.text: مازن خاف طول الليل من التقييم!
examples.trans: Mazen worried all night about the review!
I was afraid your stubborn brother would stay home.

meanings.note: Polite traditional title of respect for a woman in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لو الجرس رن مرة واحدة يا خانوم كنت استغربت.
examples.trans: If the bell rang only once, madam, I would be surprised.

examples.text: تفضلي الكرسي هادا يا خانوم سعاد.
examples.trans: Please take this chair, Madam Suad.

meanings.note: Active participle of خاف, very common in speech for 'feeling scared right now' (كنت خايفة).

examples.trans: I was very scared at the time.
I'm afraid you'll tell someone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خبازين.

examples.trans: The baker opens the oven at five in the morning.
The bakers' market is near the overpass.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أخبار.

examples.trans: I have good news for you today!
They have no news yet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خبزات.

examples.trans: The morning bread is fresh and hot.
We ate bread with cheese and olives.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبط, بيخبط).

examples.text: شوي شوي عاللفة، لا تخبطوا الحيط!
examples.trans: Easy on the turn, do not bump the wall!
The wind rattled the window at night.

meanings.note: Form II verb used for the action of hiding something. Can be past tense 'they hid' or imperative 'hide (you pl)'.

examples.trans: They hid the money in the closet.

examples.text: خبوا البطاقة التالتة جوا غلاف الدفتر.
examples.trans: Hide the third card inside the notebook cover.

meanings.note: Occupation pattern فعّال from خبز (bread), meaning 'baker'.

examples.text: الخبّاز اللي براس الشارع بطلّع الخبز سخن من الفجر.
examples.trans: The baker at the top of the street pulls fresh warm bread out from dawn.

examples.text: جبت كعك سمسم طازة من عند الخبّاز.
examples.trans: I brought fresh sesame ka'ak from the baker.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبر, بيخبر).

examples.trans: Wait till I tell the bakers' market!
We told the guests the breakfast time.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبي, بيخبي).

examples.trans: Why did you save it away for me all these years?
She tucked the recipe away in the kitchen notebook.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أختام.

examples.trans: The envelope has an official red stamp on it.
Put the stamp at the bottom of the page.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine verb; past خجل (khijil), present بيخجل (byikhjal).

examples.trans: Honestly I felt too shy to ask for my bag.
Do not be shy, make yourself at home.

meanings.note: Refers to a minor cut or scrape on a surface or skin.

examples.text: في خدش صغير على شاشة التلفون.
examples.trans: There is a small scratch on the phone screen.

examples.text: في خدش خفيف على غطا العلبة المعدنية.
examples.trans: There is a faint scratch on the lid of the metal tin.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخدع, بيخدع).

examples.trans: Tell me my glasses are playing tricks on me!
Appearances sometimes deceive.

meanings.note: Feminine Arabic noun meaning 'trick' or 'illusion'.

examples.text: طلعت القصة كلها خدعة بصرية معموله بالمرايا.
examples.trans: The whole thing turned out to be an optical illusion made with mirrors.

examples.text: انتبه، الإعلان هاد شكله خدعة عشان ياخدوا مصاريك.
examples.trans: Be careful, this ad looks like a trick to take your money.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخدم, بيخدم).

examples.trans: The tables serve the neighbours every day.
We served the neighbourhood for fifteen years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: خدمات.

examples.trans: The service at this guesthouse is excellent.
Any other service, sir?

meanings.note: Imperative form addressed to a group, asking them to take something feminine.

examples.trans: Here is the gift, take it with you.
The cake is ready; take it out to the balcony for tea.

meanings.note: Intransitive: the machine breaks by itself (السخان خرب 'the heater broke down'). Compare خرّب, to break something.

examples.trans: The phone broke down last night.
This car never breaks down.

meanings.note: Colloquial Jordanian adjective for broken machines, bells, or spoiled food.

examples.text: الجرس ما برن منيح، أكيد السلك خربان.
examples.trans: The bell is not ringing properly; the wire must be broken.
The old clock has been out of order for two years.

meanings.note: Colloquial feminine noun from خربط ('to mess up/mix up'). Used for small administrative or scheduling mix-ups.

examples.text: صار في خربطة بسيطة بالمواعيد بس انحلت.
examples.trans: There was a small mix-up in the times, but it got sorted.

examples.text: مكتبي صار خربطة من كتر الأوراق.
examples.trans: My desk became a mess from so many papers.

meanings.note: Plural noun (from Persian khurda) used in دكان الخردوات ('hardware shop').

examples.trans: The hardware shop sells screws and wrenches.
I found the part at the hardware market.

meanings.note: Standard word for a geographical or digital map.

examples.text: افتح الخريطة على التلفون عشان ما نضيع.
examples.trans: Open the map on the phone so we don't get lost.
We followed the blue lines on the old map.

meanings.note: Season name ('autumn'); بالخريف means 'in autumn'.

examples.text: ورق الشجر بالساحة بيصير أصفر بالخريف.
examples.trans: The tree leaves in the courtyard turn yellow in autumn.

examples.text: أول مطر بالخريف بيغسل حجر الياسمين.
examples.trans: The first rain in autumn washes the stone around the jasmine.

meanings.note: Transitive, with a doubled middle r (kharrab): someone breaks something. Written the same as خرب; the past خربت is 'I broke' (kharrabt) or 'it broke down' (khirbat) depending on context.

examples.trans: The boy broke the toy on the first day.
Be careful not to break the lock!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: خزاين.

examples.trans: The clean towels are in the linen closet.
We locked the suitcase inside the closet.

meanings.note: Names smooth fired ceramic or porcelain, including old-style porcelain electrical fuses and glazed bowls.

examples.text: الفيوز القديم مصنوع من خزف أبيض قوي.
examples.trans: The old fuse is made of strong white porcelain.

examples.text: على الرف صحون خزف ملونة من السوق.
examples.trans: On the shelf sit colourful ceramic plates from the market.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The rug is in the storeroom downstairs.
We tidied the pantry shelves in the morning.

meanings.note: Feminine noun (plural خسائر) widely used in Jordanian speech as an exclamation: خسارة! ('what a shame!').

examples.text: خسارة نترك شغل طوب ممتاز فاضي!
examples.trans: It is a shame to leave good brick work empty!

examples.text: يا خسارة، خلصت الكيكة قبل ما نوصل.
examples.trans: What a shame, the cake ran out before we arrived.

meanings.note: Used in تخسر كل إشي ('lose everything').

examples.trans: I don't want to lose my friends.
She could lose everything in a moment.

meanings.note: Used for the material wood or timber.

examples.trans: This table is made of wood.

examples.text: الصندوق مصنوع من خشب جوز قديم وناعم.
examples.trans: The chest is made of smooth old walnut wood.

meanings.note: Feminine word derived from خشب ('wood'), agreeing with عدة.

examples.text: عندي عدة خشبية صغيرة بصلّح فيها الكراسي.
examples.trans: I have a small wooden toolkit I use to fix the chairs.

examples.text: الباب الخشبي القديم بيعطي البيت دفا وروح.
examples.trans: The old wooden door gives the house warmth and character.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خصومات.

examples.trans: We gave him a fifty-percent discount.
There is a special discount for weekly guests.

meanings.note: Used with ب- as بخصوص ('regarding / about').

examples.trans: I am calling you regarding the booking.
We spoke regarding the lease.

meanings.note: Everyday adverb meaning 'especially' or 'in particular'.

examples.text: بحب أتمشى بوسط البلد الصبح، خصوصاً يوم الجمعة.
examples.trans: I love walking around downtown in the morning, especially on Friday.

examples.text: الأكل الشامي زاكي كتير، وخصوصاً الكنافة السخنة.
examples.trans: Levantine food is delicious, especially warm knafeh.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: Salma cooked hot vegetable soup.
We bought fresh vegetables from the market.

meanings.note: Can mean a physical line, a phone line, a bus route, or handwriting.

examples.trans: There is no coverage, the line is disconnecting.

examples.text: رسمنا خط مستقيم بالمسطرة على الورقة.
examples.trans: We drew a straight line with the ruler on the sheet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خطابات.

examples.trans: He prepared a long, neat speech.

examples.text: ما في داعي لخطاب رسمي بين الإخوان.
examples.trans: There is no need for a formal speech between brothers.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: خطط.

examples.trans: What is your plan for tomorrow morning?
That is an excellent, practical plan.

meanings.note: Form II verb (khattat); بتضلك تخططي لحالك means 'you keep planning by yourself'.

examples.trans: We planned the trip together.
Why are you planning without us?

meanings.note: A literal physical step or a metaphorical step in a process.

examples.trans: Let's walk step by step.

examples.text: كل خطوة بهاللغز بتقربنا من المخبز القديم.
examples.trans: Every step in this puzzle brings us closer to the old bakery.

meanings.note: Plural of 'khatt', referring to lines, phone numbers, or routes.

examples.trans: There are red lines in the matter.

examples.text: الخطوط اللي عالخريطة بتدل على البوابات.
examples.trans: The lines on the map point toward the gates.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخطط, بيخطط).

examples.trans: Did you plan this entire meeting?
We planned to open the café in spring.

meanings.note: Used for weight, rain, noise or pain getting less (المطر خف 'the rain eased').

examples.trans: The bag got lighter when we took the books out.
The pain has eased a little today.

meanings.note: Feminine noun from خفيف ('light'). With preposition بـ, بخفة means 'lightly' or 'gently'.

examples.text: حرك السكر بخفة عشان ما يطير.
examples.trans: Stir the sugar gently so it doesn't fly about.

examples.text: بيمشي بخفة كأنه ما في وزن.
examples.trans: He walks lightly as if there were no weight.

meanings.note: Culinary verb for whisking eggs, lemon curd, or cream until smooth.

examples.text: نور بتخفق البيض مع الليمون والسكر بهدوء.
examples.trans: Nour whisks the eggs gently with lemon and sugar.

examples.text: خفقت سلمى الكريمة حتى صارت ناعمة ومتساوية.
examples.trans: Salma whisked the curd until it turned smooth and glossy.

meanings.note: Past tense verb in the first-person plural indicating fear.

examples.trans: We got scared of the explosion sound.

examples.text: ما خفنا من العتمة لأن معنا فوانيس.
examples.trans: We were not afraid of the dark because we had lanterns.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خفيفة, plural: خفاف).

examples.trans: Coffee with milk and light sugar.
A light, tasty breakfast in the morning.

meanings.note: Adjective used to describe something feminine that is light in weight, intensity, or even a 'light-hearted' person (khafiifat dam).

examples.trans: This meal is light on the stomach.

examples.text: نكهة الليمون خفيفة ومنعشة مع الشاي.
examples.trans: The lemon flavour is light and refreshing with tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخفف, بيخفف).

examples.text: الخشب بيخفف الصدى عن حجر الشارع.
examples.trans: The wood softens the echo off the street stone.
We dimmed the light in the courtyard in the evening.

meanings.note: Household vinegar used both in cooking and for streak-free window washing.

examples.text: نقطة خل بالمي الدافية بتخلي القزاز يلمع.
examples.trans: A drop of vinegar in warm water makes the glass sparkle.

examples.text: حطيت شوية زيت زيتون وخل عالسلطة.
examples.trans: I dressed the salad with a little olive oil and vinegar.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خلافات.

examples.trans: Family disagreements take patience.
The disagreement ended with a kind word.

meanings.note: Temporal preposition meaning 'during' (خلال عزفنا 'during our playing') or 'within' (خلال ساعة 'within an hour').

examples.trans: During our piano playing, he sketched all of us!

examples.text: بنخلص ترتيب الساحة خلال عشر دقايق.
examples.trans: We will finish tidying the courtyard within ten minutes.

meanings.note: Form II past tense verb indicating someone (f) allowing or leaving something.

examples.trans: She left the door open and went out.

examples.text: سعاد خلت الباب مفتوح عشان يطلع البخار.
examples.trans: Suad left the door open so the steam would get out.

meanings.note: Ubiquitous Jordanian interjection meaning 'enough / okay / that's it!'.

examples.text: خلص، لا تزعل حالك، بنحل الموضوع بكرة.
examples.trans: Okay, don't upset yourself—we'll sort it out tomorrow.

examples.text: خلص يا أولاد، بكفي لعب، صار وقت النوم!
examples.trans: Enough, kids—that's enough playing, it's bedtime!

meanings.note: Feminine instance noun from خلط ('to mix'): a spice blend, pastry glaze, or sauce mix.

examples.trans: We prepared the sugar and lemon glaze for the cake.

examples.text: كل بيت عنده خلطة بهارات خاصة.
examples.trans: Every home has its own special spice blend.

meanings.note: Opposite of أمامي ('front').

examples.text: الفانوس معلق جنب الباب الخلفي للساحة.
examples.trans: The lantern hangs beside the back door to the courtyard.

examples.text: الغرفة الخلفية أهدى غرفة بالبيت كله.
examples.trans: The back room is the quietest room in the whole house.

meanings.note: Form II verb asking a group to let or leave something, or third-person plural past tense.

examples.trans: Leave the things in their place.

examples.text: خلوا الكيكات تبرد على الشبكة قبل التزيين.
examples.trans: Let the cakes cool on the rack before decorating.

meanings.note: Imperative forms with object pronouns give خليكم بحالكم ('stay in your own business') and خلوني بحالي ('leave me in mine').

examples.trans: Let me speak for a bit.
Stay calm, Mariam.

meanings.note: Used in cooking for cake batter and in general for any mix.

examples.text: اطوي التوت شوي شوي جوا خليط اللوز.
examples.trans: Fold the berries gently into the almond batter.

examples.text: هادا الخليط فيه عسل وبرش برتقال.
examples.trans: This mixture has honey and grated orange zest.

meanings.note: Extremely common phrase used to suggest doing something together, like 'let's...'.

examples.trans: Let's go out to eat dinner outside.

examples.text: خلينا نقرأ البطاقة الأخيرة قبل ما نحكم.
examples.trans: Let us read the last card before we judge.

meanings.note: Common phrase used to ask for permission or time to do something, 'let me...'.

examples.trans: Let me think about the matter and I'll get back to you.

examples.text: خليني أشوف الرقم المرسوم تحت الشمع.
examples.trans: Let me look at the number drawn under the wax.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخلص, بيخلص).

examples.trans: I finished making the bed quickly!

examples.text: كل ما أخلص عزف كنا نحكي.
examples.trans: Whenever I finished playing, we used to chat.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: The number five, typically used before feminine counted nouns.

examples.trans: There are five minutes left and we will arrive.

examples.text: ضفت خمس معالق زبدة دايبة للعجين.
examples.trans: I added five spoonfuls of melted butter to the batter.

meanings.note: The number five, used in counting abstractly or before masculine counted nouns.

examples.trans: I bought five books today.

examples.text: عندنا خمسة أبواب خشب بتطلع عالحديقة.
examples.trans: We have five wooden doors leading out to the garden.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'fifteen' before a counted noun (خمستعشر سنة 'fifteen years').

examples.trans: I have not seen it in fifteen years!
The landing is after fifteen steps.

meanings.note: Colloquial Jordanian numeral for 15 (also خمسطعشر before singular nouns).

examples.trans: It is three-fifteen right now.
We walked fifteen steps up to the tree.

meanings.note: Numeral 'fifty'.

examples.trans: Here is fifty dinars from the cash box.
She saved fifty piastres on the bill.

meanings.note: Colloquial Jordanian word for something thick, dense, or bulky, typically used for objects like books or clothes, rather than people.

examples.trans: Wear a thick jacket, the weather is cold.

examples.text: القماش خميل كتير وما بنفذ الضو منه.
examples.trans: The cloth is very thick and light does not pass through it.

meanings.note: Form II causative verb (khawwaf) from خاف: خوفتيني ('you startled me'), أخوفك ('scare you').

examples.trans: You honestly startled me when you walked in!
I didn't mean to scare you.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian speech, خيال commonly means a cast 'shadow' or 'silhouette' as well as 'imagination'.

examples.text: شفت خيال القطة على الحيط تحت الفانوس.
examples.trans: I saw the cat's shadow on the wall beneath the lantern.

examples.text: خيال الشجرة واصل لحد باب المطبخ.
examples.trans: The tree's shadow reaches right to the kitchen door.

meanings.note: Core word in صباح الخير ('good morning'), مساء الخير ('good evening'), تصبح على خير ('good night'), and rising-tone خير؟ ('is everything okay?').

examples.trans: Good morning, neighbours!

examples.text: خير إن شاء الله، شو صار؟
examples.trans: Hopefully all is well, what happened?

meanings.note: Used literally for a sewing thread or metaphorically for a clue (kheet amal = thread of hope).

examples.text: بدي خيط أسود عشان أخيط القميص.
examples.trans: I need a black thread to sew the shirt.

examples.text: ربطنا الطرد بخيط أبيض رفيع ولزقناه.
examples.trans: We tied the package with thin white string and sealed it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبز, بيخبز).

examples.text: اخبزي قطع زوايا كتير يا سلمى!
examples.trans: Bake plenty of corner pieces, Salma!

examples.text: قديش بيقدر فرنك يخبز كل صبح؟
examples.trans: How much can your oven bake every morning?

meanings.note: Verbal noun (masdar) disambiguated with fatha-sukun from noun خُبز ('bread').

examples.text: ريحة الخبز الطازة رح تعبي الساحة من الصبح.
examples.trans: The smell of fresh baking will fill the courtyard from early morning.

examples.text: وقت الخبز بالفرن عشرين دقيقة بالتمام.
examples.trans: The baking time in the oven is twenty minutes sharp.

خِلِص.gloss: to run out; be finished; end

meanings.en: to run out; be finished; end
meanings.note: Form I intransitive counterpart of transitive خلّص ('to finish something'): خلص الخبز means 'the bread has run out'.

examples.text: يلا نمشي قبل ما يخلص الخبز السخن.
examples.trans: Let's walk over before the hot bread sells out.

examples.text: خلصت القهوة، رح أعمل إبريق جديد.
examples.trans: The coffee ran out; I will make a fresh pot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دوائر.

examples.trans: A paper arrived from the property department.
The department office is downtown.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دائمة, plural: دائمين).

examples.trans: She became the permanent reception manager at the guesthouse.
He wrote it in the ledger in permanent ink.

meanings.note: Active participle of دخل ('to enter'), used like a progressive verb in Arabic (بيت الياسمين داخل على المهرجان 'is entering the festival').

examples.text: بيت الياسمين داخل على مهرجان الساحات!
examples.trans: Jasmine Courtyard House is entering the Courtyard Festival!

examples.text: هي سعاد داخلة من باب الساحة.
examples.trans: Look, Suad is coming in through the courtyard door.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from داخل (inside), given the -ة ending to match قعدة.

examples.text: الجو برد برا، خلينا نقعد بالقعدة الداخلية.
examples.trans: It's cold outside; let's sit in the indoor seating area.

examples.text: الرحلة الداخلية للعقبة بتاخد أقل من ساعة بالطيارة.
examples.trans: The domestic flight to Aqaba takes less than an hour by plane.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian verb meaning 'to manage, run (a shop/inn)' and in دير بالك ('take care!').

examples.text: عمتي كانت تدير قاعة الشاي لحالها.
examples.trans: My aunt used to run the tea room on her own.

examples.text: مازن بيدير النزل مع طارق ونور وسلمى.
examples.trans: Mazen runs the inn with Tariq, Nour, and Salma.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دافعة, plural: دافعين).

examples.text: ما بدنا نزعج ضيف دافع حق غرفته.
examples.trans: We do not want to bother a paying guest.
All the guests have paid the bill in advance.

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The weather today is very warm.

examples.text: الحليب الدافي بسكر الخميرة وبخليها تتفاعل.
examples.trans: Warm milk activates the yeast and helps it rise.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine hollow verb (from Classical ذاق, with ذ -> د); imperative دوق / دوقي ('taste!').

examples.text: دوقي هالمربى الحلو قبل ما نشتري المرطبان.
examples.trans: Taste this sweet jam before we buy the jar.
Ziad tasted the honey and smiled right away.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine feminine noun (from Classical أذن). Dual دينين is used as the normal plural for ears.

examples.text: سمعت الخبر من دان لدان بسرعة.
examples.trans: I heard the news from ear to ear quickly.

examples.text: حطيت إيدي على داني عشان أسمع أوضح.
examples.trans: I cupped my hand to my ear to hear more clearly.

meanings.note: Spoken form of دائم (constant/regular); زبون دايم means a regular patron.

examples.text: أبو طارق زبون دايم بالمقهى من عشر سنين.
examples.trans: Abu Tariq has been a regular customer at the café for ten years.

examples.text: إن شاء الله الفرح دايم ببيتكم عامر.
examples.trans: May joy always abide in your home.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of دائما ('always').

examples.trans: I always walk fast on the first day.
Noon traffic is always slow.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine pronunciation (daayman) of classical دائماً.

examples.trans: She always comes early.
We always sit here.

meanings.note: Colloquial adjective describing honey, syrup, or gluey surfaces.

examples.text: العسل الدافي مبين دبق بس طعمه بجنن.
examples.trans: Warm honey looks sticky, but its taste is amazing.
His hands got sticky from the sugar syrup.

meanings.note: Small metal pin, tack, or brass hinge pivot pin.

examples.text: دبوس المفصلة النحاس صغير كتير وبده ملقط.
examples.trans: The brass hinge pin is tiny and requires tweezers.

examples.text: علقت الورقة على اللوح بدبوس صغير.
examples.trans: I pinned the note onto the board with a small tack.

دخل.gloss: to enter; come in; go in

meanings.en: to enter; come in; go in
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بدخل, بيدخل).

examples.text: تفضل ادخل من المطر يا أستاذ.
examples.trans: Please come in out of the rain, sir.

examples.text: الزوجين دخلوا غرفة ستة قبل ساعة.
