examples.trans: The couple checked into room six an hour ago.

meanings.note: In Jordanian urban speech, دخلة specifically means a narrow lane or turn-off.

examples.text: هاي الدخلة الضيقة بتوصل دغري عالساحة.
examples.trans: This narrow lane leads straight to the courtyard.
The entrance lane to the house is lined with jasmine trees.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of دخل ('to enter'). تسجيل دخول means 'check-in' at a hotel or guesthouse.

examples.text: كل ضيف بيسجل دخول بيشوف الخريطة.
examples.trans: Every guest who checks in will see the map.
Entry to the festival is free for everyone.

meanings.note: Affectionate, dramatic Levantine plea: دخيلك (to one person), دخيلكم (to several).

examples.trans: Please tell me room six is free!
Please do not forget the receipt!

meanings.note: Form II causative of دخل ('enter'), meaning 'carry/bring indoors'.

examples.text: دخلنا الكراسي الخشب للممر قبل المطر.
examples.trans: We brought the wooden chairs into the hallway before the rain.
Help me carry the baskets into the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for a wooden or iron railing.

examples.trans: The balcony railing is made of oak wood.
Hold the banister as you go down the stairs.

meanings.note: Unvocalised درج covers both daraj ('stairs', masculine collective) and durj ('desk drawer').

examples.trans: Go up the stairs to the second floor.
The big notebook is inside the drawer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: درجات.

examples.trans: The boy sat on the third step.

examples.text: انتبه على درجة الحجر عند الباب.
examples.trans: Watch the stone step by the door.

meanings.note: Warm colloquial verb for casual, friendly chatting (ندردش طول الليل).

examples.trans: We sat chatting in the courtyard.
I love chatting with my friends.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دروس.

examples.trans: The piano lesson is every Friday.
I was not late for the lesson today.

meanings.note: Single hinged panel or leaf of a double window, shutter, or cupboard.

examples.text: فتحنا الدرفة الشمال وبعدين الدرفة اليمين.
examples.trans: We swung open the left shutter leaf and then the right one.

examples.text: كل شباك إله درفتين خشب متينات.
examples.trans: Each window has two sturdy wooden shutter panels.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine market word (from Italian dozzina) for a set of twelve; dual دزينتين ('two dozen' = 24).

examples.trans: We bought a dozen white cups for the café.

examples.text: الدكان بيعمل خصم إذا أخدت دزينتين.
examples.trans: The shop gives a discount if you take two dozen.

meanings.note: Geminate Form I verb (بدس / دسّيت). Used for tucking a small packet or note neatly into a corner.

examples.trans: Tuck a small packet of dried mint in the corner.
I slipped the letter under the room door.

دعا.gloss: to pray for; wish well; invite

meanings.en: to pray for; wish well; invite
meanings.note: With ل- (ادعيلي / ادعولنا بالتوفيق) it means 'wish me / wish us luck!'.

examples.text: ادعولنا يخلص الشغل قبل يوم الأربعا!
examples.trans: Wish us luck finishing the work before Wednesday!

examples.text: إمي دايما بتدعيلنا بالخير كل صبح.
examples.trans: My mother always wishes us well every morning.

meanings.note: Form I verb; used both physically and for backing an idea.

examples.text: هادا هو البحث اللي انا بدعمه بقوة!
examples.trans: That is the research that I strongly support!

examples.text: كل الجيران دعموا فكرة مهرجان الحارة.
examples.trans: All the neighbours supported the idea of the neighbourhood festival.

meanings.note: Feminine noun for a formal or friendly invitation (دعوة لمهرجان 'invitation to a festival'). Plural: دعوات.

examples.trans: An invitation to the Historic Courtyard Festival reached us!
Thank you for your kind invitation to tea.

meanings.note: Essential Jordanian word used for giving directions ('go straight') or to mean doing something immediately.

examples.trans: Walk straight and then turn right.

examples.text: امشي دغري لعند القوس وبعدين لف يسار.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead to the arch and then turn left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Old stone holds warmth at night.
Morning warmth from the sun is comforting.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دفايات.

examples.trans: The radiator in the corner started warming up.
We turned on the heaters when it got cold.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دفاتر.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in the booking ledger.
I forgot my leather notebook on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بدفع, بيدفع).

examples.trans: Lift the handle first and then push.
I paid for both valves in cash!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بدفن, بيدفن).

examples.text: لا تدفنا قبل ما نقرأ الورقة كلها!
examples.trans: Do not bury us before we read the whole sheet!
He buried the key in a small box.

meanings.note: Form II transitive verb (contrast دفي 'to become warm').

examples.text: دفي الكيكة عالفرن لبين ما أرجع بالعسل.
examples.trans: Keep the cake warm on the stove until I get back with the honey.

examples.text: دفينا الشاي عالنار عشان الجو بارد.
examples.trans: We warmed the tea on the fire because the weather is cold.

meanings.note: Past tense verb for knocking on a door, hammering a nail, or sometimes calling someone on the phone ('daqq 'ala').

examples.trans: Someone knocked on the door.

examples.text: حدا دق جرس البوابة الساعة تمانية الصبح.
examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell at eight in the morning.

meanings.note: Covers daqqa ('a knock / clock chime', pl. دقات) and diqqa ('precision / punctuality', الدقة بالمواعيد).

examples.text: سمعنا اطنعشر دقة من برج الساعة.
examples.trans: We heard twelve chimes from the clock tower.
I always love punctuality.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Common Arabic verb meaning 'to knock' or 'tap'.

examples.text: في حدا عم بدقّ عالباب، شوف مين اجا.
examples.trans: Someone is knocking on the door—go see who came.

examples.text: دقّيتلك مرتين مبارح بس تلفونك كان مسكّر.
examples.trans: I called you twice yesterday, but your phone was off.

meanings.note: Form II verb; commonly paired with النظر (to look closely / squint).

examples.text: دقق النظر تحت درابزين البلكونة يا طارق.
examples.trans: Look closely under the balcony railing, Tariq.

examples.text: مازن بدقق بكل تفاصيل الوصفة قبل الحكم.
examples.trans: Mazen scrutinizes every detail of the recipe before judging.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دكاكين.

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
I bought milk and bread from the shop.

meanings.note: Common everyday word for a medical doctor or a PhD holder.

examples.trans: The doctor examined the patient.

examples.text: الدكتور نصحنا نشرب شاي أعشاب دافي.
examples.trans: The doctor advised us to drink warm herbal tea.

meanings.note: The word 'doctor' with a second person masculine singular possessive suffix.

examples.trans: What did your doctor tell you?
Your doctor wrote you an easy, convenient prescription.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.text: السقف سليم، ما فيه ولا نقطة دلف.
examples.trans: The roof is sound, without a single drop of leaking.
We fixed the leak before the winter rain.

meanings.note: Can mean evidence, proof, or a guide (both a person and a guidebook).

examples.trans: Do you have evidence for what you're saying?

examples.text: هادا الرقم الصغير هو أول دليل للوصول للكنز.
examples.trans: This small number is the first clue for reaching the treasure.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دماء.

examples.trans: The cup of tea calmed my blood pressure.
He is good-humoured and loves joking.

meanings.note: Form II verb (dammar): أنا رح أدمرك ('I am going to ruin you').

examples.trans: Lying destroys trust.
She thought she could ruin me.

meanings.note: Broken plural of دمعة (teardrop).

examples.text: دمعة فرح نزلت من عيونها لما سمعت الخبر.
examples.trans: A tear of joy rolled down from her eyes when she heard the news.
He wiped his tears quickly and tried to smile.

meanings.note: Form II verb (بتدمّع / دمّعت) from دمع ('tears'). Used when someone's eyes well up with emotion.

examples.text: قبل ما تدمّع عيونك يا معلم، ساعدني!
examples.trans: Before your eyes get misty, boss, help me!
Her eyes watered with joy at the gift.

meanings.note: Expressive quadriliteral verb for humming a melody softly without words.

examples.text: سعاد صارت تدندن اللحن وهي بتقرا الورقة.
examples.trans: Suad began humming the melody as she read the sheet.

examples.text: طارق بيدندن أغنية قديمة وهو بيصلح الباب.
examples.trans: Tariq hums an old song while fixing the door.

meanings.note: Softly humming a melody without words.

examples.text: سمعنا دندنة هادية طالعة من غرفة البيانو.
examples.trans: We heard gentle humming coming from the piano room.

examples.text: دندنتها للحن خلت الغرفة كلها تبتسم.
examples.trans: Her humming of the melody made the whole room smile.

meanings.note: Feminine noun used in Jordanian weather expressions: الدنيا بتمطر ('it is raining'), الدنيا برد ('it is cold out').

examples.trans: It is raining outside right now.
It is sunny and lovely out this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دهانات.

examples.trans: Room eight has fresh paint.

examples.text: ريحة الدهان راحت لما فتحنا الشباك.
examples.trans: The smell of paint cleared when we opened the window.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronunciation and spelling of ذهب ('gold'). Used both for the metal and a rich golden colour.

examples.trans: The bread came out the colour of gold.
My grandmother has an old gold bracelet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دهبية, plural: دهبيين).

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.

examples.text: فوق الباب في رسمة مفتاح دهبي.
examples.trans: Above the door there is a painted golden key.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for painting walls, shutters, or wooden furniture (noun دهان 'paint').

examples.text: رح ندهن الشيش باللون الأخضر يوم التنين.
examples.trans: We are going to paint the shutters green on Monday.

examples.text: دهنا الكراسي الخشب وتركناها تنشف بالشمس.
examples.trans: We painted the wooden chairs and left them to dry in the sun.

meanings.note: Noun of instance from دهن (to spread/brush).

examples.text: الكيكة بدها دهنة خفيفة من العسل الدافي.
examples.trans: The cake needs a light brush of warm honey.

examples.text: الحيط محتاج دهنة بوية جديدة قبل العيد.
examples.trans: The wall needs a fresh coat of paint before the holiday.

meanings.note: Solfege name standard across the Arab world for the note C (دو، ري، مي...).

examples.text: نغمة دو بالبيانو صوتها صافي وواضح.
examples.trans: The C note on the piano sounds clean and clear.

examples.text: بلش اللحن من نغمة دو الوسطى.
examples.trans: The melody begins on middle C.

meanings.note: Instrumental noun from داس ('step/press with the foot'); names piano pedals or car/bicycle pedals.

examples.text: لمعت دواسات البيانو النحاس حتى صارت تبرق.
examples.trans: I polished the brass piano pedals until they gleamed.

examples.text: اضغطي عالدواسة اليمين بنعومة بآخر المقطع.
examples.trans: Press the right pedal gently at the end of the passage.

meanings.note: Used in دوام كامل ('full-time job') and دوام جزئي ('part-time').

examples.trans: She started a new full-time job.
Office hours are from eight to five.

meanings.note: With possessive suffixes (دورك 'your turn', دوري 'my turn') it marks whose turn it is next.

examples.text: هلا دورك تكبسي المفتاح يا نور!
examples.trans: Now it is your turn to press the switch, Nour!
We waited our turn in front of the pottery table.

meanings.note: Levantine musical term (from Ottoman/Persian dūzān) for tuning stringed instruments; مفتاح دوزان is a tuning wrench.

examples.text: البيانو القديم حافظ على دوزانه بشكل مدهش.
examples.trans: The old piano held its tuning remarkably well.

examples.text: لقينا مفتاح الدوزان بالدرج التحتاني للصندوق.
examples.trans: We found the tuning key in the bottom drawer of the chest.

meanings.note: Quadriliteral Levantine verb from دوزان ('musical tuning').

examples.text: مدام سعاد بتدوزن أوتار البيانو كل فصل.
examples.trans: Madam Suad tunes the piano strings every season.

examples.text: دوزنا الأوكتاف الوسطاني وصار صوته صافي.
examples.trans: We tuned the middle octave and its tone came out clear.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دوشات.

examples.trans: The shower water is hot and great.
The bathroom has a clean shower.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بدور, بيدور).

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.
Look for a blue wooden door.

meanings.note: Often used in the phrase 'diir baalak' meaning 'take care' or 'pay attention'.

examples.trans: Take care of yourself.

examples.text: دير بالك وانت بتشيل الصينية السخنة.
examples.trans: Watch out while you are lifting the hot tray.

meanings.note: Jordan's national currency (JOD), divided into 100 piastres (قرش).

examples.trans: The bill is twenty dinars, please.
I gave him fifty dinars in cash.

meanings.note: Hollow Form I verb (often pronounced داق in casual Jordanian).

examples.text: مين رح يذوق التلات كيكات ويختار الأحسن؟
examples.trans: Who is going to taste the three cakes and pick the best one?

examples.text: ذقت العسل البلدي وكان طعمه روعة.
examples.trans: I tasted the local honey and its flavour was wonderful.

meanings.note: Warm everyday Jordanian word for 'ear', especially in idioms like الضحكة من الذان للذان ('grinning ear to ear').

examples.text: مازن كان مبتسم والضحكة من الذان للذان.
examples.trans: Mazen was smiling from ear to ear.

examples.text: همس الكلمة بذاني عشان ما يسمع الباقي.
examples.trans: He whispered the word in my ear so the others wouldn't hear.

meanings.note: Refers to the chin or beard, with a third person masculine singular possessive suffix.

examples.trans: He grew his beard a lot.

examples.text: حك ذقنه وهو بفكر بطريقة فتح القفل.
examples.trans: He rubbed his chin while thinking of a way to open the lock.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ذكريات.

examples.trans: This house is full of sweet memories.
Childhood memories are never forgotten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ذكية, plural: أذكياء).

examples.trans: Smart, quick thinking, Nour!
A clever idea solved the problem right away.

meanings.note: A combination of the word 'smart' (fem) and the imperative verb 'look' (pl).

examples.trans: The girl is smart, and look how she plays.

examples.text: الفكرة ذكية وشوفوا كيف رح تشتغل بسرعة.
examples.trans: The idea is clever—watch how it will work quickly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بذكر, بيذكر).

examples.trans: Do not remind him of the old mix-up!
Remind me of the bus time tomorrow.

meanings.note: Pronounced dahab in Jordanian Arabic (often spelled دهب in dialectal writing). ورق دهب means 'gold leaf'.

examples.text: بيت الياسمين مرسوم بورق دهب دافي.
examples.trans: Jasmine Courtyard House is painted in warm gold leaf.

examples.text: ساعة الجد فيها إطار ذهب قديم.
examples.trans: Grandfather's watch has an old gold frame.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from ذهب (gold); also pronounced دهبي in everyday Jordanian.

examples.text: اخبزي الكيكة ليصير لونها ذهبي حلو.
examples.trans: Bake the cake until its colour turns a lovely golden.
She won a gold medal in the cooking competition.

meanings.note: Someone with a discerning palate who tests food or tea (plural ذواقة zawwaaqa).

examples.text: رامي وزياد صاروا ذواقة الشوربة والتارت بالكافيه.
examples.trans: Rami and Ziad became the soup and tart tasters for the café.

examples.text: أبوي ذواق قهوة وبيعرف البن الطازة فورا.
examples.trans: My dad is a coffee connoisseur and spots fresh beans right away.

meanings.note: Used in the warm Jordanian thank-you كلك ذوق ('you are all kindness / how gracious of you').

examples.trans: How kind of you, sir, thank you!
Your taste in colours is calm and lovely.

meanings.note: Form II transitive verb; also pronounced دوّب in casual speech.

examples.text: سلمى رح تذوب العسل والزبدة بطنجرة صغيرة.
examples.trans: Salma is going to melt the honey and butter in a small pot.

examples.text: ذوبنا السكر بالمي الدافية قبل ما نخلطه.
examples.trans: We dissolved the sugar in warm water before mixing it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: رئيسية, plural: رئيسيين).

examples.trans: We shut off the main water valve in the cellar.
The main gate is on the quiet street.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: رائعة, plural: رائعين).

examples.trans: A wonderful choice with morning tea!
The weather in the courtyard today is splendid.

meanings.note: Active participle of ربح (to win).

examples.text: الورقة الرابحة تبعت سلمى كانت دهنة العسل.
examples.trans: Salma's winning card was the honey glaze.

examples.text: الفريق الرابح رح يحتفل بالساحة اليوم.
examples.trans: The winning team will celebrate in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Ordinal number from أربعة (four). Feminine: رابعة.

examples.text: البند الرابع عشر من قانون عمان القديمة.
examples.trans: Clause fourteen of the Amman Old Quarter Act.
This is the fourth cup of coffee today.

meanings.note: Regular monthly pay for a job.

examples.trans: The salary arrives at the end of the month.
The salary of the new job is good.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: راجعة, plural: راجعين).

examples.trans: I am running right back across the bridge now!
Salma is coming back from the table.

meanings.note: Common everyday verb for 'went' in the past tense. Also used as a future particle.

examples.trans: He went to work in the morning.

examples.text: رامي راح عالمكتبة يدور على الكتاب القديم.
examples.trans: Rami went to the library to look for the old book.

meanings.note: Core word in خد راحتك / خدوا راحتكم ('make yourself at home / take your time').

examples.trans: Please sit down and make yourselves comfortable.
After the long trip he needs rest.

meanings.note: Feminine past tense of the verb 'to go'. Also means 'it went' (for feminine subjects).

examples.trans: She went to the market to buy things.

examples.text: سلمى راحت عالسوق تشتري عسل وتوت.
examples.trans: Salma went to the market to buy honey and berries.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: روس.

examples.trans: My glasses were on my head!

examples.text: انتبه على راسك من السقف الواطي.
examples.trans: Watch your head on the low ceiling.

meanings.note: Active participle of رسم used as an agent noun (compare رسّام).

examples.text: ملاحظة راسم الخريطة مكتوبة على جنب الكرت.
examples.trans: The mapmaker's note is written on the side of the card.

examples.text: راسم اللوحة وقع اسمه بالزاوية التحتانية.
examples.trans: The drawer of the painting signed his name in the bottom corner.

meanings.note: With مش (مش راضي يفتح), idiomatically means a stubborn door or latch 'refuses to / won't' budge!

examples.text: القفل القديم مش راضي يتحرك بدون نقطة زيت.
examples.trans: The old lock refuses to budge without a drop of oil.

examples.text: الكل طلع راضي ومبسوط من طعم الشوربة.
examples.trans: Everyone came away happy and satisfied with the soup.

meanings.note: Form III verb meaning 'keep a close eye on an oven, timer, or process'.

examples.text: أبو طارق بيراقب درجة حرارة الفرن والمؤقت.
examples.trans: Abu Tariq watches the oven temperature and the timer.

examples.text: أنا براقب من الكرسي وبعطيكم التعليمات.
examples.trans: I'll watch from the chair and give you instructions.

meanings.note: Describes a light, buoyant waltz melody.

examples.text: أول اللحن فيه نغمة خفيفة وراقصة.
examples.trans: The opening of the melody has a light, dancing lilt.

examples.text: الضو كان يرمي ظلال راقصة على حيط الحجر.
examples.trans: The lantern cast dancing shadows across the stone wall.

meanings.note: Active participle of ركض; commonly used in Levantine for progressive action ('I am running').

examples.text: أنا راكضة عالدكانة أشتري عسل وراجعة فورا!
examples.trans: I am running to the shop to buy honey and coming right back!

examples.text: شفته راكض بالشارع عشان يلحق الباص.
examples.trans: I saw him running down the street to catch the bus.

meanings.note: Male given name belonging to Ziad's younger brother, the quiet architect.

examples.text: رامي رسم خريطة الحارة كلها بإيده.
examples.trans: Rami drew the map of the whole neighborhood by hand.

examples.text: نادي لرامي عشان يشوف التصميم الجديد.
examples.trans: Call Rami so he can take a look at the new design.

meanings.note: Active participle of راح ('to go'), used like a present progressive in Levantine ('am/is/are going').

examples.text: أنا وسلمى رايحين عالسوق نجيب ليمون.
examples.trans: Salma and I are heading to the market to get lemons.

examples.text: وين رايح بهالسلة الكبيرة يا زياد؟
examples.trans: Where are you heading with that big basket, Ziad?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أرباب.

examples.trans: Oh goodness, help us today!
Praise be to the Lord of all worlds.

meanings.note: Derived from أربعة ('four'). Used for four-hand piano pieces or four-sided shapes.

examples.trans: Our four-hand piano piece is ready.
The table has a four-sided shape.

meanings.en: to tie; fasten with a cord
meanings.note: Everyday Form I verb (يربط / بيربط). Related to مربوط ('tied').

examples.trans: Tie the cord with a strong knot.
Tariq tied the bar in the middle.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أرباع.

examples.trans: Breakfast is at seven fifteen in the morning.
I will be back in fifteen minutes.

meanings.note: Literally 'bring up'; colloquially لازم نربيهم على غلطهم means 'we must teach them a lesson for their wrongdoing'.

examples.trans: My parents raised me to be honest.
We need to teach them a lesson for their mistake.

meanings.note: One of the four seasons: صيف summer, خريف autumn, شتا winter, ربيع spring.

examples.trans: Spring in Amman is short and lovely.
In spring we go out to the hills.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from ربيع (spring).

examples.text: اليوم في هبات هوا ربيعية نشطة بالبلد.
examples.trans: Today there are brisk spring wind gusts in town.

examples.text: الجو الربيعي بخلي القعدة بالساحة بتجنن.
examples.trans: The spring weather makes sitting in the courtyard wonderful.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برتب, بيرتب).

examples.trans: Life arranges sweeter melodies than we do.
I straighten my ties and keys every day.

meanings.note: Used mainly in polite/earnest requests: أرجوك (to a man), أرجوكي (to a woman), أرجوكم (plural) — 'please!'.

examples.trans: Please write down that sentence!
Please do not open the white parcel.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: زلام.

examples.text: في رجال طويل واقف عند الباب.
examples.trans: There is a tall man standing by the gate.
The man is wearing a grey coat.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: رجالية, plural: —).

examples.trans: We found a large pair of men's shoes in the bag.
A dark grey men's coat.

رجع.gloss: to return; come back; start again

meanings.en: to return; come back; start again
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برجع, بيرجع).

examples.trans: Can you run there and come back in ten minutes?
Did the pipe start dripping again?

meanings.note: Instance noun (ism marra) from رجع ('return').

examples.text: قطار الرجعة بيطلع من المحطة الساعة سبعة.
examples.trans: The return train leaves the station at seven o'clock.

examples.text: بطريق الرجعة من السوق، اشترينا نعنع أخضر.
examples.trans: On the way back from the market, we bought fresh green mint.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برجف, بيرجف).

examples.trans: My hands are shaking with nerves.
His voice trembled slightly at the start of the call.

meanings.note: Feminine body-part noun in Levantine Arabic (رجلك اليمين 'your right foot').

examples.text: ارفعي رجلك عالمخدة وارتاحي نص ساعة.
examples.trans: Prop your foot up on the pillow and rest for half an hour.

examples.text: حطيت كيس تلج ملفوف بمنشفة على رجلي.
examples.trans: I placed an ice pack wrapped in a towel on my foot.

meanings.note: Form II causative of رجع ('come back').

examples.trans: I put the keys back in the desk drawer.

examples.text: هاد اللحن القديم بيرجعنا لأيام زمان.
examples.trans: This old melody takes us back to the old days.

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.trans: I will travel tomorrow.

examples.text: رح نذوق التلات كيكات بعد ما يبردوا شوي.
examples.trans: We will taste the three cakes after they cool a little.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: رحلات.

examples.trans: How was the bus trip today?
We wish you a happy, comfortable journey.

meanings.note: Used constantly in the respectful phrase الله يرحمه / الله يرحمها ('may God rest his/her soul; the late...').

examples.text: جدي الله يرحمه هو اللي زرع شجرة الياسمين.
examples.trans: My late grandfather is the one who planted the jasmine tree.

examples.text: عمتي الله يرحمها كانت تحب الموسيقى كتير.
examples.trans: My late aunt used to love music dearly.

meanings.note: Commonly used in blessings and exclamations like يا رحمتك يا رب.

examples.text: يا رحمتك يا رب، ضايل معنا عشر دقايق بس!
examples.trans: Have mercy, Lord, we only have ten minutes left!

examples.text: الله يرحم جدتي، كانت كلها رحمة وطيبة.
examples.trans: May God bless my grandmother; she was all mercy and kindness.

meanings.note: Form II verb رحّب takes the preposition بـ before the person welcomed.

examples.text: صاحب البيت رحّب فينا أحسن ترحيب.
examples.trans: The host welcomed us most warmly.

examples.text: رح نرحّب بالضيوف عالباب قبل ما يفوتوا القاعة.
examples.trans: We'll welcome the guests at the door before they enter the hall.

meanings.note: Standard Levantine kitchen term for the work counter (originally a slab of marble, رخام).

examples.text: مسحنا الرخامة ورتبنا مرتبانات السكر والملح.
examples.trans: We wiped the countertop and arranged the sugar and salt jars.

examples.text: فرد طارق العجينة الرقيقة عالرخامة الباردة.
examples.trans: Tariq rolled the thin dough out on the cool counter.

meanings.note: Describes something that is not tight, loose, or soft (feminine form).

examples.trans: The knot is loose, tighten it.

examples.text: العقدة اللي عالخيط صارت رخوة وبسهولة بتنحل.
examples.trans: The knot on the string became loose and comes undone easily.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برخي, بيرخي).

examples.text: البيوت القديمة بترخي برغي كل أسبوع!
examples.trans: Old houses loosen a screw every week!
Loosen the rope a little, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برد, بيرد).

examples.text: اشربي شاي أول وبعدين ردي عالجرس.
examples.trans: Drink tea first and then answer the bell.
Nobody answered the phone at the station.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: رسايل.

examples.trans: An official letter arrived at noon.
We read the letter line by line.

meanings.note: Intensive occupation noun from رسم ('draw/paint'). رسام خرايط means 'mapmaker/cartographer'.

examples.text: رسام الخرايط قعد على طاولة واحد.
examples.trans: The mapmaker sat down at table one.

examples.text: هاد الرسام عمل لوحة رائعة للشارع.
examples.trans: This artist made a wonderful painting of the street.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for drawing a picture, a map or a plan.

examples.trans: He drew me a map to the shop on a piece of paper.

examples.text: بنتي بترسم بيوت وشجر كل يوم.
examples.trans: My daughter draws houses and trees every day.

meanings.note: A noun referring to a single drawing, illustration, or painting.

examples.trans: This drawing is very beautiful.

examples.text: في رسمة صغيرة لورقة زيزفون على الهامش.
examples.trans: There is a small drawing of a linden leaf in the margin.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: رسمية, plural: رسميين).

examples.trans: Save the formal talk for the guests only!
An official letter arrived in the noon post.

meanings.note: Adverb formed from رسمي ('official'); used both seriously and playfully ('Room Nine officially has light!').

examples.text: الكافيه رح يفتح رسميا آخر الأسبوع.
examples.trans: The café will open officially at the end of the week.

examples.text: نور صارت رسميا موظفة الاستقبال بالنزل.
examples.trans: Nour has officially become the inn's receptionist.

meanings.note: Profession noun from رسم ('to draw'); رسام خرائط is a mapmaker.

examples.text: فيه رسّام موهوب بقعد بساحة اللويبدة وبرسم البورتريه.
examples.trans: There's a talented artist who sits in Al-Weibdeh square and draws portraits.

examples.text: رسّام الخرائط اشتغل شهرين عاللوحة هاي.
examples.trans: The cartographer worked for two months on this chart.

meanings.note: Geminate verb used for splashing water or sprinkling herbs/sugar.

examples.trans: I sprinkled a little water on the flowers in the morning.

examples.text: سلمى رشت قرفة مطحونة فوق الكيكة.
examples.trans: Salma dusted ground cinnamon over the cake.

meanings.note: Instance noun from رش ('sprinkle/spray'): رشة ملح = 'a pinch of salt'.

examples.text: الشوربة بدها بس رشة ملح وعصرة ليمون.
examples.trans: The soup just needs a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lemon.

examples.text: حطي رشة قرفة ناعمة فوق الفنجان.
examples.trans: Put a light sprinkle of ground cinnamon on top of the cup.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: رشفات.

examples.trans: Take a sip of cold water first.
He took a small sip of the coffee.

meanings.note: Can mean the metal lead, or bullets. Often used in 'qalam rSaaS' (pencil).

examples.trans: Write with a pencil so you can erase it.

examples.text: الرقم مكتوب بقلم رصاص خفيف جنب الزاوية.
examples.trans: The number is written in light pencil near the corner.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أرصفة.

examples.trans: The car pulled up beside the pavement.
We walked along the wide sidewalk downtown.

meanings.note: Describes wet fresh paint, damp morning stone, or moist cake.

examples.text: انتبه، طرف اللوح لسا رطب من الدهان!
examples.trans: Careful—the edge of the board is still wet with paint!

examples.text: مسحنا الطاولة بقماشة رطبة قبل ما نحط الفناجين.
examples.trans: We wiped the table with a damp cloth before setting down the cups.

meanings.note: Refers to moisture in the air or dampness in walls.

examples.trans: The humidity is high today.

examples.text: الرطوبة خلت الورق القديم يتجعد شوي.
examples.trans: Humidity made the old paper wrinkle a little.

meanings.note: Broken plural of رغيف, the classic Arabic word for a loaf of bread.

examples.text: جيب أربعة أرغفة خبز عربي سخن من المخبز.
examples.trans: Bring four loaves of warm Arabic flatbread from the bakery.

examples.text: رغيف الطابون الصبح مع زيت وزعتر ما في أطيب منه.
examples.trans: A loaf of taboon bread in the morning with olive oil and za'atar can't be beat.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: رفوف.

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.
There are two pieces left on the shelf.

meanings.note: Standard Form I verb.

examples.text: إذا بردت الكيكة رح ترفض طبقة العسل.
examples.trans: If the cake cools down it will reject the honey glaze.

examples.text: رفض ياخد المصاري وقال إنها على حساب المحل.
examples.trans: He refused to take the money and said it was on the house.

meanings.note: Standard verb for lifting something up or raising.

examples.trans: He lifted the heavy box by himself.

examples.text: مازن رفع الصينية بحذر من جوا الفرن.
examples.trans: Mazen carefully lifted the tray out of the oven.

meanings.note: Opposite of سميك ('thick'); describes thin glass cups, fine lines, or narrow strips.

examples.text: كاسات القزاز الرفيعة حلوة للشاي بالنعنع.
examples.trans: Thin glass cups are lovely for mint tea.

examples.text: رسم رامي خط رفيع بقلم الرصاص.
examples.trans: Rami drew a fine line in pencil.

meanings.note: Feminine noun from رقيق ('thin'). Broken plural رقائق refers to flakes (such as toasted almond flakes) or thin wafers.

examples.trans: We sprinkled toasted almond flakes on top.

examples.text: رقاقة العجين لازم تكون رفيعة كتير.
examples.trans: The dough sheet has to be very thin.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a number, digit, or phone number.

examples.trans: What is your phone number?

examples.text: كل بطاقة إلها رقم متسلسل من واحد لعشرة.
examples.trans: Each card has a serial number from one to ten.

meanings.note: Describes thin flaky pastry, fine paper, or gentle manners.

examples.text: العجينة الرقيقة طلعت مقرمشة وخفيفة بالفرن.
examples.trans: The thin pastry came out crisp and light in the oven.

examples.text: كتب الملاحظة على ورق رقيق بقلم رصاص.
examples.trans: He wrote the note in pencil on thin paper.

meanings.note: Form II verb derived from رقم ('number').

examples.text: نور عم ترقم الملاقط بقلم رصاص.
examples.trans: Nour is numbering the clothespins with a pencil.

examples.text: رقمنا كل الطاولات من واحد لتمانية.
examples.trans: We numbered all the tables from one to eight.

ركب.gloss: to ride; take (a bus); fit cleanly

meanings.en: to ride; take (a bus); fit cleanly
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بركب, بيركب).

examples.trans: We rode the same morning bus!
The new brass thread fitted cleanly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ركب.

examples.trans: My knees got tired from climbing the stairs.
He sat on the chair to rest his knees.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: She came running back across the overpass in ten minutes.
Running in the morning energises the body.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ركضات.

examples.trans: Great dash to the shop today!
We made it in a quick dash before the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بركب, بيركب).

examples.trans: I installed a new bulb last week.
We fitted a brass lock on the door.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: رمادية, plural: رماديين).

examples.trans: He is wearing a dark grey coat.

examples.text: بدنا نحمي بيتنا من المكاتب الرمادية.
examples.trans: We want to protect our house from grey offices.

meanings.note: Refers to map symbols, emblems, or passwords.

examples.text: شو الرمز اللي لازم نلاقيه عالكرت الأول؟
examples.trans: What is the symbol that we need to find on the first card?
The jasmine tree is a symbol of hospitality in this house.

meanings.note: Form I verb; can take عيون/عينيكي as object.

examples.text: ليش رمشتي عينيكي لما شفتي السطر التحتاني؟
examples.trans: Why did you squint your eyes when you saw the bottom line?

examples.text: ما رمش عينه وهو براقب الساعة.
examples.trans: He did not blink an eye while watching the clock.

meanings.note: Common word for sand, whether at the beach or in construction.

examples.trans: The kids are playing in the sand.

examples.text: لقينا آثار خطوات صغيرة على رمل الساحة.
examples.trans: We found tiny footprints on the courtyard sand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برمي, بيرمي).

examples.trans: Maybe he tossed my card in the bin.
Do not throw away the old receipt.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برن, بيرن).

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
The old wire always rings twice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: رنات.

examples.trans: The doorbell gave a single ring.
I heard two quick rings from the buzzer.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of رنّ (to ring).

examples.text: هاد الرنين المزدوج أكيد من غرفة أربعة.
examples.trans: That double ringing is definitely from Room Four.

examples.text: سمعنا رنين الجرس من آخر الساحة.
examples.trans: We heard the ringing of the bell from the far end of the courtyard.

meanings.note: Verb رنّ means 'to ring' (for a bell, phone, or timer).

examples.text: المنبّه رنّ الساعة ستة بس ما قمت علطول.
examples.trans: The alarm rang at six, but I didn't get up right away.

examples.text: جرس الباب عم برنّ، شكله الضيوف وصلوا.
examples.trans: The doorbell is ringing; looks like the guests have arrived.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian, رهيب / رهيبة enthusiastically praises food or ideas ('amazing, terrific!').

examples.text: الزبدة المالحة رهيبة مع البيض المقلي!
examples.trans: Salted butter is terrific with fried eggs!
Salma's morning coffee is amazing.

meanings.note: Used frequently as an appreciative exclamation ('Wonderful!').

examples.text: روعة! الكيكة طلعت أطيب مما توقعنا.
examples.trans: Wonderful! The cake turned out even better than we expected.
Their carpentry work has precision and beauty.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine Arabic Arabic verb روّح specifically meaning 'to go home'.

examples.text: صار الوقت متأخر، خلينا نروّح عالبيت.
examples.trans: It's gotten late; let's head home.

examples.text: روّحت من الشغل تعبانة ونمت علطول.
examples.trans: I got home from work exhausted and went straight to sleep.

meanings.note: The imperative روق (rawwiq, to a man) or روقي (to a woman) means 'chill, relax'. Related to رايق, calm and in a good mood.

examples.text: روقي يا بنت، لسا في وقت.
examples.trans: Relax, girl, there is still time.
I drink my coffee and relax a bit.

meanings.note: Solfege name standard in Arabic music education for the note D (ري الوسطى 'middle D').

examples.text: نغمة ري الوسطى هي المفتاح اللي كان ساكت.
examples.trans: Middle D is the exact key that was silent.

examples.text: الأغنية بتنزل بهدوء على نغمة ري بالأخير.
examples.trans: The song settles gently onto D near the end.

meanings.note: Grammatically feminine noun in Arabic (often with plural رياح).

examples.text: اركضي متل الريح يا نور عشان نلحق الكيكة!
examples.trans: Run like the wind, Nour, so we catch the cake in time!
The strong wind moved the courtyard lanterns.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: روايح.

examples.trans: The aroma of coffee in the morning is wonderful!
The scent of cinnamon reaches the second floor.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بركض, بيركض).

examples.text: اركضي بسرعة قبل ما يصحوا الضيوف!
examples.trans: Run fast before the guests wake up!
You ran across half the town this morning.

meanings.note: Hollow verb (يزيد / بزيد). Used both transitively ('to add something') and intransitively ('to grow').

examples.text: كل يوم بزيد ملاحظة جديدة بالدفتر.
examples.trans: Every day I add a new note to the ledger.
The wind picked up in the afternoon.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian everyday word for 'delicious' (equivalent to طيب in Syria/Lebanon).

examples.trans: The fried eggs are so delicious!
The lemon cake turned out delicious today.

meanings.note: Hard, fine-grained beechwood (خشب الزان) used for piano actions and café chairs.

examples.text: مطارق البيانو مصنوعة من خشب الزان المتين.
examples.trans: Piano hammers are crafted from sturdy beechwood.

examples.text: كراسي خشب الزان بتعيش عشرات السنين.
examples.trans: Beechwood chairs last for decades.

meanings.note: Refers to a corner of a room or street, or a geometric angle.

examples.trans: Put the chair in the corner.
The chest is placed in the northern corner of the room.

meanings.note: Colloquial active participle of زاد (to increase), pronounced zaayid without medial hamza.

examples.text: في عسل زايد بالمرطبان، خليه للكيكة التانية.
examples.trans: There is extra honey in the jar; save it for the second cake.

examples.text: الكلام الزايد ما إله داعي هلق.
examples.trans: Extra talk is unnecessary right now.

meanings.note: Active participle noun from زار ('to visit'). Everyday plural: زوار ('visitors').

examples.trans: Hundreds of visitors will come to the festival!
The visitor loved the mint tea very much.

meanings.note: Everyday word for butter. Metaphorically means 'the essence' or 'bottom line'.

examples.trans: Give me the bottom line, what happened?

examples.text: دوبنا معلقة زبدة بلدية بالصينية قبل الخبز.
examples.trans: We melted a spoonful of local butter in the pan before baking.

meanings.note: Standard Jordanian/Levantine household word for a ceramic or glass soup/breakfast bowl (plural زبادي).

examples.text: حطت سلمى الزيتون بزبدية فخار بيضا.
examples.trans: Salma put the olives in a white ceramic bowl.

examples.text: ع الطاولة أربع زبادي صغار للمربى.
examples.trans: On the table sit four small bowls for jam.

meanings.note: Used almost universally in the Levantine adverbial phrase بالزبط (biz-zabt, 'exactly / right on').

examples.text: هاد هو اللون الأخضر اللي بدنا إياه بالزبط!
examples.trans: That is the exact shade of green we want!

examples.text: وصل السايق عالباب الساعة تنتين بالزبط.
examples.trans: The driver arrived at the gate at two o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Everyday Arabic word for a shop or café customer.

examples.text: هاد الزبون بيجي يشرب قهوته الصبح كل يوم.
examples.trans: This customer comes to drink his morning coffee every single day.

examples.text: لازم نحترم كل زبون بفوت المحل ونبتسم بوجهه.
examples.trans: We should treat every customer who walks into the shop with respect and a smile.

meanings.note: Colloquial verb meaning to slip or slide, often accidentally.

examples.trans: He slipped on the peel and fell.

examples.text: انتبه لا تزحلق عالبلاط المبلول عند النافورة.
examples.trans: Be careful not to slip on the wet tiles by the fountain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: زحمات.

examples.trans: The breakfast rush finished at ten.
The market has a crowd on Thursdays.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: زروع.

examples.trans: We water the courtyard plants every morning.
Green plants brighten the entrance.

meanings.note: Feminine form of the color blue. Also the name of a major Jordanian city.

examples.trans: Her car is blue.

examples.text: حطينا البطاقات بعلبة زرقا صغيرة عالرف.
examples.trans: We put the cards in a small blue tin on the shelf.

meanings.note: Fresh wild thyme (or the dried herb blend), an iconic Levantine culinary herb.

examples.text: منقوشة الزعتر السخنة هي فطورنا المفضل الصبح.
examples.trans: Warm za'atar flatbread is our favorite morning breakfast.

examples.text: أمي بتجيب زعتر بلدي من جبال عجلون كل سنة.
examples.trans: My mom gets wild country za'atar from the Ajloun hills every year.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: زعلانة, plural: زعلانين).

examples.trans: A guest must not sit around upset.
Do not sit there upset, he will arrive soon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أزقة.

examples.trans: The stone alley is narrow and quiet.
We turned past the narrow lane.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine/Jordanian word for 'man / guy' (plural: زلم). Warm and conversational.

examples.text: الزلمة اللي قص القماش جاهز من زمان!
examples.trans: The man who cut the cloth was ready long ago!
Tariq is a kind man with a big heart.

meanings.note: Used constantly as 'long ago' (من زمان for a long time, صحاب زمان old friends).

examples.trans: My family lived here long ago.
We have not seen you in a long time!

meanings.note: Often used to mean 'a long time ago' (min zaman).

examples.trans: I haven't seen you in a long time.

examples.text: من زمن طويل وهادا المخبز معروف بالعسل.
examples.trans: For a long time this bakery has been famous for honey.

meanings.note: Feminine word derived from زمن ('time'), forming كبسولة زمنية ('time capsule').

examples.text: دفنّا كبسولة زمنية بحديقة المدرسة عشان نفتحها بعد عشر سنين.
examples.trans: We buried a time capsule in the school garden to open ten years from now.
The timeline for the project is clear and well organized.

meanings.note: Adjective modifying feminine nouns, related to time or duration.

examples.trans: The timeline (temporal plan) is ready.

examples.text: عملنا خطة زمنية لكل مرحلة من التذوق.
examples.trans: We made a timetable for every stage of the tasting.

meanings.note: Used by teachers and students for a female classmate (زميلتك بالصف).

examples.trans: She is my classmate in the same class.
Respect your classmates at school.

meanings.note: Singular noun of unity with ta marbuta; collective noun is زهر (flowers). Also used for cauliflower in Levantine food contexts.

examples.text: في زهرة بيضا مرسومة على غلاف الكتاب.
examples.trans: There is a white flower drawn on the cover of the book.
The garden is full of colourful blossoms in spring.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أزواج.

examples.text: الزوجين دخلوا غرفة ستة قبل ساعة.
examples.trans: The couple checked into room six an hour ago.
They booked a quiet table for the couple.

meanings.note: Extremely common Levantine preposition meaning 'like' or 'similar to'.

examples.trans: You are like my brother.

examples.text: ريحة الزيزفون زي ريحة الربيع بالقرية.
examples.trans: The scent of linden is like the scent of spring in the village.

meanings.note: Male given name, here referring to Rami's older brother.

examples.text: زياد بيساعد أخوه الصغير بحسابات المقهى.
examples.trans: Ziad helps his younger brother with the café's accounts.

examples.text: اسأل زياد وين حط الفواتير الشهرية.
examples.trans: Ask Ziad where he put the monthly invoices.

meanings.note: Placed directly after a noun in Jordanian to mean 'extra' (قطع زيادة extra pieces, الدرج الزيادة the extra stairs).

examples.trans: I brought two extra chairs for the courtyard.
I put a little extra mint in the tea.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of زار ('to visit').

examples.trans: Your brother's visit made us very happy today.
They moved the date of the visit forward to Wednesday.

meanings.note: Usually implies olive oil in Jordan unless specified otherwise, but used for all oils.

examples.trans: Put oil and thyme on the bread.

examples.text: دهنا القالب بشوية زيت زيتون نضيف.
examples.trans: We greased the pan with a little clean olive oil.

meanings.note: Collective noun for olives, iconic to Jordanian tables and courtyards.

examples.text: فطور الصبح ما بيكمل بدون زيت وزيتون أخضر.
examples.trans: Morning breakfast isn't complete without olive oil and green olives.

examples.text: شجرة الزيتون بآخر الحارة عمرها مية سنة.
examples.trans: The olive tree at the end of the lane is a hundred years old.

meanings.note: Aromatic tree whose dried blossoms are brewed as soothing herbal tea across Jordan and the Levant.

examples.text: سعاد زرعت شجرة زيزفون جنب البوابة الشرقية.
examples.trans: Suad planted a linden tree beside the eastern gate.

examples.text: شاي الزيزفون الدافي بريح الأعصاب بالليل.
examples.trans: Warm linden tea soothes the nerves at night.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بزرع, بيزرع).

examples.trans: Did you plant these herbs with your own hands?
We planted jasmine and mint in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسأل, بيسأل).

examples.trans: Ask him what his name is on the phone!
I came down to ask about the sink water.

meanings.note: Often used as a cognate object with سأل (سألتك سؤال 'she asked you a question').

examples.trans: I have just one question.
The question was very easy.

meanings.note: With لـ + الـ, becomes للسائق ('to the bus driver').

examples.trans: I told the driver to wait for me.
The bus driver arrived on time.

meanings.note: Ordinal adjective on the faa'il pattern corresponding to سبعة (seven); inflects for feminine سابعة.

examples.text: المخبز القديم موجود بالشارع السابع عاليمين.
examples.trans: The old bakery is on the seventh street on the right.

examples.text: هاي المرة السابعة اللي بنعد فيها الخطوات.
examples.trans: This is the seventh time we count the steps.

meanings.note: Used in the mild exclamation يا ساتر! ('goodness! / heaven forbid!').

examples.trans: Goodness, I nearly dropped the glass!
Goodness, what heavy rain outside!

meanings.note: Hollow verb (يسيح / بيسيح). Used for ice melting, chocolate softening, or ink smearing in water.

examples.text: حبر القلم بيسيح إذا اجت عليه مي.
examples.trans: Pen ink runs if water gets on it.
The butter melted in the hot pan.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.en: plain; solid-coloured; without pattern or sugar
meanings.note: Invariable adjective used after nouns for plain paper, fabric, or unsweetened coffee (قهوة سادة).

examples.text: جبت ورق سادة عشان الرسم يبين.
examples.trans: I brought plain paper so the drawing shows clearly.

examples.text: بدي فنجان قهوة سادة لو سمحت.
examples.trans: I'd like a cup of plain black coffee, please.

meanings.note: Describes light, sun, or colors that are bright and radiant.

examples.trans: The sun is shining bright today.

examples.text: الشمس ساطعة عالبلكونة من الصبح بدري.
examples.trans: The sun has been bright on the balcony since early morning.

meanings.note: Traditional Levantine craft title formed from ساعة ('watch/clock') + occupational suffix ـاتي.

examples.text: استعرت مفتاح صغير من جارنا الساعاتي بالحارة.
examples.trans: I borrowed a tiny wrench from our watchmaker neighbour down the lane.
A watchmaker trains his hand for precision and patience.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: I've been waiting for you for an hour.

examples.text: المكتبة بتفتح كمان ساعة، خلينا نستنى بالحديقة.
examples.trans: The library opens in another hour; let us wait in the garden.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بساعد, بيساعد).

examples.trans: He will surely love to help us!
We helped the guest carry her suitcase.

meanings.note: Imperative plural verb meaning 'help me!'.

examples.trans: Guys, help me lift the table.
Help me arrange the cards in order by the numbers.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; ساعي البريد means 'postman / courier'. Plural: سعاة.

examples.trans: The postman brought a thick envelope.
I handed the signature to the mail carrier.

meanings.note: From سكت, to fall silent: a person who says nothing, or a thing that makes no sound.

examples.trans: Why are you so quiet today? Is something wrong?
The phone has been silent since the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ساكنة, plural: ساكنين).

examples.trans: Does your older brother live here in Amman?
We used to live on Jasmine Street years ago.

meanings.note: Warm Jordanian word; plural سواليف (sawaaliif) means relaxed afternoon chats and stories.

examples.text: سواليف العصر مع كاسة شاي ما بتمل منها.
examples.trans: You never tire of afternoon conversation over a glass of tea.
We sat in the courtyard and the warm stories began.

meanings.note: Form III verb (بسامح / سامح). سامحني / سامحوا means 'forgive me / excuse me'.

examples.text: سامحوا صوتي التعبان من السفر الطويل.
examples.trans: Forgive my tired voice from the long trip.

examples.text: سامحني يا معلم، ما كان قصدي.
examples.trans: Forgive me, boss, I did not mean to.

meanings.note: Active participle of سمع ('to hear'), standard in Jordanian for 'can you hear?' (سامعني؟).

examples.trans: I hear you clearly on the phone.
Do you hear the sound of a car outside the gate?

meanings.note: Active participle used as 'I hear' or 'hearing' for a feminine subject.

examples.trans: I hear a strange sound.

examples.text: أنا سامعة صوت طنين نحل قريب من الشباك.
examples.trans: I hear the sound of bees buzzing near the window.

meanings.note: Colloquial pronunciation of 'saa'il', meaning liquid.

examples.trans: This detergent is liquid, not powder.

examples.text: العسل السايل بنصب بسهولة على وجه الكيكة.
examples.trans: Runny honey pours easily over the top of the cake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسباب.

examples.trans: I chose the neighbourhood for a family reason.
There is no reason to worry at all.

meanings.note: Primary weekday meaning is Saturday (يوم السبت); as a rural/Levantine noun can also mean a woven basket.

examples.text: سوق العسل بنفتح كل يوم سبت الصبح.
examples.trans: The honey market opens every Saturday morning.

examples.text: السبت الجاي رح نروح نجمع التوت من المزرعة.
examples.trans: Next Saturday we will go pick berries from the farm.

meanings.note: Construct cardinal numeral used directly before masculine or feminine counted plural nouns (e.g., سبع ورقات).

examples.text: مشينا سبع خطوات وبعدين لفينا شمال.
examples.trans: We walked seven steps and then turned left.

examples.text: في سبع بطاقات مخبية جوا العلبة.
examples.trans: There are seven cards hidden inside the tin.

meanings.note: Numeral 'seven' (عالسبعة 'at seven o'clock').

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
I booked room seven yesterday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسبق, بيسبق).

examples.text: بكرا الصبح رح نسبق المي الباردة!
examples.trans: Tomorrow morning we will beat the cold water!
You beat me to the kitchen by two minutes.

meanings.note: In Amman and Levantine cities, سبيل المي is a public stone drinking fountain.

examples.trans: Wait for me by the stone drinking fountain.

examples.text: سبيل الحارة مبني من حجر أبيض.
examples.trans: The neighbourhood fountain is built of white stone.

meanings.note: Respectful and warm Levantine title for a woman ('Madam / Mrs. / lady').

examples.text: يسلموا إيديكي يا ست سعاد عاللحن الحلو.
examples.trans: Bless your hands, Madam Suad, for the lovely melody.

examples.text: كل ست وشيخ بالحارة معزومين عالافتتاح.
examples.trans: Every lady and elder on the lane is invited to the opening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ستاير.

examples.trans: Open the curtain so we can see the sun.
He peeked at the street from behind the curtain.

meanings.note: The number 6.

examples.trans: I have six brothers.

examples.text: عدينا ستة كراسي خشب حوالين طاولة الساحة.
examples.trans: We counted six wooden chairs around the courtyard table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian spoken number for 16 (adds -er before a counted noun: ستعشر سنة).

examples.trans: I did not rush bar sixteen at all!

examples.text: في ستعشر كرسي فاضي حول الشجرة.
examples.trans: There are sixteen empty chairs around the tree.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سجاد.

examples.trans: We put a blue rug beside the bed.
The wool rug warms the floor.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسجل, بيسجل).

examples.text: سجلنا بالغلط حجزين على غرفة سبعة!
examples.trans: By mistake we booked two reservations into room seven!
I wrote the name down in the big ledger.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سحابات.

examples.trans: The suitcase zipper works great.
Her name is written beside the zipper.

meanings.note: Pull a door, a drawer or a heavy thing; also to withdraw money from a bank.

examples.trans: Pull the door towards you, don't push it.
I took money out of the bank this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سحرية, plural: سحريين).

examples.trans: This is a magical guesthouse in the heart of Amman!
The courtyard at night has a magical atmosphere.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سخانات.

examples.trans: We started the boiler before breakfast.
The boiler room is down in the basement.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سخنة, plural: سخنين).

examples.trans: Drink a glass of hot tea first.
Pour the hot water into the pot.

meanings.note: Describes something hot (like food, water) for feminine nouns.

examples.trans: The water is very hot.

examples.text: انتبهي، الصينية لسه سخنة من الفرن.
examples.trans: Careful, the tray is still hot from the oven.

meanings.note: Traditional Levantine domestic storage loft or overhead cupboard (السدة).

examples.text: خبيت هاد الصندوق من رف السدة.
examples.trans: I saved this box from the attic shelf.
The old suitcases are up in the loft.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسرار.

examples.trans: Rest assured, your secret is safe with us.

examples.text: سر الكيكة الزاكية هو الليمون الطازج.
examples.trans: The secret to tasty cake is fresh lemon.

meanings.note: With ب- forms the very common adverb بسرعة ('quickly / fast').

examples.trans: I always walk fast in the morning.
Your quick wit saved the day!

meanings.note: Used in بكل سرور ('with pleasure!').

examples.trans: With pleasure, please have a seat!
They welcomed us with joy and delight.

meanings.note: From سر, a secret. A secret room is غرفة سرية.

examples.trans: I have a secret plan for the holiday.

examples.text: هاد الرقم سري، لا تحكيه لحدا.
examples.trans: This number is secret, do not tell anyone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سريعة, plural: سريعين).

examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast!
Quick service and a kind smile.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 16; before a counted singular noun it may appear as سطاش or سطاعشر.

examples.text: مدام سعاد رح تكتب السطاش مازورة الناقصة.
examples.trans: Madam Suad is going to write the sixteen missing bars.

examples.text: صفينا سطاش فنجان أبيض على الرف.
examples.trans: We lined up sixteen white cups on the shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سطوح.

examples.trans: We heard the sound of rain on the roof.
From the rooftop we see the hills of Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سطور.

examples.trans: Read me the top line of the letter.
He wrote two short lines on the card.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for a water or paint bucket (plural سطول stuul).

examples.text: جهزنا سطلين مي دافية عشان نغسل الشبابيك.
examples.trans: We got two buckets of warm water ready to wash the windows.

examples.text: انتبه لا يوقع سطل الصابون عن الدرج.
examples.trans: Careful the bucket of soapy water doesn't tip off the step.

meanings.note: Female given name of the retired piano teacher.

examples.text: المس سعاد بتعلمنا العزف على البيانو من خمس سنين.
examples.trans: Ms. Suad has been teaching us to play piano for five years.

examples.text: خالتو سعاد دايماً بتجيب حلويات معها بس تزورنا.
examples.trans: Auntie Suad always brings sweets with her when she visits us.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسعار.

examples.trans: Tonight the room is at half price.
The shop's prices are fair and reasonable.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سعيدة, plural: سعيدين); يومك سعيد means 'have a nice day'.

examples.trans: Have a lovely day, ma'am!

examples.text: رحلة سعيدة ومريحة إن شاء الله.
examples.trans: A happy and comfortable trip, God willing.

meanings.note: كتب السفر are travel books; على سفر means 'away travelling'.

examples.trans: I love travelling by bus.
My brother is away travelling this week.

meanings.note: Feminine noun from سفر ('travel'), meaning 'a trip or journey'.

examples.text: سفرتي لإسطنبول السنة الماضية كانت من أحلى الرحلات.
examples.trans: My trip to Istanbul last year was one of the nicest journeys.

examples.text: السفرة الطويلة بالباص بتعب، بس المناظر بتستاهل.
examples.trans: A long trip by bus is tiring, but the scenery is worth it.

meanings.note: Standard feminine noun (plural سفن) used for large sea-going vessels and sailing ships.

examples.trans: We saw a large ship entering the harbour.
Old ships used to travel by sail.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سقوف.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is high and beautiful.
I slept well under the attic ceiling.

meanings.note: Feminine noun with broken plural سكك; refers especially to railway tracks (سكة الحديد).

examples.text: القطار مشي على سكة نضيفة اليوم.
examples.trans: The train ran on a clear track today.

examples.text: لا تقربوا من سكة القطار وقت العبور.
examples.trans: Don't go near the train track at crossing time.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسكت, بيسكت).

examples.text: حتى جرس غرفة أربعة سكت المسا!
examples.trans: Even room four's bell stayed quiet this evening!

examples.text: الكل سكت لما دق برج الساعة.
examples.trans: Everyone fell silent when the clock tower chimed.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: I like black tea without sugar.
We sprinkled powdered sugar over the cake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسكن, بيسكن).

examples.text: عيلتك سكنت قريب من هون زمان؟
examples.trans: Did your family live near here back then?
They lived on Jasmine Street for twenty years.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a knife. Can be pronounced 'sikkiin' or 'sikkiina'.

examples.trans: Bring the knife so we can cut the cake.

examples.text: قصينا الكيكة بسكينة رفيعة عشان تطلع مرتبة.
examples.trans: We cut the cake with a thin knife so it comes out neat.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسكر, بيسكر).

examples.trans: He said thank you and hung up!
Did you shut off the main water valve?

meanings.note: Used with بـ (بسلاسة 'smoothly / effortlessly').

examples.text: بعد نقطة الزيت، الباب فتح بسلاسة.
examples.trans: After a drop of oil, the door swung open smoothly.

examples.text: نغمة دو بتطلع وبتنزل بكل سلاسة.
examples.trans: The C key rises and falls completely smoothly.

meanings.note: Means peace, safety, and is widely used as a greeting or farewell.

examples.trans: Pass on my greetings to him.

examples.text: سلّم عالجميع وقلهم سلام حار مني.
examples.trans: Greet everyone and give them warm greetings from me.

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سلال.

examples.trans: I put the yellow lemons in the basket.
He tossed the paper into the wastebasket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسلاك.

examples.trans: The old wire needs a slight adjustment.
We checked the bell wire by the door.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سلالم.

examples.trans: He played the musical scale slowly.
He climbed the ladder to fit the bulb.

meanings.note: Female given name belonging to the café's morning baker.

examples.text: سلمى بتخبز الكرواسون والخبز كل يوم الفجر.
examples.trans: Salma bakes the croissants and bread every day at dawn.

examples.text: سلمى جابت صينية كعك طازة للضيوف.
examples.trans: Salma brought a tray of fresh cookies for the guests.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سليمة, plural: سليمين).

examples.trans: Thank goodness your cup is still intact!
All the plates arrived unbroken.

سلّم.gloss: to greet; say hello; hand over

meanings.en: to greet; say hello; hand over
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسلم, بيسلم).

examples.trans: Give my regards to Salma in the kitchen!
We hand the suitcase over to its owner on Friday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سماوات.

examples.trans: The evening sky is clear and calm.
The lanterns are glowing beneath the sky.

meanings.note: Verbal noun (masdar) of سمع ('hear/listen').

examples.text: سماع الموسيقى بهالغرفة الهادية بيرح البال.
examples.trans: Listening to music in this quiet room puts the mind at ease.
We were delighted to hear the good news.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سماعات.

examples.trans: Hand me the phone receiver, please.
He set the handset back down gently.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمح, بيسمح).

examples.trans: Take the guesthouse number, please.
Allow me to pour the orange juice.

meanings.note: Most common in the phrase 'iza samaHt' or 'law samaHt' meaning 'if you please' or 'excuse me'.

examples.trans: Excuse me, where is the bank?

examples.text: لو سمحت، وين رف كتب الطبخ بالمكتبة؟
examples.trans: Excuse me, where is the cookbook shelf in the library?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمع, بيسمع).

examples.trans: Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?
Inside the courtyard we hear the tree leaves.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سميكة, plural: سماك).

examples.text: مين ترك هاد المغلف السميك هون؟
examples.trans: Who left this thick envelope here?
Thick stone walls hold the warmth.

meanings.note: Form II causative of سمع ('to hear'). سمّعونا means 'let us hear / play for us'.

examples.text: سمّعونا أحلى عزف يا غرفة تسعة!
examples.trans: Let us hear the loveliest playing, Room Nine!

examples.text: سمّعنا نغمة ري الوسطانية مرة تانية.
examples.trans: Let us hear middle D one more time.

meanings.note: Takes the thing first and the name after it: بيسموها 'غرفة الشاي' 'they call it the tea room'. Related to اسم, name.

examples.text: سموا البنت ياسمين على اسم ستها.
examples.trans: They named the girl Yasmin after her grandmother.
What do you call this in Arabic?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سنان.

examples.trans: The new brass thread screwed in cleanly.
Be careful not to strip the screw thread.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a year.

examples.trans: This car is this year's model.

examples.text: مرّت سنة كاملة على آخر زيارة للمزرعة.
examples.trans: A whole year has passed since the last visit to the farm.

meanings.note: Shortened in speech to سنتي (dual سنتيين 'two centimetres').

examples.text: قيس المسافة بالمسطرة، لازم تكون عشرة سنتي.
examples.trans: Measure the gap with the ruler—it has to be ten centimetres.

examples.text: كم قميصك بعيد سنتيين بس عن الدهان الرطب!
examples.trans: Your shirt sleeve is only two centimetres from the wet paint!

meanings.note: Transitive verb meaning 'to lean or prop something upright against a wall or arch'.

examples.text: اسند السلم منيح عالحيط قبل ما تطلع.
examples.trans: Prop the ladder firmly against the wall before climbing up.

examples.text: سندنا الكراسي المطوية تحت القوس الحجر.
examples.trans: We leaned the folded chairs under the stone arch.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سنوية, plural: سنويين).

examples.trans: He writes in the annual Amman tourist guide.

examples.text: عندنا صيانة سنوية للسخان قبل الشتا.
examples.trans: We do annual maintenance on the heater before winter.

meanings.note: Likely a typo combining 'years' (sniin) and 'teacher/sir' (ustaaz) without a space.

examples.trans: He has been a teacher at the school for years.

examples.text: إله سنين أستاذ بعلم الرسم والخرايط بالجامعة.
examples.trans: He has been a professor teaching drawing and maps at the university for years.

meanings.note: Warm social verb for staying up at night talking with friends (نسهر طول الليل).

examples.trans: We stayed up until morning yesterday.
We love staying up and chatting together.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'easy to do'.

examples.text: هاي الوصفة سهلة وبتجهز بنص ساعة.
examples.trans: This recipe is easy and comes together in half an hour.

examples.text: سهل نرتب الكراسي بعد ما يخلص الدهان.
examples.trans: It will be easy to arrange the chairs once the painting is done.

meanings.note: Paired with أهلا in the classic welcome أهلا وسهلا! ('may you find family and smooth ground — welcome!').

examples.trans: Welcome! Please come into the courtyard.
A hundred welcomes to you all!

meanings.note: An arrow on a sign or a map; the plural أسهم also means shares in a company.

examples.trans: Follow the arrow to the end of the hallway.
The red arrow points to the door.

meanings.note: Abstract noun from سهل ('easy'); بسهولة means 'easily, with ease'.

examples.trans: The new key turns in the lock easily.

examples.text: كل كرسي بيطوي بسهولة بكبسة وحدة.
examples.trans: Every chair folds easily with a single press.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for 'together'.

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
We drank morning coffee together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Denotes a perimeter wall or stone garden wall around a yard or compound rather than an interior room wall (حيط).

examples.trans: The garden wall is covered with white jasmine.

examples.text: نط القط فوق سور الساحة وهرب.
examples.trans: The cat jumped over the courtyard wall and ran off.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسواق.

examples.text: سوق وسط البلد مليان حركة الصبح.
examples.trans: The downtown market is bustling in the morning.
We bought fresh herbs from the market.

meanings.note: Spoken defective verb meaning 'to be worth' (يسوى / بتسوى). Distinct from سوّى ('to do/make').

examples.text: الراحة بعد التعب بتسوى الدنيا كلها.
examples.trans: Rest after hard work is worth the whole world.
How much is this rug worth in the market?

meanings.note: Past tense Arabic verb سوّى meaning 'to level out' or 'fix'.

examples.text: سوّيت الحجر عند الباب عشان ما حدا يتعثر فيه.
examples.trans: I leveled out the stone by the door so nobody trips over it.
What did you guys do over the holiday last week?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سيئة, plural: سيئين).

examples.trans: I have bad news about the water heater.
The weather outside is not bad today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سياحية, plural: سياحيين).

examples.trans: We bought the Amman tourist guide.
The old quarter is a quiet tourist area.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سيارات.

examples.trans: We heard a car stop outside.

examples.text: ما في صوت سيارات جوا الساحة.
examples.trans: There is no sound of cars inside the courtyard.

meanings.note: Masculine noun for 'gentleman' or formal 'Mr.' (plural: سادة).

examples.text: هادا السيد الوقور جنب البوابة وسيم كتير!
examples.trans: That distinguished gentleman by the gate is very handsome!
Mr. Mazen welcomes guests with a smile.

meanings.en: lady; madam; respectful title for a woman
meanings.note: Feminine counterpart of سيد ('sir/Mr.'); plural سيدات.

examples.text: أهلاً وسهلاً بالضيوف، تفضلوا يا سيدات.
examples.trans: Welcome guests, please come in, ladies.

examples.text: سألت سيدة بالشارع عن مكان الصيدلية.
examples.trans: I asked a lady in the street where the pharmacy is.

meanings.note: Used in جاب سيرة ('to bring up / mention a topic').

examples.text: لا حدا يجيب سيرة الشغل عالعشا!
examples.trans: Nobody bring up work at dinner!
Everyone speaks kindly of you.

meanings.note: Intransitive verb سخن ('to heat up / become warm'), agreeing with الطنجرة.

examples.text: بس تسخن الطنجرة شوي، حط البصل والزيت.
examples.trans: Once the pot heats up a little, put in the onions and oil.

examples.text: المي سخنَت بسرعة لأنو الغاز عالي.
examples.trans: The water warmed up quickly because the burner is high.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسخن, بيسخن).

examples.trans: The brass pipe started getting hot right away!
The water heated up within five minutes.

meanings.note: Used in everyday speech inside the fixed phrase إن شاء الله ('God willing / hopefully').

examples.trans: Everything alright, hopefully?
You will arrive safely, God willing.

meanings.note: Used both as a masculine adjective ('young traveller' مسافر شاب) and a noun ('young man'). Feminine: شابة, plural: شباب.

examples.text: أسبوع شتا حبس مسافر شاب هون.
examples.trans: A rainy week trapped a young traveller here.
The young people helped carry the chairs to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Heavy delivery truck or freight lorry.

examples.text: فكرنا صوت الرعد شاحنة كبيرة مارة بالشارع.
examples.trans: We thought the rumble of thunder was a big truck passing down the street.

examples.text: الشاحنات الكبيرة ما بتدخل الحارة بالليل.
examples.trans: Heavy trucks do not drive into the neighbourhood at night.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.en: to take part; participate; share something with
meanings.note: Form III verb (بشارك / شارك). Often followed by بـ ('participate in') or مع ('share with').

examples.trans: All the neighbours took part in hanging the lanterns.
Share your new idea for the project with us.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: شاشات.

examples.trans: Let me look at the tablet screen.
The numbers are clear on the screen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian tool word used in carpentry and household repairs; plural شواكيش.

examples.text: جيب الشاكوش من صندوق العدة عشان نثبت اللوح.
examples.trans: Bring the hammer from the toolbox so we can fasten the board.

examples.text: سمعنا صوت شاكوش بطرق بالورشة تحت.
examples.trans: We heard the sound of a hammer knocking in the workshop below.

شال.gloss: to carry away; remove; lift out

meanings.en: to carry away; remove; lift out
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشيل, بيشيل).

examples.text: بنقدر نشيل أربع صناديق بخمس دقايق.
examples.trans: We can move four boxes in five minutes.
Sparkling water lifts the stain right out.

meanings.note: Active participle plural form of the verb 'to smell'. Used like 'are you smelling...'.

examples.trans: Are you guys smelling something burning?

examples.text: شامين ريحة القرفة واللوز المحمص بالممر؟
examples.trans: Do you smell the scent of cinnamon and roasted almonds in the hall?

meanings.note: A staple beverage in Jordanian culture, typically served with mint or sage.

examples.trans: I like to drink tea after lunch.

examples.text: صبينا كاسات شاي ساخن مع ورق النعناع.
examples.trans: We poured glasses of hot tea with mint leaves.

meanings.note: Active participle of شاف ('to see'), standard in Jordanian for 'I see / do you see?'.

examples.text: شايفة رسمة المفتاح الدهبي فوق الباب!
examples.trans: I see the painted golden key above the door!
Do you see the yellow light in the attic window?

meanings.note: Extremely common word for a young man, guy, or youth.

examples.trans: This young man is very respectful.
A kind young man who works at the library helped us.

meanings.note: Plural of 'shabb'. Often used to address a group of people collectively, like 'guys'.

examples.trans: Come on guys, let's go.

examples.text: يا شباب، تعالوا نبدأ التذوق قبل ما تبرد الكيكة.
examples.trans: Guys, come start the tasting before the cake gets cold.

meanings.note: Plural of 'shubbaak' (window).

examples.trans: Open the windows so the room airs out.

examples.text: فتحنا كل شبابيك المطبخ عشان يدخل هوا بارد.
examples.trans: We opened all the kitchen windows so cool air would come in.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شبابيك.

examples.trans: The window overlooks the courtyard tree.
We painted the wooden shutters in summer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شباك.

examples.trans: The cake is cooling on the wire rack now.
We fitted an iron grille on the window.

meanings.note: Form I transitive verb taking the thing resembled directly without a preposition.

examples.trans: This cup looks like my grandmother's cup.
The two boys resemble each other in their laugh.

meanings.note: In Jordanian Arabic, شتا means both the winter season and rain.

examples.trans: Winter water is very cold in the morning.
I love the sound of winter rain on the window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: شتويات.

examples.trans: This house has lived through eighty winters.
Last winter was cold and long.

meanings.note: Levantine Arabic verb for 'to rain', derived from شتا ('winter/rain').

examples.text: الدنيا عم بتشتّي برا، خد معك شمسية!
examples.trans: It's raining outside—take an umbrella with you!

examples.text: تشرين الثاني بلّش تشتّي فيه بغزارة بعمان.
examples.trans: In November it started raining heavily in Amman.

meanings.note: Common adjective describing boldness or bravery; plural is broken شجعان.

examples.text: طارق ولد شجاع ما بخاف من العتمة.
examples.trans: Tariq is a brave boy who is not afraid of the dark.

examples.text: هاي خطوة شجاعة كتير من فريق المطبخ.
examples.trans: That is a very courageous step from the kitchen team.

meanings.note: Singulative شجرة ('a tree', feminine), collective شجر ('trees').

examples.trans: We placed the table under the old tree.
We hear the rustle of tree leaves in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a tree.

examples.trans: We planted an olive tree in the garden.

examples.text: قعدنا تحت شجرة الزيزفون الكبيرة بالساحة.
examples.trans: We sat under the big linden tree in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أشخاص.

examples.trans: The person left a small note on the door.
The table seats four people.

meanings.note: Adverbial accusative of شخصي (personal), often placed after a pronoun for emphasis (أنا شخصيا).

examples.text: أنا شخصيا بفضل كيكة العسل واللوز.
examples.trans: I personally prefer the honey and almond cake.
The manager handed us the invitation personally in the lobby.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشد, بيشد).

examples.trans: Wait ten seconds while I tighten this screw.
Pull the corner of the sheet nice and tight.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from شراع ('sail'): قارب شراعي ('sailboat').

examples.text: رسمت قارب شراعي صغير على الفانوس.
examples.trans: I drew a small sailboat on the lantern.
Sailing vessels depend on the wind.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشرب, بيشرب).

examples.trans: Drink hot tea first.

examples.text: شرب كل نقطة من شوربة الخضار.
examples.trans: He drank every drop of the vegetable soup.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشرح, بيشرح).

examples.trans: Explain the story to him in your calm voice.
He explained the legal clause to us simply.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شراشف.

examples.trans: We spread a clean white cloth on the table.
I brought fresh sheets from the closet.

meanings.note: With ب- forms بشرط ('on condition that / provided that').

examples.text: بجي معكم بشرط نشرب شاي سوا.
examples.trans: I will come with you provided we drink tea together.
We read all the conditions of the contract clearly.

meanings.note: Abstract noun meaning honour or prestige, also appearing in polite expressions like إلنا الشرف (the honour is ours).

examples.trans: Your visit to our house is a great honour for us.

examples.text: أعطانا كلمة شرف إنه يحفظ السر.
examples.trans: He gave us his word of honour to keep the secret.

meanings.note: Standard feminine noun (plural شرفات) for a balcony or upper open terrace; everyday Amman speech also uses برندة or سطح.

examples.text: شربنا الشاي على الشرفة وقت الغروب.
examples.trans: We drank tea on the terrace at sunset.
We hung colourful lanterns on the upper rooftop terrace.

meanings.note: Cardinal direction noun; frequently appears in directional phrases like للشرق or باتجاه الشرق.

examples.text: اتجهنا ناحية الشرق مع ضو الشمس الصبح.
examples.trans: We headed toward the east with the morning sunlight.
The big window faces directly east.

meanings.note: Names both wooden shutter slats/louvres and thin slices of bread or lemon.

examples.text: دهنا شرائح الشيش الخشب وحدة ورا التانية.
