examples.trans: The suitcase's color is dark blue.
A dark grey wool coat.

meanings.note: Colloquial Levantine noun describing hazy vision, mist, or blurred ink.

examples.text: الدنيا الصبح كانت كلها غباش من الضباب.
examples.trans: Everything this morning was blurry with fog.

examples.text: لو في غباش بالعدسة، امسحها بمنديل ناعم.
examples.trans: If there is haze on the lens, wipe it with a soft cloth.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: Wipe the dust off the brass plate.
The shelves are clean with no dust on them.

meanings.note: The main meal of the day in Jordan, usually eaten in the early afternoon.

examples.trans: What's for lunch today?
We have lunch together after work.

meanings.note: Everyday carpenter's word (ghira) for wood or craft glue.

examples.text: نقطة غرا خشب ناشف بتثبت اللباد بمكانه.
examples.trans: A dab of dry wood glue holds the felt right in place.

examples.text: سكر علبة الغرا منيح عشان ما تنشف.
examples.trans: Close the glue bottle tightly so it doesn't dry out.

meanings.note: Can mean a unit of mass (gram) or deep love/infatuation depending on context.

examples.trans: I want a hundred grams of cheese.

examples.text: الوصفة بتحتاج ميتين غرام طحين وتمانين غرام زبدة.
examples.trans: The recipe needs two hundred grams of flour and eighty grams of butter.

meanings.note: Cardinal direction noun paired with شرق (east); used with directional prepositions like للغرب.

examples.text: البوابة التانية بتطلع على جهة الغرب.
examples.trans: The second gate faces toward the west.

examples.text: امشوا عشر خطوات للغرب بتلاقوا العلامة.
examples.trans: Walk ten steps to the west and you will find the mark.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective formed from غرب (west); feminine غربية.

examples.text: القاعة الغربية فيها شبابيك كبيرة ومشمسة.
examples.trans: The western hall has big sunny windows.

examples.text: زرعنا النعناع بالركن الغربي من الحديقة.
examples.trans: We planted mint in the western corner of the garden.

meanings.note: Masculine noun whose plural أغراض ('things, belongings, groceries') is one of the commonest words in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Put your things in the cupboard beside the door.
I have a quick errand in the market and I'll be back.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: The bedroom is very spacious.

examples.text: غرفة المكتبة هادية ومليانة كتب خرائط.
examples.trans: The library room is quiet and full of atlases.

meanings.note: Masculine verbal noun (from غرب 'to set/go west'). Commonly paired with وقت ('time') or قبل ('before'): قبل الغروب.

examples.trans: We need to finish a few minutes before sunset.

examples.text: السما بتصير وردية وقت الغروب بعمان.
examples.trans: The sky turns pink at sunset in Amman.

meanings.note: As an adjective غريب / غريبة means 'strange, odd'; as a noun (plural غرباء) it means 'stranger(s)'.

examples.trans: I heard a strange metallic knock at night.
Why would he leave his bag with strangers?

meanings.note: Standard collocation with rain: مطر غزير ('heavy downpour').

examples.text: نزل مطر غزير طول الليل وغسل الشجر.
examples.trans: Heavy rain fell all night and washed the trees clean.

examples.text: النشرة بتتوقع مطر غزير لبكرا الضهر.
examples.trans: The forecast predicts heavy rain until tomorrow noon.

meanings.note: Wash dishes, clothes, windows or your hands.

examples.trans: I washed the cups and put them on the shelf.
Wash your hands before eating.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The clean sheets are in the linen closet.
We hung the laundry in the morning sun.

meanings.note: Leafy branch of a tree or climbing shrub.

examples.text: رفعنا الغصن الأخضر عن شنكل الشباك بلطف.
examples.trans: We gently lifted the green branch off the window latch.

examples.text: عصفور صغير وقف على غصن شجرة الليمون.
examples.trans: A little bird perched on a branch of the lemon tree.

meanings.note: Refers to a lid, cover, or sometimes a blanket.

examples.trans: Where is the pot's lid?

examples.text: رفعنا غطا الصندوق وشوفنا شو جواه.
examples.trans: We lifted the lid of the box and looked at what was inside.

meanings.note: Form II verb meaning 'dip a sponge in water or dunk bread/biscuits in tea'.

examples.text: غطست الإسفنجة بالمي الدافية ومسحت اللوح.
examples.trans: I dipped the sponge in warm water and wiped the pane.

examples.text: بحب أغطس البسكوت بكاسة الشاي السخن.
examples.trans: I love dipping biscuits in a glass of hot tea.

meanings.note: Refers to a book cover, box sleeve, or outer wrapping; plural أغلفة.

examples.text: غلاف الدفتر القديم لونه أزرق باهت.
examples.trans: The cover of the old notebook is a faded blue.

examples.text: حطينا غلاف شفاف عشان نحمي الخريطة.
examples.trans: We put a clear cover on to protect the map.

غلب.gloss: to defeat; to beat; to overcome

meanings.en: to defeat; to beat; to overcome
meanings.note: Form I sound verb meaning to win against or surpass; in Form II غلّب means to trouble or bother someone.

examples.text: كيكة اللوز دايما بتغلب أي حلو تاني بالتذوق.
examples.trans: The almond cake always beats every other dessert at the tasting.

examples.text: مازن غلب أخوه بلعبة الألغاز مرتين.
examples.trans: Mazen beat his brother at the puzzle game twice.

meanings.note: Very Jordanian polite apology: آسف عالغلبة ('sorry for the trouble/hassle').

examples.trans: Sorry for all the trouble today.

examples.text: ولا غلبة ولا شي، أهلا وسهلا!
examples.trans: No trouble at all, you are most welcome!

meanings.note: Used as noun in بالغلط ('by mistake') and عالغلط ('for the mistake'), and invariable predicate 'wrong' (في شي غلط something is wrong).

examples.trans: He took the other suitcase by mistake.
Sorry for the mistake, my apologies.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: غلطانة, plural: غلطانين).

examples.trans: Both of us were in the wrong back then.
Sorry, I had the wrong address.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غلطات.

examples.trans: This is not your fault at all.
We fixed the slip-up in two minutes.

meanings.note: Everyday kitchen verb for boiling liquids.

examples.text: بس تغلي المي، وطّي الغاز وحط الشاي.
examples.trans: Once the water boils, turn down the stove and put in the tea.

examples.text: الحليب غلى وفار عالغاز لأني سهيت عنه.
examples.trans: The milk boiled and overflowed on the stove because I got distracted.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بغلب, بيغلب).

examples.trans: Please do not trouble yourself on our account!
Sorry if I put you to trouble today.

meanings.en: to wrap; to cover; to seal in a cover
meanings.note: Form II verb from root غ-ل-ف (same root as غلاف 'cover/envelope').

examples.trans: We wrapped it in wax paper.
We need to wrap the gift before the party.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The mystery story was finally solved!
I enjoy novels with a bit of mystery.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بغمض, بيغمض).

examples.trans: Close your eyes and taste the cake!
She closed her eyes and listened to the rain.

meanings.note: Describes a wealthy person as well as rich flavours, colours, or musical tones (طعم غني 'rich taste').

examples.text: عسل الجبل طعمه غني ودافي مع الشاي.
examples.trans: Mountain honey has a rich, warm taste with tea.

examples.text: خشب الجوز بيعطي البيانو صوت غني.
examples.trans: Walnut wood gives the piano a rich sound.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for singing; a song is أغنية.

examples.trans: My grandmother sings while she cooks.
We all sang at his birthday.

meanings.note: After negation, ما ... غير means 'only / nothing except'.

examples.text: ما معي غير المعطف اللي علي!
examples.trans: I have nothing with me except the coat I have on!
There are only two valves on the shelf.

meanings.note: Unit noun of collective غيم ('clouds'); plural غيوم. Frequently used in Levantine speech alongside سحابة.

examples.text: القمر عم بيطلع من ورا غيمة خفيفة.
examples.trans: The moon is peeking out from behind a light cloud.

examples.text: اليوم السما صافية وما فيها ولا غيمة.
examples.trans: Today the sky is clear with not a single cloud.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بغير, بيغير).

examples.trans: Rami changed his shirt three times!
We gave him a discount because we changed the room.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بغلط, بيغلط).

examples.text: لما يغلط بنغمة بيانو كان يكشر!
examples.trans: Whenever he missed a piano note, he would frown!

examples.text: كل واحد ممكن يغلط بأول يوم.
examples.trans: Anyone can make a mistake on the first day.

meanings.note: Used mostly in formal contexts, but occasionally spills into educated colloquial speech to mean 'then it is' or 'because it'.

examples.trans: If you study, then indeed you will succeed.

examples.text: إذا اتبعنا البوصلة، فإنه رح نوصل للبوابة بسهولة.
examples.trans: If we follow the compass, then indeed we will reach the gate easily.

meanings.note: The Levantine everyday verb for entering a room or building (فوت! 'come in!'), where formal Arabic says دخل.

examples.trans: Come in, the door is open.
We went into the restaurant at eight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: فواتير.

examples.trans: The shopkeeper gave me a receipt and change.
We sorted all the invoices in the drawer.

meanings.note: Feminine verb agreeing with non-human plural الدفاتر, from فاز ('to win').

examples.text: فريقنا فاز بالمباراة النهائية باللحظة الأخيرة!
examples.trans: Our team won the final match at the last moment!

examples.text: الدفاتر المرسومة بإيدهم فازت بالجائزة الأولى.
examples.trans: The notebooks they drew by hand won first prize.

meanings.en: interval; gap; break or divider between items
meanings.note: Masculine noun (plural فواصل) from فصل ('to separate'). Used for regular spacing along a line or a short pause.

examples.text: اترك فاصل متساوي بين كل فانوس والتاني.
examples.trans: Leave an even interval between each lantern and the next.

examples.text: خدنا فاصل قصير قبل ما نكمل الشغل.
examples.trans: We took a short break before continuing the work.

meanings.note: Used to describe an empty container or a person who has free time.

examples.trans: I am free today in the afternoon.

examples.text: الرف الفوقاني فاضي، بنقدر نحط العلبة عليه.
examples.trans: The top shelf is empty; we can put the tin on it.

meanings.note: Idiomatic Arabic colour modifier (أصفر فاقع 'bright lemon yellow', أخضر فاقع 'vivid green').

examples.text: لون الليمون الأصفر الفاقع طالع حلو جنب الأخضر.
examples.trans: The bright lemon-yellow colour looks great next to the green.

examples.text: ما بدنا لون فاقع، بدنا أخضر هادي متل الغابة.
examples.trans: We don't want a flashy shade—we want a calm forest green.

meanings.note: Active participle of فكر used as a stative predicate meaning 'remembers' (أنا فاكر 'I remember').

examples.trans: Do you remember where we put the keys?

examples.text: كلنا فاكرين القصة اللي حكيتها زمان.
examples.trans: We all remember the story you told back then.

meanings.note: Active participle of فلت ('to slip loose'): feminine فالتة, plural فالتين.

examples.text: انتبه، في حبل فالت من الجهة اليمين.
examples.trans: Careful, there is a loose rope on the right side.

examples.text: عقدنا كل الخيوط الفالتة قبل ما يطيروا.
examples.trans: We tied all the loose threads before they blew away.

meanings.note: Musical loanword (from French valse) for a triple-time piano or orchestral waltz.

examples.text: عزفت سعاد فالس هادي بغرفة القزاز.
examples.trans: Suad played a gentle waltz in the sunroom.

examples.text: عنوان الورقة القديمة هو فالس الساحة.
examples.trans: The title on the old sheet is Courtyard Waltz.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فوانيس.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns are lit in the courtyard.
We hung a brass lantern by the entrance.

meanings.note: Invariable culinary loanword treated grammatically as feminine in Jordanian recipes.

examples.text: حطي معلقة فانيليا صغيرة على خليط الكيك.
examples.trans: Put a small spoonful of vanilla into the cake batter.

examples.text: ريحة الفانيليا طالعة من المطبخ للدور التاني.
examples.trans: The scent of vanilla is drifting from the kitchen to the second floor.

meanings.note: Active participle of فات (to enter), agreeing with نسمة.

examples.text: في نسمة هوا باردة فايتة من الشباك المفتوح.
examples.trans: There's a cool breeze coming in through the open window.

examples.text: أنا فايت عالسوبرماركت، بدك إشي أجيبه معي؟
examples.trans: I'm heading into the supermarket—do you want me to pick up anything?

meanings.note: Colloquial pronunciation of فائز with glide -y- replacing medial hamza; also serves as a predicate adjective.

examples.text: الفايز بالمسابقة رح ياخد علبة شوكولاتة.
examples.trans: The winner of the contest will get a box of chocolates.
We congratulated the winners at the end of tasting day.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun; فتحة قفل means 'keyhole'. Plural: فتحات.

examples.trans: There is a small keyhole on the front.
Air is coming through the window opening.

فتحت.gloss: I opened / you (m) opened / she opened

meanings.en: I opened / you (m) opened / she opened
meanings.note: Past tense verb meaning 'opened', conjugated for 1st person, 2nd person masc, or 3rd person fem.

examples.trans: I opened the window so the house airs out.

examples.text: سلمى فتحت الشباك الكبير عشان تشم الورد.
examples.trans: Salma opened the big window to smell the roses.

meanings.note: With demonstrative هـ + الـ, هالفترة means 'during this period / right now'.

examples.trans: I'm very busy these days.
A hard period passed over us.

meanings.note: Charming colloquial Jordanian word for a tiny crumb or morsel.

examples.text: ما ضل ولا فتفوتة خبز بالصينية، أكلوها كلها!
examples.trans: Not even a single crumb of bread was left on the tray—they ate it all!

examples.text: في فتفوتة سكر عالطاولة، امسحها لو سمحت.
examples.trans: There's a tiny bit of sugar on the table—wipe it off, please.

meanings.note: Sets up an unexpected turn in a story (فجأة ليان إجت).

examples.trans: Suddenly everyone in the classroom went quiet.
She appeared in front of me suddenly.

meanings.note: Early pre-sunrise morning (الفجر), prime baking hour in Levantine bakeries.

examples.text: الخبازين بيصحوا قبل الفجر عشان يخبزوا العجين.
examples.trans: Bakers wake up before dawn to bake the dough.

examples.text: هوا الفجر بعمان بيكون بارد ومنعش كتير.
examples.trans: Dawn air in Amman is crisp and deeply refreshing.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفحص, بيفحص).

examples.trans: Tariq will inspect the cellar right away.
We checked the heater and pipes this morning.

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for charcoal (for grilling or sketching); a single piece is فحمة.

examples.trans: A quick charcoal sketch will do.
We lit the charcoal for grilling in the garden.

meanings.note: Handcrafted fired clay vessels and cups, a staple of Jordanian and Levantine street markets.

examples.text: اشترينا إبريق وفناجين من بسطة الفخار.
examples.trans: We bought a pitcher and cups from the pottery stall.

examples.text: المي ببريق الفخار بتضل باردة بالصيف.
examples.trans: Water in a clay pitcher stays cool in summer.

meanings.note: Prepositional adverbial phrase meaning 'with pride / proudly'.

examples.text: الأم اتطلّعت على بنتها بفخر كبير يوم التخرج.
examples.trans: The mother looked at her daughter with great pride on graduation day.

examples.text: عرضت شغلها بفخر قدام كل الضيوف.
examples.trans: She presented her work proudly in front of all the guests.

meanings.note: Takes بـ ('proud of someone or something').

examples.text: أنا فخور فيكم واحد واحد عالشغل المتقن.
examples.trans: I'm proud of every single one of you for the careful work.

examples.text: نور كانت فخورة بلوحة البوابة اللي رسمتها.
examples.trans: Nour was proud of the gate sign she lettered.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: Strawberry jam is sweet and delicious.
We bought fresh strawberries from the market.

meanings.note: Idiomatic Jordanian exclamation فرجت! ('relief has arrived! / we are saved!').

examples.trans: We are saved! The hot water is back!
Things tighten up and then work out.

meanings.note: Classic Levantine everyday verb for 'to show' (فرجيني 'show me!').

examples.trans: Show the shopkeeper this brass valve.
Let me show you my real work!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفرح, بيفرح).

examples.trans: Let the two brothers enjoy their Friday!
We were overjoyed at the good news.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: فرحات.

examples.trans: His eyes shone with joy!
The family's joy is beyond words.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفرد, بيفرد).

examples.text: افرد كتافك يا رامي وخد نفس!
examples.trans: Square your shoulders, Rami, and take a breath!
We spread the white tablecloth over the table.

فرش.gloss: to spread; lay out (cloth or light)

meanings.en: to spread; lay out (cloth or light)
meanings.note: Used literally for spreading a tablecloth or rug and figuratively for warm light spreading across a room.

examples.text: فرشت سلمى شراشف بيضا عالطاولات الخشب.
examples.trans: Salma spread white cloths over the wooden tables.

examples.text: ضو الصبح بيفرش دفا حلو عالساحة.
examples.trans: Morning light spreads lovely warmth across the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for a paintbrush, hairbrush, or pastry brush.

examples.text: غسلنا الفرشايات بمي دافية أول ما خلصنا دهان.
examples.trans: We washed the brushes in warm water right after finishing the painting.

examples.text: لا ترفع الإيد اللي ماسكة الفرشاية الخضرا!
examples.trans: Don't lift the hand that's holding the green paintbrush!

meanings.note: Masculine noun used both literally for tree branches and figuratively for shop branches. Plural: فروع.

examples.trans: Let's leave it by the almond branch.

examples.text: هاد الفرع قريب من وسط البلد.
examples.trans: This branch is close to downtown.

meanings.note: Everyday noun meaning 'difference' or 'gap' in time or amount.

examples.text: شو الفرق بين القهوة العربية والقهوة التركية؟
examples.trans: What's the difference between Arabic coffee and Turkish coffee?

examples.text: وصلنا بفرق خمس دقايق بس قبل ما يسكر الباب.
examples.trans: We arrived just five minutes apart before the door closed.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine kitchen verb for chopping vegetables or herbs.

examples.text: زياد بيقشر البصل وبيفرم الجزر للشوربة.
examples.trans: Ziad peels the onions and chops the carrots for the soup.

examples.text: فرمت ضمة بقدونس طازة فوق الصحن.
examples.trans: I chopped a fresh bunch of parsley over the dish.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أفران.

examples.text: لفائف القرفة طلعت من الفرن هلا.
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.
The bakery down the street bakes in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: فرنسية, plural: فرنسيين).

examples.trans: We made French-style eggs.
Hot French bread with butter.

meanings.note: The word for oven with the 1st person possessive suffix.

examples.trans: My oven is broken and I need to fix it.

examples.text: فرني بسخن بسرعة وبخبز الكيكة بانتظام.
examples.trans: My oven heats up quickly and bakes the cake evenly.

meanings.note: Masculine Arabic noun for a team or crew.

examples.text: فريق الصيانة خلص تصليح السقف قبل العصر.
examples.trans: The maintenance crew finished repairing the roof before afternoon.

examples.text: انضميت لفريق الكشافة بالمدرسة هاد الفصل.
examples.trans: I joined the scout team at school this semester.

meanings.note: In Levantine Arabic, a noun for a neighbourhood baker, from فرن ('oven').

examples.text: الفرّان بالحارة عندنا بطلّع المناقيش مقرمشة ولذيذة.
examples.trans: The baker in our neighborhood turns out crispy, delicious manaqish.

examples.text: ودّينا صينية اللحمة عند الفرّان عشان يشويها بالفرن.
examples.trans: We took the meat tray to the neighborhood baker to roast it in his oven.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فساتين.

examples.trans: She folded the dresses and packed them in the suitcase.
The blue dress is neat and comfortable.

meanings.note: Polysemous noun used for a season of the year, a chapter in a book, or a school class; plural فصول.

examples.text: الأرز البري بنجمع بفصل الصيف عادة.
examples.trans: Wild rice is usually harvested in the summer season.

examples.text: اقرأ الفصل الأول من الدفتر قبل ما تكمل.
examples.trans: Read the first chapter of the notebook before continuing.

meanings.note: Used when someone nearly blows a secret in public (كنتي رح تفضحينا 'you were going to expose us').

examples.trans: Lower your voice, don't give us away!
Her look gave everything away.

meanings.note: Mostly heard in من فضلك / من فضلكم, 'please', literally 'from your kindness'.

examples.trans: Excuse me, where is the station?
A glass of water, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: فضولية, plural: فضوليين).

examples.trans: Tariq is twice as curious as we are!
One small curious question, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: فضية, plural: فضيين).

examples.trans: Here is the small silver key to the attic.
An old silver tea tray.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفضي, بيفضي).

examples.text: أنقذت العلبة قبل ما العمال يفضوا البيت.
examples.trans: I saved the box before the movers cleared the house.
We cleared the boxes off the stairs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.
We prepared a warm breakfast for the guests.

meanings.note: Covers both sweet fruit tarts (فطاير ليمون 'lemon tarts') and savoury baked pastries; Levantine plural فطاير.

examples.text: سلمى رح تخبز فطاير ليمون طازة ليوم الجمعة.
examples.trans: Salma is going to bake fresh lemon tarts for Friday.

examples.text: ريحة الفطاير السخنة واصلة لباب النزل.
examples.trans: The aroma of hot pastries reaches the inn door.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: فظيعة, plural: فظيعين).

examples.text: خايف يكتب تقييم فظيع عن النزل!
examples.trans: I am afraid he will write a terrible review of the inn!
The rain outside was awful yesterday.

meanings.note: Adverbial accusative from فعل ('deed'), used to confirm a surprising or welcome fact.

examples.text: فعلا الجو برد كتير بعد المغرب.
examples.trans: Actually, the weather got very cold after sunset.
This work really turned out well crafted.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: فقاعات.

examples.trans: There was an air bubble in the pipe.
Tiny bubbles rose in the boiling water.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: فقرات.

examples.trans: We read all the paragraphs in the contract.
The second paragraph clarifies the law.

meanings.note: Vivid Jordanian verb for losing patience after holding frustration inside (الواحد بيفقع 'a person snaps/bursts').

examples.trans: I'm going to burst from this unfairness.
I burst out laughing at the joke.

meanings.note: Geminate verb for unscrewing hinges, bolts, or panels.

examples.text: طارق فك اللوح الأمامي للبيانو بهدوء.
examples.trans: Tariq unscrewed the front panel of the piano gently.
We took the shutter panels off to sand them in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday market word for coins and small notes given back as change.

examples.text: معك فكة عشرة دنانير لو سمحت؟
examples.trans: Do you have change for ten dinars, please?

examples.text: ضل معنا فكة بكيس الكاش بعد السوق.
examples.trans: We still had coins to spare in the cash pouch after the market.

meanings.note: Form II verb (fakkar): فكرت ما في حدا هون ('I thought nobody was here').

examples.trans: I thought you went home.
Think carefully before deciding.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: أفكار.

examples.trans: I have a great idea for breakfast!
What do you think of this idea?

meanings.note: Imperative verb directed at a female, commanding her to untie, loosen, or take apart something.

examples.trans: Untie the knot slowly.

examples.text: فكي الربطة اللي عالطرد بهدوء بدون ما تقطعيها.
examples.trans: Untie (f.) the knot on the parcel gently without cutting it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفكر, بيفكر).

examples.trans: I thought it was lost when we sold the house!
We thought the matter through calmly.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine noun for bell peppers and mild peppers, contrasted with فلفل (black or hot pepper).

examples.trans: We chopped green and red bell peppers for the salad.

examples.text: سلة الخضار فيها فليفلة طازجة من المزرعة.
examples.trans: The vegetable basket has fresh bell peppers from the farm.

meanings.en: art; artistic skill; branch of art
meanings.note: Masculine noun (plural فنون) covering painting, craft, and fine arts.

examples.text: بشوف إنه هاد العمل فن حقيقي.
examples.trans: I think this piece is genuine art.

examples.text: مازن بحب كل أنواع الفن والرسم.
examples.trans: Mazen loves all kinds of art and drawing.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فناجين.

examples.trans: I set two teacups on the tray.
This is my favourite coffee cup.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فنادق.

examples.trans: All the hotels near the station are full.
The small hotel on our street is quiet.

meanings.en: artistic; technical; relating to art or craft
meanings.note: Nisba adjective from فن ('art'): feminine فنية, plural فنيين. Means 'artistic' with work/taste and 'technical' with problems/details.

examples.text: كل فانوس فيه لمسة فنية مختلفة.
examples.trans: Every lantern has a different artistic touch.

examples.text: صار معنا عطل فني بسيط بس حليناه.
examples.trans: We had a minor technical glitch, but we fixed it.

meanings.note: Used in بدي أفهم القصة كلها ('I want to understand the whole story').

examples.trans: I understood you clearly.
Let me understand what happened.

meanings.note: Form II causative of فات ('enter'): 'carry/bring inside'.

examples.text: تعالوا نفوت الطاولات الخشب قبل ما تشتي.
examples.trans: Come help us carry the wooden tables inside before it rains.

examples.text: فوتنا درفات الشيش عالممر عشان تنشف.
examples.trans: We brought the shutter panels into the hallway to dry.

meanings.note: Adverb 'right away, at once'.

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading out right away!
The hot water came back immediately.

meanings.note: Crisp adverb meaning 'at once / immediately', ending in adverbial tanwin -an.

examples.text: بس سمعت الخبر طلعت من البيت فوراً.
examples.trans: As soon as I heard the news, I left the house immediately.

examples.text: إذا في أي مشكلة بالطلب، خبرني فوراً.
examples.trans: If there's any issue with the order, let me know right away.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: فوط.

examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water.
She wiped the table with a damp cloth.

meanings.note: Used as a preposition or adverb meaning 'above', 'over', or 'upstairs'.

examples.trans: The book is on top of the table.

examples.text: الخريطة معلقة فوق الرف الخشبي بالمكتبة.
examples.trans: The map is hanging above the wooden shelf in the library.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: فوقانية, plural: فوقانيين).

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.
The red ribbon is in the top pocket.

meanings.note: Tempered steel used for piano strings and tools.

examples.text: أوتار البيانو مصنوعة من سلك فولاذ قوي.
examples.trans: Piano strings are made of strong steel wire.

examples.text: هاد المفك راسه فولاذ وما بينحني.
examples.trans: This screwdriver has a steel tip and never bends.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There are many people in the market.

examples.text: في تلات بطاقات ملونة جوا الظرف الكبير.
examples.trans: There are three coloured cards inside the big envelope.

meanings.note: Colloquial spelling of فيزياء (physics), dropping the final hamza.

examples.text: امتحان الفيزيا بكرا، ولازم أراجع كل القوانين اليوم.
examples.trans: The physics exam is tomorrow, and I have to review all the formulas today.

examples.text: أختي بتدرس فيزيا بالجامعة وحابة تكمل ماجستير.
examples.trans: My sister studies physics at the university and wants to do a master's.

meanings.note: With contracted عـ + الـ, عالفيلم means 'to the movie'.

examples.trans: We watched a good movie yesterday.
What's the name of the new movie?

meanings.note: Preposition 'fī' with 3rd person masculine pronoun suffix, often pronounced identically to 'fī' meaning 'there is'.

examples.trans: The box has many things in it.

examples.text: الدرج التاني فيه دفتر صغير عليه خريطة مطوية.
examples.trans: The second drawer has a small notebook in it with a folded map.

meanings.note: Preposition 'fī' with 3rd person feminine pronoun suffix.

examples.text: السيارة مريحة بس ما فيها مكيف.
examples.trans: The car is comfortable but doesn't have AC in it.

examples.text: العلبة الزرقا فيها ثلاث بطاقات وختم شمع.
examples.trans: The blue tin has three cards and a wax seal inside it.

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'fuse'; when one blows, people say الفيوز ضرب.

examples.trans: I changed the fuse and the light came back.
The fuse box is next to the door.

meanings.note: Colloquial Levantine noun for cooling shade under a tree or awning (distinct from the particle/preposition في).

examples.trans: Sit in the shade under the mulberry tree.
The shade in the garden refreshes the spirit in summer.

meanings.note: A written list or a restaurant menu; with -i it is قائمتي, 'my list'.

examples.trans: I wrote the shopping list before the market.
May I have the menu?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقابل, بيقابل).

examples.trans: Did you ask him to meet you here at noon?
We met the neighbours in the courtyard this morning.

قاد.gloss: to lead; to guide; to drive

meanings.en: to lead; to guide; to drive
meanings.note: Form I hollow verb (medial -w-); imperfect يقود / بقود. Used for leading people, teams, or clues leading somewhere.

examples.text: كل دليل قادنا للغرفة اللي ورا المكتبة.
examples.trans: Every clue led us to the room behind the library.

examples.text: سلمى قادت الفريق بحل اللغز بسرعة.
examples.trans: Salma led the team in solving the puzzle quickly.

meanings.note: Active participle of قدر; أنا مش قادرة أستوعب means 'I am unable to take in / process'.

examples.trans: I can't believe the news.
You are definitely able to succeed.

meanings.en: boat; small rowing or sailing craft
meanings.note: Masculine noun (plural قوارب) for a small boat, contrasted with سفينة ('large ship').

examples.text: في قارب شراعي أبيض مرسوم عالورق.
examples.trans: There is a white sailboat drawn on the paper.
We rode a small boat in Aqaba.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقيس, بيقيس).

examples.trans: I measure quietness and acoustics in courtyards.
The shopkeeper measured it against the old valve.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قاسية, plural: قاسيين).

examples.text: كان يعمل حاله قاسي خمس ثواني بس!
examples.trans: He used to act tough for just five seconds!
Amman's winter cold is sometimes harsh.

meanings.note: Defective noun on the faa'i pattern; drops final -y in indefinite nominative/genitive only in formal Arabic, kept as قاضي in Jordanian.

examples.trans: The judge asked to hear the two witnesses' statements.

examples.text: العم سالم معروف عند الجيران كأنه قاضي الحكيم.
examples.trans: Uncle Salem is known among the neighbours like a wise judge.

meanings.note: Refers to the bottom of a pot, pan, or valley.

examples.text: المفتاح وقع في قاع الشنطة تحت الكتب.
examples.trans: The key fell to the bottom of the bag underneath the books.

examples.text: انتبه لا ينحرق الرز بقاع الطنجرة.
examples.trans: Be careful not to let the rice burn at the bottom of the pot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قاعات.

examples.trans: The old hall has clear acoustics.
They met in the meeting hall in the morning.

meanings.note: Literally 'sitting', but widely used as an auxiliary participle to denote continuous present action (like English '-ing').

examples.trans: I am (currently) studying for the exam.

examples.text: مازن قاعد بقرا التعليمات بصوت عالي عشان الكل يسمع.
examples.trans: Mazen is sitting reading the instructions aloud so everyone can hear.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قواعد.

examples.text: أول قاعدة: اشرب شاي سخن الصبح!
examples.trans: Rule one: drink hot tea in the morning!
The work rules here are simple and clear.

meanings.note: Plural form of 'قاعد' (gāʕid), used as a continuous action marker for plural subjects.

examples.trans: The boys are playing in the street.

examples.text: إحنا قاعدين بالحديقة بنستنى الكيكة تبرد عالبلكونة.
examples.trans: We are sitting in the garden waiting for the cake to cool on the balcony.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقول, بيقول).

examples.trans: What does clause fourteen say?
He said thank you and hung up!

meanings.note: Hollow verb meaning 'stand up / get up' (اوعي تقومي 'don't you dare get up!').

examples.text: خليكي قاعدة عالكرسي ولا تقومي أبدا.
examples.trans: Stay seated on the chair and don't get up at all.

examples.text: أبو طارق قام بكير وجهز إبريق الشاي.
examples.trans: Abu Tariq got up early and made a pot of tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قوانين.

examples.trans: Heritage law protects historic houses.
Rami knows building regulations well.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قانونية, plural: قانونيين).

examples.trans: Legal clauses are hard to read.
The lease contract is legal and protected.

meanings.note: Used to describe something directly across from or facing something else.

examples.trans: The shop is exactly opposite our house.

examples.text: المخبز القديم موجود قبال المكتبة بالزبط عالزاوية.
examples.trans: The old bakery is right opposite the library on the corner.

meanings.note: Feminine noun for a brimmed sun hat, straw hat, or cap.

examples.text: البس قبعة قش لما تمشي بالشمس.
examples.trans: Wear a straw hat when you walk in the sun.
Her floral hat is hanging on the door.

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.trans: I have to arrive before five o'clock.

examples.text: غسلنا الفواكه منيح قبل ما نقطعها للتذوق.
examples.trans: We washed the fruit thoroughly before slicing it for the tasting.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أقبية.

examples.trans: The boiler is down in the basement.
He went down to the cellar to get the toolbox.

قد.gloss: as much as; the size of

meanings.en: as much as; the size of
meanings.note: Expresses equal amount or degree: قدنا مرتين ('twice as much as us'), قد ما بقدر ('as much as I can').

examples.trans: Tariq is twice as curious as we are!
I tried to smile as much as I could!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'in front of, before'.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns against the evening sky.
The car is parked in front of the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقدر, بيقدر).

examples.text: بنقدر نقدم زبدة مالحة مع المربى؟
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with jam?

examples.text: ليش ما قدرت تعطيه القطار بإيدك؟
examples.trans: Why could you not hand him the train yourself?

meanings.note: The primary interrogative word for quantity, price, or duration in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: How much does this book cost?

examples.text: قديش ضايل وقت حتى تطلع الصينية التانية من الفرن؟
examples.trans: How much time is left until the second tray comes out of the oven?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Feminine adjective for things (not people) that are old, ancient, or outdated.

examples.trans: I have an old car but it's excellent.

examples.text: لقينا خريطة قديمة مرسومة بالحبر جوا غلاف الدفتر.
examples.trans: We found an old map drawn in ink inside the notebook cover.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word from قد إيه ('how much / how very'), used in exclamations.

examples.text: قديه حق هاد الصحن الخزف لو سمحت؟
examples.trans: How much does this ceramic plate cost, please?

examples.text: قديه حلوة القعدة هون تحت شجرة الليمون!
examples.trans: How lovely it is sitting here under the lemon tree!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقدم, بيقدم).

examples.trans: We serve fresh breakfast every morning.
She served the guests mint tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Feminine command form of قرا ('to read') in spoken Jordanian Arabic.

examples.text: قرا الرسالة مرتين عشان يفهم كل التفاصيل.
examples.trans: He read the letter twice so he could understand every detail.

examples.text: اقري العنوان بصوت عالي عشان الكل يسمع.
examples.trans: Read the title out loud so everyone can hear.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قراءات.

examples.trans: We put a brass reading lamp by the desk.
I love reading in the quiet courtyard.

meanings.note: Standard and spoken noun for a choice or resolution (قرار حكيم 'a wise decision').

examples.text: تغيير الملصقات الليلة كان قرار حكيم بجد.
examples.trans: Replacing the labels tonight was truly a wise decision.

examples.text: أخدنا قرار نفتح الكافيه يوم الأربعا الصبح.
examples.trans: We made the decision to open the café on Wednesday morning.

meanings.note: Verbal noun referring to the act of reading or, more broadly, academic studying.

examples.trans: Reading is very beneficial for the mind.

examples.text: قراية الملاحظات المكتوبة بالهامش ساعدتنا كتير.
examples.trans: Reading the notes written in the margin helped us a great deal.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قروش.

examples.trans: The bill is exact to the last piastre.
A dinar has one hundred piastres.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: The warm scent of cinnamon filled the kitchen.
We ate a cinnamon roll with tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for soon or near.

examples.trans: I will arrive very soon.

examples.text: سلمى رح ترجع قريب ومعها مرطبان العسل الجبلي.
examples.trans: Salma will be back soon bringing the jar of mountain honey.

meanings.note: Adverb 'soon, shortly'.

examples.trans: Its owner will look for it soon.
We will meet soon, hopefully.

meanings.note: Form II verb used both transitively ('bring the lamp closer') and intransitively ('come closer').

examples.text: قرب الفانوس شوي عشان أشوف القفل.
examples.trans: Bring the lantern a little closer so I can see the lock.
We pulled the chairs closer to the big table.

meanings.note: Refers to the material glass, a pane of glass, or sometimes a glass bottle.

examples.text: دير بالك، في قزاز مكسور عالأرض.
examples.trans: Careful, there is broken glass on the floor.

examples.text: انكسر مرطبان القزاز الصغير بس العسل ضل بالصحن.
examples.trans: The small glass jar broke, though the honey stayed in the dish.

meanings.note: Used for dividing tasks across days or cutting pastry into portions.

examples.text: قسمنا الشغل بيننا عشان نخلص بدري.
examples.trans: We divided the work among ourselves so we would finish early.
Salma divided the tart into even slices.

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for woven straw used in hats, baskets, and matting.

examples.trans: We bought a straw basket for fresh bread.
A straw hat is light and comfortable in summer.

meanings.note: Collective noun for fruit peels, citrus zest, or eggshells; single piece is قشرة.

examples.text: بشرنا قشر الليمون فوق خليط الكيكة.
examples.trans: We grated the lemon peel over the cake batter.

examples.text: قشر البرتقال المطبوخ بعطي نكهة غنية بالعسل.
examples.trans: Cooked orange peel gives a rich flavour with honey.

meanings.note: Singulative of collective قشر ('peel, bark, shell'); قشرة الليمونة means 'the skin/zest of the lemon'.

examples.text: قشرة الليمون الأصفر ريحتها قوية وحلوة.
examples.trans: Yellow lemon peel has a strong, sweet scent.

examples.text: بتحط سلمى برش قشرة ليمون بعجينة الكيك.
examples.trans: Salma puts grated lemon peel into the cake batter.

قص.gloss: to cut; snip; trim (with scissors or shears)

meanings.en: to cut; snip; trim (with scissors or shears)
meanings.note: Geminate verb for cutting stems, paper, or tape cleanly.

examples.text: لا تقص عرق الياسمين الأخضر، ارفعه لفوق.
examples.trans: Don't cut the green jasmine stem—lift it upward.
I cut a strip of black tape for the wire.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قصص.

examples.trans: The whole story started with a blue suitcase.
My grandfather used to tell us sweet stories.

meanings.note: Noun used especially with possessive suffixes (قصدي what I mean, قصدك what you mean).

examples.trans: What do you mean by this word?
The meaning is clear and simple.

meanings.note: Adjective for short in length, height, or time.

examples.text: الفيلم كان حلو بس كثير قصير.
examples.trans: The movie was nice but very short.

examples.text: النص المكتوب عالكرت قصير بس معناه واضح جدا.
examples.trans: The text written on the card is short, yet its meaning is crystal clear.

meanings.note: Defective verb (بقضي / قضيت) from root ق-ض-ي, meaning to spend hours, days, or a summer.

examples.text: قضوا الساعات اللي بعد الضهر جوا.
examples.trans: They spent the afternoon hours inside.
We spent the whole summer in Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قطارات.

examples.trans: The grandfather carved a small wooden train.
Children love playing with trains.

meanings.note: Noun of unity from قطر; used both for liquid drops in recipes and eye/nose drops.

examples.text: زدنا قطرة مي زهر على الكريمة.
examples.trans: We added a drop of orange-blossom water to the cream.

examples.text: ما ضل ولا قطرة عسل بقاع المرطبان.
examples.trans: Not a single drop of honey was left at the bottom of the jar.

meanings.note: Past tense Arabic verb meaning 'to cut' or 'interrupt'.

examples.text: الكهربا قطعت بالحارة كلها نص ساعة مبارح.
examples.trans: The power went out in the whole neighborhood for half an hour yesterday.

examples.text: لا تقطع كلامه، خليه يكمل حكايته للأخر.
examples.trans: Don't interrupt him—let him finish his story to the end.

meanings.note: Used to count items, or mean a portion, slice, or spare part.

examples.trans: I want a piece of cake please.

examples.text: كل واحد فينا أخذ قطعة صغيرة من كيكة اللوز.
examples.trans: Each one of us took a small piece of the almond cake.

meanings.note: Refers to the material, plant, or cotton wool used in medicine or cosmetics.

examples.trans: This shirt is one hundred percent cotton.

examples.text: غطينا الخبز السخن بمنديل قطن نضيف عشان يضل طري.
examples.trans: We covered the hot bread with a clean cotton cloth so it stays soft.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقطع, بيقطع).

examples.text: جدي كان يقطع كيكة ليمون دافية.
examples.trans: My grandfather used to slice warm lemon cake.
Salma sliced the hot bread.

meanings.note: Past tense verb meaning to sit down, or sometimes to stay/remain in a place.

examples.trans: He sat on the chair and rested.

examples.text: طارق قعد جنب النافورة يكتب أرقام البطاقات.
examples.trans: Tariq sat beside the fountain writing down the card numbers.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قعدات.

examples.trans: Sitting in the courtyard under the tree is cosy.

examples.text: قعدة الصبح مع القهوة ما بتتعوض.
examples.trans: A morning sit-down with coffee is priceless.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قفال.

examples.trans: The shopkeeper unlocked the padlock in the morning.
We fitted a new brass lock on the closet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قلوب.

examples.trans: My heart is beating fast with joy!
Welcome from the bottom of my heart.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقلق, بيقلق).

examples.text: لا تقلقي يا مدام، هلا بنشوف البطاقة.
examples.trans: Do not worry, ma'am, we will check the tag right now.
We worried a little when the bus ran late.

meanings.note: Levantine adjective on the فَعْلان pattern from root ق-ل-ق; often followed by على ('about').

examples.trans: Why do you look so worried?
We were worried about you the whole way.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; قلم رصاص means 'pencil'. Plural: أقلام.

examples.trans: I found my pen in the jacket pocket.
We write the names with a pencil.

meanings.note: Any fabric; سلك قماش is old cloth-covered electrical wire.

examples.trans: She bought blue fabric for the curtains.
This fabric is very soft.

meanings.note: Singulative of قماش ('fabric'); names a wiping or polishing cloth.

examples.text: جيب شوية مي دافية وقماشة نضيفة لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Bring a little warm water and a clean cloth, please.

examples.text: نشف الخشب بقماشة قطن قبل ما تدهن.
examples.trans: Wipe the wood dry with a cotton cloth before you paint.

meanings.en: moon; also used affectionately for someone radiant
meanings.note: Masculine noun (plural أقمار). Very common in both literal night-sky descriptions and compliments.

examples.trans: The moon is full today and lighting up the sky.

examples.text: الفانوس الأزرق طالع كأنه قمر بالليل.
examples.trans: The blue lantern looks just like a moon at night.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قمصان.

examples.trans: He put on a neat, ironed white shirt.
He changed his shirt twice before the appointment.

meanings.en: hemp fibre; coarse twine used for tying
meanings.note: Masculine collective noun; in Jordan حبل قنب means sturdy natural hemp twine.

examples.text: جبت لفة خيط قنب عشان نربط الزينة.
examples.trans: I brought a roll of hemp twine so we can tie the decorations.

examples.text: القنب أقوى بكتير من الخيط القطن الرفيع.
examples.trans: Hemp cord is much stronger than thin cotton thread.

meanings.en: hanging oil or candle lamp; small lantern
meanings.note: Masculine noun (plural قناديل), traditional Levant term alongside فانوس.

examples.text: ضوّوا قناديل الحوش قبل ما تيجي الناس.
examples.trans: They lit the courtyard lamps before the people arrived.

examples.text: عندي قنديل نحاس قديم من بيت جدي.
examples.trans: I have an old brass oil lamp from my grandfather's house.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قناني.

examples.trans: We bought three bottles of fresh milk.
Put the bottle of cold water on the table.

meanings.note: The beloved beverage, often Arabic coffee or Turkish-style, and by extension a coffee shop.

examples.trans: Would you drink coffee or tea?

examples.text: حضرنا فنجان قهوة بالهيل للضيوف باللوبي.
examples.trans: We prepared a cup of cardamom coffee for the guests in the lobby.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Levantine word (qawwaar, plural qawaawiir) for a clay courtyard plant pot.

examples.text: زرعنا نعنع أخضر بقواوير فخار بالساحة.
examples.trans: We planted green mint in clay pots in the courtyard.

examples.text: سقت نور قوار الليمون جنب الدرج.
examples.trans: Nour watered the lemon pot beside the stairs.

meanings.note: In baking and cooking, قوام specifically refers to the thickness, crumb, or consistency of a batter or cake.

examples.text: قوام الكيكة طلع طري ومتماسك بنفس الوقت.
examples.trans: The texture of the cake came out soft and firm at the same time.

examples.text: لازم نخفق البيض لحد ما يتقل قوامه.
examples.trans: We need to beat the eggs until their consistency thickens.

meanings.note: With بـ + الـ, بالقوة means 'by force / forcefully'.

examples.trans: She grabbed my hand forcefully.
Honesty gives us strength.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أقواس.

examples.text: ادخل عالساحة من هاد القوس الحجري.
examples.trans: Step into the courtyard through this stone arch.

examples.text: الأقواس القديمة مبنية من حجر عمان.
examples.trans: The old arches are built of Amman limestone.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian plural is قوايا (qawaaya): كرسيين قوايا ('two sturdy chairs').

examples.trans: The gate rang with one strong ring.
We brought two sturdy wooden chairs to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قياسات.

examples.trans: He took the measurements of the courtyard and windows.
The sound-measuring meter is sensitive and accurate.

meanings.note: Plural القيم ('values / moral principles') is a favorite word of Principal Ms. Faten.

examples.trans: Respect is an important value at school.
Our most important value is honesty.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقفل, بيقفل).

examples.trans: We locked your suitcase safe in the storage closet.
I lock the iron gate at night.

meanings.note: Vocalized in the dictionary to distinguish Form I قَلَب ('to flip, turn a page over') from the noun قلب ('heart').

examples.text: اقلبي الصفحة وشوفي شو مكتوب وراها.
examples.trans: Turn the page over and see what is written on the back.

examples.text: قلب طارق الصندوق عشان يقرا الرقم تحت.
examples.trans: Tariq flipped the box over to read the number underneath.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقبل, بيقبل).

examples.trans: Will you accept staying on as our reception manager?
She accepted the invitation gladly.

meanings.note: Takes pronoun suffixes: كأنها ('as if it'), كأنهم ('as if they').

examples.text: بتحكي مع الجيران كأنهم صحاب زمان.
examples.trans: She talks with the neighbours as if they were old friends.
It sounded as if it came from the heating pipe.

meanings.note: Introduces a vivid comparison ('as if / just like'); takes pronoun suffixes or stands as كأن before nouns.

examples.text: الخشب الأخضر والليمون الأصفر كأنهم جنينة حقيقية.
examples.trans: The green wood and yellow lemons look just like a real garden.

examples.text: البيانو بعد الدوزان صار يرن كأنه جديد.
examples.trans: After tuning, the piano rings out as if it were brand new.

meanings.note: Loanword used for ship/flight captains, sports team captains, and respectfully when addressing a male driver or waiter.

examples.text: الكابتن وجه الفريق كله بهدوء وثقة.
examples.trans: The captain guided the whole team calmly and confidently.

examples.text: صورة كابتن السفينة معلقة بمدخل القاعة.
examples.trans: The portrait of the ship's captain hangs at the hall entrance.

meanings.note: Mariam contrasts her old love of school with المدرسة صارت كابوس إلي ('school became a nightmare for me').

examples.trans: I had a nightmare yesterday.
The exam was like a nightmare.

meanings.note: Anatomical and everyday word for 'ankle' (كاحلي اليمين 'my right ankle').

examples.text: الحمد لله كاحلي مش وارم، بس بده راحة.
examples.trans: Thankfully my ankle isn't swollen—it just needs rest.

examples.text: حطينا تلج عالكاحل ربع ساعة وخف الوجع.
examples.trans: We put ice on the ankle for fifteen minutes and the ache eased.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كاسات.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
He poured half a glass of orange juice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: I paid the bill in cash at the shop.
Do you prefer paying cash or card?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كافيهات.

examples.trans: We opened a small café in the house courtyard.
The morning café serves all the neighbours.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كاملة, plural: كاملين).

examples.trans: He hired her for a full-time job at the guesthouse.
They stayed with us a full week.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.trans: The weather was cold yesterday.

examples.text: الطعم كان متوازن كتير بين العسل والليمون.
examples.trans: The flavour was very well balanced between the honey and lemon.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person feminine singular.

examples.trans: The car was broken.

examples.text: الورقة كانت مطوية جوا غلاف الدفتر الجلد.
examples.trans: The sheet was folded inside the leather notebook cover.

meanings.note: Used to express resemblance, likelihood, or a hypothesis.

examples.trans: It looks as if it will rain today.

examples.text: كانه في ريحة قرفة طالعة من المطبخ التحتاني.
examples.trans: It seems as if there is a scent of cinnamon coming from the downstairs kitchen.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person plural.

examples.trans: The boys were playing outside.

examples.text: الأولاد كانوا يدوروا عالعلبة الزرقا طول الصبح.
examples.trans: The children were looking for the blue tin all morning.

كب.gloss: to spill; pour out; pour down (rain)

meanings.en: to spill; pour out; pour down (rain)
meanings.note: Quintessential Jordanian verb for spilling coffee, throwing out water, or rain pouring down (عم تكب مطر).

examples.text: امسك الفنجان منيح قبل ما تكب القهوة.
examples.trans: Hold the cup steady before you spill the coffee.

examples.text: السما بلشت تكب مطر بنص الليل.
examples.trans: The sky started pouring rain at midnight.

meanings.note: Used with بقلبه for holding hurt and anger inside until reaching a breaking point.

examples.trans: It isn't good to bottle your hurt up inside.
A person holds things in up to a certain point.

meanings.note: Intransitive verb (past كبرت kbirt 'I grew up') from the root ك-ب-ر ('big, great').

examples.text: زياد ورامي كبروا قريب من سوق السبت.
examples.trans: Ziad and Rami grew up near the Saturday market.

examples.text: شجرة الياسمين كبرت ووصلت للطابق التاني.
examples.trans: The jasmine tree grew and reached the second floor.

meanings.note: The Amman verb for pressing a button, doorbell or switch.

examples.text: اكبس الزر الأحمر عشان يفتح الباب.
examples.trans: Press the red button to open the door.

examples.text: كبست الجرس مرتين وما حدا فتح.
examples.trans: I pressed the bell twice and nobody opened.

كبسة.gloss: a press; a click (of a button)

meanings.en: a press; a click (of a button)
meanings.note: One press of a button: بكبسة وحدة 'with one click'.

examples.trans: With one press the machine starts.
Two presses on the bell means it is me.

meanings.note: Refers to a pill in medical contexts or sometimes a coffee capsule.

examples.text: لازم توخذ كبسولة وحدة كل يوم.
examples.trans: You must take one capsule every day.

examples.text: البذور الصغيرة محفوظة جوا كبسولة شفافة عشان الرطوبة.
examples.trans: The tiny seeds are preserved inside a clear capsule against humidity.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كبيرة, plural: كبار).

examples.trans: We use this big paper ledger.
You know older brothers well!

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural كتب (kutub), written like the verb كتب 'he wrote' (katab) but said differently.

examples.trans: This book is about the history of Amman.
I put the books on the shelf.

meanings.note: The word for book attached with the 1st person plural possessive suffix.

examples.trans: We got lost because we forgot our book at home.

examples.text: كتابنا فيه وصفات جدتي بالخط القديم والرسومات.
examples.trans: Our book contains my grandmother's recipes in old handwriting and drawings.

meanings.note: Masculine material noun used both for woven linen fabric and flax/linen twine.

examples.text: هاد المريول مصنوع من قماش الكتان البارد.
examples.trans: This apron is made from cool linen fabric.
Linen holds up well in summer and its heat.

meanings.note: Depending on vowels, it means 'he wrote' (katab) or plural 'books' (kutub).

examples.trans: He wrote a long letter.

examples.text: الرسام كتب الملاحظات بالحبر الأسود عالهامش.
examples.trans: The illustrator wrote the notes in black ink in the margin.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كتاف.

examples.trans: Square your shoulders and smile with confidence!
He carried the heavy bag on his shoulder.

meanings.note: Placed AFTER the adjective or verb it intensifies: تقيلة كتير ('very heavy'), شكرا كتير ('thank you very much').

examples.trans: The smell is so good!
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Extremely common adverb and adjective denoting abundance or intensity.

examples.trans: I am very tired today.

examples.text: حطينا لوز محمص كثير على وجه الصينية الأولى.
examples.trans: We put lots of toasted almonds on top of the first tray.

meanings.note: Intensive adjective/noun; feminine كذابة! ('she's a liar!').

examples.trans: Don't believe him, he's a liar.
She called her a liar in front of the teacher.

meanings.note: Construes with على for lying to or about someone (كذبوا علي، عم بكذبوا عليكي).

examples.trans: I have never lied to you.
The girls are lying to the principal.

meanings.note: Plural of chair (kursī).

examples.trans: We need to buy new chairs for the living room.

examples.text: صفينا خمس كراسي خشب حوالين طاولة الساحة.
examples.trans: We lined up five wooden chairs around the courtyard table.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for a necktie (from French cravate).

examples.text: لبس البدلة الرمادية مع كرافة كحلية للحفل.
examples.trans: He wore the gray suit with a navy tie for the ceremony.

examples.text: وين حطيت الكرافة تبعتي؟ ما لقيتها بالخزانة.
examples.trans: Where did you put my tie? I couldn't find it in the closet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كرافات.

examples.trans: He arranged the blue ties in the wardrobe.
A drop of juice landed on my tie!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: He retreated to his office calmly and with dignity!
Dignity and respect are the basis of dealing with others.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; كرت بريد means 'postcard'. Plural: كروت.

examples.text: بعتتله كرت بريد قصير الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: I sent him a short postcard last week.
I recognised his neat handwriting on the card right away.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كراتين.

examples.text: امسك الكراتين الخفيفة وأنا بفتح الباب.
examples.trans: Hold the light cartons while I open the door.
We packed the old books in a cardboard box.

meanings.note: An everyday item of furniture for sitting.

examples.trans: This chair is not comfortable.

examples.text: جدي قعد على كرسي القش جنب شجرة الليمون.
examples.trans: My grandfather sat on the wicker chair beside the lemon tree.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بكره, بيكره).

examples.trans: Honestly, I dislike noisy street-side rooms.

examples.text: ما حدا بيكره خبز القرفة السخن!
examples.trans: Nobody dislikes hot cinnamon bread!

meanings.note: Polite Jordanian reception phrase: شو الاسم الكريم؟ ('May I have your name, please?').

examples.trans: May I have your name, sir?
The people of the neighbourhood are generous and kind.

meanings.note: Culinary noun used for كريمة الليمون ('lemon curd / cream') and pastry fillings.

examples.text: نور جهزت كريمة الليمون الصفرا للتارت.
examples.trans: Nour prepared the bright yellow lemon curd for the tarts.

examples.text: ريحة كريمة الليمون الطازة عبت المطبخ كله.
examples.trans: The aroma of fresh lemon curd filled the entire kitchen.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from كريمة (cream); describes smooth dairy textures or off-white/cream hues.

examples.text: لون الحشوة كريمي ناعم وبدوب بالتم.
examples.trans: The filling is creamy, smooth, and melts in the mouth.

examples.text: اشترينا ورق رسم لونه كريمي دافي.
examples.trans: We bought drawing paper in a warm cream colour.

meanings.en: to win; to earn; to gain
meanings.note: Sound Form I verb (بكسب / كسبت) from root ك-س-ب; used for winning games or earning trust.

examples.trans: Nour won the final round.
We all gained lovely memories.

meanings.note: Transitive Form I verb ('break something, break up visual monotony').

examples.text: الخشب الجاف بيكسر حدة الحجر بالساحة.
examples.trans: Warm dry wood breaks up the starkness of the courtyard stone.

examples.text: انتبه لا تكسر المرطبان القزاز عالرف.
examples.trans: Be careful not to break the glass jar on the shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كشافات.

examples.trans: Hold the flashlight steady on the pipe joint.
The flashlight beam is bright and clear in the basement.

meanings.note: Colloquial noun from كشّر (to frown/scowl); describes a sour or grumpy facial expression.

examples.text: تغيرت كشرة وجهه لضحكة أول ما ذاق العسل.
examples.trans: The frown on his face turned into a smile as soon as he tasted the honey.

examples.text: بلاش هالكشرة الصبح، اليوم رح يكون حلو.
examples.trans: Drop that morning frown; today is going to be good.

كشف.gloss: to uncover; to reveal; to inspect

meanings.en: to uncover; to reveal; to inspect
meanings.note: Form I verb taking direct objects or عن (about) when revealing a hidden clue or secret.

examples.text: الحرارة كشفت الحبر السري المكتوب عالورقة.
examples.trans: The heat revealed the secret ink written on the sheet.
The doctor examined the patient and reassured him.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أكشاك.

examples.trans: The flower stall is on the corner of the street.
I bought a paper from the little kiosk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بكشر, بيكشر).

examples.text: لما يغلط بالنغمة كان يكشر عالحيط!
examples.trans: When he missed a note, he used to scowl at the wall!
Do not frown, smile!

meanings.note: Names the heel of a foot or shoe (كعب القدم / كعب الحذاء).

examples.text: زحلق كعب حذائي عن حرف الطبلية الواطية.
examples.trans: The heel of my shoe slipped off the edge of the low stool.

examples.text: اسندي كعبك عالوسادة الطرية عشان ترتاح رجلك.
examples.trans: Rest your heel on the soft cushion so your foot can relax.

meanings.note: Traditionally feminine noun with broken plural كفوف ('palms; gloves'). Used in baking to measure a light palm touch.

examples.trans: Test the warmth of the tin with the back of your palm.

examples.text: لبست كفوف المطبخ قبل ما تمسك الصينية.
examples.trans: She put on kitchen gloves before picking up the tin.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for gloves or oven mitts (literally 'palms').

examples.text: البس كفّ الفرن قبل ما تسحب الصينية السخنة.
examples.trans: Put on the oven mitt before pulling out the hot tray.

examples.text: اشتريت كفوف صوف دافية عشان برد الشتا.
examples.trans: I bought warm wool gloves for the winter chill.

meanings.note: Form II verb كفّى means 'to suffice / be enough', agreeing with الضيافة.

examples.text: الأكل اللي طبخناه بكفّي عشر أشخاص وزيادة.
examples.trans: The food we cooked is enough for ten people and more.

examples.text: كفّت الضيافة والقهوة لكل الضيوف بالحفل.
examples.trans: The refreshments and coffee were enough for all the guests at the party.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: All people love summer.

examples.text: كل بطاقة بالعلبة بتحكي عن نبتة عطرية مختلفة.
examples.trans: Every card in the tin talks about a different aromatic plant.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective derived from European classic; used for traditional recipes, architecture, and music.

examples.text: هاي الوصفة الكلاسيكية ما بتتغير من زمان.
examples.trans: This classic recipe has not changed for ages.
They played a classical piece on the piano in the lobby.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Explain the matter to me in plain words.
Your words are kind and reassuring.

meanings.note: Plural of word (kilma). Used in everyday contexts and formal situations.

examples.trans: This song has nice words (lyrics).

examples.text: الكلمات المكتوبة عالغلاف انمسحت شوي من المي.
examples.trans: The words written on the cover faded slightly from the water.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كلمات.

examples.trans: She did not say a single word to anyone.
The word thank you warms the heart.

meanings.note: Adverbial accusative of كلي (total); frequently paired with negations like مش كليا (not completely).

examples.text: طعم القرفة مختلف كليا عن طعم الزيزفون.
examples.trans: The taste of cinnamon is completely different from linden.

examples.text: نسيت الموضوع كليا مع عجقة التحضير.
examples.trans: I completely forgot about the matter in the rush of preparation.

meanings.en: to cost (money or effort); to assign someone a duty
meanings.note: Form II verb (بكلّف / كلّف). Can take two objects: هالحبل ما بكلّف كتير ('this rope doesn't cost much').

examples.trans: How much did this big lantern cost you?
City Hall tasked us with preparing the garden for the show.

meanings.note: In questions كم + singular noun asks 'how many?'; in statements كم + singular noun means 'a few' (كم دقيقة 'a few minutes').

examples.trans: Give him a few minutes, Rami.

examples.text: كم لفة قرفة بيقدر فرنك يخبز؟
examples.trans: How many cinnamon rolls can your oven bake?

meanings.note: Indispensable Levantine and Egyptian particle meaning 'also', 'too', or 'as well'.

examples.trans: I want tea, and also coffee.

examples.text: ذقنا التانية وكمان التالتة عشان نقارن القوام.
examples.trans: We tasted the second one and also the third to compare the texture.

meanings.note: Everyday Arabic word for violin (from Persian kamancha), used alongside كمان.

examples.text: زياد بيعزف عالكمانجة من لما كان صغير.
examples.trans: Ziad has played the violin since he was small.
Put the violin in its case after practice.

meanings.note: The musical instrument 'violin' (kamanga) with the 3rd person masculine possessive suffix.

examples.trans: He played his violin skillfully.

examples.text: طالع كمانجته من الصندوق الخشب وعزف لحن هادي.
examples.trans: He took his violin out of the wooden case and played a gentle tune.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كمبيوترات.

examples.trans: The desk here runs without a computer!
I logged the appointments on the computer.

meanings.note: Used intransitively (تكمل قبل الجمعة 'to be finished before Friday') alongside transitive كمّل ('to complete something').

examples.text: رح تكمل الغرفة أول ما نرتب الكراسي.
examples.trans: The room will be complete as soon as we arrange the chairs.

examples.text: الفرحة ما بتكمل إلا بوجود الجيران.
examples.trans: The celebration is only complete with the neighbours there.

meanings.note: In Levantine Arabic, a noun for the violin (also pronounced كمنجة).

examples.text: صوت الكمنجة مع البيانو طلع كتير حنون ورايق.
examples.trans: The sound of the violin with the piano came out super tender and mellow.

examples.text: بنت خالتي بتتعلم عزف الكمنجة بالمعهد الموسيقي.
examples.trans: My cousin is learning to play the violin at the music conservatory.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كميات.

examples.trans: We need double the amount for tomorrow morning.
This quantity is enough for ten guests.

meanings.note: Classic Levantine word for dress shoes (pair of shoes, treated as feminine singular).

examples.text: مسح الكندرة ولمّعها قبل ما يروح عالشغل.
examples.trans: He wiped and polished his dress shoes before going to work.

examples.text: اشتريت كندرة جلد بنية كتير مريحة للمشي.
examples.trans: I bought a really comfortable pair of brown leather shoes for walking.

meanings.note: Refers to a literal treasure or something highly valued metaphorically.

examples.trans: They found an old treasure underground.

examples.text: الوصفات السرية اللي بالدفتر أغلى من أي كنز.
examples.trans: The secret recipes in the notebook are more precious than any treasure.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كنزات.

examples.trans: Wear a warm wool cardigan in the evening.
He folded the grey sweaters inside the bag.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بكنس, بيكنس).

examples.text: حطيت الشنتة هون وأنا بكنس الخزانة.
examples.trans: I set the bag here while sweeping the closet.
We swept the fallen leaves from the courtyard.

meanings.note: Spoken form of كهرباء; الكهربا قطعت 'the power is cut'.

examples.trans: The power came back after an hour.
The electricity bill is expensive this month.

meanings.note: Everyday musicians' term in Amman for a piano or guitar chord.

examples.text: اعزفي كورد صول الكبير واسمعي كيف رنته صافية.
examples.trans: Play a G major chord and hear how clear it rings.

examples.text: ختمت سعاد الأغنية بكورد هادي وطويل.
examples.trans: Suad ended the song with a quiet, lingering chord.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كياس.

examples.trans: Give me a cloth bag for the shop.
I carried the bag of apples and bread.

meanings.note: The main interrogative word for asking about manner or state.

examples.trans: How are you today?

examples.text: كيف قدرت تفتح القفل القديم بدون ما تكسره؟
examples.trans: How did you manage to open the old lock without breaking it?

meanings.note: Refers generally to cake as a type of food.

examples.trans: I like eating cake with tea.

examples.text: خبزنا كيك بالعسل واللوز وعملنا جنبه شاي نعناع.
examples.trans: We baked honey and almond cake and made mint tea alongside it.

meanings.note: Refers to a single, whole cake, or a distinct slice (singulative form of kēk).

examples.trans: I made a delicious chocolate cake.

examples.text: كيكة التوت اللي عملتها سلمى طلعت خفيفة وهشة.
examples.trans: The berry cake that Salma made turned out light and fluffy.

meanings.note: Stays invariable after numbers in everyday market speech: تلاتة كيلو ليمون ('three kilos of lemons').

examples.text: اعطيني اتنين كيلو تفاح أحمر لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Give me two kilos of red apples, please.

examples.text: تلاتة كيلو ليمون بيكفوا لكل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Three kilos of lemons are enough for the whole week.

meanings.note: Vocalized with fatha-sukun to distinguish noun كَسْر ('fracture') from verb كسر ('to break').

examples.text: طمنونا، ما في أي كسر بالرجل الحمد لله.
examples.trans: Good news—there is no fracture in the foot, thank goodness.

examples.text: اللوية الخفيفة بتطيب بسرعة لما ما يكون فيها كسر.
examples.trans: A mild sprain heals quickly when there's no fracture.

meanings.note: Vocalized lemma distinguishing 'sleeve' (kumm, pl. kmaam كمام) from كم ('how many?').

examples.text: شمرت عن كمامي قبل ما نغسل الشبابيك.
examples.trans: I rolled up my sleeves before we washed the windows.

examples.text: تبللت كمام قميصي لما ركضنا تحت المطر.
examples.trans: My shirt sleeves got soaked when we ran in the rain.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ل- before nouns ('for/to'); before pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian it takes the stem إل-: إلي ('for me / mine'), إلك ('for you / yours'), إله ('his'), إلها ('hers'), إلنا ('ours'), إلكم ('yours pl.').

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is mine.
Thank you all very much!

meanings.note: Preposition 'for' or 'to' followed by the number four.

examples.trans: We divided the pizza into four parts.

examples.text: قسمنا الورقة لأربعة مربعات متساوية بالمسطرة.
examples.trans: We divided the sheet into four equal squares with the ruler.

meanings.note: Takes pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian: لأني (because I), لأنك (because you), لأنه (because he/it — also general 'because'), لأنكم (because you pl.).

examples.text: لأنه القهوة الطيبة بتخلي الناس لطاف!
examples.trans: Because good coffee makes people pleasant!
Thank you because you kept the bag safe.

meanings.note: Used to give a reason, usually meaning 'because' broadly, or specifically 'because he/it is...'.

examples.trans: He didn't come because he is sick.

examples.text: ما فتحنا الشباك لأنه الهوا كان بارد كتير.
examples.trans: We did not open the window because the wind was very cold.

meanings.note: Takes pronoun endings directly in speech: لإني ('because I'), لإنها ('because she').

examples.trans: I stayed home because I was tired.
I apologized because I was late.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'no' or 'not', used exactly like Standard Arabic.

examples.trans: No, I don't want to go today.

examples.text: لا تنسوا تطفيوا الفرن بعد ما تخلصوا الخبيز.
examples.trans: Do not forget to turn off the oven after you finish baking.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: لابسة, plural: لابسين).

examples.trans: He is standing outside wearing a grey coat.
She is wearing a warm wool sweater.

meanings.note: Form III verb (بلاحظ / لاحظت) from root ل-ح-ظ, common in both formal and everyday Jordanian speech.

examples.trans: Do you know what I noticed first?
I didn't notice that the window was open.

meanings.note: Invariant modal word followed by a subjunctive verb (without ب-) to express 'must / have to / need to'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everything has to be just right!

meanings.note: Noun meaning a street sign, shop sign, or banner, from لفت (to draw attention).

examples.text: علّقنا لافتة خشب مدهونة جديد فوق باب المقهى.
examples.trans: We hung a freshly painted wooden sign above the café door.

examples.text: اللافتة اللي عالشارع الرئيسي مبينة من بعيد.
examples.trans: The sign on the main street is visible from far away.

لاقى.gloss: to find; to encounter; to meet

meanings.en: to find; to encounter; to meet
meanings.note: Form III defective verb widely used in Jordanian Arabic as the everyday verb meaning to find (alongside لقي).

examples.text: أخيرا لاقينا المفتاح الضاع تحت السجادة.
examples.trans: We finally found the lost key under the rug.

examples.text: إذا دورت منيح بالدرج بتلاقي الكرت.
examples.trans: If you look carefully in the drawer you will find the card.

meanings.note: Hollow verb (laam / biluum) meaning 'blame someone or something'.

examples.text: لا تلوم الهوا إذا طارت الورقة عن الطاولة!
examples.trans: Don't blame the wind if the sheet flew off the table!

examples.text: ما بنلوم مازن لو توتر قبل التفتيش.
examples.trans: We can't blame Mazen for feeling nervous before the inspection.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لامبات.

examples.trans: Plug in the brass lamp beside the desk.
The lamp casts a calm yellow light.

meanings.note: Describes something that shines: polished wood, clean glass, new shoes.

examples.trans: The floor is shiny after we mopped it.
He bought shiny black boots.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلين, بيلين).

examples.text: كان يعمل حاله قاسي خمس ثواني وبعدين يلين!
examples.trans: He would act tough for five seconds and then soften up!
His kind heart softens quickly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian contraction of 'li-anna-hu', used to provide a reason or cause.

examples.trans: He didn't come because he is sick.

examples.text: خلي العسل بره الثلاجة لانه بجمد بالبرد.
examples.trans: Keep the honey out of the fridge because it thickens in the cold.

meanings.note: Dense wool felt that cushions piano hammers and bushings.

examples.text: لباد الصوف بيخلي صوت البيانو ناعم ودافي.
examples.trans: Wool felt keeps the piano's tone soft and warm.

examples.text: حطينا قطع لباد صغيرة تحت رجلين الكراسي.
examples.trans: We stuck small felt pads under the chair legs.

لبرية.gloss: to the wild / to the outside

meanings.en: to the wild / to the outside
meanings.note: Often refers to an outdoor area, nature, or sometimes a wasteland depending on context.

examples.trans: We went out to the wilderness of Amman to get some fresh air.

examples.text: سافروا لبرية الأردن بالربيع عشان يشموا هوا نقي.
examples.trans: They went out to the Jordanian countryside in spring to breathe fresh air.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلبس, بيلبس).

examples.text: أنا أكيد ما بلبس مقاس أربعة وأربعين!
examples.trans: I certainly do not wear size forty-four!

examples.text: لبس معطفه قبل ما يطلع بالمطر.
examples.trans: He put on his coat before going out in the rain.

meanings.note: Climbing green ivy covering courtyard stone walls.

examples.text: اللبلاب الأخضر غطى نص حيط الساحة القديم.
examples.trans: Green ivy covered half of the old courtyard wall.

examples.text: ورق اللبلاب بيلمع تحت المي بعد المطر.
examples.trans: The ivy leaves glisten after the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; ألبان means 'dairy products'. Plural: ألبان.

examples.trans: The dairy van arrives early in the morning.
We have yoghurt, olive oil, and thyme for breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian prepositional phrase indicating motion directed to a lower place.

examples.text: انزل لتحت عشان تشوف الطابق الأرضي.
examples.trans: Go downwards so you can see the ground floor.

examples.text: انزلوا لتحت عالمطبخ بتلاقوا كل الصواني جاهزة.
examples.trans: Go downstairs to the kitchen and you will find all the trays ready.

meanings.note: Directional phrase indicating movement into the interior of a place or object.

examples.trans: Go inside, it's cold outside.

examples.text: فوتوا لجوا قبل ما تبرد القهوة عالبلكونة.
examples.trans: Come inside before the coffee gets cold on the balcony.

meanings.note: Common Levantine conjunction meaning 'until' or 'so that'.

examples.text: استنى هون لحتى أخلص شغل وأجي معك.
examples.trans: Wait here until I finish work and come with you.

examples.text: بدرس منيح لحتى أنجح بالامتحان بأعلى علامة.
examples.trans: I study hard so that I pass the exam with the highest grade.

meanings.note: Used to mark the limit of a time period, distance, or extent in colloquial Jordanian.

examples.trans: I will wait until you come.

examples.text: استنينا بالساحة لحد ما دقت الساعة تمانية.
examples.trans: We waited in the courtyard until the clock struck eight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لحظات.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, let me read the line.
We waited a moment by the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلحق, بيلحق).

examples.trans: Follow me quickly to the third floor!

examples.text: لحقنا دكان الخردوات أول ما فتح.
examples.trans: We caught the hardware shop right as it opened.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ألحان.

examples.trans: She played old melodies on the piano.
This gentle tune is familiar to me.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لخبطات.

examples.trans: What a strange mix-up with the suitcases!
We sorted out the mix-up calmly and quickly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word (lazzaaq) for sticky tape or electrical tape (لزاق كهربا).

examples.text: لف طارق السلك الجديد بلزاق كهربا أسود.
examples.trans: Tariq wrapped the new wire with black electrical tape.

examples.text: عندك لفة لزاق بالمكتب يا نور؟
examples.trans: Do you have a roll of tape at the desk, Nour?

meanings.note: Intransitive/transitive verb meaning 'stick fast' (paint on dry wood, stamp on postcard).

examples.text: الدهان ما بيلزق منيح عالخشب المبلول.
examples.trans: Paint does not stick well to wet wood.

examples.text: لزقنا ورقة المواعيد على باب المطبخ.
examples.trans: We stuck the schedule sheet onto the kitchen door.

meanings.note: Very common Jordanian word to indicate that an action is ongoing or hasn't happened yet.

examples.trans: I still haven't finished my work.
