examples.text: الكيكة لسا بالفرن وبدها كمان خمس دقايق.
examples.trans: The cake is still in the oven and needs five more minutes.

meanings.note: Used in idioms about speaking or keeping quiet (تضبي لسانك).

examples.trans: She has a sharp tongue when replying.
Hold your tongue in front of them.

meanings.note: An alternative spelling and pronunciation variant of 'لسا', used widely in the Levant.

examples.trans: I am still studying for the exam.

examples.text: مازن لسه عم بدور عالبطاقة الأخيرة بالدرج.
examples.trans: Mazen is still searching for the final card in the drawer.

meanings.note: Usually used in exaggerations to mean staying up very late or doing something all night.

examples.trans: We stayed up until morning.

examples.text: ضلينا نقرأ بالخرايط لصبح اليوم التاني.
examples.trans: We kept reading the maps until the next morning.

meanings.note: Form II verb (lattaf): ألطف الجو ('lighten the tense mood').

examples.trans: She told a joke to lighten the mood.
A kind word softens the atmosphere.

meanings.note: Also used in the mild Jordanian exclamation يا لطيف! ('goodness gracious!').

examples.trans: Hot bread makes people pleasant!
Goodness gracious, the suitcase is so heavy!

meanings.note: Jordanian Arabic word meaning 'then' or 'well then!'.

examples.text: مو حابب تشرب شاي؟ لعاد شو أعملك؟
examples.trans: You don't feel like drinking tea? Well then, what should I make you?

examples.text: الباص راح علينا، لعاد خلينا ناخد تاكسي.
examples.trans: We missed the bus—in that case, let's take a taxi.

meanings.note: Literally 'play', and idiomatically ما حدا بيلعب معها / معي ('nobody messes with her / me').

examples.trans: We played ball in the courtyard.
Don't play this game with me.

meanings.note: Prepositional phrase denoting direction towards a particular but usually indefinite room.

examples.trans: They moved the patient to another room.

examples.text: نقلنا العلبة لغرفة الضيوف عشان التذوق.
examples.trans: We moved the tin to the guest room for the tasting.

meanings.note: Built from و plus لغز ('mystery/puzzle') and the 'our' ending.

examples.text: الأولاد قعدوا يحلّوا لغز الكنز المخبّى طول العصر.
examples.trans: The kids spent all afternoon solving the mystery of the hidden treasure.

examples.text: هادي الرسالة القديمة صارت لغز محيّر للعيلة كلها.
examples.trans: This old letter became a puzzling mystery for the whole family.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine dative preposition ('for us').

examples.text: جبتلنا عصير ليمون بارد عشان الحرّ.
examples.trans: I brought us cold lemonade because of the heat.

examples.text: هاد البيت إله ذكريات غالية لإلنا كلنا.
examples.trans: This house holds precious memories for all of us.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلف, بيلف).

examples.text: لفي شمال برا البوابة وامشي دغري.
examples.trans: Turn left outside the gate and walk straight.
Turn left at the stair landing.

meanings.note: Plural of لفافة ('roll/scroll'), used in bakeries for cinnamon rolls.

examples.text: عملت سلمى لفائف قرفة سخنة مع سكر ناعم عالوجه.
examples.trans: Salma made warm cinnamon rolls with powdered sugar on top.

examples.text: لقينا لفافة ورق قديمة مربوطة بخيط جوا الصندوق.
examples.trans: We found an old paper scroll tied with string inside the box.

meanings.note: Used in Jordan to mean a wrap or a sandwich (e.g. falafel or shawarma), or a turn in the road.

examples.trans: I want a falafel sandwich with fries.

examples.text: أخذنا لفة سريعة بالسوق واشترينا زعتر وفستق.
examples.trans: We took a quick stroll around the market and bought thyme and pistachios.

meanings.note: Pairs with انتباه ('catch attention': لفت انتباهي) or نظر ('draw eyes': نلفت نظرهم).

examples.trans: Her words caught the principal's attention.
We don't want to draw anyone's attention.

meanings.note: Compound directional adverb combining لـ (toward) and فوق (above); opposite of لتحت.

examples.text: اطلع لفوق عالطابق التاني بتلاقي الغرفة.
examples.trans: Go upstairs to the second floor and you will find the room.
The red arrow on the map points upwards.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لفائف.

examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls smell mouth-watering.
We baked a tray of fresh rolls in the morning.

meanings.note: Imperative of لفّ (to turn, wrap, or rotate).

examples.text: لفّ على اليمين بعد الإشارة التانية بتلاقي المخبز.
examples.trans: Turn right after the second traffic light and you'll find the bakery.

examples.text: لفّ الساندويش بورق الزبدة عشان يضل سخن.
examples.trans: Wrap the sandwich in parchment paper so it stays warm.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: In Jordanian Arabic, a slang word meaning a total 'steal' or 'bargain'.

examples.text: هاد الكرسي الخشبي بهذا السعر عنجد لقطة!
examples.trans: This wooden chair at that price is honestly a total steal!

examples.text: أخدت لقطة حلوة للغروب من فوق السطح.
examples.trans: I took a great shot of the sunset from up on the roof.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لقم.

examples.trans: Taste just one bite of the cake!
We had a quick bite before work.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلاقي, بيلاقي).

examples.trans: Tell me how to find the hardware shop.

examples.text: لقيت هاد الصندوق الخشب ورا الحيط!
examples.trans: I found this wooden box behind the wall!

meanings.note: Form I defective verb (fa'il class: لقي / يلقى) used extensively in Jordanian speech for finding lost objects.

examples.text: لقينا ثلاث بطاقات قديمة جوا الكتاب.
examples.trans: We found three old cards inside the book.

examples.text: مازن لقي الوصفة الأصلية بخط جدته.
examples.trans: Mazen found the original recipe in his grandmother's handwriting.

meanings.note: Classic Levantine discourse word meaning 'then / well then / in that case'.

examples.text: خلصتوا شغلكم؟ لكان يلا نشرب شاي سوا.
examples.trans: Did you finish your work? In that case, let's drink tea together.

examples.text: لكان كيف بدك نروح إذا السيارة خربانة؟
examples.trans: Then how do you expect us to go if the car is broken?

meanings.note: Used to specify a duration or an assignment belonging to the week.

examples.trans: This is the allowance for the whole week.

examples.text: رتبنا جدول التذوق للأسبوع كله عاللوح.
examples.trans: We arranged the tasting schedule for the whole week on the board.

meanings.note: Polite way to soften bad news ('unfortunately').

examples.text: للاسف ما في رقم تليفون عالبطاقة.
examples.trans: Unfortunately there is no phone number on the tag.
Unfortunately all the rooms are taken tonight.

meanings.note: Typically used when referring to a time limit, meaning up to the fifth hour or up to the number five.

examples.trans: I will keep working until five.

examples.text: المكتبة بتضل فاتحة كل يوم للخمسة العصر.
examples.trans: The library stays open every day until five in the afternoon.

meanings.note: Points to something belonging to, or intended for, a specific illustration or drawing.

examples.trans: I brought new colors for the drawing.

examples.text: زدنا شوية تفاصيل صغيرة للرسمة بالقلم الأسود.
examples.trans: We added a few tiny details to the drawing with the black pen.

meanings.note: Directional phrase guiding movement or pointing out a location towards the east.

examples.trans: Walk to the east and then turn right.

examples.text: اتجهنا للشرق خمسين متر لعند البوابة التانية.
examples.trans: We headed to the east fifty metres up to the second gate.

للشمال.gloss: to the north / to the left

meanings.en: to the north / to the left
meanings.note: Depending on context, it can mean heading north or taking a left turn in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: At the intersection, turn left.

examples.text: لفوا للشمال بعد النافورة بتلاقوا المخبز.
examples.trans: Turn to the left after the fountain and you will find the bakery.

meanings.note: Refers to something designated to be eaten or used during the morning meal.

examples.trans: I bought cheese and olives for breakfast.

examples.text: حضرنا جبنة بلدية وزيتون وزعتر للفطور.
examples.trans: We prepared local cheese, olives, and thyme for breakfast.

meanings.note: Indicates an object, message, or action directed towards the boss or manager.

examples.trans: Send this email to the manager.
We handed the final report to the manager in his office.

meanings.note: Used in religious contexts, oaths, or expressions of exasperation or gratitude (e.g. 'الحمد لله').

examples.trans: Do good for the sake of God.

examples.text: العمل المتقن لوجه لله دايما فيه بركة.
examples.trans: Work done sincerely for the sake of God always carries blessing.

meanings.note: Common conjunction used to introduce a time clause, distinct from the question word 'when' (mita).

examples.trans: Call me when you reach home.

examples.text: لما بردت الكيكة صبينا فوقها العسل الدافي.
examples.trans: When the cake cooled, we poured the warm honey over it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لمبات.

examples.trans: I fitted a new bulb in the attic bathroom.
The white lightbulb is bright.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلمس, بيلمس).

examples.trans: Touch the radiator — it is warm on top.
Touch the brass pipe — it heated up!

meanings.en: to shine; to gleam; to sparkle
meanings.note: Sound Form I verb (بلمع / لمعت) from root ل-م-ع, used for polished metal or bright ink.

examples.trans: The drawings still shine on the paper.
The brass lock gleamed in the sun.

meanings.note: Often used colloquially in Jordan to refer to a boss, a skilled tradesman, or a person in charge.

examples.trans: The boss said that the work is finished.

examples.text: لمعلم بالورشة علمنا كيف نصلح القفل النحاس.
examples.trans: The master craftsman in the workshop taught us how to fix the brass lock.

لمكانه.gloss: to his place / to its place

meanings.en: to his place / to its place
meanings.note: Prepositional phrase denoting movement towards a specific location belonging to someone or something.

examples.trans: Return the book to its place.

examples.text: رجعنا الكتاب القديم لمكانه على الرف التالت.
examples.trans: We returned the old book to its place on the third shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلمع, بيلمع).

examples.trans: Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

examples.text: خمستعشر سنة وأنا بلمع مفاتيح النحاس!
examples.trans: Fifteen years I have been polishing the brass keys!

meanings.note: Used when dividing or cutting something into exactly two pieces.

examples.trans: Cut the apple into two halves.

examples.text: قسمنا رغيف الخبز السخن لنصين وتقاسمناه.
examples.trans: We split the warm loaf of bread into two halves and shared it.

لهون.gloss: here; hither; up to this point

meanings.en: here; hither; up to this point
meanings.note: Combines لـ (to, toward) with هون (here); used for motion toward the speaker or stopping at a limit.

examples.text: تعال لهون يا طارق عشان تشوف الرسمة.
examples.trans: Come over here, Tariq, so you can see the drawing.

examples.text: لهون وبس، خلصنا حل اللغز بنجاح!
examples.trans: Up to here and no further—we have solved the puzzle successfully!

meanings.note: Conditional particle used for hypothetical or impossible situations (contrary-to-fact conditions).

examples.text: لو بعرف إنك جاي، كنت استنيتك.
examples.trans: If I knew you were coming, I would have waited for you.

examples.text: لو لقينا المفتاح بدري كنا فتحنا الصندوق امبارح.
examples.trans: If we had found the key earlier we would have opened the chest yesterday.

meanings.note: Refers to a whiteboard (اللوح الأبيض), wooden plank, or windowpane (لوح قزاز).

examples.text: كتبنا مهام الأسبوع التلاتة عاللوح الأبيض.
examples.trans: We wrote the three tasks for the week on the whiteboard.

examples.text: نضفنا كل ألواح القزاز من الغبرة القديمة.
examples.trans: We cleaned all the glass panes of their old dust.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لوحات.

examples.text: شوف لوحة المفاتيح الخشب ورا المكتب.
examples.trans: Look at the wooden key board behind the desk.
We wiped the dust off the brass plate.

meanings.note: Indicates movement or position towards the rear or back direction.

examples.text: ارجع لورا شوي عشان تمرق السيارة.
examples.trans: Go back a bit so the car can pass.

examples.text: ارجعوا خطوتين لورا عشان تشوفوا النقش اللي فوق القوس.
examples.trans: Step two paces backwards so you can see the carving above the arch.

meanings.note: Literally means almonds, but heavily used in Jordanian youth slang to mean 'everything is perfect' or 'great'.

examples.trans: The situation is perfect, don't worry.

examples.text: زينت سلمى وش الكيكة بشرايح لوز محمص.
examples.trans: Salma decorated the top of the cake with toasted almond slices.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ألوان.

examples.trans: The colour of the suitcase is dark blue.
The courtyard colours are soothing to the eye.

meanings.note: Instance noun from لوى ('twist/turn'): لوية خفيفة = 'a minor twist/sprain'.

examples.text: هي بس لوية خفيفة بالكاحل وبكرا بتكون أحسن.
examples.trans: It's just a minor twist in the ankle and tomorrow it'll feel better.

examples.text: الراحة والتلج أحسن دوا للوية الكاحل.
examples.trans: Rest and ice are the best remedy for an ankle twist.

meanings.note: Compound Levantine interrogative (لـ 'to' + وين 'where').

examples.text: لوين نوجه المروحة عشان ينشف اللوح أسرع؟
examples.trans: Where should we point the fan so the panel dries faster?
Where are you heading in this rain without an umbrella?

meanings.note: Plural of 'līra'. In Jordan, people commonly refer to the Jordanian Dinar as a 'lira' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I only have five dinars left.

examples.text: دفعنا عشر ليرات حق المرطبانات الزجاج الجديدة.
examples.trans: We paid ten dinars for the new glass jars.

meanings.note: The standard colloquial interrogative for 'why' in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: Why were you late to work today?

examples.text: ليش الحبر على طرف الورقة مبين أغمق من النص؟
examples.trans: Why does the ink at the edge of the sheet look darker than the middle?

meanings.note: Collective noun denoting fibrous plant material or scrubbing sponge; unit noun is ليفة.

examples.trans: The box is wrapped in coarse palm-fibre twine.
Whole wheat is rich in natural fibres.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليالي.

examples.trans: The guest arrived last night.
The neighbourhood is very quiet at night.

meanings.note: Definite الليلة means 'tonight', while indefinite ليلة means 'one night / night of'.

examples.trans: I am going to sleep well tonight.
We booked the room for three nights.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليمون.

examples.trans: The warm lemon cake is ready.
I squeezed half a lemon into the soup.

meanings.note: Vocalized in the dictionary to distinguish Form I intransitive لَمَع ('to shine') from Form II لمّع ('to polish').

examples.text: القزاز النظيف عم يلمع بشمس الصبح.
examples.trans: The clean glass is shining in the morning sun.

examples.text: خشب البيانو بيلمع تحت الضو الدافي.
examples.trans: The piano wood gleams under the warm light.

meanings.note: Masculine abstract noun (distinct from the verb لطف 'to soften'). Used for kind manners and gentle handling.

examples.text: الضيافة باللطف والابتسامة أحلى ما يكون.
examples.trans: Hospitality with kindness and a smile is the nicest thing.
Thank you for your kindness and help today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مألوفة, plural: مألوفين).

examples.trans: The handwriting on the tag looked familiar to me.
The sound of the piano is familiar on this street.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle from أدب ('manners'): describes courteous speech or polite people.

examples.trans: The new students are very polite and kind.

examples.text: بنت صغيرة مؤدبة فتحت النا الباب.
examples.trans: A polite little girl opened the door for us.

meanings.note: Kitchen or oven timer (from وقت 'time').

examples.text: عيرت المؤقت على تمنطاعشر دقيقة للتارت.
examples.trans: I set the timer for eighteen minutes for the tarts.

examples.text: أبو طارق عينه عالمؤقت عشان ما يتحمر الخبز زيادة.
examples.trans: Abu Tariq keeps his eye on the timer so the bread doesn't over-brown.

meanings.note: Active participle of ألّف ('to compose music, write a book'); feminine مؤلفة.

examples.text: مين المؤلف اللي كتب هاللحن الهادي؟
examples.trans: Who is the composer who wrote this gentle melody?

examples.text: اسم المؤلف مكتوب بالحبر بأول الصفحة.
examples.trans: The composer's name is written in ink at the top of the page.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: I haven't eaten anything since the morning.

examples.text: ما عرفت إنه العلبة فيها طابق سري من تحت.
examples.trans: I did not know that the box had a secret compartment underneath.

meanings.note: Relates to water, used for colors (light blue/watery), animals, or parks (e.g. water park).

examples.trans: We went to an aquatic amusement park (water park).

examples.text: استعمل الرسام لون مائي أزرق عشان يرسم البحر.
examples.trans: The painter used a blue watercolour to paint the sea.

meanings.note: Masculine participle of أخد ('to take'), used for a planned near-future trip.

examples.text: أنا ماخد إجازة الأسبوع الجاي عشان نسافر عالعقبة.
examples.trans: I'm taking time off next week so we can travel to Aqaba.

examples.text: هو ماخد الأمور ببساطة ومو مستعجل أبداً.
examples.trans: He's taking things easy and isn't in a rush at all.

meanings.note: Colloquial active participle of مرق (to pass by); used adjectivally and verbally for someone currently passing.

examples.text: كنت مارق من جنب المخبز وشميت ريحة الكيك.
examples.trans: I was passing by the bakery and smelled the cake.

examples.text: شخص مارق بالشارع دلنا على المكتبة.
examples.trans: A passer-by in the street pointed us to the library.

meanings.note: Male given name of the guesthouse owner.

examples.text: مازن استقبل النزلاء بنفسه وساعدهم بالشنط.
examples.trans: Mazen greeted the guests himself and helped them with their bags.

examples.text: اتصل بمازن قبل ما نطبع المنيو الجديد.
examples.trans: Call Mazen before we print the new menu.

meanings.note: Standard Arabic conservatory/musicians' term (from Italian misura) for one bar of music.

examples.text: عزفت سعاد أول أربع مازورات من الفالس.
examples.trans: Suad played the first four bars of the waltz.

examples.text: اللحن بيوقف بنص المازورة الرابعة والعشرين.
examples.trans: The melody stops in the middle of the twenty-fourth bar.

meanings.note: Active participle indicating the ongoing state of gripping or grasping something.

examples.trans: He is holding the phone all day.

examples.text: طارق ماسك البوصلة بإيده وبتبع الاتجاهات.
examples.trans: Tariq is holding the compass in his hand and following the directions.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مواسير.

examples.trans: The copper pipe started warming up right away.
Old pipes need maintenance in winter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ماشية, plural: ماشيين).

examples.trans: I saw my brother walking down this street.
Everything is going smoothly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ماضية, plural: ماضيين); الأسبوع الماضي means 'last week'.

examples.trans: I put in the bulb last week.
All the tiredness of the past days is gone.

meanings.note: Classic Jordanian/Levantine craftsmanship word for a solid joint, wall, or hinge.

examples.text: ركبنا الشيش ببراغي طويلة فطلعت الدرفة ماكنة.
examples.trans: We mounted the shutters with long screws so the panel came out sturdy.

examples.text: الكرسي الخشب ماكن وبيتحمل شغل الساحة يوميا.
examples.trans: The wooden chair is solid and handles daily courtyard use.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ماكينات.

examples.trans: The coffee machine is running in the kitchen.
We cleaned the espresso machine in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بميل, بيميل).

examples.trans: Listen when I tilt the box slightly!
The afternoon sun slanted into the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مالحة, plural: مالحين).

examples.trans: I brought a tub of salted butter by mistake!
The white cheese is salty and delicious.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for 'yesterday' (مبارح بالليل 'last night').

examples.trans: Look what arrived last night!
I booked the room by phone yesterday.

meanings.note: Adverbial accusative from مباشر ('direct'): immediately or without detours.

examples.text: من المحطة رح نروح مباشرة عالبيت.
examples.trans: From the station we will go straight home.
Write the note right after the lesson.

meanings.note: Active participle of ابتسم ('to smile').

examples.text: أبو طارق وقف بنص الساحة مبتسم ومبسوط.
examples.trans: Abu Tariq stood in the middle of the courtyard smiling happily.

examples.text: نور بتستقبل الضيوف الصبح بوجه بشوش ومبتسم.
examples.trans: Nour greets guests in the morning with a warm, smiling face.

meanings.note: Passive participle of بحّ ('to grow hoarse'), describing a warm, scratchy, or husky voice.

examples.text: وصوت رامي اللي لسا مبحوح شوي.
examples.trans: And Rami's voice, which is still a little hoarse.
My voice is hoarse from the cold today.

meanings.note: Passive participle of the quadriliteral verb بروز ('to frame', from برواز 'frame').

examples.trans: It'll be framed before dinner.
The framed photo is hung in the living room.

meanings.note: Passive participle of برش (to grate); very common in recipes for grated lemon zest, cheese, or coconut.

examples.text: حطينا قشر برتقال مبروش فوق الكيكة.
examples.trans: We put grated orange zest on top of the cake.
Grated cheese melts quickly in the oven.

meanings.note: Universal Arabic congratulatory word, literally 'blessed'.

examples.text: ألف مبروك على افتتاح المقهى، الله يباركلكم فيه!
examples.trans: A thousand congratulations on opening the café—may God bless it for you!

examples.text: مبروك التخرج يا سلمى، رفعتي راسنا!
examples.trans: Congratulations on graduating, Salma—you made us proud!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مبسوطة, plural: مبسوطين).

examples.trans: We are very glad that you liked the courtyard.
The guests left happy from breakfast.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle from root ب-ط-ن ('lining/inside'), describing boxes, coats, or envelopes.

examples.trans: The box is lined with blue fabric.
The jacket is lined with warm wool.

meanings.note: Form II active participle from بكر ('early morning'), used in formal/semi-formal phrases like الموعد المبكر ('the early appointment').

examples.text: القطار المبكر بيوصل الساعة سبعة الصبح.
examples.trans: The early train arrives at seven in the morning.

examples.text: هاد الصباح المبكر أهدى وقت بالشوارع.
examples.trans: This early morning is the quietest time on the streets.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مبلولة, plural: مبلولين).

examples.trans: The wet wood on the shutters softens the echo.
His coat was wet from the rain.

meanings.note: Used to describe something feminine or plural non-human that is soaked or damp with water.

examples.trans: The clothes are still wet, they haven't dried.

examples.text: الأوراق كانت مبلولة شوي من ندى الصباح بالحديقة.
examples.trans: The pages were slightly damp from the morning dew in the garden.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مباني.

examples.text: المباني القديمة بعمان مبنية من حجر.
examples.trans: Old buildings in Amman are built of stone.
He works in restoring heritage buildings.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مبينة, plural: مبينين).

examples.trans: The wooden train looks old and precious.
It looks like it is going to rain tonight.

meanings.note: From بيّن (to appear/seem); asks how something looks right now.

examples.text: مبيّن عليك التعب اليوم، ما نمت منيح مبارح؟
examples.trans: You look tired today—didn't you sleep well last night?

examples.text: السما مبيّنة صافية اليوم وما في غيم.
examples.trans: The sky looks clear today and there aren't any clouds.

meanings.note: Plural متأخرين is used in spoken Jordanian for both mixed and all-female groups (بشوفكم متأخرين).

examples.trans: Sorry that I arrived late.
Why are you always late to class?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: متأكدة, plural: متأكدين).

examples.trans: Are you sure you do not need this sweater?
I am one hundred percent sure.

meanings.note: Form V participle from root ب-د-ل ('exchange'), describing things that have been switched around.

examples.trans: The three keys are swapped here.
The weather is changeable this week.

meanings.note: Form V active participle from جال ('to roam'), used as a noun for hikers, walkers, or strolling visitors.

examples.trans: The hikers reached the mountain before sunset.
There is a trail set aside for hikers in the forest.

meanings.note: Feminine متحمسة ('excited': كنت كتير متحمسة).

examples.trans: Dina is super excited for the trip.
We're all excited to see the movie.

meanings.note: Plural of متدرّب (trainee/apprentice), from تدرّب (to train).

examples.text: في متدرّب جديد عم بتعلم شغل الحلويات مع سلمى.
examples.trans: There's a new apprentice learning pastry work with Salma.
The trainees at the company helped set up the exhibition.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: متذكرة, plural: متذكرين).

examples.trans: Do you still remember that story after all these years?
I remember the building number well.

meanings.note: Form V active participle widely used in Levantine Arabic instead of a present tense verb for 'I remember' (أنا متذكّر).

examples.trans: I still remember the color of the lantern.
Do you remember the name of the shop?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أمتار.

examples.trans: The table is ten metres away.
The courtyard is eight metres wide.

meanings.note: Form VI active participle meaning 'even in thickness, spacing, or size'.

examples.text: طبقة الدهان طلعت ناعمة ومتساوية من أول لوح لآخره.
examples.trans: The coat of paint came out smooth and even from one end of the panel to the other.

examples.text: قطعنا العجينة لدوائر متساوية لصواني التارت.
examples.trans: We cut the dough into even circles for the tart pans.

meanings.note: Form VI participle adjective (feminine متشابكة, plural متشابكين) used for tangled strings or interlaced lines.

examples.trans: The strings got tangled up inside the bag.

examples.text: الخطوط المتشابكة عطت شكل حلو للفانوس.
examples.trans: The crisscrossed lines gave the lantern a lovely shape.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: متصلين.

examples.trans: The caller left his phone number.
Who was the caller on the line?

meanings.note: Active participle describing someone who has experienced a sudden, unexpected event or news.

examples.text: أنا متفاجئ من قرار الشركة الجديد.
examples.trans: I am surprised by the company's new decision.

examples.text: الكل كان متفاجئ من دقة طعم الكيكة التالتة.
examples.trans: Everyone was surprised by the refined flavour of the third cake.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine form of مثل ('like, similar to').

examples.trans: Its color is dark blue like your suitcase!
The water is cold as ice.

meanings.en: parallel; running alongside at equal distance
meanings.note: Form VI participle adjective (feminine متوازية, plural متوازيين) from وازى ('to run parallel to').

examples.trans: We stretched two parallel ropes across the courtyard.
Parallel lines never meet.

meanings.note: From تواصل (to connect continuously), meaning 'unbroken/continuous'.

examples.text: اشتغلنا ست ساعات متواصلة لحد ما خلصنا الجرد.
examples.trans: We worked six continuous hours until we finished the inventory.

examples.text: المطر المتواصل خلى الشوارع كلها تلمع.
examples.trans: The continuous rain made all the streets glisten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: متوترة, plural: متوترين).

examples.trans: His voice on the phone sounded a little nervous.
Mint tea calms tense nerves.

meanings.note: Feminine متينة, plural متان. Used for strong rope, thick paper, or solid construction.

examples.text: لازمنا حبل متين يتحمل وزن الفوانيس.
examples.trans: We need a sturdy rope that can bear the weight of the lanterns.
The cardboard is sturdy and doesn't tear easily.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from مثال (example, model); describes ideal timing, conditions, or results.

examples.text: حرارة الجو اليوم مثالية للجلسة بالحديقة.
examples.trans: The weather today is ideal for sitting in the garden.

examples.text: هادا المكان مثالي لتخبية صندوق الكنز.
examples.trans: This spot is ideal for hiding the treasure box.

meanings.en: pierced; having a hole punched through
meanings.note: Passive participle of ثقب ('to pierce/punch a hole'): feminine مثقوبة, plural مثقوبين.

examples.text: كل ورقة مثقوبة من الزاوية عشان الخيط يفوت.
examples.trans: Each sheet is punched at the corner so the string goes through.
This bucket has a hole and leaks water.

meanings.note: Chiefly used in ما إله / ما إلها مثيل ('unmatched / unbeatable').

examples.text: خبز سلمى السخن الصبح ما إله مثيل بالحارة.
examples.trans: Salma's warm bread in the morning has no equal in the neighbourhood.

examples.text: ليمون سوق السبت ريحته وطعمته ما إلهم مثيل.
examples.trans: The scent and flavour of Saturday market lemons are unbeatable.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مجانية, plural: —).

examples.text: فطور مجاني طول الأسبوع مع الغرفة!
examples.trans: Complimentary breakfast all week with the room!
Morning coffee is free for the neighbours today.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle from root ج-ف-ف ('dry'), used for dried flowers, herbs, and leaves.

examples.trans: There are dried olive leaves in them too.
We drink dried sage in the winter.

meanings.note: From جهل (not to know); plural form agrees with the dual noun مرتبانين.

examples.text: لقينا مرتبانين مجهولين بالخزانة بدون أي ورقة عليهم.
examples.trans: We found two mystery jars in the cupboard with no label on them.

examples.text: رقم مجهول رنّ عليّ الصبح بس ما رديت.
examples.trans: An unknown number called me this morning, but I didn't answer.

meanings.note: Colloquial Levantine Form II passive participle (from جوز 'pair'): عقدة مجوز ('double knot'), حبل مجوز ('doubled rope').

examples.text: عملت عقدة مجوز عشان الحبل ما ينفلت.
examples.trans: I tied a double knot so the rope doesn't slip loose.

examples.text: اطوي الورقة مجوز حتى تصير أقوى.
examples.trans: Fold the paper double so it becomes stronger.

meanings.note: Form III verbal noun from حضر ('to attend'), used for university classes and public talks.

examples.text: عندي محاضرة تاريخ الساعة عشرة الصبح.
examples.trans: I have a history lecture at ten in the morning.
University lectures started last week.

meanings.note: Form III active participle of حافظ; with على means preserving/maintaining, and standalone can mean conservative.

examples.text: المخبز محافظ على وصفته الأصلية من خمسين سنة.
examples.trans: The bakery has preserved its original recipe for fifty years.

examples.text: العسل البلدي محافظ على طعمه الطبيعي الصافي.
examples.trans: The local honey keeps its pure natural flavour.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: محامين.

examples.trans: The letter came from the lawyer's office.
We consulted a skilled contracts lawyer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: محابس.

examples.trans: I turned off the main water shutoff in the basement.
Open the shutoff tap slowly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: محتاجة, plural: محتاجين).

examples.trans: I needed a quiet place nearby.
Tell me if you need any help.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: محترمة, plural: محترمين).

examples.trans: His voice is calm and very polite.
A respectable, well-known family in the quarter.

meanings.note: Form I passive participle from حجز ('to reserve/book'): refers to booked seats, tables, or scheduled trains.

examples.trans: The corner table is reserved for our guests.
All the rooms are booked until the end of the week.

meanings.note: A very common Jordanian way to say 'no one' or 'nobody'.

examples.text: محدش كان في البيت لما رنيت.
examples.trans: Nobody was at home when I called.

examples.text: محدش شاف مين حط البطاقة الخامسة جوا الكتاب.
examples.trans: Nobody saw who placed the fifth card inside the book.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: محركات.

examples.trans: I heard the sound of a car engine outside.
The bus engine is quiet and new.

meanings.note: Literally 'burnt', used in Arabic for a blown electrical fuse or lightbulb.

examples.trans: The fuse is blown and the light in the hallway is out.

examples.text: الخبز هاد محروق شوي من تحت، جيب غيره.
examples.trans: This bread is a bit burnt on the bottom—grab another one.

meanings.note: Used when someone or something is jammed in a tight space or stuck in traffic. Also used for needing to go to the bathroom urgently.

examples.trans: The car was stuck in traffic for an hour.

examples.text: الكرت كان محشور بين الغلاف الخشبي والورقة الأولى.
examples.trans: The card was wedged between the wooden cover and the first page.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: محطات.

examples.trans: I arrived at the bus station in the morning.
The hotel is close to the station.

meanings.note: Passive participle indicating that an object has been set down or positioned somewhere.

examples.trans: The key is placed on the table.

examples.text: المرطبان الدهبي محطوط على أعلى رف بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: The golden jar is placed on the highest shelf in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Noun of place/instrument from حفظ (to keep/guard); covers pocket wallets, purses, and school satchels.

examples.text: كان في ورقة مطوية جوا محفظة الجلد.
examples.trans: There was a folded paper inside the leather wallet.
I forgot my wallet on the table in the lobby.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: محفورة, plural: محفورين).

examples.trans: My grandfather's hand-carved wooden train!
There are two initials engraved on the corner.

meanings.note: Describes a feminine object (or plural non-human) that has a design, hole, or text carved into it.

examples.trans: This panel is carved from wood.

examples.text: النجمة الصغيرة محفورة جوا الحجر فوق الباب.
examples.trans: The small star is carved into the stone above the door.

meanings.note: Used to describe something securely fastened, well-constructed, or sealed tightly.

examples.trans: The lid is tightly sealed.

examples.text: غطا العلبة محكم الإغلاق عشان يحفظ النكهة.
examples.trans: The lid of the tin is tightly sealed to preserve the flavour.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian noun for any retail shop or spot (pl. محلات).

examples.trans: Below is the signature of the antique shop.
There's a pastry shop next to the house.

meanings.note: Can mean 'sweetened' (muḥallā) or be part of an exclamation 'how beautiful' (ma aḥlā -> maḥlā).

examples.text: يا محلى الجو اليوم في عمان.
examples.trans: How beautiful the weather is today in Amman.

examples.text: يا محلى ريحة الشاي بالنعناع وقت الغروب بالساحة!
examples.trans: How lovely is the scent of mint tea at sunset in the courtyard!

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from محل (place); refers to local products, markets, or customs.

examples.text: دايما بنشتري الزبدة والعسل من الإنتاج المحلي.
examples.trans: We always buy butter and honey from local production.

examples.text: الجريدة المحلية كتبت عن مهرجان الخبز.
examples.trans: The local newspaper wrote about the bread festival.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: محمية, plural: محميين).

examples.trans: Your lease is protected by city law!
The courtyard is sheltered from street wind.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle from حمّص ('to toast/roast'): describes nuts, coffee, or bread.

examples.trans: Toasted walnuts give a nice crunch.

examples.text: شوية لوز محمص فوق الرز كتير زاكي.
examples.trans: A few toasted almonds on top of the rice are delicious.

meanings.note: Noun of place from خبز (to bake), with -ي ('my').

examples.text: ريحة الخبز الطازة طالعة من مخبز الحارة من الساعة ستة.
examples.trans: The smell of fresh bread has been wafting out of the neighborhood bakery since six.

examples.text: فتحت مخبزي الصغير بهالشارع قبل تلات سنين.
examples.trans: I opened my small bakery on this street three years ago.

meanings.note: Passive participle of خبّى, to hide (something). Also heard as مخبّي.

examples.trans: The key is hidden under the rug.
We found a letter hidden in the book.

meanings.note: Active/Passive participle for someone or something that is concealed or keeping out of sight.

examples.trans: The boy is hiding behind the door.

examples.text: الدليل التالت مخبي ورا ساعة الحيط القديمة.
examples.trans: The third clue is hidden behind the old wall clock.

meanings.note: From خبّى (to hide); agrees with feminine غرفة.

examples.text: في غرفة صغيرة مخبّاة ورا المكتبة الخشبية.
examples.trans: There's a small hidden room behind the wooden bookcase.

examples.text: الصندوق هاد كان مخبّى بالعلية من أيام جدي.
examples.trans: This box was hidden away in the attic since my grandfather's days.

meanings.note: Masculine participle from خبّى ('to hide/keep away').

examples.text: حاسس إنك مخبّي عني خبر حلو، احكي شو في!
examples.trans: I feel like you're hiding good news from me—tell me what's up!

examples.text: طارق مخبّي المفاتيح الاحتياطية بالدرج التاني.
examples.trans: Tariq keeps the spare keys tucked away in the second drawer.

meanings.note: Passive-participle/place noun from Form VIII اختبر; denotes a science lab, culinary test room, or clinic lab.

examples.text: سلمى حولت المطبخ لمختبر تذوق صغير.
examples.trans: Salma turned the kitchen into a small tasting lab.

examples.text: الطلاب عملوا تجربة جديدة بمختبر الكيمياء.
examples.trans: The students ran a new experiment in the chemistry lab.

meanings.note: Form VIII participle of اختلف; precedes plural nouns or follows singular nouns to indicate difference.

examples.text: كل صينية إلها رقم وطعم مختلف عن التانية.
examples.trans: Each tin has a different number and taste from the next.

examples.text: جربنا تلات طرق مختلفة لتسخين العسل.
examples.trans: We tried three different ways to warm the honey.

meanings.note: Passive participle of ختم (to stamp/seal), modifying مغلف in definiteness and gender.

examples.text: وصل مغلّف مختوم من البلدية اليوم الصبح.
examples.trans: A stamped envelope from the municipality arrived this morning.

examples.text: لازم الورقة تكون مختومة بختم رسمي عشان يقبلوها.
examples.trans: The paper has to be stamped with an official seal for them to accept it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مخدات.

examples.trans: I put two soft pillows on the bed.
The cotton pillow is comfortable for sleeping.

meanings.note: Used for architectural/room floor plans, schedules, and blueprints.

examples.text: رسمنا المخطط الجديد للطاولات بملف الاستقبال.
examples.trans: We drew the new table floor plan in the front-desk folder.

examples.text: حسب المخطط في مكان مريح لست طاولات بالساحة.
examples.trans: According to the layout there is comfortable room for six tables in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Form I passive participle from خفق ('to whisk'): describes beaten egg whites, cream, or batters.

examples.text: أضف البيض المخفوق شوي شوي عالخليط.
examples.trans: Add the beaten eggs little by little to the mixture.
Whipped cream is light and smooth.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مخفية, plural: مخفيين).

examples.trans: A hidden door in the cellar is drawn on the map!
The key was hidden inside the box.

meanings.note: Fabric name, also used metaphorically to describe something very soft or luxurious (e.g., 'mukamali' for elite).

examples.trans: I bought a red velvet dress.

examples.text: العلبة مبطنة بقماش مخمل أحمر ناعم من جوا.
examples.trans: The box is lined with soft red velvet fabric on the inside.

meanings.note: Polite everyday Jordanian address for an adult woman or female guest.

examples.trans: Good morning, madam, please come in!
The room is booked under Madam Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مدد.

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
He travelled for two weeks in summer.

meanings.note: Sound Form I verb (بمدح / مدحت) from root م-د-ح, used when admiring someone's work or cooking.

examples.trans: Everyone praises you at the restaurant.
The guests praised the Arabic coffee.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مداخل.

examples.trans: The guesthouse entrance is lit by a brass lantern.
We greeted the guests at the entrance.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مدارس.

examples.trans: Children walk to the school in the morning.
He learned music at a small conservatory.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مدفوعة, plural: مدفوعين).

examples.trans: Our rent is paid through next summer.
The entire bill is paid in full.

meanings.note: Something placed underground or covered heavily. Can also refer to a traditional rice and meat dish.

examples.trans: The treasure is buried underground.

examples.text: الصندوق النحاس كان مدفون تحت بلاطة الساحة.
examples.trans: The brass chest was buried under a courtyard paving stone.

meanings.note: From دهن (to paint); agrees in feminine gender with اللافتة.

examples.text: اللافتة مدهونة باللون الأخضر ومكتوب عليها بخط جميل.
examples.trans: The sign is painted green and written on in lovely calligraphy.

examples.text: لا تسند عالحيط لأنو لسه مدهون جديد.
examples.trans: Don't lean against the wall because it was just freshly painted.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مدورة, plural: مدورين).

examples.trans: Where should I hang the round mirror?
We put a round wooden table in the corner.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken word for 'round' or 'circular'.

examples.text: حطّينا طاولة مدوّرة بنص الصالة عشان القعدة تصير أدفى.
examples.trans: We put a round table in the middle of the hall to make the seating cozier.

examples.text: الخبز المدوّر الصغير بطلع حلو مع الحمص.
examples.trans: Small round bread comes out great with hummus.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: مديرة). Plural: مدراء.

examples.trans: She became the permanent front-desk manager at the guesthouse.
The manager welcomed the new guests.

meanings.note: Refers to Ms. Faten, headmistress of AlRawabi School.

examples.trans: The principal called us to her office.
We spoke with the principal this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مدن.

examples.trans: Amman is an old, lovely hilltop city.
City law protects public gardens.

meanings.note: Common Arabic verb مدّد meaning 'to extend' a stay or deadline.

examples.text: قررت تمدّد إقامتها بعمان كمان أسبوع عشان المعرض.
examples.trans: She decided to extend her stay in Amman for another week for the exhibition.

examples.text: البلدية مدّدت مهلة الترخيص لنهاية الشهر.
examples.trans: The municipality extended the licensing deadline until the end of the month.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمر, بيمر).

examples.trans: Pass right beside the green pharmacy.

examples.text: أنا مريت من جنب السبيل الحجري!
examples.trans: I just passed the stone fountain!

meanings.note: Verbal noun of راجع (to review/check); commonly used for official inspections or follow-ups.

examples.text: عندي مراجعة بالدائرة الحكومية بكرا الساعة تسعة.
examples.trans: I have a follow-up inspection at the government office tomorrow at nine.

examples.text: بعد مراجعة الحسابات، لقينا إنو كل الأرقام مزبوطة.
examples.trans: After reviewing the accounts, we found that all the numbers were right.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مرايا.

examples.trans: We hung the round mirror beside the window.
Look in the mirror behind the desk.

meanings.note: Denotes a square shape or a square area in geometry or real-world objects.

examples.trans: Draw a square on the paper.

examples.text: رسمنا مربع صغير جنب كل رقم عالورقة.
examples.trans: We drew a small square next to each number on the sheet.

meanings.note: Feminine form of 'murabbaʿ', used to modify feminine nouns having a square shape.

examples.trans: The table is square in shape.

examples.text: اختاروا علبة مربعة صغيرة عشان البطاقات المتساوية.
examples.trans: They chose a small square tin for the equal-sized cards.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مربوطة, plural: مربوطين).

examples.trans: There is a paper tag tied to the handle.
The red ribbon is tied securely.

meanings.note: Describes a feminine object that is tied up, securely fastened, or restricted.

examples.trans: The cow is tied to the tree.

examples.text: الورقة مربوطة بخيط قنب ومختومة بشمع أحمر.
examples.trans: The paper is tied with hemp string and sealed with red wax.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مربيات.

examples.trans: Would you like honey or strawberry jam?
The apple jam is homemade.

meanings.note: 'Marrah' means 'a time/once' (e.g. waḥdeh marrah = one time), but 'mara' (مَرَة) means 'woman/wife' in colloquial Jordanian.

examples.trans: I went to Petra one time.

examples.text: جربنا الوصفة مرة تانية بس بخففنا السكر شوي.
examples.trans: We tried the recipe one more time, though we reduced the sugar slightly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مرتاحة, plural: مرتاحين).

examples.text: عندي حرام صوف دافي فأنا مرتاح.
examples.trans: I have a warm wool blanket, so I am comfortable.
We were glad to see you at ease.

meanings.note: Used to describe a neat person, a well-organized room, or generally something of high quality (e.g. 'a nice car').

examples.trans: Working with him is very neat and well-organized.

examples.text: خطها مرتب وواضح كتير حتى عالورق الصغير.
examples.trans: Her handwriting is very neat and clear even on small paper.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine pantry word (also pronounced مرطبان) for glass storage jars (dual مرتبانين).

examples.text: حطيت مرتبانين قزاز كبار عالرف: واحد سكر وواحد ملح.
examples.trans: I put two big glass jars on the shelf: one sugar and one salt.

examples.text: لزقنا ملصق واضح على كل مرتبان بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: We stuck a clear label onto every jar in the kitchen.

meanings.note: As an adjective (mrattabeh), it means a tidy feminine noun. As a noun (martabeh), it means a rank/status or a mattress.

examples.trans: She is a tidy and polite girl.

examples.text: خزانة المطبخ مرتبة والمرطبانات مصفوفة بالألوان.
examples.trans: The kitchen cupboard is tidy and the jars are lined up by colour.

meanings.en: coral pink/orange; made of or resembling coral
meanings.note: Nisba adjective from مرجان ('coral'): feminine مرجانية, plural مرجانيين.

examples.trans: I chose the coral colour for the sunset in the drawing.

examples.text: شوف الفوانيس المرجانية كيف بتضوي بالليل.
examples.trans: Look how the coral-coloured lanterns glow at night.

meanings.note: Friendly all-day Jordanian greeting usable with anyone.

examples.trans: Hello! You must be Nour.
Hello, Ziad, welcome!

meanings.note: لمرحلة معينة means 'up to a certain point / stage'.

examples.trans: We reached a difficult stage.
High school is a very important stage.

meanings.note: Passive participle adjective (feminine مرخية, plural مرخيين) used for a sagging rope or loose wire.

examples.text: الحبل بالنص شوي مرخي، شده كمان.
examples.trans: The rope in the middle is a bit slack, pull it tighter.

examples.text: خيطان الزينة صارت مرخية بعد الهوا.
examples.trans: The decoration strings became slack after the wind.

meanings.note: Form IV active participle of أرسل used substantively for the sender named on a letter or parcel.

examples.text: اسم المرسل مكتوب على ظهر المغلف بالحبر الأسود.
examples.trans: The sender's name is written on the back of the envelope in black ink.

examples.text: وصلنا الطرد بس ما عرفنا مين المرسل.
examples.trans: We received the parcel, but we did not know who the sender was.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مرسومة, plural: مرسومين).

examples.text: في مفتاح دهبي مرسوم فوق الباب.
examples.trans: There is a golden key painted above the door.
The map is drawn by hand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a glass jam, honey, or olive jar (dual مرطبانين, plural مرطبانات).

examples.trans: We lined the jars of jam and honey up on the shelf.
Open the new jar of honey for breakfast.

meanings.note: Passive participle of رفع ('lift/raise').

examples.text: خلي رجلك مرفوعة عالمخدة طول السهرة.
examples.trans: Keep your foot propped up on the pillow all evening.

examples.text: راسك مرفوع يا طارق، خبزاتك بطيروا العقل!
examples.trans: Hold your head high, Tariq—your loaves are amazing!

مرق.gloss: to pass by; walk past; drop by

meanings.en: to pass by; walk past; drop by
meanings.note: Quintessential Levantine verb for walking past a street or dropping by.

examples.text: أي حدا بيمرق من شارع الرينبو بيقرأ اللوحة بوضوح.
examples.trans: Anyone walking down Rainbow Street can read the sign clearly.

examples.text: مرق جارنا الساعاتي الصبح وسلم علينا.
examples.trans: Our watchmaker neighbour dropped by in the morning and said hello.

meanings.note: Everyday kitchen word for broth, stock, or sauce.

examples.text: مرقة الجاج بالبهارات هي سرّ طعم الرز الزاكي.
examples.trans: Spiced chicken broth is the secret to the rice's delicious flavor.

examples.text: زيدي شوية مرقة عالبامية عشان ما تنشف بالفرن.
examples.trans: Add a little broth to the okra so it doesn't dry out in the oven.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle of رقّم ('to number'): feminine مرقمة, plural مرقمين.

examples.text: الأوراق مرقمة من واحد لعشرة بالترتيب.
examples.trans: The sheets are numbered from one to ten in order.
I found the numbered boxes next to the door.

meanings.note: Indicates that multiple items have been given sequential numbers.

examples.trans: The chairs in the theater are numbered.

examples.text: كل الكراتين مرقمين من واحد لعشرة بالحبر الأسود.
examples.trans: All the boxes are numbered from one to ten in black ink.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle of رقّم ('to number'), from رقم ('number').

examples.trans: The three envelopes are numbered.
The pages are numbered from one to a hundred.

meanings.note: Relative adjective from مركز ('centre'): used in المحطة المركزية ('Central Station') and السوق المركزي.

examples.trans: Let's meet at the Central Station entrance.
The central market is always full of activity.

meanings.note: Electric fan or hand fan (from ريح 'wind/breeze').

examples.text: شغلنا المروحة بالممر عشان ينشف الدهان أسرع.
examples.trans: We turned on the fan in the hallway so the paint would dry faster.

examples.text: هوا المروحة الخفيف حرك ريحة الدهان لبرا.
examples.trans: The gentle breeze from the fan carried the paint smell outside.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مريحة, plural: مريحين).

examples.trans: It has a very comfortable wooden bed.
The bus ride was comfortable and calm.

meanings.note: Masculine Levantine noun (plural مراييل) worn while cooking, painting, or crafting.

examples.text: البس مريول الرسم قبل ما تفتح الألوان.
examples.trans: Put on the painting apron before you open the paints.
The apron got splashed all over with blue ink.

meanings.note: Form III verbal noun from مزح ('to joke'): lighthearted teasing or playful banter.

examples.trans: No joking now—the matter is serious.
Friendly banter makes the atmosphere relaxed.

meanings.note: Core Jordanian adjective meaning 'right, straight, accurate, on point'.

examples.text: كلامك مزبوط مية بالمية، لازم نبلش بكير.
examples.trans: What you're saying is a hundred percent right—we need to start early.

examples.text: تأكد إنو البرواز معلّق مزبوط ومو مايل.
examples.trans: Make sure the frame is hung straight and isn't crooked.

meanings.note: Masculine verbal noun (masdar) from مزح ('to joke'); used in expressions like بلا مزح ('no kidding').

examples.trans: The jokes are all ordinary teasing.
I'm speaking seriously, not joking.

meanings.note: Feminine Arabic word meaning 'double' or 'twofold', agreeing with رنة.

examples.text: الجرس رنّ رنة مزدوجة قبل ما يفتحوا الباب.
examples.trans: The bell gave a double ring before they opened the door.

examples.text: الشبابيك الجديدة لها زجاج مزدوج لعزل الصوت والبرد.
examples.trans: The new windows have double-pane glass to insulate against noise and cold.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for tearing or ripping something apart.

examples.trans: He tore the paper and threw it in the trash.

examples.text: طارق مزع طرف المغلف بحذر عشان ما يخرب الختم.
examples.trans: Tariq tore the edge of the envelope carefully so as not to ruin the seal.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مزعجة, plural: مزعجين).

examples.trans: I dislike noisy rooms facing the street.

examples.text: ما في أي صوت مزعج بالعلية.
examples.trans: There is no annoying noise in the attic.

meanings.note: Noun for a flower vase, built from زهر (blossom/flowers).

examples.text: حطّت مزهرية قزاز بنص الطاولة وعبتها ورد أبيض.
examples.trans: She put a glass vase in the middle of the table and filled it with white flowers.

examples.text: انتبه لا توقع المزهرية وأنت بتشيل الكتب!
examples.trans: Be careful not to knock over the vase while you're picking up the books!

meanings.note: Derived from زيت (oil) via Form II زيّت (to oil/lubricate hinges).

examples.text: المفصلات مزيّتة منيح وما عادت تطّلع صوت أبداً.
examples.trans: The hinges are well oiled and don't make a sound anymore.

examples.text: صينية الفرن مزيّتة وجاهزة عشان نحط فيها العجين.
examples.trans: The baking tray is oiled and ready for us to put the dough in.

meanings.note: Standard Jordanian private-school address for a female teacher or principal, used alone (يا مس) or before her first name (مس فاتن، مس عبير).

examples.trans: Yes Miss, I'm ready.
Ms. Faten is in her office now.

meanings.note: Pairs naturally with تحمل ('take/bear responsibility': نتحمل المسؤولية).

examples.trans: Every student has a responsibility.
You must take responsibility for your words.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form مسا (masa) alongside standard مساء in مساء الخير ('good evening').

examples.trans: The eight o'clock evening bus is arriving.
The air is calm and pleasant this evening.

meanings.note: Standard Arabic noun for 'evening', starting the universal greeting مساء الخير.

examples.text: مساء الخير يا جيران، كيف حالكم اليوم؟
examples.trans: Good evening, neighbors—how are you doing today?

examples.text: الحفل ببلش الساعة سبعة مساءً بالساحة.
examples.trans: The concert starts at seven in the evening in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Masculine word derived from مساء ('evening'), meaning 'evening'.

examples.text: عندي دوام مسائي بالمكتبة كل يوم أربعاء.
examples.trans: I have an evening shift at the library every Wednesday.

examples.text: بشرب فنجان قهوة مسائي بالبلكونة بس يبرد الجو.
examples.trans: I drink an evening cup of coffee on the balcony once the weather cools down.

meanings.note: Used for physical space, land area, or a wiper (e.g. for floors).

examples.trans: The area of the room is large.

examples.text: مساحة الحديقة بتكفي لطاولتين كبار وكراسي خشب.
examples.trans: The area of the garden is enough for two large tables and wooden chairs.

meanings.en: distance; physical gap or space between points
meanings.note: Feminine noun (plural مسافات) used for distances on a road or spacing between objects.

examples.text: خلّي مسافة متر بين الفانوس والتاني.
examples.trans: Leave a metre's distance between one lantern and the next.

examples.text: المسافة من البيت للبلد مش بعيدة.
examples.trans: The distance from the house to downtown isn't far.

meanings.note: Form III active participle of سافر ('to travel'), used as a noun for someone on a trip or at a bus station.

examples.trans: I should ask another traveller.
The passengers are standing by the door.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مستحيلة, plural: —).

examples.trans: There is no way I would bother a guest with our problems!
It is impossible for us to forget this week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مستعجلة, plural: مستعجلين).

examples.trans: He was always in a hurry during music lessons.
Have some tea if you are not in a hurry.

meanings.note: Form X passive participle of استعمل (to use); standard label for second-hand books, furniture, or gear.

examples.text: لقينا هادا الدفتر النادر بمحل كتب مستعملة.
examples.trans: We found this rare notebook in a second-hand bookshop.

examples.text: العلبة مبينة مستعملة بس نظيفة ومرتبة.
examples.trans: The tin looks used, yet it is clean and neat.

meanings.note: Form X passive participle of استقبل ('to face what comes ahead'); used as a masculine noun meaning 'the future'.

examples.trans: This letter is for future Rami.

examples.text: ما حدا بعرف شو مخبّي المستقبل.
examples.trans: Nobody knows what the future holds.

meanings.note: Form X active participle from root ق-و-م ('to stand straight'), describing lines, posture, or directions.

examples.trans: Walk straight down the street.
We drew a straight line with the ruler.

meanings.note: Form VIII participle from root س-و-ي. Means level/flat for surfaces, and 'well-cooked/ripe' for food.

examples.trans: Put it on a level surface.
The table isn't level, it wobbles.

meanings.note: Passive participle of سجّل ('to record, register').

examples.trans: We found a recorded message on the desk phone.
Every reservation is recorded in the front-desk ledger.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمسح, بيمسح).

examples.trans: Wipe the dust off the brass plate.
We wiped down the tables before breakfast.

meanings.note: Used for flat surfaces like roofs or fields.

examples.trans: The roof of the house is flat.

examples.text: فردنا العجينة على لوح خشب مسطح ونضيف.
examples.trans: We rolled the dough out on a clean, flat wooden board.

meanings.note: Feminine form of msattah, applied to feminine nouns.

examples.trans: The area here is flat.

examples.text: الصينية المعدنية مسطحة عشان هيك الكيكة انخبزت بسرعة.
examples.trans: The metal tray is flat, which is why the cake baked quickly.

meanings.note: Used for measuring and drawing crisp straight lines on signs or labels.

examples.text: سطرت نور الملصقين بالمسطرة وقلم الحبر الأسود.
examples.trans: Nour ruled both labels with a straightedge and a black ink pen.

examples.text: قيس الحروف بالمسطرة عشان تطلع بوسط اللوحة.
examples.trans: Measure the letters with the ruler so they sit centered on the sign.

meanings.note: Feminine singular form agreeing with non-human plural بلاطات.

examples.text: البلاطات المسطّحة بتخلي المشي بالحوش أسهل.
examples.trans: Flat flagstones make walking in the courtyard easier.

examples.text: بدنا صحن مسطّح كبير عشان نقدم فيه الكعك.
examples.trans: We need a big flat platter to serve the cookies on.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمسك, بيمسك).

examples.trans: Hold this torch steady right here.
Grab the boxes, Tariq!

مسكة.gloss: handle; catch (of a door or window)

meanings.en: handle; catch (of a door or window)
meanings.note: From مسك, to hold: the part you hold to open a door, window or drawer.

examples.trans: The drawer handle broke.
The window catch is a bit high.

meanings.note: Commonly used in Jordanian Arabic instead of the MSA word 'mughlaq'.

examples.trans: The shop is closed today.

examples.text: باب المخبز مسكر هلق لأنهم طلعوا عالسوق.
examples.trans: The bakery door is closed right now because they went out to the market.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مسكونة, plural: مسكونين).

examples.trans: Room seven is occupied tonight!
All the rooms on the second floor are occupied.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مسكينة, plural: مساكين).

examples.trans: The poor gentleman was worried about the guesthouse.
He arrived in the rain, poor thing, and cold.

meanings.note: General word for a metal nail, peg, or tuning pin inside a piano.

examples.text: ركبت المفتاح بحذر على مسمار الدوزان التاني.
examples.trans: I fitted the wrench carefully onto the second tuning pin.

examples.text: دقينا مسمارين صغار عشان نعلق لوحة البوابة.
examples.trans: We tapped in two small nails to hang the gate sign.

meanings.note: Passive participle describing panels, ladders, or chairs leaning against a wall.

examples.text: السلم الخشب مسند على حيط الساحة.
examples.trans: The wooden ladder is leaning against the courtyard wall.

examples.text: درفات الشيش كانت مسندة برا بعد الصنفرة.
examples.trans: The shutter panels were propped outside after sanding.

meanings.note: The most common negation particle in Levantine Arabic for non-verbs.

examples.trans: I am not upset with you.

examples.text: هادا المفتاح مش للباب الرئيسي، هادا للخزانة.
examples.trans: This key is not for the main door; this one is for the cupboard.

meanings.note: Form III verbal noun of شارك ('share/take part in').

examples.text: هاد البيانو انصنع لمشاركة الموسيقى مع الناس.
examples.trans: This piano was made for sharing music with people.

examples.text: شكرا إلكم كلكم على مشاركتكم بتجهيز الكافيه.
examples.trans: Thank you all for taking part in getting the café ready.

meanings.note: Instrumental noun from شبك ('fasten/clip'): names a shutter catch/hook or paper clip.

examples.text: ثبتنا الشيش عالحيط بمشبك حديد أسود ماكن.
examples.trans: We secured the shutter against the wall with a sturdy black iron catch.

examples.text: تأكد إن المشبك مسكر منيح قبل ما تهب الريح.
examples.trans: Make sure the catch is latched tightly before the wind blows.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مشبوكة, plural: مشبوكين).

examples.text: في صفحة تانية مشبوكة ورا الرسالة.
examples.trans: There is a second page clipped behind the letter.
The lamp is plugged in.

meanings.note: Vocalized with shadda to distinguish passive participle مشبّك ('clipped', لوح مشبّك = clipboard) from noun مشبك ('clasp/clip').

examples.text: نور مسكت اللوح المشبك وسجلت مهام يوم الأربعا.
examples.trans: Nour held the clipboard and wrote down Wednesday's tasks.

examples.text: الورق مشبك ببعضه عشان ما يطير مع الهوا.
examples.trans: The sheets are clipped together so they don't blow away in the breeze.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مشترين.

examples.trans: The new buyers will inspect the building.
The seller and buyer agreed on the price.

meanings.note: Passive participle of شد ('to pull/tighten'): feminine مشدودة, plural مشدودين.

examples.text: الحبل هيك مشدود تمام وما رح يهتز.
examples.trans: Like this the rope is completely taut and won't wobble.
The fabric is stretched tight over the wooden frame.

meanings.note: Describes bright morning light or an upbeat musical ending.

examples.text: النهاية السريعة بتعطي الأغنية طابع مشرق.
examples.trans: A fast ending gives the song a bright feel.

examples.text: صباح الأحد كان مشرق ودافي بالساحة.
examples.trans: Sunday morning was bright and warm in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Spoken Arabic word for a chipped or hairline-cracked cup or plate.

examples.text: هاد الفنجان مشروخ من الطرف، لا تسكبي فيه قهوة سخنة.
examples.trans: This cup is chipped at the rim—don't pour hot coffee into it.

examples.text: شباك المخزن مشروخ شوي بس ما بفوّت مي.
examples.trans: The storeroom window has a hairline crack, though it doesn't let water in.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مشغولة, plural: مشغولين).

examples.text: كل المفاتيح من واحد لسبعة مشغولة.
examples.trans: All the keys from one to seven are taken.
Salma is busy preparing breakfast.

meanings.note: Passive participle of شق ('split/crack').

examples.text: الحمد لله الخشب سليم وما فيه إشي مشقوق.
examples.trans: Thankfully the wood is sound and nothing is cracked.
We replaced the cracked cup with a new one.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مشاكل.

examples.trans: There is no problem at all with your booking.
Every problem has a simple solution.

meanings.note: Describes weather or a place receiving plenty of sunlight.

examples.trans: The weather is sunny and nice today.

examples.text: الصبح كان مشمس ودافي عشان نقعد بالساحة.
examples.trans: The morning was sunny and warm enough for us to sit in the courtyard.

meanings.note: البنت المشهورة describes Layan's high-profile popularity across school.

examples.trans: Layan is well-known across the whole school.
This is a famous restaurant in Amman.

meanings.note: Passive participle of شوى ('roast/grill').

examples.text: البندورة المشوية بالفرن بتعطي الشوربة طعمة غنية.
examples.trans: Oven-roasted tomatoes give the soup a rich flavour.

examples.text: ريحته زاكية مع خضار مشوية وزيت زيتون.
examples.trans: It smells delicious with roasted vegetables and olive oil.

meanings.note: Common defective verb for walking on foot or things running smoothly.

examples.text: ممنوع تمشي عكاحلك لحد بكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: You mustn't walk on your ankle until tomorrow morning.

examples.text: مشينا عالهدا بالساحة بعد ما وقفت المطر.
examples.trans: We walked gently across the courtyard after the rain stopped.

meanings.note: The basic verb for walking, traveling on foot, or things moving forward.

examples.trans: We walked from home to school.

examples.text: مازن مشي عشر خطوات للشرق ووقف عند الشجرة.
examples.trans: Mazen walked ten steps to the east and stopped by the tree.

meanings.note: Noun of instance/manner from مشى; refers to a leisurely walk or someone's manner of walking.

examples.text: طلعنا بمشية خفيفة بالساحة بعد الغدا.
examples.trans: We went out for a light stroll in the courtyard after lunch.

examples.text: عرفته من مشيته السريعة قبل ما يلتفت.
examples.trans: I recognized him from his brisk gait before he turned around.

meanings.note: Plural-form noun that is THE everyday Jordanian/Levantine word for money.

examples.trans: Take cash from the box for the shop.
We saved money for annual maintenance.

meanings.note: Noun of place from صبّ (to pour); designates the pouring spout of a jug or kettle as well as a river mouth.

examples.text: مصب إبريق الشاي النحاسي مزخرف بنقش ناعم.
examples.trans: The spout of the copper teapot is decorated with fine engraving.

examples.text: تجمع المي عند مصب النافورة بالحوش.
examples.trans: The water gathers at the fountain outlet in the yard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مصدقة, plural: مصدقين).

examples.text: مش مصدق إنك نازلة بنفس النزل!
examples.trans: I cannot believe you are staying at the same inn!

examples.text: مش مصدقة قديش الغرفة صارت حلوة.
examples.trans: I cannot believe how lovely the room turned out.

meanings.note: Everyday noun from the root ص-ر-ف (spending), used for pocket money or household expenses.

examples.trans: Household expenses this month are low.
I have enough spending money for the week.

مصفوف.gloss: lined up; parked neatly; arranged in rows

meanings.en: lined up; parked neatly; arranged in rows
meanings.note: Form I passive participle from صفّ ('to line up/park'): used for parked vehicles or pastries arranged in rows.

examples.trans: The buses are parked neatly in rows in front of the station.
The chairs are lined up in the garden for the guests.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مصفاية, plural: مصفايين).

examples.trans: The valve is shut and the line is drained.
Strained mint tea in a glass cup.

meanings.note: Form I passive participle from صقل ('to polish'): describes glossy tile, stone, or glazed surfaces.

examples.trans: The hall tile is polished and gleaming.

examples.text: النحاس المصقول بيعكس الضو متل المراية.
examples.trans: Polished brass reflects the light like a mirror.

meanings.note: Masculine Arabic word meaning 'frosted' or 'sandblasted' glass.

examples.text: باب الحمام له زجاج مصنفر عشان الخصوصية.
examples.trans: The bathroom door has frosted glass for privacy.

examples.text: الخشب المصنفر ناعم عالملمس وجاهز للورنيش.
examples.trans: The sanded wood is smooth to the touch and ready for varnish.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun; يا مصيبتي means 'oh dear! / what a disaster!'. Plural: مصايب.

examples.trans: Oh dear me, I forgot my glasses in the office!

examples.text: الحمد لله طلعت شغلة بسيطة مش مصيبة.
examples.trans: Thank goodness it turned out minor, not a disaster.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مصايد.

examples.trans: That little device is a trap for mistakes!
Thankfully we did not fall into the trap.

meanings.note: Pronounced mazbuut in Amman; means 'properly, accurately, that's right!'.

examples.trans: Let me speak with him properly!
What you say is one hundred percent right.

meanings.note: Form IV active participle of أضحك (to make laugh).

examples.text: طارق حكى موقف مضحك خلى الكل يضحك.
examples.trans: Tariq told a funny story that made everyone laugh.

examples.text: رسمة القط بالدفتر طلعت مضحكة كتير.
examples.trans: The drawing of the cat in the notebook turned out very funny.

meanings.note: Form I sound verb describing chewing food carefully, especially during tasting.

examples.text: مضغ اللقمة على مهله عشان يميز البهارات.
examples.trans: He chewed the bite slowly so he could tell the spices apart.

examples.text: امضغ الأكل منيح قبل ما تبلعه.
examples.trans: Chew the food well before swallowing it.

meanings.note: Passive participle of ضغط ('to press/squeeze'), used for tight-fitting covers or packed schedules.

examples.trans: The box lid is pressed snug and tight.
My schedule is very packed this week.

meanings.note: Form III active participle of طابق ('to match/correspond'), used for identical copies or signatures.

examples.trans: That's an exact match of the original signature.
The two copies match each other completely.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مطابخ.

examples.trans: The smell of bread is coming from the kitchen.
The guesthouse kitchen is spacious and clean.

meanings.note: Feminine participle from طبع ('to print'), agreeing with قائمة ('menu').

examples.text: القائمة المطبوعة الجديدة عليها كل أسعار المشروبات.
examples.trans: The new printed menu has all the drink prices on it.

examples.text: معي نسخة مطبوعة من العقد عشان نراجعها سوا.
examples.trans: I have a printed copy of the contract so we can review it together.

meanings.note: Used for things like coffee, spices, or meat.

examples.trans: I want freshly ground coffee.

examples.text: ضفنا نص معلقة هيل مطحون ناعم عالقهوة.
examples.trans: We added half a spoonful of finely ground cardamom to the coffee.

meanings.note: Standard word for rain, commonly used across all registers of Arabic.

examples.trans: There is a lot of rain outside.

examples.text: نزل مطر خفيف وغسل أوراق الياسمين بالساحة.
examples.trans: Light rain fell and washed the jasmine leaves in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Used both for a carpenter's hammer and the small felt-covered wooden hammers inside a piano.

examples.text: كل مفتاح بالبيانو بيحرك مطرقة خشب صغيرة.
examples.trans: Every key on the piano moves a small wooden hammer.

examples.text: المطرقة السليمة بتضرب الأوتار وبترجع فورا.
examples.trans: A healthy hammer strikes the strings and rebounds cleanly.

meanings.note: Passive participle of طرق (to hammer or tread); refers to hammered brass/copper crafts or a frequently walked path.

examples.text: الصينية مصنوعة من نحاس مطروق بإيد حرفي.
examples.trans: The tray is made of hammered copper crafted by an artisan.

examples.text: هادا الدرب مطروق كتير بين السوق والمكتبة.
examples.trans: This path is well-trodden between the market and the library.

meanings.note: Form IV passive participle of أطلق; also forms the adverbial phrase على الإطلاق (at all).

examples.text: كان في هدوء مطلق بالقاعة وقت الفحص.
examples.trans: There was absolute silence in the hall during the exam.

examples.text: أعطوه حرية مطلقة باختيار مكونات الكيكة.
examples.trans: They gave him complete freedom in choosing the cake ingredients.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مطوية, plural: مطويين).

examples.trans: We found an old folded map in the box.

examples.text: في ورقة تانية مطوية ورا الإشعار.
examples.trans: There is a second folded sheet behind the notice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمطر, بيمطر).

examples.trans: It is raining outside!
It rained all night in Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Levantine active participle of عبّى (to fill), functioning like an ongoing verb.

examples.text: الورد معبّي الحوش ألوان وريحة حلوة بالربيع.
examples.trans: The flowers are filling the courtyard with colors and lovely scent in spring.

examples.text: أبوي معبّي الكرتونة كتب قديمة عشان نتبرع فيها.
examples.trans: My dad has filled the box with old books to donate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: معتمة, plural: معتمين).

examples.trans: The entrance was dim during the rain.
We lit the lanterns because the hallway is dim.

meanings.note: Feminine plural of معجزة, meaning 'miracles'.

examples.text: إنو لحقنا الطيارة بآخر لحظة كان عنجد معجزة!
examples.trans: That we caught the plane at the very last second was honestly a miracle!

examples.text: ستي دايماً بتحكي الصبر والعمل بسوّوا معجزات.
examples.trans: My grandma always says patience and hard work work miracles.

meanings.note: Everyday Arabic bakery noun for pastries and baked doughs.

examples.text: جبنا صحن معجنات مشكلة بالجبنة والزعتر للفطور.
examples.trans: We brought a platter of assorted cheese and za'atar pastries for breakfast.

examples.text: المخبز هاد مشهور بالمعجنات الطازة كل يوم الصبح.
examples.trans: This bakery is famous for its fresh pastries every morning.

meanings.note: Refers to metallic materials or sometimes one's inner character.

examples.text: هذا الباب مصنوع من معدن قوي.
examples.trans: This door is made of strong metal.

examples.text: العلبة مصنوعة من معدن خفيف ما بصدي مع الوقت.
examples.trans: The box is made of a light metal that does not rust over time.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from معدن (metal, mineral); describes metal containers as well as mineral water.

examples.text: البطاقات محفوظة جوا علبة معدنية صغيرة.
examples.trans: The cards are kept inside a small metal tin.

examples.text: أعطتنا قزازة مي معدنية باردة بعد المشي.
examples.trans: She gave us a cold bottle of mineral water after the walk.

meanings.note: Describes climbing vines like ivy, jasmine, or grapevines.

examples.text: الياسمين المعرش عالقوس بلش يفتح ورد أبيض.
examples.trans: The climbing jasmine on the archway has started opening white blossoms.

examples.text: اللبلاب المعرش غطى الشنكل الحديد كله.
examples.trans: The climbing ivy covered the iron hook completely.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: معروضة, plural: معروضين).

examples.trans: The building was put up for sale.
The fresh bread is laid out on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: معصبة, plural: معصبين).

examples.trans: His voice is nervous, not angry.

examples.text: لا ترد وأنت معصب، خد نفس.
examples.trans: Do not answer while angry; take a breath.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: معاطف.

examples.trans: Take off your heavy coat and rest.
Hang the grey coat beside the door.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: معطية, plural: معطيين).

examples.trans: The landlord has given us thirty days.
I gave him my word yesterday.

meanings.note: Standalone معقول! is a classic Jordanian exclamation of amazed disbelief ('No way! / Could it really be?!').

examples.text: معقول! قطار جدي الخشب لسا موجود!
examples.trans: Could it be! Grandfather's wooden train is still around!
The price is reasonable and fair for everyone.

meanings.note: Common preposition with second-person masculine singular suffix.

examples.trans: I want to talk with you about an important topic.

examples.text: جبت البوصلة معك عشان نحدد اتجاه الشمال؟
examples.trans: Did you bring the compass with you so we can find north?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: معلقة, plural: معلقين).

examples.trans: The paper lanterns hanging in the courtyard are lovely.
The key is hanging on the wooden board.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine metathesis of ملعقة ('spoon'), placing the ع before the ل.

examples.text: حطّي معلقة صغيرة قرفة على وجه السحلب.
examples.trans: Put a teaspoon of cinnamon on top of the sahlab.

examples.text: نسيت أجيب المعلقة عشان أحرك الشاي فيها.
examples.trans: I forgot to bring the spoon to stir the tea with.

meanings.note: In Jordanian speech, يا معلم is an affectionate, respectful way to address a boss or skilled craftsperson.

examples.trans: You are all generosity, boss!
She was a very gifted piano teacher.

meanings.note: Masculine participle from علّق ('to hang'), meaning 'hung up' or 'hanging'.

examples.text: البرواز القديم معلّق عالحيط فوق البيانو.
examples.trans: The old frame is hanging on the wall above the piano.

examples.text: المعطف معلّق ورا الباب عشان ما ينسى ياخده معه.
examples.trans: The coat is hung behind the door so he doesn't forget to take it with him.

meanings.note: In Jordanian Arabic, يا معلم is an affectionate respectful title meaning 'boss'.

examples.text: يسلمو إيديك يا معلّم طارق، الشغل طلع فخم!
examples.trans: Bless your hands, Master Tariq—the work turned out top-notch!

examples.text: المعلّم بالورشة بعرف يصلّح أي عطل بالخشب.
examples.trans: The master craftsman at the workshop knows how to fix any wood damage.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: معمارية, plural: معماريين).

examples.trans: I am an architectural acoustics engineer.

examples.text: حجر عمان إله طابع معماري جميل.
examples.trans: Amman stone has a beautiful architectural character.

meanings.note: Defective noun on the maf'al pattern from عنى; plural معاني.

examples.text: هلق فهمنا معنى الجملة المكتوبة بالهامش.
examples.trans: Now we understand the meaning of the sentence written in the margin.

examples.text: كلام الجد دايما إله معنى عميق وحلو.
examples.trans: Grandfather's words always carry a deep and lovely meaning.

meanings.note: Follows an indefinite noun to mean 'a certain / particular' (لمرحلة معينة 'up to a certain point').

examples.trans: Do you have a specific time we can meet?
Is there a particular reason for your question?

meanings.note: Form III verbal noun of غامر (to venture); plural مغامرات.

examples.text: البحث عن الخريطة الضائعة كان مغامرة ممتعة.
examples.trans: Searching for the lost map was a fun adventure.

examples.text: الجد حكالنا عن مغامراته لما كان يبحر.
examples.trans: Grandfather told us about his adventures when he used to sail.

meanings.note: Form II participle adjective (feminine مغبرة, plural مغبرين) from غبرة ('dust').

examples.text: الدرابزين كان مغبر قبل ما نمسحه.
examples.trans: The railing was dusty before we wiped it.
The old boxes in the storeroom are all dusty.

meanings.note: Levantine adjective describing frosted lamp glass (قزاز مغبش) or fogged-up spectacles.

examples.text: القزاز المغبش بيخلي ضو اللمبة هادي للعين.
examples.trans: Frosted glass makes the lamp light gentle on the eyes.

examples.text: نظارتي مغبشة من بخار إبريق الشاي!
