examples.trans: My glasses are fogged up from the steam of the teapot!

meanings.note: Feminine Levantine Arabic word meaning 'misty', 'foggy', or 'blurry'.

examples.text: زجاج الشباك مغبّش من البخار، لازم نمسحه.
examples.trans: The windowpane is fogged up from the steam; we need to wipe it.

examples.text: الصورة طلعت مغبّشة شوي لأنو إيدي تحركت.
examples.trans: The photo came out a bit blurry because my hand moved.

meanings.note: Noun of instrument (مَفْعَلة) from غرف ('to scoop/ladle out'); pl. مغارف.

examples.trans: Bring me the big ladle.
He ladled the soup with a wooden ladle.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مغاسل.

examples.trans: The sink water is warm now.
We cleaned the washbasin and mirror in the morning.

meanings.note: Refers to a paper envelope used for letters or documents.

examples.trans: I put the money in an envelope.

examples.text: حطينا البطاقات كلها جوا مغلف ورق بني.
examples.trans: We put all the cards inside a brown paper envelope.

meanings.note: Feminine participle meaning 'coated/wrapped' or 'laminated' in everyday Arabic.

examples.text: القائمة المطبوعة مغلّفة بالبلاستيك عشان ما تتوسخ.
examples.trans: The printed menu is laminated in plastic so it doesn't get dirty.

examples.text: الهدية جاهزة ومغلّفة بورق ملون وشريطة.
examples.trans: The gift is ready and wrapped in colored paper and a ribbon.

meanings.note: Means both a door key and a mechanic's spanner/wrench (مفتاح حديد iron wrench).

examples.trans: Here is the key to room four.
We have eight brass keys on the board.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مفتشين.

examples.trans: We thought he was a hotel inspector from the guidebook!
The inspector checked the building's safety features.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مفتوحة, plural: مفتوحين).

examples.trans: Is the hardware shop open right now?
Here is to neighbours and our open gates!

meanings.note: Broken plural of مفرش, the everyday word for a tablecloth or table runner.

examples.text: فرشنا مفرش أبيض مكوي على كل طاولة بالقاعة.
examples.trans: We spread a pressed white tablecloth on every table in the hall.

examples.text: المفارش المطرزة بتعطي السفرة منظر تراثي حلو.
examples.trans: Embroidered tablecloths give the dining table a lovely traditional look.

meanings.note: Passive participle of فرد ('to spread/unfold'), describing flat sheets of paper or rolled dough.

examples.trans: They stayed flat inside the box.
The papers are spread out on the table.

meanings.note: Used with الـ (المفروض + imperfect verb) to mean 'is supposed to'.

examples.text: المفروض ينشف الدهان تماما قبل الساعة ستة.
examples.trans: The paint is supposed to dry completely before six o'clock.

examples.text: كان المفروض نركب الشيش العصر بس بلشت تمطر.
examples.trans: We were supposed to hang the shutters in the afternoon, then it started raining.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مفصلات.

examples.text: حطيت نقطة زيت على مفصلة الباب.
examples.trans: I put a drop of oil on the door hinge.
The brass hinges of the chest are intact.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مفضلة, plural: مفضلين).

examples.trans: This is my favourite cup for tea.

examples.text: كيكة الليمون هي الحلو المفضل عندهم.
examples.trans: Lemon cake is their favourite dessert.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine plural noun; مكتب المفقودات means 'lost and found'.

examples.trans: We called the lost-and-found office at the station.
He handed the wallet in to lost property.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مفكات.

examples.trans: He always carries a small screwdriver in his pocket.
Pass me the screwdriver from the toolbox.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مفكرة, plural: مفكرين).

examples.trans: Wait, do you think I am a hotel inspector?
I thought the shop was closed today.

meanings.note: وجود نوف معهم مفيد إلنا means 'Noaf's presence with them is helpful to us'.

examples.trans: This book is very useful.
Your advice was helpful to me.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مقابلة, plural: —).

examples.trans: He stood on the pavement on the opposite street.
The pharmacy is in the building across the way.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مقاسات.

examples.trans: This size fits you perfectly.
The shop sells all pipe sizes.

meanings.note: In Arabic music, names both a traditional melodic mode (maqam) and a Western musical key.

examples.text: سعاد كتبت التكملة على نفس المقام بالزبط.
examples.trans: Suad wrote the continuation in the exact same key.

examples.text: هاد اللحن مكتوب على مقام دافي وهادي.
examples.trans: This melody is written in a warm, gentle key.

meanings.note: Favorite Levantine food word for crusty fresh bread or crisp pastry.

examples.text: الخبز طلع من الفرن سخن ومقرمش.
examples.trans: The bread came out of the oven hot and crusty.

examples.text: قشرة اللوز المقرمشة أطيب إشي بالتارت.
examples.trans: The crisp almond crust is the best part of the tart.

meanings.note: Used for things that are cut or split into parts.

examples.trans: The cake is divided into two halves.

examples.text: الورقة مقسومة بخط رصاص إلى تلات أقسام متساوية.
examples.trans: The sheet is divided by a pencil line into three equal sections.

meanings.note: Masculine noun with broken plural مقاطع, used for a musical passage, verse, or text excerpt.

examples.text: خلينا نعيد المقطع الوسطاني من الأغنية.
examples.trans: Let's repeat the middle section of the song.
This is the nicest passage in the whole story.

meanings.note: Noun of place from ق-ع-د ('to sit'); names the seat of a chair or a garden bench.

examples.text: ارفع مقعد الكرسي شوي عشان يطوي معك.
examples.trans: Lift the chair seat slightly so it folds for you.

examples.text: في مقعد خشب طويل تحت شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: There is a long wooden bench under the courtyard tree.

meanings.note: From قفل (to lock); agrees with feminine غرفة.

examples.text: غرفة المخزن مقفولة والمفتاح مع مازن.
examples.trans: The storeroom is locked and Mazen has the key.

examples.text: تأكد إنو الشباك مقفول قبل ما تطلع من المكتب.
examples.trans: Make sure the window is locked before you leave the office.

meanings.note: Form I passive participle from قلب ('to flip'). With بـ, بالمقلوب means 'upside down / backwards'.

examples.trans: The sign is hung upside down on the door!

examples.text: الورقة مقلوبة، لفها عشان تقرأ المكتوب.
examples.trans: The sheet is upside down—turn it round to read what's written.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مقلية, plural: مقليين).

examples.text: البيض المقلي مع الأعشاب زاكي كتير.
examples.trans: Fried eggs with herbs are delicious.
Hot, crispy fried potatoes.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle from قلّم ('to stripe/trim'): describes striped cloth, bags, or notebooks.

examples.text: شنطة القماش المقلمة كانت على الكرسي.
examples.trans: The striped canvas bag was on the chair.
He wore a blue shirt striped with white.

meanings.note: From قنطرة (arch), describing the classic arched stone windows of old Amman.

examples.text: الشبابيك المقنطرة بالحجر الأبيض بتزين بيوت عمان القديمة.
examples.trans: Arched windows in white stone adorn the old houses of Amman.

examples.text: القاعة فيها سقف مقنطر وباب عالي كتير.
examples.trans: The hall has a vaulted arched ceiling and a very tall door.

meanings.note: Formal/signboard Arabic word for 'café' (alongside conversational كافيه), ideal for painted signs.

examples.text: كتبنا عاللوحة: مقهى جنينة الغرفة تسعة.
examples.trans: We painted on the sign: Room Nine Garden Café.

examples.text: المقهى رح يفتح يوميا من الصبح للمسا.
examples.trans: The café will be open daily from morning till evening.

meanings.note: From قوس, an arch or bow: arched windows are شبابيك مقوسة.

examples.trans: The mosque's door is arched and tall.
They have old arched windows.

meanings.note: Feminine singular word built from قوس ('arch'), agreeing with الشبابيك.

examples.text: المدخل له قوس حجري مقوّس من الطراز القديم.
examples.trans: The entrance has an arched stone doorway in the old style.

examples.text: حطّينا مرايا مقوّسة فوق المغسلة بالحمام.
examples.trans: We placed arched mirrors above the sink in the bathroom.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مكالمات.

examples.trans: An important phone call came in on the landline.
She finished the call in two minutes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أماكن.

examples.trans: This place is very quiet and comfortable.
Everything is tidy in its proper place.

meanings.note: Used for both a workplace (office) and the piece of furniture (desk).

examples.trans: I am waiting for you in my office.

examples.text: لقينا الخريطة التانية جوا درج مكتب جدي.
examples.trans: We found the second map inside my grandfather's desk drawer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مكتبات.

examples.trans: There are old bookshops in downtown Amman.
The public library is a quiet place to read.

meanings.note: Often used as a noun meaning 'letter' (mail) or 'destiny' in traditional contexts.

examples.trans: The name is written on the board.

examples.text: الرقم مكتوب بخط صغير تحت الختم الأحمر.
examples.trans: The number is written in small handwriting beneath the red seal.

meanings.note: Feminine form of maktub, used as an adjective for feminine nouns.

examples.trans: The message is written in nice handwriting.

examples.text: الوصفة الأصلية مكتوبة على ضهر كرت التذوق.
examples.trans: The original recipe is written on the back of the tasting card.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle of كرّم ('to honour'): الضيوف المكرمين ('the honoured guests').

examples.trans: Welcome to our honoured guests on the rooftop terrace!
This area is reserved for honoured visitors.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle from كرّم ('to honour'): used for distinguished guests.

examples.trans: The guest of honour arrived early for the reception.
We welcomed the honoured teachers in the hall.

meanings.note: Plural-only feminine noun (f. pl.) used across Jordan for roasted almonds, pistachios, walnuts, and cashews.

examples.text: رشينا مكسرات محمصة على وجه الكيكة.
examples.trans: We sprinkled roasted nuts on top of the cake.

examples.text: قدمنا الشاي مع صحن فواكه ومكسرات.
examples.trans: We served tea with a plate of fruit and nuts.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مكسورة, plural: مكسورين).

examples.trans: Put the broken valve in your coat pocket.
We fixed the broken chair leg.

meanings.note: Describes sanded bare wood (خشب مكشوف) or an open-air courtyard.

examples.text: الخشب المكشوف بعد الصنفرة لازم يضل ناشف.
examples.trans: Bare wood after sanding has to stay dry.
We sat in the open courtyard beneath the stars.

meanings.note: Used for ice cubes (مكعب تلج), sugar cubes, and diced vegetables.

examples.text: دوق الشوربة وشوف إذا بدها كمان مكعب جزر.
examples.trans: Taste the soup and see if it needs another cube of carrot.

examples.text: لفينا مكعبات التلج بمنشفة قطن نضيفة.
examples.trans: We wrapped the ice cubes in a clean cotton towel.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle of كوّن used as a noun; plural مكونات (ingredients).

examples.text: العسل البلدي هو أهم مكون بهاي الكيكة.
examples.trans: Local honey is the most important ingredient in this cake.

examples.text: قارنوا قائمة المكونات على الكرت التاني.
examples.trans: Compare the list of ingredients on the second card.

meanings.note: From كوى (to iron clothes or linens).

examples.trans: Your shirt is ironed and hanging in the closet on the right.

examples.text: المفارش لازم تكون مكوية ومنظمة قبل ما يوصلوا الضيوف.
examples.trans: The tablecloths need to be ironed and neat before the guests arrive.

meanings.note: Used for remarks, annotations, or paying attention to details.

examples.trans: I have a small note on the work.

examples.text: سجلنا ملاحظة صغيرة عن نكهة قشر البرتقال.
examples.trans: We jotted down a short note about the orange peel flavour.

meanings.note: Active participle of لقى ('to find'); مش ملاقي means 'I cannot find'.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
I cannot find the key in my pocket.

meanings.note: Essential kitchen noun; ملح بحر = 'sea salt'.

examples.text: إوعك تخربط بين مرتبان السكر ومرتبان الملح!
examples.trans: Don't ever mix up the sugar jar and the salt jar!

examples.text: حطيت نص معلقة ملح بالعجين قبل الخبز.
examples.trans: I added half a spoonful of salt to the dough before baking.

meanings.note: Musical composer; feminine ملحنة (mulahhine).

examples.text: مدام سعاد صارت ملحنتنا الرسمية لليلة الافتتاح!
examples.trans: Madam Suad has become our official composer for opening night!

examples.text: الملحن كتب أول أربعة وعشرين مازورة بالحبر الأسود.
examples.trans: The composer wrote the first twenty-four bars in black ink.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ملزقة, plural: ملزقين).

examples.trans: There is a white envelope taped to the handle.
The key was taped underneath the box.

meanings.note: Dual ملصقين ('the two labels'), plural ملصقات ('labels / stickers').

examples.text: نور كتبت ملصقات واضحة وكبيرة لكل المرتبانات.
examples.trans: Nour wrote big, clear labels for all the jars.

examples.text: تأكد إن الملصقين ناشفين قبل ما تمسك القزاز.
examples.trans: Make sure both labels are dry before you pick up the glass.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle of لطّخ (to smear/stain); describes ink, paint, or jam stains.

examples.text: الحبر كان ملطخ على الزاوية التحتانية للورقة.
examples.trans: The ink was smudged on the bottom corner of the sheet.

examples.text: إيديه ملطخة بعجين وطحين من الخبيز.
examples.trans: His hands are smeared with dough and flour from baking.

meanings.note: In spoken Jordanian, standard ملعقة shifts consonants to معلقة (ma'laqa), plural معالق (ma'aaliq).

examples.text: حطي معلقة صغيرة جنب كل فنجان.
examples.trans: Put a small spoon beside every cup.
The silver spoons are in the top drawer.

meanings.note: Front-desk binder or document folder (from لف 'wrap/fold').

examples.text: نور رتبت قوائم المطبخ بملف الاستقبال الأخضر.
examples.trans: Nour organized the kitchen checklists in the green front-desk folder.

examples.text: كل الفواتير والمخططات محفوظة بنفس الملف.
examples.trans: All the receipts and floor plans are kept in the same folder.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ملفوفة, plural: ملفوفين).

examples.text: شو هاد الشي الملفوف بورق أبيض؟
examples.trans: What is this thing wrapped in white paper?
The parcel is wrapped with great care.

meanings.note: Fine tweezers for delicate repair work, or small kitchen tongs.

examples.text: طارق طلب ملقط رفيع عشان يمسك الدبوس النحاس.
examples.trans: Tariq asked for thin tweezers to hold the tiny brass pin.

examples.text: البرغي الصغير ما بينمسك إلا بملقط.
examples.trans: That tiny screw can only be picked up with tweezers.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from ملك ('king'): feminine ملكية, plural ملكيين.

examples.text: صبغت السما بلون أزرق ملكي غامق.
examples.trans: I painted the sky in a deep royal blue colour.

examples.text: القصر الملكي مبين من فوق التلة.
examples.trans: The royal palace is visible from the top of the hill.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun; نقل ملكية means 'transfer of ownership / title deed'. Plural: ملكيات.

examples.trans: We read the notice of property transfer.
The title deeds are kept in the safe.

meanings.note: Passive participle of لمّع ('to polish shoes, brass, or wood').

examples.text: مازن إجا بقميص أبيض مكوي وحذاء أسود ملمع.
examples.trans: Mazen arrived in a pressed white shirt and polished black shoes.

examples.text: الطاولات الخشب الملمعة بتعكس ضو الفوانيس.
examples.trans: The polished wooden tables reflect the glow of the lanterns.

meanings.note: Everyday verb meaning 'fill a house, jug, or basket'.

examples.text: ريحة الخبز السخن ملت الساحة كلها.
examples.trans: The scent of hot bread filled the entire courtyard.

examples.text: ضيوف الصيف ملوا كل غرف البيت.
examples.trans: Summer guests filled every room of the house.

meanings.note: Everyday short form of مليمتر ('millimetre'); ولا ملي ('not a single millimetre').

examples.text: الشنكل المصدي ما تحرك ولا ملي قبل الزيت.
examples.trans: The rusty latch wouldn't budge a single millimetre before the oil.

examples.text: قاس رامي عرض البرواز بالمتر والملي.
examples.trans: Rami measured the width of the frame down to the millimetre.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مليانة, plural: مليانين).

examples.trans: All the hotels on our street are full tonight!
The pot is full of hot mint tea.

meanings.note: Popular aromatic herb in Jordanian tea traditions, prized for its gentle citrus scent.

examples.text: نقعنا أوراق مليسة طازجة مع الشاي الأخضر.
examples.trans: We steeped fresh lemon balm leaves with green tea.

examples.text: ريحة المليسة بالحديقة بتشبه قشر الليمون.
examples.trans: The scent of lemon balm in the garden resembles lemon zest.

meanings.note: Standard measurement unit, borrowed into Arabic.

examples.trans: The difference is only one millimeter.

examples.text: قاس المسافة بالمسطرة بدقة مليمتر واحد.
examples.trans: He measured the distance with the ruler to within a single millimetre.

meanings.note: Very common word of approval or rating something highly.

examples.trans: Your work is excellent today.

examples.text: توازن السكر والليمون بهاي الكيكة ممتاز جدا.
examples.trans: The balance of sugar and lemon in this cake is truly excellent.

meanings.note: Agent noun from مثّل (to represent), meaning a delegate or representative.

examples.text: اجا ممثّل عن البلدية عشان يشوف التصاريح الجديدة.
examples.trans: A representative from the municipality came to inspect the new permits.

examples.text: هو ممثّل مسرحي معروف بعمان وشارك بعروض كتيرة.
examples.trans: He's a well-known stage actor in Amman and has appeared in many shows.

meanings.note: An inside hallway or a narrow passage between buildings.

examples.trans: The bathroom is at the end of the hallway.
The hallway is dark, turn on the light.

meanings.note: Levantine passive participle of مزع ('to tear/rip'): feminine ممزوعة, plural ممزوعين.

examples.text: الورقة ممزوعة من الطرف، لازم نبدلها.
examples.trans: The sheet is torn at the edge, we need to replace it.

examples.text: كمّ القميص كان ممزوع من الشغل.
examples.trans: The shirt sleeve was torn from working.

meanings.note: Describes a rainy day, season or night (يوم ممطر 'a rainy day').

examples.trans: It was a cold, rainy day.
Winter this year is very rainy.

meanings.note: Used to ask for permission 'is it possible?' or to say 'perhaps'.

examples.trans: Is it possible for you to give me the pen?

examples.text: ممكن تعطينا الورقة التانية عشان نقارن الأرقام؟
examples.trans: Could you hand us the second sheet so we can compare the numbers?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مملة, plural: مملين).

examples.text: تاني يوم شغل ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: Day two at work will not be boring!
We thought it was a dull municipal notice.

meanings.note: Conversational vocalization expressing either delight at tasty food or thoughtful hesitation.

examples.trans: Mmm, the smell of the cake in the oven is mouth-watering!

examples.text: ممم، خلينا نفكر شوي قبل ما نجاوب.
examples.trans: Hmm, let us think a moment before we answer.

meanings.note: Used on signs or to indicate rules against doing something.

examples.trans: Smoking is forbidden here.

examples.text: ممنوع حدا يفتح الصينية قبل ما يخلص التوقيت.
examples.trans: Nobody is allowed to open the tin before the timer finishes.

meanings.note: Describes a café's signature dish (كيكة مميزة) or a special occasion.

examples.text: كل كافيه ناجح عنده كيكة مميزة بيعرفوها الناس.
examples.trans: Every great café has one signature cake people know it for.

examples.text: يوم الافتتاح رح يكون يوم مميز للكل.
examples.trans: Opening day is going to be a special day for everyone.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am from Jordan.

examples.text: جبنا العسل البلدي الصافي من مزرعة قريبة.
examples.trans: We brought the pure local honey from a nearby farm.

meanings.note: Originally plural of منخار ('nostril'), used universally in Levantine Arabic as the normal word for 'nose'.

examples.trans: He has my exact nose, I swear.
My nose is red from the cold.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مناسبة, plural: مناسبين).

examples.trans: The sweater's size fits you perfectly.
The courtyard is quiet and suitable for work.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: منبهات.

examples.trans: Set the alarm for six in the morning.
The alarm rang and we woke up early.

meanings.note: Passive participle of نحت (to carve stone or wood); used for architectural reliefs and carved wooden items.

examples.text: في رقم منحوت على الحجر فوق البوابة.
examples.trans: There is a number carved into the stone above the gate.

examples.text: القوس المنحوت بالحيط قديم ومتقن كتير.
examples.trans: The carved arch in the wall is old and very finely crafted.

meanings.note: Everyday colloquial Jordanian word for nose (more common in casual speech than أنف); plural مناخير.

examples.text: قرب منخاره من الصحن عشان يشم الهيل.
examples.trans: He brought his nose close to the plate to smell the cardamom.

examples.text: منخاري بردان من نسمة الهوا بالبلكونة.
examples.trans: My nose is cold from the breeze on the balcony.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مندهشة, plural: مندهشين).

examples.trans: You look amazed, Madam Suad!
We were all amazed by the coincidence.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مناديل.

examples.trans: We arranged the white napkins on the tables.
Here is a clean paper napkin.

meanings.note: Literary/MSA preposition for 'since/for', highlighting Mazen's overly stiff speech.

examples.text: يعمل هذا المقهى في خدمة الحي منذ أكثر من ثلاثين عاماً.
examples.trans: This café has been serving the neighborhood for over thirty years.

examples.text: لم نلتقِ بصديقنا القديم منذ تخرجنا من الجامعة.
examples.trans: We haven't met our old friend since we graduated from university.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مناشف.

examples.trans: The room has clean white towels.
Here is a dry towel after the rain.

meanings.note: Passive participle of نشر (to publish).

examples.text: المقال منشور بالجريدة الرسمية تبع اليوم.
examples.trans: The article is published in today's official gazette.

examples.text: شفت منشور حلو عالفيسبوك عن افتتاح المعرض.
examples.trans: I saw a nice post on Facebook about the exhibition opening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مناطق.

examples.trans: We rode the same bus to the same district.
This area is famous for its stone houses.

meanings.note: Masculine noun of place (plural مناظر) from نظر ('to look'). Common exclamation: يا سلام على هالمنظر!

examples.text: من الشرفة بنشوف أحلى منظر لعمان وقت الغروب.
examples.trans: From the terrace we see the prettiest view of Amman at sunset.
The lit lanterns made an amazing sight.

meanings.note: Active participle from أنعش (to refresh); naturally captures bright, zesty citrus aroma.

examples.text: عصير الليمون بالنعنع مشروب منعش كتير بالصيف.
examples.trans: Lemon-mint juice is a very refreshing drink in the summer.

examples.text: الهوا الصبح عالبلكونة كان بارد ومنعش.
examples.trans: The morning air on the balcony was cool and crisp.

meanings.note: Form IV active participle of أنقذ (to rescue); plural منقذين.

examples.text: إجا رامي بالمفتاح الاحتياطي وكان المنقذ بالوقت الصح.
examples.trans: Rami arrived with the spare key and was the rescuer just in time.

examples.text: الكل شكر المنقذ اللي لاقى الخريطة الضائعة.
examples.trans: Everyone thanked the rescuer who found the lost map.

meanings.note: From نور, light. Also a warm compliment to a guest: البيت منور! 'the house shines (with you)!'.

examples.trans: The room is bright in the morning.
Welcome, your visit lights up the house!

meanings.en: bright; radiant; lighting up the room
meanings.note: Form II active participle of نوّر ('to illuminate'); also a warm welcome: الدار منوّرة بوجودك!

examples.trans: His face looked radiant in the photo.
The house is bright today with your presence.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'good' and adverbially 'well' (نمت منيح؟ 'did you sleep well?').

examples.trans: It has a good, comfortable wooden bed.
Did you sleep well under the wooden ceiling?

meanings.note: Levantine equivalent for 'jayyida', feminine form.

examples.trans: The idea is very good.

examples.text: نتيجة التذوق طلعت منيحة وأحسن من المرة الأولى.
examples.trans: The tasting result came out good and better than the first time.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle of هذّب (to refine manners); common praise for children and guests.

examples.text: طارق ولد مهذب وبحكي مع الكل باحترام.
examples.trans: Tariq is a polite boy and speaks to everyone respectfully.

examples.text: سلمت علينا بطريقة لطيفة ومهذبة كتير.
examples.trans: She greeted us in a very kind and polite manner.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (pl. مهرجانات) used for street festivals, fairs, and cultural events.

examples.trans: We should put up a poster for the festival.
The street is full of people during the festival.

meanings.note: Lives in the chunk على مهل (or على مهلك), 'slowly, take your time'.

examples.trans: Walk slowly, the stairs are slippery.
Drive slowly, it is raining.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مهمة, plural: مهمين).

examples.text: يوم الجمعة يوم مهم كتير إلي.
examples.trans: Friday is a very important day for me.
I have an important note at the bottom of the page.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine plural noun; سلة المهملات means 'wastebasket / rubbish bin'.

examples.trans: Put the old paper in the wastebasket.
We emptied the wastebin in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; مهندس معماري means 'architect'. Plural: مهندسين.

examples.trans: His brother is a skilled architect in Amman.
The engineer inspected the walls of the old building.

meanings.note: Common Levantine variant of مش used to negate adjectives and nouns.

examples.text: الجو اليوم مو بارد كتير متل مبارح.
examples.trans: The weather today isn't as cold as yesterday.

examples.text: هادي الشنطة مو إلي، اسأل مازن إذا لإلو.
examples.trans: This bag isn't mine—ask Mazen if it's his.

meanings.note: Form III active participle of وافق ('to agree'); common as a quick reply: موافق ('deal / agreed').

examples.trans: Agreed, uncle — let's do it.
Everyone agrees on the new idea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: موافقات.

examples.trans: He nodded his head in agreement with a smile.
We received official municipal approval.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: موجودة, plural: موجودين).

examples.trans: Your glasses are right there on your forehead!
Tariq is down in the workshop.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle from ورد ('rose/flower'): describes floral fabric or patterns.

examples.trans: She put a floral shawl over her shoulders.
The floral curtain brightened up the room.

meanings.note: Used for literal weight or metaphorically for a balanced, rational person or idea.

examples.trans: Her decisions are always balanced.

examples.text: المقادير موزونة بالميزان بدقة عشان ما تخرب الوصفة.
examples.trans: The ingredients are weighed on the scale accurately so the recipe does not fail.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: We found an old music book in the suitcase.
Gentle music is soothing in the evening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: موسيقية, plural: موسيقيين).

examples.trans: Play the musical scale slowly.
She has a sensitive musical ear.

meanings.note: Passive participle of وصل ('to connect, join').

examples.text: السلك النحاس موصول منيح بعلبة الكهربا.
examples.trans: The copper wire is firmly connected to the electrical box.
The sunroom is connected to the back hallway.

meanings.note: Feminine loanword used in everyday speech for clothing trends, hairstyles, or anything stylish.

examples.trans: That was the summer fashion back then.
She follows fashion every season.

meanings.note: Used for an issue under discussion (هاد الموضوع، أي موضوع بالضبط؟).

examples.trans: Let's close this topic.
The matter is more serious than I thought.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: موظفة). Plural: موظفين.

examples.trans: I am the new receptionist at the guesthouse.
All the staff here are helpful and friendly.

meanings.note: Feminine form of موظف, revealing the municipal inspector is a woman.

examples.text: الموظفة بالشباك التاني ساعدتني أخلص المعاملة بسرعة.
examples.trans: The clerk at the second counter helped me finish the paperwork quickly.

examples.text: أختي موظفة ببنك بعمان من خمس سنين.
examples.trans: My sister has been an employee at a bank in Amman for five years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مواعيد.

examples.trans: I always appreciate punctuality.

examples.text: عندنا موعد مهم يوم الجمعة الظهر.
examples.trans: We have an important appointment Friday at noon.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle of وقّع ('to sign a document, check, or letter'), root و-ق-ع.

examples.trans: The little notebook is signed by Suad.
The paper is signed and stamped, ready.

meanings.note: Traditional Levantine term for seasonal homemade pantry preserves such as olive oil, pickles, herbs, and jams.

examples.text: الجدة دايما بتحفظ مونة العسل والزعتر بالرف العالي.
examples.trans: Grandmother always keeps the honey and thyme pantry provisions on the top shelf.

examples.text: بيت المونة مليان مرطبانات مربى ومخلل.
examples.trans: The pantry room is full of jars of jam and pickles.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مواهب.

examples.trans: She has a natural gift for cooking and hospitality.
Playing music takes talent and daily practice.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word for water (feminine!). Before another noun in possession ('water of...'), becomes مية (mayyet): مية الدوش ('shower water'), مية الشتا ('winter water').

examples.trans: Please drink a glass of cold water.
The hot water is working again in the bathroom.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'one hundred' (مية مرة 'a hundred times' — construct مية miyyet before a noun).

examples.trans: Yes, a hundred times yes!
I am one hundred percent sure.

meanings.note: Colloquial pronunciation of the dual form for 100.

examples.trans: I only have two hundred dinars.

examples.text: الوصفة بتحتاج ميتين غرام طحين منخول ومية غرام سكر.
examples.trans: The recipe needs two hundred grams of sifted flour and a hundred grams of sugar.

meanings.note: Loanword used both for competition medals and small keychains or pendant medallions.

examples.text: المفتاح مربوط بميدالية نحاس على شكل نجمة.
examples.trans: The key is attached to a star-shaped brass keychain.
He won a silver medal in the swimming competition.

meanings.note: From ميزان ('scales, balance'); everyday word for a household or project budget.

examples.text: اشترينا كل الأغراض وضلينا ضمن الميزانية.
examples.trans: We bought all the supplies and stayed within budget.
Nour worked out the café budget in the notebook.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun used for people.

examples.trans: Who rang the bell?

examples.text: مين كتب هاي الملاحظة عالورقة بالحبر الأزرق؟
examples.trans: Who wrote this note on the paper in blue ink?

meanings.note: Colloquial spelling of ميناء (masculine or feminine; plural موانئ / مينايات).

examples.text: سفينة الصيد رجعت عالمينا قبل الليل.
examples.trans: The fishing boat returned to the harbour before nightfall.

examples.text: رسمت قوارب صغيرة واقفة عند المينا.
examples.trans: I drew small boats docked by the harbour.

meanings.note: Form II verb ميّز means 'to distinguish' or 'tell apart'.

examples.text: ما قدرت أميّز بين المرتبانين بدون ما أدوقهم.
examples.trans: I couldn't tell the two jars apart without tasting them.

examples.text: من بعيد ما بتميّز الخط إذا كان صغير كتير.
examples.trans: From far away you can't make out the writing if it's very small.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمنع, بيمنع).

examples.trans: The old stone keeps out street noise.
The awning kept the rain off the window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمشي, بيمشي).

examples.trans: I always walk fast on the first day.

examples.text: اسمع، المي عم بتمشي جوا الماسورة!
examples.trans: Listen, the water is flowing inside the pipe!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنادي, بينادي).

examples.trans: Do we call each other by first name here?
Salma called everyone to breakfast.

meanings.note: Feminine noun (unmarked, without ة ending). Used both for campfires and a kitchen stove flame.

examples.trans: The kitchen stove fire is still a bit low.
Put the kettle on the fire.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: نازلة, plural: نازلين).

examples.trans: The guests are coming down the stairs for breakfast.

examples.text: مش مصدق إنك نازلة بنفس النزل!
examples.trans: I cannot believe you are staying at the same inn!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ناس.

examples.trans: You are kind, generous people.
Morning coffee brings people together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Can refer to objects lacking moisture or metaphorically to a rude or blunt person.

examples.trans: The bread is dry, it can't be eaten.

examples.text: لازم نمسح الصحن بمنديل ناشف قبل ما نحط الكيكة.
examples.trans: We must wipe the plate with a dry cloth before putting the cake on.

meanings.note: Feminine adjective for dry objects.

examples.trans: The ground is dry, it needs water.

examples.text: الأعشاب بالمرطبان ناشفة ومحفوظة بعيد عن الرطوبة.
examples.trans: The herbs in the jar are dry and stored away from humidity.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ناعمة, plural: ناعمين); سكر ناعم means 'powdered sugar'.

examples.trans: I brought two soft pillows for the attic.
Lemon cake dusted with powdered sugar.

meanings.note: Used for decorative water fountains in parks or squares.

examples.trans: There is a beautiful fountain in the park.

examples.text: نافورة المي اللي بنص الساحة صوتها هادي ومريح.
examples.trans: The water fountain in the middle of the courtyard has a calm, soothing sound.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ناقصة, plural: ناقصين).

examples.trans: Tell me what is missing in the room?

examples.text: الأغراض كاملة ما فيها شي ناقص.
examples.trans: Everything is complete with nothing missing.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنام, بينام).

examples.trans: I feel I will sleep well tonight.
Did you sleep well under the wooden ceiling?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بناول, بيناول).

examples.trans: Hand me the heavy iron wrench.
Pass me the teacup, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ناوية, plural: ناويين).

examples.trans: Were you planning to watch from afar?
We intend to open the courtyard to the neighbours in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: نايمة, plural: نايمين).

examples.trans: The new guest is sleeping on the third floor.
The whole neighbourhood is asleep and quiet.

meanings.note: Generic noun for plants and flora; plural نباتات.

examples.text: الدفتر فيها رسومات عن كل نبات بالحديقة.
examples.trans: The notebook has drawings of every plant in the garden.
We watered the aromatic plants before sunset.

meanings.note: Verb for putting a picture or document in a frame.

examples.trans: We must frame this picture.

examples.text: خلينا نبروز الخريطة القديمة ونعلقها بالمكتبة.
examples.trans: Let us frame the old map and hang it in the library.

meanings.note: Formal word for a prediction of the future, often religious.

examples.trans: The ancient prophecy came true.

examples.text: الكلام المكتوب بالدفتر طلع كأنه نبوءة تحققت اليوم.
examples.trans: The words written in the notebook turned out like a prophecy fulfilled today.

meanings.note: Used for physically following someone or metaphorically following rules/ideas.

examples.trans: We must follow the instructions.

examples.text: لازم نتبع كل خطوة بالوصفة عشان تطلع الكيكة هشة.
examples.trans: We must follow every step in the recipe so the cake turns out fluffy.

meanings.note: Used for physical motion or starting to take action.

examples.trans: We are late, we need to move now.

examples.text: صار لازم نتحرك عالسوق قبل ما يسكر محل العسل.
examples.trans: We need to head out to the market now before the honey shop closes.

meanings.note: Vivid Levantine word for a tiny pinch or scrap; ولا نتفة means 'not a single scrap / zero'.

examples.text: ما ضل ولا نتفة غبرة عالرفوف.
examples.trans: Not a single speck of dust is left on the shelves.

examples.text: حطي نتفة قرفة صغيرة فوق الكيك.
examples.trans: Put a tiny pinch of cinnamon on top of the cake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: نجارين.

examples.text: النجار صنع الطاولة من خشب بلوط.
examples.trans: The carpenter built the table out of oak wood.
My grandfather was a master carpenter in the quarter.

نجح.gloss: to succeed; pass with flying colours

meanings.en: to succeed; pass with flying colours
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنجح, بينجح).

examples.trans: You passed the breakfast rush with flying colours, Nour!
The plan succeeded and we saved the house.

meanings.note: Everyday word for attempting something or tasting food.

examples.trans: Let's try this new restaurant.

examples.text: تعالوا نجرب نخلط الزيزفون مع قشر الليمون بالشاي.
examples.trans: Come let us try mixing linden with lemon zest in the tea.

meanings.note: Can be used for physical cuts or emotional hurt.

examples.trans: We don't want to hurt anyone's feelings.

examples.text: انتبهوا بالسكينة عشان ما نجرح إيدينا واحنا بنقطع.
examples.trans: Be careful with the knife so we do not cut our hands while slicing.

meanings.note: Used for celestial stars, geometric shapes, or famous celebrities.

examples.trans: The sky is full of stars today.

examples.text: رسموا نجمة صغيرة بالحبر الأحمر جنب الرقم سبعة.
examples.trans: They drew a small star in red ink beside the number seven.

meanings.note: Used for the metal or objects made of it.

examples.trans: This jug is made of copper.

examples.text: الإبريق والمصفاية معمولين من نحاس مطروق قديم.
examples.trans: The teapot and strainer are made of old hammered copper.

meanings.note: Adjective indicating something is made of or related to copper.

examples.trans: He bought an old copper antique.

examples.text: لقينا ميدالية نحاسية مدورة تحت شجرة الزيزفون.
examples.trans: We found a round brass medallion under the linden tree.

meanings.note: In Levantine Arabic, a noun for a sharp twinge or sudden prick of pain.

examples.text: حسّيت بنخزة خفيفة بضهري لما رفعت الصندوق التقيل.
examples.trans: I felt a slight twinge in my back when I lifted the heavy box.

examples.text: نخزة الإبرة كانت سريعة وما وجعت أبداً.
examples.trans: The prick of the needle was quick and didn't hurt at all.

meanings.note: Most common verb for searching ('ndawwir 'ala') or turning something around.

examples.trans: We have been looking for you for an hour.

examples.text: خلينا ندور بالرفوف التحتانية بلكي نلاقي الدفتر.
examples.trans: Let us look through the bottom shelves; maybe we will find the notebook.

meanings.note: Used for lifting objects, raising voices, or uploading files.

examples.trans: We have to raise the volume to hear.

examples.text: بدنا نرفع الصندوق الخشب مع بعض على الطاولة.
examples.trans: We want to lift the wooden box together onto the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: نزل.

examples.text: نزل الساحة فيه تمن غرف هادية.
examples.trans: The courtyard guesthouse has eight quiet rooms.
Welcome to our small guesthouse.

meanings.note: Imperative addressed to a female to take something down, drop off, or lower a price.

examples.trans: Put the bag down on the floor.

examples.text: نزلي الصواني من الرف وحطيهم عالطاولة الكبيرة.
examples.trans: Bring (f.) the trays down from the shelf and put them on the big table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: Let us bring the suitcase down into the light.
Let me lower my glasses from my forehead!

meanings.note: Common Arabic phrase بالنسبة لـ meaning 'as for' or 'what about'.

examples.text: بالنسبة للموعد بكرا، خلينا نتلاقى الساعة عشرة.
examples.trans: As for tomorrow's appointment, let's meet at ten o'clock.

examples.text: وبالنسبة للأكل، سلمى رح تجهز الفطاير.
examples.trans: And regarding the food, Salma will prepare the pastries.

meanings.en: to copy; trace a drawing; transcribe text
meanings.note: Form I verb (بنسخ / نسخ) used both for hand-copying drawings and copying text or files.

examples.text: نسخت الرسمة القديمة على ورقة نظيفة.
examples.trans: I copied the old drawing onto a clean sheet.

examples.text: ممكن تنسخ لي الوصفة على دفتري؟
examples.trans: Could you copy the recipe into my notebook for me?

meanings.note: Feminine noun from نسخ ('to copy'); used for photocopies, spare keys, or book editions. Plural: نسخ.

examples.trans: There's a second copy inside the house.
Make me a copy of the key.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نسمات.

examples.trans: There is a pleasant breeze in the courtyard.
The boy is as quiet as a breeze.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنسى, بينسى).

examples.trans: You forgot the notebook beside the soup bowl.
With all the rush, I completely forgot!

meanings.note: Masculine noun (plural نسمات / أنسام) for a pleasant light breeze, especially in the evening.

examples.text: في نسيم بارد لطيف عالسطح بالليل.
examples.trans: There is a pleasant cool breeze on the roof at night.
The sea breeze moved the lanterns gently.

meanings.note: Used for wood shavings left after carpentry.

examples.trans: The floor is full of sawdust.

examples.text: كان في نشارة خشب ناعمة عالأرض جوا الورشة.
examples.trans: There was fine sawdust on the floor inside the workshop.

meanings.note: Instrument noun from نشّف (to dry); denotes blotting paper for wet ink as well as a clothes dryer.

examples.text: استعملوا ورقة النشافة عشان ما يلطخ الحبر.
examples.trans: Use the blotting paper so the ink does not smudge.

examples.text: حطينا الغسيل بالنشافة عشان ينشف بسرعة.
examples.trans: We put the laundry in the dryer so it dries quickly.

نشر.gloss: to spread out; hang out (laundry/lanterns); publish

meanings.en: to spread out to dry; hang along a line; publish
meanings.note: Form I verb (بنشر / نشر). Classic Levantine verb for hanging laundry or paper decorations along a rope.

examples.text: نشرنا الفوانيس على طول الحبل بين العواميد.
examples.trans: We hung the lanterns along the length of the rope between the posts.
My mother hung the laundry out on the roof in the morning.

meanings.note: Short for نشرة الطقس / النشرة الجوية ('weather forecast').

examples.text: نشرة يوم التنين بتقول في مطر غزير الصبح.
examples.trans: Monday's forecast says heavy rain in the morning.

examples.text: خليني أشوف نشرة الطقس قبل ما ندهن برا.
examples.trans: Let me check the weather forecast before we paint outside.

meanings.note: Short adjective from root ن-ش-ط alongside نشيط; feminine نشطة.

examples.text: النحل الصبح بكون نشط وحوالين الزهر.
examples.trans: In the morning the bees are active around the blossoms.

examples.text: الفريق ضل نشط طول اليوم لحد ما حل اللغز.
examples.trans: The team stayed energetic all day until they solved the puzzle.

meanings.note: Form I intransitive verb (nishif / byinshaf) meaning 'dry out'.

examples.text: لما تطلع الشمس، الحجار بتنشف بسرعة.
examples.trans: When the sun comes out, the stones dry quickly.

examples.text: استنينا ساعتين لحد ما ينشف الدهان.
examples.trans: We waited two hours until the paint dried.

meanings.note: Form II transitive counterpart of نشف ('to become dry'): used for drying berries, dishes, or towels.

examples.text: اغسل التوت ونشفه منيح بفوطة نضيفة.
examples.trans: Wash the berries and dry them well with a clean towel.

examples.text: نشفي إيديكي قبل ما تفتحي الدفتر.
examples.trans: Dry your hands before opening the notebook.

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: The time is five and a half (half past five).

examples.text: التقينا بالساحة الساعة تمانية ونص تماما.
examples.trans: We met in the courtyard at eight-thirty sharp.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: نصانية, plural: —).

examples.trans: The notebook opened to the middle page.
I picked the middle table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Noun 'half' with the feminine 3rd person singular pronoun suffix.

examples.trans: I ate half of it and left the rest.

examples.text: قرأنا نصها والباقي رح نكمله بكرة بالمكتبة.
examples.trans: We read half of it and the rest we will finish tomorrow in the library.

meanings.note: In Levantine Arabic, a noun for eyeglasses (usually plural in Arabic), with 'my'.

examples.text: وين حطيت نضارتي؟ ما بقدر أقرأ المنيو بدونها.
examples.trans: Where did I put my glasses? I can't read the menu without them.

examples.text: اشتريت نضارة شمسية جديدة قبل السفر.
examples.trans: I bought a new pair of sunglasses before traveling.

meanings.note: Colloquial Levantine spelling of نظافة (standard dental ظ -> alveolar ض in Amman speech).

examples.text: شوف نضافة الشرفة بعد ما مسحنا الدرابزين.
examples.trans: Look at the cleanliness of the terrace after we wiped the railing.
Cleanliness is the most important thing in the kitchen and workshop.

meanings.note: Natural spoken Levantine pronunciation of نظيف ('clean'), broken plural نضاف.

examples.text: مسحنا الفرشاية بقماشة نضيفة ومي دافية.
examples.trans: We wiped the brush with a clean cloth and warm water.

examples.text: المطبخ صار نضيف ومرتب وجاهز لبكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: The kitchen is spotless, tidy, and ready for tomorrow morning.

meanings.note: Geminate verb (ن-ط-ط) for jumping or hopping over an obstacle.

examples.text: القطة نطت عن الحيط للجنينة بهدوء.
examples.trans: The cat jumped quietly off the wall into the garden.

examples.text: ما بدنا الضيوف ينطوا فوق الكراسي بالممر!
examples.trans: We don't want guests climbing over chairs in the hallway!

meanings.note: Colloquial verb for bending metal or denting a car.

examples.trans: Be careful so we don't dent the car.

examples.text: دير بالك لا نطعج أطراف الورقة واحنا بنحطها بالعلبة.
examples.trans: Be careful we do not bend the edges of the sheet while putting it in the tin.

meanings.note: Plural noun with second person masculine singular suffix.

examples.trans: Where did you put your glasses?

examples.text: البس نظاراتك عشان تقرأ الخط الصغير بالهامش.
examples.trans: Put on your glasses so you can read the small handwriting in the margin.

meanings.note: Plural noun with first person singular suffix.

examples.trans: My glasses broke yesterday.
I forgot my glasses next to the cup on the balcony.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Used for rules, computer systems, or political regimes.

examples.trans: We must follow the system.

examples.text: رتبنا البطاقات حسب نظام ألوان وأرقام واضح.
examples.trans: We arranged the cards according to a clear system of colours and numbers.

meanings.note: In نلفت نظرهم ('draw their eyes/attention'), pairs with لفت.

examples.trans: We don't want to catch the teacher's eye.
Your point of view is clear.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun; ألقى نظرة means 'take a look / cast a glance'. Plural: نظرات.

examples.trans: Let me take a quick look at the letter.
He spotted the problem at first glance.

meanings.note: Form II verb (نظّف) with doubled middle radical; imperative نظّف / نظّفي.

examples.text: نظفوا الطاولة منيح قبل ما نحط الصواني.
examples.trans: Clean the table well before we set down the trays.

examples.text: مازن نظف العلبة المعدنية بقطعة قماش ناشفة.
examples.trans: Mazen cleaned the metal tin with a dry cloth.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for clean or tidy.

examples.trans: The house is clean after the deep cleaning.

examples.text: لوح الرخام نظيف وجاهز عشان نفرد عليه العجينة.
examples.trans: The marble slab is clean and ready for us to roll out the dough on.

meanings.note: Clear, polite 'yes' (slightly warmer and more formal than casual آه).

examples.trans: Yes, room four is on the second floor!
Yes, a hundred times yes!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian pronunciation (often نعنع in rapid speech) for fresh or dried mint added to tea.

examples.text: قطفنا شوية نعناع أخضر عشان الشاي.
examples.trans: We picked some fresh mint for the tea.
The dried mint in the jar has a strong aroma.

meanings.note: A very common herb used in Levantine tea and cuisine.

examples.trans: I want a cup of tea with mint.

examples.text: حطينا عرق نعنع أخضر بالكاسة قبل ما نصب الشاي.
examples.trans: We put a sprig of fresh mint in the glass before pouring the tea.

meanings.note: Feminine abstract noun from ناعم ('soft/smooth'). Common phrase: بنعومة ('gently / softly').

examples.trans: The lanterns sway gently with the breeze.

examples.text: مسكت الفرشاية بنعومة عشان ما تسيح الألوان.
examples.trans: I held the brush gently so the colours wouldn't run.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نغمات.

examples.text: سمع كل نغمة من البيانو بهدوء.
examples.trans: He listened quietly to every note of the piano.
The chime of the bell is gentle, not harsh.

meanings.note: Describes wood swelling from dampness as well as blowing air.

examples.text: الخشب القديم نفخ شوي من رطوبة الشتا.
examples.trans: The old wood swelled slightly from the winter damp.
The pastry puffed up in the oven and turned golden.

meanings.note: Often used to mean 'the same' when followed by a noun, or as a reflexive.

examples.trans: We live in the same building.

examples.text: استعملنا نفس الوصفة بس زدنا شوية برش برتقال.
examples.trans: We used the exact same recipe, though we added a little orange zest.

meanings.note: Reflexive pronoun for third person feminine.

examples.trans: She herself told me this.

examples.text: هاي هي الخريطة نفسها اللي شوفناها بدفتر الجد.
examples.trans: This is the very same map that we saw in Grandfather's notebook.

meanings.note: Can refer to a physical dot, a score point, or a drop of liquid.

examples.trans: I just want a drop of water.

examples.text: التقت الخطوط كلها عند نقطة واحدة بالزاوية الشمالية.
examples.trans: All the lines met at a single point in the northern corner.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: We read the property transfer paper.
Moving the boxes took five minutes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنقط, بينقط).

examples.text: آسف نقطت مي على أرضكم النظيفة.
examples.trans: Sorry I dripped water on your clean floor.
The pipe stopped dripping.

meanings.note: Key culinary term in baking and tasting notes; plural نكهات.

examples.text: في نكهة قرفة خفيفة بطرف الكيكة.
examples.trans: There is a light cinnamon flavour at the edge of the cake.

examples.text: كل صينية جربت نكهة عسل مختلفة.
examples.trans: Each tin tried a different honey flavour.

meanings.note: First person plural present verb.

examples.trans: Maybe we will find a solution to the problem.

examples.text: بلكي نلاقي الحل بسرعة لما نقرأ البطاقات بالترتيب.
examples.trans: Maybe we will find the answer quickly when we read the cards in order.

meanings.note: Standard first person plural verb often used in colloquial speech.

examples.trans: When will we meet again?

examples.text: خلينا نلتقي بكرا العصر بوسط البلد نشرب قهوة.
examples.trans: Let's meet tomorrow afternoon downtown to have coffee.

meanings.note: Commonly used for turning a vehicle or wrapping food.

examples.trans: Let's turn from this street.

examples.text: لازم نلف السندويشات بورق عشان ما تبرد عالطريق.
examples.trans: We need to wrap the sandwiches in paper so they don't get cold on the way.

meanings.note: Contrasts with ليل ('nighttime'): بنور النهار = 'in broad daylight'.

examples.text: الشيش الأخضر طالع أحلى بكتير بنور النهار!
examples.trans: The green shutters look even lovelier in daylight!

examples.text: شتغلنا طول النهار وبالمسا شربنا شاي بالنعنع.
examples.trans: We worked all day long and in the evening had mint tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun; نهاية الأسبوع means 'weekend'. Plural: نهايات.

examples.trans: There is a new booking for the weekend.

examples.text: بالنهاية كل شي انحل على خير.
examples.trans: In the end everything worked out well.

meanings.note: Standard word for a river.

examples.trans: We sat next to the Jordan River.

examples.text: سافرنا عالأغوار وشفنا نهر اليرموك من بعيد.
examples.trans: We traveled to the Jordan Valley and saw the Yarmouk River from afar.

نوتة.gloss: sheet music; musical score; pocket notepad

meanings.en: sheet music; musical score; pocket notepad
meanings.note: Used across the Levant for printed or handwritten musical notation (نوتة موسيقية).

examples.text: فتحت سعاد نوتة البيانو القديمة عالصفحة الأولى.
examples.trans: Suad opened the old piano score to page one.

examples.text: كتب المؤلف النوتة بحبر أسود واضح.
examples.trans: The composer wrote the score in clear black ink.

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (plural أنواع). Extremely common: شو نوع الحبل؟ ('what kind of rope?').

examples.trans: Which type of paper is best for lanterns?

examples.text: عنا أنواع كتيرة من الخيوط والألوان.
examples.trans: We have many kinds of strings and colours.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of على النوم, used briskly to send everyone to bed.

examples.text: صار الوقت متأخر كتير، يلا عالنوم يا جماعة!
examples.trans: It's gotten really late—off to bed, everyone!

examples.text: النوم الكويس بالليل بعطيك نشاط طول اليوم.
examples.trans: Sleeping well at night gives you energy all day long.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نومات.

examples.trans: I had the best sleep in a month!
A quiet room makes for a restful sleep.

meanings.note: Colloquial pronunciation of نيء (dropping final hamza); describes unbaked batter or undercooked food.

examples.text: العجين لسا ني بنص الصينية، بده كمان عشر دقايق.
examples.trans: The batter is still raw in the middle of the tin; it needs ten more minutes.
Do not eat potatoes while they are raw.

meanings.note: Vocalized lemma distinguishing the verb 'to move/relocate' from the noun نقل ('transport').

examples.trans: We moved the piano to the dry corner of the room.

examples.text: نور نقلت المواعيد من الدفتر للوح الأبيض.
examples.trans: Nour copied the dates from the notebook onto the whiteboard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: The guests will come down at half past seven.
I came down to ask about the sink water.

meanings.note: Lively conversational exclamation of triumph or attention ('ha! / there!').

examples.text: ما صاب قميصي ولا نقطة دهان، ها!
examples.trans: Not a single drop of paint touched my shirt—ha!

examples.text: ها، شو رأيكم باللون الأخضر تحت الشمس؟
examples.trans: Well, what do you think of the green colour in the sunshine?

meanings.note: Imperative-only verb in everyday Arabic, inflected for gender and number: هات (to a man), هاتي (to a woman), هاتوا (plural).

examples.text: هات السلة التقيلة عنك يا أستاذ مازن.
examples.trans: Give me that heavy basket for you, Mr Mazen.

examples.text: هاتي القلم الرصاص من على المكتب يا نور.
examples.trans: Hand me the pencil from the desk, Nour.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: This boy is very smart.

examples.text: هاد المحل ببيع أطيب كنافة نابلسية بعمان.
examples.trans: This shop sells the best Nabulsi kunafa in Amman.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian spelling/pronunciation of هذا ('this/that').

examples.text: هادا الكتاب من أحلى الروايات اللي قرأتها هالسنة.
examples.trans: This book is one of the best novels I've read this year.

examples.text: مين جاب هادا الفانوس الحلو عالطاولة؟
examples.trans: Who brought this lovely lantern onto the table?

meanings.note: Masculine هادي ('quiet') is homographic with the feminine demonstrative هادي ('this'); context and agreement distinguish them cleanly.

examples.trans: The spot above the tree is very quiet.
We prepared the quiet attic room for you.

meanings.note: Jordanian spoken feminine distal demonstrative ('that one over there'), matching masc. هداك.

examples.trans: Open the drawer under that screen.
That table is close to the window.

meanings.note: Combination of demonstrative prefix and plural noun.

examples.trans: How beautiful these colors are together.

examples.text: من وين جبت هالألوان الزيتية اللي بترسم فيها؟
examples.trans: Where did you get these oil paints you're painting with?

meanings.note: Used to point out a specific group of four things.

examples.trans: You must read these four books.

examples.text: خلصنا هالاربع صحون بسرعة لأنهم كانوا بشهوا.
examples.trans: We finished these four plates quickly because they were delicious.

meanings.note: Demonstrative attached to a loanword.

examples.trans: This portrait was painted by a famous artist.

examples.text: علقنا هالبورتريه بنص الصالون عشان يبين للضيوف.
examples.trans: We hung this portrait in the middle of the living room so guests can see it.

meanings.note: Demonstrative attached to the word for compass.

examples.trans: This compass will help you on the way.

examples.text: أخدنا معنا هالبوصلة واحنا طالعين رحلة لوادي رم.
examples.trans: We brought this compass along when we went on a trip to Wadi Rum.

meanings.note: Commonly used when referring to potholes on the road.

examples.trans: Watch out for this pothole.

examples.text: السيارة طبت في هالجورة بنص الشارع وطق العجل.
examples.trans: The car hit this pothole in the middle of the street and the tire blew out.

meanings.note: Demonstrative phrase pointing out a rock.

examples.trans: Throw this stone far away.

examples.text: شيل هالحجر من الممر قبل ما يتفركش فيه حدا.
examples.trans: Move this stone out of the walkway before someone trips over it.

meanings.note: Used extensively to refer to preceding statements, rumors, or ongoing discussions.

examples.trans: This talk is not correct at all.

examples.text: بكفي هالحكي الفاضي وخلينا نركز بالشغل.
examples.trans: Enough of this empty talk—let's focus on the work.

meanings.note: Points out an aroma or odor.

examples.trans: Where is this nice smell coming from?

examples.text: هالريحة الزاكية جاية من المخبز اللي تحتنا.
examples.trans: This delicious smell is coming from the bakery downstairs.

meanings.note: Used to describe an echoing sound.

examples.trans: Do you hear this echo in the valley?

examples.text: اسمع هالصدى لما نصيح بين الجبال بعجلون.
examples.trans: Listen to this echo when we shout between the mountains in Ajloun.

meanings.note: Refers to a container or can.

examples.trans: Open this box and take some biscuits from it.

examples.text: حط المسامير جوا هالعلبة الحديد عشان ما يضيعوا.
examples.trans: Put the nails inside this metal tin so they don't get lost.

meanings.note: Demonstrative phrase for a book.

examples.trans: This book is very useful for the exam.

examples.text: استعرت هالكتاب من مكتبة الجامعة عشان البحث.
examples.trans: I borrowed this book from the university library for the research paper.

meanings.note: Points out a written piece.

examples.trans: This text is long and needs time to read.

examples.text: قرأنا هالنص القصير بالصف وجاوبنا على كل الأسئلة.
examples.trans: We read this short passage in class and answered all the questions.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for feminine singular objects.

examples.trans: This girl is very smart.

examples.text: هاي الطريقة أسهل بكثير من اللي جربناها امبارح.
examples.trans: This method is much easier than the one we tried yesterday.

meanings.en: to blow suddenly (of wind); spring up
meanings.note: Geminate verb (بهب / هب). Used especially for sudden gusts of wind: الهوا هب فجأة ('the wind blew suddenly').

examples.trans: The wind blew hard and scattered the papers.

examples.text: كل يوم العصر بيهب نسيم حلو بالجبل.
examples.trans: Every afternoon a nice breeze blows on the hill.

meanings.note: Noun of instance (مرة) from هب ('to blow'): هبة هوا ('a gust of wind'). Plural هبات.

examples.text: إجت هبة هوا قوية على الشرفة.
examples.trans: A strong gust of wind came onto the terrace.
The gusts of wind in autumn cool the weather down.

meanings.note: Contracted phrase pointing out a card or ticket.

examples.trans: Take this card so you can enter.

examples.text: سجل اسمك على هبطاقة وحطها بالصندوق.
examples.trans: Write your name on this card and drop it in the box.

meanings.note: Used chiefly in the idiomatic Levantine adverbial phrase عالهدا ('gently, slowly, carefully').

examples.text: حركي أصابع رجلك عالهدا وخدي نفس عميق.
examples.trans: Wiggle your toes gently and take a deep breath.

examples.text: نزلنا السلم عالهدا خطوة خطوة بالساحة.
examples.trans: We brought the ladder down gently step by step in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian distal demonstrative ('that over there / that past...'); feminine هديك (hadiik), plural هدولاك.

examples.text: بتذكر هداك الربيع لما فتحنا النزل؟
examples.trans: Do you remember that spring when we opened the inn?

examples.text: حط الصندوق على هداك الرف العالي.
examples.trans: Put the box on that high shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine feminine noun from هدي ('to calm down'). بهداوة means 'gently / calmly / take it easy'.

examples.text: امشي بهداوة يا سيدي، معنا وقت.
examples.trans: Walk gently, sir—we have time.
With calmness, every knot untangles.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The morning quiet of the courtyard is very peaceful.
We talked the matter through calmly and patiently.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian plural demonstrative ('these / those') for people or things.

examples.trans: Whose are these brass keys?
I have grown fond of those two rings!

meanings.note: Feminine past tense of هدي ('to calm down/go quiet'), agreeing with الغرفة.

examples.text: أخيراً هدي الشارع بالليل بعد ما روّحوا الناس.
examples.trans: The street finally quieted down at night after people went home.

examples.text: الغرفة هديت فجأة أول ما بلشت سعاد تعزف.
examples.trans: The room suddenly went quiet as soon as Suad started playing.

meanings.note: Standard Arabic word for 'gift' or 'present'.

examples.text: جبتلك هدية بسيطة بمناسبة افتتاح المقهى.
examples.trans: I brought you a small gift for the café's opening.

examples.text: أحلى هدية وصلتني كانت البطاقة اللي كتبتيها بإيدك.
examples.trans: The nicest gift I received was the card you wrote by hand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بهدي, بيهدي).

examples.text: هدي بالك يا مازن، الغرفة جاهزة.
examples.trans: Calm down, Mazen, the room is ready.
A cup of anise tea calms the nerves.

meanings.note: MSA feminine demonstrative used in Mazen's stiff written draft.

examples.text: يسرّنا أن نقدم هذه الوثيقة الرسمية للبلدية.
examples.trans: We are pleased to submit this official document to the municipality.

examples.text: هذه القاعة التاريخية بُنيت قبل مئة عام.
examples.trans: This historic hall was built a hundred years ago.

meanings.note: Feminine demonstrative used more in formal speech or by older/Bedouin speakers.

examples.trans: This car is new.

examples.text: هذي القهوة العربية محمصة على الطريقة البدوية.
examples.trans: This Arabic coffee is roasted in the Bedouin style.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بهرب, بيهرب).

examples.trans: Why did the person run off without his bag?
You left the bag on the doorstep and bolted!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بهز, بيهز).

examples.trans: My brother nodded his head in agreement!
The breeze shook the jasmine branches.

meanings.note: Very common adverb denoting the current time in Jordan and Palestine.

examples.trans: I want to go now.

examples.text: استناني دقيقتين، هسا بلبس وبنزل لعندك.
examples.trans: Wait two minutes for me; I'll get dressed and come down to you right now.

meanings.note: In baking, هش describes a tender, airy cake crumb or crisp pastry that melts lightly.

examples.text: الكيكة طلعت هشة وخفيفة متل الإسفنج.
examples.trans: The cake came out fluffy and light like a sponge.
Crumbly biscuits break easily in the tin.

meanings.note: Formal/educated yes-no question marker also heard in careful Jordanian speech; often omitted in casual speech.

examples.text: هل هادا هو الدفتر اللي كنت تدور عليه؟
examples.trans: Is this the notebook you were looking for?

examples.text: ما بعرف هل المكتبة فاتحة اليوم أو مسكرة.
examples.trans: I do not know whether the library is open today or closed.

meanings.note: High-frequency Levantine word for 'now' (contracted from هاد الوقت).

examples.trans: We have to go to class right now.
I feel a bit relieved now.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Signature urban Jordanian/Levantine adverb for now (also spelled هلا in Jordan).

examples.text: هلق رح نفتح الصينية ونذوق أول قطعة.
examples.trans: Right now we will open the tin and taste the first piece.
We finished writing the notes just now.

meanings.note: Used especially in the warm Jordanian reassurance ولا يهمك! ('never mind! / do not worry at all!').

examples.trans: Do not worry at all, sir, it is nothing!
What matters to us is the guests' comfort.

meanings.note: Sound Form I verb (بهمس / همست) from root ه-م-س ('soft sound/whispering').

examples.trans: Word whispered to me that you opened the box.

examples.text: همست بإذنها عشان ما حدا يسمع.
examples.trans: She whispered in her ear so nobody would hear.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'they' for people or things.

examples.trans: Are they in your jacket pocket?
They live at the end of the street.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun, heard warmly in صحتين وهنا ('bon appétit / enjoy your meal').

examples.trans: Enjoy your tea and cake!
May the home be filled with goodness and joy.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'there / over there' (لهناك 'over there').

examples.trans: Mazen has put old boxes over there.
Can you run over there and back?

meanings.note: Refers to the field of engineering or geometry.

examples.trans: He is studying engineering at the university.

examples.text: تخرجت اختي من كلية هندسة العمارة السنة الماضية.
examples.trans: My sister graduated from the architecture engineering faculty last year.

meanings.note: Colloquial Levantine demonstrative adverb parallel to هناك (over there).

examples.text: اللوحة القديمة معلقة هنيك عند الدرج.
examples.trans: The old painting is hanging over there by the stairs.

examples.text: روحوا هنيك تحت شجرة الزيزفون الجو أبرد.
examples.trans: Go over there under the linden tree; it is cooler.

meanings.note: Third person masculine pronoun.

examples.trans: He is the one who said so.

examples.text: طارق هو اللي اقترح نطلع رحلة على البترا.
examples.trans: Tareq is the one who suggested we take a trip to Petra.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A little air got into the old pipes.
Morning air in Amman is crisp and clean.

meanings.note: Feminine noun (plural هوايات) from هوى ('to be fond of / love').

examples.text: الرسم بالألوان المائية أحلى هواية عندي.
examples.trans: Watercolour painting is my favourite hobby.
What are your favourite hobbies in your free time?

meanings.en: whoosh! phew! (sound of blowing air or a gust passing)
meanings.note: Expressive sound word imitating wind rushing or a sigh of relief.

examples.text: هوف! والله الورقة كانت رح تطير.
examples.trans: Phew! Honestly the sheet was about to fly away.

examples.text: سمعنا هوف الهوا لما فتحنا باب السطح.
examples.trans: We heard the whoosh of the wind when we opened the roof door.

meanings.note: Standard adverb for physical location.

examples.trans: Put the things here, please.

examples.text: الجو هون بالجبل أبرد بكثير من وسط البلد.
examples.trans: The weather up here on the hill is much cooler than downtown.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'she' or 'it' (feminine).

examples.trans: Take a piece of bread while it is hot.
Family is what remains.

meanings.note: Extremely common adverb used to express similarity or concluding a statement.

examples.text: هيك الحياة، يوم الك ويوم عليك.
examples.trans: Such is life, one day for you and one day against you.

examples.text: ما تحكي معه هيك قدام الناس، احكي معه على جنب.
examples.trans: Don't talk to him like that in front of people; speak to him privately.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from هيكل (frame, structure, skeleton); feminine هيكلية.

examples.text: في رسم هيكلي للبيت جوا ملف المهندس.
examples.trans: There is a structural drawing of the house inside the architect's file.
We made a small structural adjustment to the plan.

meanings.note: Colloquial attention-getting exclamation, used playfully among friends or family.

examples.trans: Hey! Tariq drove the bus himself!
Hey, where are you going so fast?

meanings.note: Presentative pronoun used to point out a group of people or objects.

examples.trans: Where are the kids? Here they are playing outside.

examples.text: طلبت مفاتيحي وهيهم محطوطين على الرف عند الباب.
examples.trans: You asked for my keys—here they are sitting on the shelf by the door.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian presentative word ('here is! / look!') pointing to someone or something right now; takes suffixes (هيهم hayy-hum 'here they are!').

examples.text: هي تاكسي وقف عند الباب هلا!
examples.trans: Look, a taxi just stopped at the door!
Here they come down the stairs!

meanings.note: The universal coordinating conjunction.

examples.trans: I bought bread and milk.

examples.text: جبت قهوة و شاي و سكر من الدكان.
examples.trans: I brought coffee, tea, and sugar from the corner shop.

meanings.note: Conjunction and indefinite noun.

examples.trans: Bring a thread and a needle with you.

examples.text: جابت تيته بكرة خيط وإبرة عشان ترقع الثوب.
examples.trans: Grandma brought a spool of thread and a needle to patch the robe.

meanings.note: Conjunction attached to the first person plural pronoun.

examples.trans: A problem happened while we were going home.

examples.text: نزل المطر فجأة وإحنا ماشيين بالشارع.
examples.trans: The rain suddenly came down while we were walking down the street.

meanings.note: Introduces a playful warning or consequence ('or else…').

examples.trans: Drink your coffee now or else it'll go cold!

examples.text: خبي قطعة تارت لطارق وإلا بيزعل منا!
examples.trans: Save a slice of tart for Tariq or else he'll be cross with us!

meanings.note: Refers to the front of a building or a digital interface.

examples.trans: The building's facade is built of stone.

examples.text: المصمم غير شكل واجهة التطبيق بالكامل.
examples.trans: The designer changed the look of the app's interface completely.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: There is someone asking about you.

examples.text: اشتريت كتاب واحد بس من المعرض لأنه كان غالي.
examples.trans: I bought just one book from the fair because it was expensive.

meanings.note: Conjunction attached to a feminine imperative verb.

examples.trans: Hold the box and lift it up.

examples.text: امسكي طرف السجادة من هناك وارفعي شوي لفوق.
examples.trans: Hold the edge of the rug from over there and lift it up a little.

meanings.note: Active participle of ورم ('swell up').

examples.text: كويس إن كاحلك مش وارم، التلج فاد علطول.
examples.trans: It's good that your ankle isn't swollen—the ice helped right away.

examples.text: إذا ضلت الرجل وارمة الصبح منروح عالدكتور.
examples.trans: If the foot is still swollen in the morning, we'll see the doctor.

meanings.note: Form III verb from وزن (weight); commonly used for balancing flavours in a recipe.

examples.trans: Lemon balances the sweetness of the honey in the cake.

examples.text: سلمى وازنت بين النكهات بدقة شاطرة.
examples.trans: Salma balanced the flavours with clever precision.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واسعة, plural: واسعين).

examples.trans: Careful, the pitcher's spout is wide!
The house's courtyard is spacious and sunny.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واصلة, plural: واصلين).

examples.text: ريحة القرفة الدافية واصلة للطابق التاني!
examples.trans: The warm cinnamon scent reaches all the way to the second floor!
The bus is pulling into the station now.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واضحة, plural: واضحين).

examples.trans: A sincere, clear sentence from the heart.
The address is clear on the card.

meanings.note: Feminine adjective used for clarity in speech or vision.

examples.trans: The picture is not very clear.

examples.text: الشروط المكتوبة بالعقد واضحة وما بدها تفسير.
examples.trans: The terms written in the contract are clear and need no explanation.

meanings.note: Feminine command to push or press.

examples.trans: Enter the password and press enter.

examples.text: اختاري اللغة العربية واضغطي على زر الحفظ.
examples.trans: Choose the Arabic language and press the save button.

meanings.note: Refers to retrieving or pulling out an object.

examples.trans: I want to open the bag and take it out.

examples.text: لازم أجيب الكرسي عشان أوصل للخزانة واطولها.
examples.trans: I need to grab the chair so I can reach the cabinet and pull it out.

meanings.note: Command used for folding clothes or paper.

examples.trans: Wash the clothes and fold the garments.

examples.text: لمي الغسيل عن الحبل واطوي كل قطعة لحالها.
examples.trans: Gather the laundry off the line and fold each piece separately.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واطية, plural: واطيين).

examples.text: انتبه على راسك من الخشب الواطي.
examples.trans: Watch your head on the low wooden beam.
They spoke in a low voice for the guests' sake.

meanings.note: Form III verb from و-ف-ق; takes على for the thing agreed to.

examples.text: وافق مازن عالخطة أول ما شاف الأرقام.
examples.trans: Mazen agreed to the plan as soon as he saw the numbers.

examples.text: كل الجيران وافقوا يحضروا حفلة الشاي.
examples.trans: All the neighbours agreed to attend the tea concert.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واقفة, plural: واقفين).

examples.trans: There is nobody standing in the courtyard.
They stood face to face under the tree.

meanings.note: Defective active participle of وقى (to protect); also used substantively in compounds like واقي شمس (sunscreen).

examples.text: حطينا غطا واقي فوق الخريطة عشان الرطوبة.
examples.trans: We put a protective cover over the map against humidity.

examples.text: لبس كفوف واقية قبل ما يمسك الصينية السخنة.
examples.trans: He put on protective gloves before holding the hot tin.

meanings.note: Refers to a ticket or a bank card.

examples.trans: I took the passport and the card.

examples.text: حطيت الهوية والبطاقة البنكية بالمحفظة قبل السفر.
examples.trans: I put my ID and bank card in my wallet before traveling.

meanings.note: Usually refers to mobile network coverage.

examples.trans: The internet is excellent and the coverage is strong here.

examples.text: سافرت عالصحرا والتغطية انقطعت نص الطريق.
examples.trans: I drove out to the desert and the cell coverage dropped halfway there.

meanings.note: Refers to something feminine colored gold.

examples.trans: I took the silver and the golden medal.

examples.text: الفريق فاز بالبطولة والميدالية الذهبية آخر السنة.
examples.trans: The team won the championship and the gold medal at the end of the year.

والشمال.gloss: and the left / and the north

meanings.en: and the left / and the north
meanings.note: Can refer to the left direction or northern region.

examples.text: اطلع دغري وبعدين لف يمين والشمال.
examples.trans: Go straight and then turn right and left.

examples.text: الشارع مقطوع من اليمين والشمال بسبب الصيانة.
examples.trans: The street is blocked off on both the right and the left due to maintenance.

meanings.note: Refers to the morning meal.

examples.trans: We drank coffee and the breakfast was delicious.

examples.text: طلبنا حمص وفول والفطور وصل بعد عشر دقايق.
examples.trans: We ordered hummus and fava beans, and breakfast arrived ten minutes later.

meanings.note: Everyday oath used earnestly to swear one is telling the truth (والله ما حكيت إشي) or surprisedly in والله جد؟ ('oh really?').

examples.trans: I swear I'm telling the truth.
Honestly, I'm glad to see you.

meanings.note: Refers to the nut, also used metaphorically for something excellent.

examples.trans: We ate fruits and green almonds.

examples.text: زينت أمي المقلوبة بالصنوبر واللوز المحمص.
examples.trans: My mom garnished the maqluba with pine nuts and toasted almonds.

meanings.note: Modern expressive exclamation of admiration or amazement, common among younger Jordanian speakers.

examples.text: واو! شكل الكيكة باللوز والعسل بجنن!
examples.trans: Wow! The honey-and-almond cake looks amazing!

examples.text: واو، كيف قدرت تحل اللغز بهالسرعة؟
examples.trans: Wow, how did you manage to solve the puzzle so fast?

meanings.note: Refers to flapping wings or hovering. The spelling appears to be a colloquial variant or typo for بيرفرف.

examples.trans: The bird is flying and fluttering its wings.

examples.text: شوف العلم كيف مرفوع فوق السطح وبيرفوف بالهوا.
examples.trans: Look how the flag is raised on the roof and fluttering in the breeze.

meanings.en: peg; wooden or metal stake; cleat for tying rope
meanings.note: Masculine noun (plural أوتاد) used for tent pegs, wall pegs, and posts for securing ropes.

examples.text: لف الحبل حوالين الوتد الثابت بالزاوية.
examples.trans: Wrap the rope around the sturdy peg in the corner.

examples.text: دقّينا أوتاد الخيمة بالأرض قبل الغروب.
examples.trans: We drove the tent pegs into the ground before sunset.

meanings.note: Stretched wire or gut string on a piano, oud, or violin.

examples.text: المطرقة بتضرب الأوتار التلاتة فبيطلع صوت صافي.
examples.trans: The hammer strikes the three strings and produces a clear note.

examples.text: كل وتر بالبيانو مشدود بدقة عالية.
examples.trans: Every string inside the piano is tensioned with great precision.

meanings.note: Refers to mulberries or any kind of berries.

examples.trans: We brought strawberries and berries from the market.

examples.text: عملت ماما مربى مشمش وتوت للفطور بالشتوية.
examples.trans: Mom made apricot and mulberry jam for breakfast during the winter.

وثق.gloss: to trust; to have confidence in

meanings.en: to trust; to have confidence in
meanings.note: Form I assimilated verb (root و-ث-ق, losing initial w- in the imperfect: يثق / بثق); takes بـ or في.
