examples.text: أنا بثق بذوق سلمى واختيارها للمكونات.
examples.trans: I trust Salma's palate and her choice of ingredients.

examples.text: الكل وثق بالخريطة القديمة وتبع الخطوات.
examples.trans: Everyone trusted the old map and followed the steps.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; وجع راس means 'headache'. Plural: أوجاع.

examples.trans: Tiny numbers give me a headache!

examples.text: راح وجع الراس بعد فنجان القهوة.
examples.trans: The headache went away after a cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Common expression indicating spatial proximity to a masculine object.

examples.trans: Put the chair and beside it the table.

examples.text: المخبز موجود عالشارع الرئيسي وجنبه صيدلية كبيرة.
examples.trans: The bakery is on the main street, and next to it is a large pharmacy.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; وجه لوجه means 'face to face'. Plural: وجوه.

examples.trans: They stood face to face under the tree.
The top of the cake turned golden in the oven.

meanings.note: Verbal noun: وجود نوف معهم ('Noaf's presence / having Noaf with them').

examples.trans: Having you with us makes us happy.
Thank you for being by my side.

meanings.note: Form II verb disambiguated with shadda from noun وجه ('face').

examples.text: خلينا نوجه المروحة لباب الساحة عشان الهوا يتحرك.
examples.trans: Let's point the fan toward the courtyard door so the air circulates.

examples.text: وجه الضو عاللوحة عشان نشوف الحروف بوضوح.
examples.trans: Point the light at the sign so we can see the letters clearly.

meanings.note: Feminine counterpart of الواحد when speaking generically about a girl or woman (لازم الوحدة تشوفه بعينها).

examples.trans: A girl has to stand up for herself.
Each one of us has a role.

meanings.note: Can be used as a noun meaning 'and a stamp' or a verb in the past tense 'and he stamped/sealed'.

examples.trans: He gave me a paper and stamped on it.

examples.text: راجع المدير المعاملة وختم عليها بنفس اللحظة.
examples.trans: The manager reviewed the paperwork and stamped it on the spot.

meanings.note: Imperative verb used to instruct a group of people to take something.

examples.trans: Come and take your belongings.

examples.text: جهزوا شناتيكم وخذوا معكم مي كافية للرحلة.
examples.trans: Pack your bags and take enough water with you for the trip.

meanings.note: Used to describe something feminine that is light in weight or mild in intensity.

examples.trans: The bag is small and light.

examples.text: السلطة هاي زاكية وخفيفة على المعدة بعد العشا.
examples.trans: This salad is tasty and light on the stomach after dinner.

meanings.note: Everyday item, combined with the conjunction 'wa' (and).

examples.trans: I brought a pen and a notebook.

examples.text: اشتريتله حقيبة ودفتر رسم لأول يوم مدرسة.
examples.trans: I bought him a backpack and a sketchbook for the first day of school.

meanings.note: Very common spatial preposition in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: The car is behind the house.

examples.text: الحديقة موجودة ورا المبنى بعيدة عن عجقة الشارع.
examples.trans: The garden is behind the building, away from the street traffic.

meanings.note: Preposition with a 3rd person masculine singular pronoun suffix.

examples.trans: Walk behind him.

examples.text: ركضت وراه للموقف عشان أعطيه مفتاحه اللي نسيه.
examples.trans: I ran after him to the bus stop to give him his key that he forgot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian collective masculine noun for roses/flowers. Singular unit: وردة.

examples.trans: We walked past the flower stall.
The scent of roses and jasmine filled the courtyard.

meanings.note: Singular form for a flower, highly used in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I picked a rose from the garden.

examples.text: قدم لوالدته وردة جورية بمناسبة عيد الأم.
examples.trans: He gave his mother a Damask rose for Mother's Day.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ورشات.

examples.trans: There is a brass lamp in my workshop downstairs.
The old bag is from my grandfather's workshop.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.text: جيب لي شوية ورق أكتب عليهم.
examples.trans: Bring me some paper to write on.

examples.text: لفينا ورق دوالي اليوم الصبح للغدا مع اللبن.
examples.trans: We rolled grape leaves this morning for lunch with yogurt.

meanings.note: One sheet of paper or one leaf; the collective ورق means paper in general.

examples.trans: Write your number down for me on a piece of paper.
The tree leaf turns yellow in autumn.

meanings.note: Masculine word formed from ورق ('paper'), meaning 'made of paper'.

examples.text: نستخدم أكياس ورقية بدل البلاستيك بالمخبز.
examples.trans: We use paper bags instead of plastic at the bakery.

examples.text: لسه بفضل القراءة من كتاب ورقي أكتر من الشاشة.
examples.trans: I still prefer reading from a paper book rather than a screen.

meanings.note: Medical/everyday noun for swelling or a bump.

examples.text: حطّيت ثلج على إيدي عشان يخفّ الورم بسرعة.
examples.trans: I put ice on my hand so the swelling would go down quickly.

examples.text: صار في ورم خفيف برجله بعد ما التوى كاحله.
examples.trans: There was a slight swelling in his foot after he twisted his ankle.

meanings.note: Masculine singular loanword for wood varnish, with the Arabic definite article.

examples.text: دهنا الطاولات بالورنيش عشان تلمع وتحمي الخشب.
examples.trans: We coated the tables with varnish so they shine and protect the wood.

examples.text: ريحة الورنيش لسه قوية بالغرفة، افتح الشبابيك.
examples.trans: The smell of the varnish is still strong in the room—open the windows.

meanings.note: Refers to a scent, often used when describing food or perfume.

examples.trans: The food is delicious and the smell is appetizing.

examples.text: المطر نزل على التراب وريحة الأرض صارت بتجنن.
examples.trans: The rain fell on the soil and the scent of the earth became wonderful.

meanings.note: Form II verb for distributing flyers, portions, or kitchen tasks.

examples.text: سلمى قعدت عالكرسي ووزعت الشغل عالكل.
examples.trans: Salma sat in the chair and assigned tasks to everyone.

examples.text: نور وزعت كروت الدعوة عجيران الحارة.
examples.trans: Nour handed out invitation cards to the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Used for physical weight on a foot, scale measurements, or poetic meter.

examples.text: لا تحطي أي وزن عكاحلك اليوم أبدا.
examples.trans: Don't put any weight on your ankle at all today.

examples.text: قيس وزن الطحين والسكر بالميزان قبل العجن.
examples.trans: Weigh the flour and sugar on the scale before kneading.

meanings.note: Arabic verb وزّع meaning 'to distribute' or 'hand out'.

examples.text: وزّعوا الحلويات والقهوة على كل الجيران بمناسبة الافتتاح.
examples.trans: Hand out the sweets and coffee to all the neighbors for the grand opening.

examples.text: المعلمة وزّعت أوراق الامتحان عالطلاب الصبح.
examples.trans: The teacher handed out the exam papers to the students in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; وسط البلد means 'downtown / city centre'. Plural: أوساط.

examples.trans: We went down to downtown in the morning.
The table is right in the middle of the courtyard.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian adjective from وسط ('middle'); pairs naturally with المفتاح الوسطاني and ري الوسطى.

examples.text: المفتاح الوسطاني بالبيانو كان عالق من الرطوبة.
examples.trans: The middle key on the piano was stuck from dampness.

examples.text: الطاولة الوسطانية بالساحة بتاخد أحلى شمس.
examples.trans: The middle table in the courtyard catches the nicest sunshine.

وسع.gloss: to fit; hold; have room for

meanings.en: to fit; hold; have room for
meanings.note: Says how much a place holds: السيارة بتوسع خمس أشخاص 'the car fits five people'. Related to واسع, wide.

examples.trans: The bag doesn't hold all the books.
The table easily fits six.

meanings.note: Classic adjective on the فَعِيل pattern from root و-س-م ('mark of beauty').

examples.trans: The young man in the photo is very handsome.
His clothes were neat and he looked handsome.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine pronunciation of وجه (wajh, 'face'), heard constantly in Amman speech.

examples.trans: His face was beaming in the photo.
Wash your face with cold water.

meanings.note: Often used when describing the weather.

examples.trans: Today the weather is nice and the sun is out.

examples.text: الجو ربيع وشمس دافية بتشجع عالقعدة بالبلكونة.
examples.trans: The weather is springlike with a warm sun inviting us to sit on the balcony.

meanings.note: Third person plural past tense, describing the act of speaking softly.

examples.trans: The students whispered in the classroom.

examples.text: البنات وشوشوا بعضهم بالسر عشان ما يسمع حدا.
examples.trans: The girls whispered to each other secretly so nobody would hear.

meanings.note: Used for both a doctor's prescription and a cooking recipe.

examples.trans: The doctor gave me the medicine prescription.

examples.text: جربت وصفة الكعك تبعت خالتي وطلعت بتشهي.
examples.trans: I tried my aunt's cookie recipe and it turned out mouthwatering.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوصل, بيوصل).

examples.trans: Our guest arrived right on the second!
An official letter arrived at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: وصلات.

examples.trans: Shine the flashlight on the pipe joint.
We tightened the brass fitting with the wrench.

meanings.note: Depending on context, it can mean 'she arrived' or 'I arrived'. Most commonly 'she arrived' with 'wislet'.

examples.trans: She arrived on time.

examples.text: الحمد لله، وصلت الطيارة مطار الملكة علياء بالسلامة.
examples.trans: Thank goodness, the plane arrived safely at Queen Alia Airport.

meanings.en: arrival; reaching a place or time
meanings.note: Masculine verbal noun (masdar) of وصل ('to arrive/reach').

examples.text: لازم نخلص كل شي قبل وصول الضيوف.
examples.trans: We need to finish everything before the guests' arrival.
Thank God for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: هاد الوضع refers to an awkward or tense arrangement.

examples.trans: The situation at school is tense today.
I'm not comfortable with this situation.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; بوضوح means 'clearly'.

examples.trans: I can hear you clearly on the phone now.
He explained the idea with complete clarity.

meanings.note: Past tense verb combined with 'and', directed at a group.

examples.trans: Did you finish the work and go out early?

examples.text: سافرتوا عالعقبة وطلعتوا بالقارب بالبحر الأحمر؟
examples.trans: Did you travel to Aqaba and go out on the boat in the Red Sea?

meanings.en: to lower; to turn down (heat, volume)
meanings.note: Form II defective verb (بوطّي / وطّيت) from root و-ط-أ; used for turning down a stove flame or voice.

examples.trans: Turn down the gas a little under the pot.
Lower the volume, the baby is sleeping.

meanings.note: In Levantine school talk, وظيفة means 'homework' (كنت بعمل وظيفة) — a false friend if you only know its adult meaning 'job'!

examples.trans: We have math homework for tomorrow.
I finished the homework before bed.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: وعود.

examples.trans: We will come next week, promise!
He kept his promise and arrived on time.

meanings.note: Used in compound numbers (e.g., twenty-one, twenty-two).

examples.trans: He is twenty-five years old.

examples.text: دفعنا سبعة وعشرين دينار حساب الغدا بالمطعم.
examples.trans: We paid twenty-seven dinars for the lunch bill at the restaurant.

meanings.note: Preposition used to indicate position or direction, attached to 'and'.

examples.text: حطيت الكتاب ع الطاولة وعلى الكرسي.
examples.trans: I put the book on the table and on the chair.

examples.text: اتفقنا عالموعد وعلى كل تفاصيل المشروع الجديد.
examples.trans: We agreed on the appointment and on all the details of the new project.

meanings.note: Common noun for room, prefixed with 'and'.

examples.trans: The house has a living room and a bedroom.

examples.text: الشقة فيها مطبخ كبير وغرفة ضيوف بتطل عالشارع.
examples.trans: The apartment has a large kitchen and a guest room overlooking the street.

وفى.gloss: to fulfil; to keep a promise; to settle

meanings.en: to fulfil; to keep a promise; to settle
meanings.note: Doubly weak verb (root و-ف-ي, dropping initial w- in formal imperfect يفي; colloquially also Form II وفّى).

examples.text: دايما بفي بوعدي وما بتأخر عالفريق.
examples.trans: I always keep my promise and never arrive late for the team.

examples.text: رامي وفى بوعده وجاب الكرت الأصلي.
examples.trans: Rami kept his promise and brought the original card.

meanings.note: Can mean 'and in' or 'and there is' depending on context.

examples.text: رحنا على السوق وفي ناس كثير.
examples.trans: We went to the market and there are many people.

examples.text: عنا جلسة الصبح وفي اجتماع تاني بعد الضهر.
examples.trans: We have a session in the morning, and there is another meeting in the afternoon.

وفيه.gloss: and in it / and there is in it

meanings.en: and in it / and there is in it
meanings.note: Refers to something containing another thing, or simply 'and there is'.

examples.trans: The box is big and there are things in it.

examples.text: فتحت الدرج الصغير وفيه شوية مفاتيح قديمة.
examples.trans: I opened the small drawer, and there are a few old keys in it.

meanings.note: Form II verb from و-ف-ر; active participle موفر / موفرين ('saving, ahead on budget').

examples.text: خصم الدزينة وفر علينا مبلغ حلو.
examples.trans: The dozen discount saved us a nice amount.

examples.text: لما ندهن الشيش بإيدنا بنوفر بالميزانية.
examples.trans: When we paint the shutters ourselves, we save on the budget.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: He greeted the guests with calm dignity.
His speech carries wisdom and poise.

meanings.note: General term for time or duration.

examples.trans: I don't have time to go out today.

examples.text: بياخد الطريق من عمان لعجلون تقريباً وقت ساعة.
examples.trans: The road from Amman to Ajloun takes roughly an hour of time.

meanings.note: Time possessed by a second person masculine.

examples.trans: Take your time and don't rush.

examples.text: رتب وقتك منيح قبل أسبوع الامتحانات النهائية.
examples.trans: Organize your time well before final exams week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقع, بيوقع).

examples.text: نظارتك وقعت عن أنفك من الفرحة!
examples.trans: Your glasses fell off your nose for joy!

examples.text: أي نزل سحري هاد اللي وقعت فيه؟
examples.trans: What magical inn is this that you stumbled into?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقف, بيوقف).

examples.trans: A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate!
My heart stopped at page one!

meanings.note: Past tense, second person feminine singular.

examples.trans: Why did you stop in the middle of the road?

examples.text: ليش وقفتي السيارة بعيد عن المدخل رغم إنه فاضي؟
examples.trans: Why did you park the car far from the entrance even though it's empty?

meanings.note: Intensive adjective (فَعُول) from وقار ('dignity/calm poise'), describing quiet grace and gravitas.

examples.trans: That young man with the dignified appearance.
The professor is dignified and everyone respects him.

meanings.note: Past tense Arabic verb meaning 'to sign' a contract or lease.

examples.text: وقّعت عقد الإيجار مع صاحب المبنى مبارح.
examples.trans: I signed the lease contract with the building owner yesterday.

examples.text: لا توقّع على أي ورقة قبل ما تقرأها منيح.
examples.trans: Don't sign any paper before reading it carefully.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقف, بيوقف).

examples.text: وقفوا كل شي، قديش الساعة هلا؟
examples.trans: Stop everything — what time is it right now?
The driver pulled the car up by the kerb.

meanings.note: Quintessential Jordanian exclamation of astonishment, disbelief, or sudden surprise (pronounced wal).

examples.text: ول! كل هادا الحبر انكب عالطاولة؟
examples.trans: Whoa! All this ink spilled onto the table?
No way, could you really have finished the tasting that fast?

meanings.note: Used in negative constructions or as a strong negative emphasis.

examples.trans: Not even one of them came.

examples.text: سألت الكل بس ولا حدا بيعرف وين حطوا المفتاح.
examples.trans: I asked everyone, yet not a single person knows where they put the key.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ولاد.

examples.trans: The two boys learned piano together.
May you be blessed, my dear boys.

meanings.note: Used to describe a group of people holding something.

examples.trans: The kids are playing and holding each other's hands.

examples.text: الشباب واقفين عالدور وماسكين التذاكر بإيديهم.
examples.trans: The young people are standing in line holding the tickets in their hands.

meanings.note: Indicates association or possession related to a feminine entity.

examples.trans: She went to the market and her mother was with her.

examples.text: اجت صاحبتي عالسهرة ومعها صحن كنافة سخن.
examples.trans: My friend came to the evening gathering bringing a warm plate of kunafa with her.

meanings.note: Passive participle feminine form, often used for gifts or food.

examples.trans: The gift is ready and wrapped.

examples.text: الحلويات وصلت مرتبة ومغلفة بورق شفاف نظيف.
examples.trans: The sweets arrived neatly arranged and wrapped in clean clear wrap.

meanings.note: Can mean a desk or an office room.

examples.trans: We rented an apartment and an office.

examples.text: في الغرفة الجديدة في تخت وخزانة ومكتب للدراسة.
examples.trans: In the new room there is a bed, a closet, and a desk for studying.

meanings.note: Used to describe something that lacks moisture.

examples.trans: The bread is old and dry.

examples.text: لمينا الغسيل عن الحبل لأنه صار دافي وناشف تماماً.
examples.trans: We took the laundry off the line because it got warm and completely dry.

meanings.note: Used heavily in telling time (e.g., 'and a half' for 30 minutes past the hour).

examples.trans: The time is five and a half (five thirty).

examples.text: اشتريت كيلو ونص بندورة حمرا من سوق الخضرة.
examples.trans: I bought a kilo and a half of red tomatoes from the produce market.

meanings.note: Refers to half of a feminine object or quantity.

examples.text: أكلت التفاحة ونصها الثاني لسه موجود.
examples.trans: I ate the apple and the other half is still there.

examples.text: قرأت القصة ونصها التاني خليته لقبل النوم.
examples.trans: I read the story and left the second half of it for bedtime.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun used for masculine objects.

examples.trans: This is my friend and this is his brother.

examples.text: هذا القلم أزرق وهاذ اللي جنبه أسود، أي واحد بدك؟
examples.trans: This pen is blue and this one next to it is black—which one do you want?

meanings.note: Used as a collective noun for paper or leaves.

examples.trans: He gave me a pen and paper.

examples.text: جبنا من المكتبة ألوان مائية وورق مقوى للمشروع.
examples.trans: We picked up watercolors and cardstock paper from the stationery shop for the project.

meanings.note: Common urban Jordanian loanword from English weekend, alternating with عطلة نهاية الأسبوع.

examples.trans: On the weekend we visit my grandfather and bake together.

examples.text: عندنا خطة حلوة للويكند الجاي بالقرية.
examples.trans: We have a nice plan for next weekend in the village.

meanings.note: Appears in the dramatic warning يا ويل البنت اللي... ('woe to the girl who... / heaven help the girl who...').

examples.text: يا ويل اللي بيتأخر عن الحصة.
examples.trans: Woe to whoever is late to class.
We're in trouble if the teacher heard us.

meanings.note: The standard interrogative adverb for location in the dialect.

examples.trans: Where are you going?

examples.text: وين حطيت مفاتيح السيارة بعد ما رجعت من الشغل؟
examples.trans: Where did you put the car keys after you got back from work?

meanings.note: Present tense verb, also used for future with the prefix 'b'.

examples.text: رح يطلع من الشغل وييجي عندنا.
examples.trans: He will leave work and come to us.

examples.text: استنى شوي هون عبين ما يخلص صاحبي وييجي لعندنا.
examples.trans: Wait here a moment until my friend finishes and comes over to us.

meanings.note: Takes ب- for the thing promised: وعدته بغرفة 'I promised him a room'.

examples.text: خليني أحزر. وعدت حدا بغرفة مش موجودة عندنا؟
examples.trans: Let me guess. You promised somebody a room we do not have?
I promised you lemon cake on Friday.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Oh Ahmed, come here.

examples.text: يا سيدي، تفضل اشرب معنا فنجان قهوة قبل ما تروح.
examples.trans: Sir, please come have a cup of coffee with us before you leave.

meanings.note: Third person masculine singular verb with a first person plural object pronoun.

examples.trans: I want the bus to take us to the university.

examples.text: أبوي بده ياخذنا بالسيارة يوم الجمعة على جرش.
examples.trans: My dad wants to take us by car to Jerash on Friday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun (unit noun ياقوتة 'one ruby'). Used metaphorically for deep ruby-red colour in berries or glaze.

examples.trans: The colour of the red berries is like ruby.

examples.text: عندها خاتم فضة عليه حجر ياقوت.
examples.trans: She has a silver ring with a ruby stone on it.

meanings.note: Often means to quit doing something or to stop functioning.

examples.trans: He must quit smoking.

examples.text: قرّر يبطل سهر بالليل عشان يصحى نشيط عالدوام.
examples.trans: He decided to quit staying up late at night so he wakes up fresh for work.

meanings.note: Refers to abandoning or leaving a feminine object or person.

examples.trans: He decided to leave it and go.

examples.text: ما قدر يتركها لحالها بالمستشفى وضل قاعد عندها.
examples.trans: He couldn't leave her alone at the hospital and stayed sitting with her.

meanings.note: Colloquial verb meaning to trip over something or for a plan to fall apart.

examples.trans: Careful that he doesn't trip on the stairs.

examples.text: اربط بوتك منيح قبل ما تطلع تركض عشان ما تتفركش.
examples.trans: Tie your sneakers properly before going out to run so you don't trip.

meanings.note: For door handles and bag handles, Jordanian speakers often say يد الباب / عاليد alongside إيد for the human hand.

examples.text: ارفعي يد الباب أول وبعدين ادفعي.
examples.trans: Lift the door handle first, then push.

examples.text: في بطاقة مربوطة على يد الشنتة.
examples.trans: There is a tag tied to the handle of the bag.

meanings.note: Standard verb for entering.

examples.trans: Let him enter the room.

examples.text: افتح الباب للضيف عشان يدخل يقعد بالصالون.
examples.trans: Open the door for the guest so he can come in and sit in the living room.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from يد ('hand') using the glide -aw- before -ي; used for crafts and handmade notebooks.

examples.trans: Also the little notebook is handmade.
We love handmade embroidery work.

meanings.note: 'yruh' means 'he goes', 'yrawweh' often means 'he goes home'.

examples.trans: He wants to go to the market.

examples.text: لازم يروح عالبنك الصبح قبل ما تخلص ساعات الدوام.
examples.trans: He has to go to the bank in the morning before business hours end.

meanings.note: Casual loanword from English yes used playfully in celebratory speech when something succeeds.

examples.text: يس! الكيكة التانية طلعت مزبوطة مية بالمية!
examples.trans: Yes! The second cake turned out one hundred percent right!
Yes, the old lock finally opened!

meanings.note: Direction noun synonymous with شمال (left) in urban speech; frequently used as عاليسار (on the left).

examples.text: المكتبة موجودة على جهة اليسار بعد القوس.
examples.trans: The library is on the left side right after the arch.

examples.text: لفوا يسار عند النافورة بتلاقوا الممر.
examples.trans: Turn left at the fountain and you will find the passage.

meanings.note: Warm Jordanian/Levantine thank-you when someone hands you food, tea, or help (short for يسلموا إيديك 'may your hands be blessed').

examples.trans: Thank you, Salma, for the hot tea!
Thank you, it smells wonderful!

meanings.note: Everyday conversational bridge introducing an inference ('so that means...'), clarification, or gentle pause ('I mean...').

examples.trans: So the house says hello by itself?
Does that mean there is no heating tonight?

meanings.note: Very common interjection used to urge action or to say goodbye ('yalla bye').

examples.trans: Come on let's go, we're late.

examples.text: يلا البس جاكيتك بسرعة، الأوبر صار واقف تحت.
examples.trans: Come on, put your jacket on quickly—the Uber is already waiting downstairs.

meanings.note: Verb indicating physical contact.

examples.trans: No one is allowed to touch the things.

examples.text: الطفل بحب يلمس كل الأغراض اللي عالرفوف بالمحل.
examples.trans: The toddler loves touching all the items on the shelves in the store.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'maybe, perhaps'.

examples.trans: He is maybe thirty-five years old.
Perhaps he got delayed in downtown traffic.

meanings.note: Used for forbidding or stopping something from happening.

examples.trans: The law forbids smoking here.

examples.text: الشرطي يمنع الوقوف عند الزاوية وقت أزمة السير.
examples.trans: The officer forbids stopping at the corner during rush hour.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The green pharmacy is on your right.
We hung the board to the right of the desk.

meanings.note: Passive/Reflexive verb often used for electricity or water being cut off.

examples.trans: The electricity might get cut off today.

examples.text: خايفين ينقطع الإنترنت بنص المكالمة المهمة.
examples.trans: We're worried the internet might cut out in the middle of the important call.

meanings.note: Used for a person or thing falling down.

examples.trans: Be careful the boy doesn't fall.

examples.text: لا تحط الصحن عالحفة عشان ما يوقع وينكسر.
examples.trans: Don't put the plate right on the edge so it doesn't fall and break.

meanings.note: Very common colloquial verb for eating.

examples.trans: He wants to eat an apple.

examples.text: أخي الصغير ما بحب يوكل خضار مسلوقة بدون ليمون.
examples.trans: My little brother doesn't like to eat boiled vegetables without lemon.

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today is a long day.

examples.text: سافرنا عالعقبة وقعدنا هناك يوم كامل عالشط.
examples.trans: We traveled to Aqaba and spent a whole day there at the beach.

meanings.note: Adverb 'on a daily basis, every day'.

examples.trans: The ground floor serves the neighbours daily.
We bake fresh bread daily.
